commit.message:
CI: Switch pr-checks and pr-commands workflows to yarn (#121930)

* CI: Switch pr-checks and pr-commands workflows to yarn

The grafana-github-actions repo has `"engines": {"npm": "please-use-yarn"}`
in its package.json, which causes `npm install` to fail now that GitHub
Actions runners enforce engine-strict mode. Switch to yarn, which is how
the upstream repo is intended to be installed.

unified-storage: update integration test setup for HA and sqlite (#121951)

unified-storage: update integration test setup for HA and sqlite use

When running in HA mode, skip integration tests with sqlite. Similary, when
*not* in HA mode, skip integration tests with mysql and postgresql.

This commit also updates the bulk import function to always set the `Error`
field in the response when an error happens so that they are caught by tests.

Makefile: Fix integration test shard.sh not reading piped input (#119523)

The integration test targets pipe pkgs-with-tests-named.sh output into
shard.sh, but shard.sh was missing the `-d -` flag needed to read from
stdin. Without it, shard.sh ignores the filtered package list and
independently discovers all packages, defeating the purpose of the
pre-filtering step.

This matches how the GitHub Actions workflow invokes the same pipeline.

commit.message:
Unified: fix write delay cancelled too early during shutdown (#121985)

* Resource server: fix write delay cancelled too early during shutdown

The sleepAfterSuccessfulWriteOperation select included a case on
s.ctx.Done(), which is cancelled by s.cancel() in Stop() before
inflight.Wait(). This meant in-flight write delays were cut short
during shutdown, breaking the search-after-write consistency guarantee.

Remove the s.ctx.Done() case so in-flight writes complete their full
artificial delay. The request context still provides cancellation if
the client disconnects, and Stop()'s inflight.Wait() (bounded by the
stop context deadline) ensures graceful shutdown.

Also remove the goleak ignore for runtimeconfig.Manager.loop and add
the missing service.stop() cleanup in quotas_test.go.

commit.message:
Storage: fix race in batchRunner when MaxIdle is zero (#122016)

* Storage: fix race in batchRunner when MaxIdle is zero

When MaxIdle was set to 0 (no idle timeout), NextBatch used a
non-blocking select with a default branch to drain additional items
from the channel. This created a race: after the first item was
consumed, the recvLoop goroutine often hadn't placed the next item
into the channel yet, causing the default branch to fire and return
an under-full batch.

Fix by replacing the non-blocking select with a blocking channel read,
matching the intended semantics of MaxIdle=0 (fill up to MaxItems with
no timeout). All termination paths (channel close, EOF, error) are
still handled correctly.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Storage: remove dead MaxIdle<=0 branch in batchRunner

Replace the duplicate MaxIdle<=0 / MaxIdle>0 code paths with a single
loop. A nil timer channel is never selected in Go, so when MaxIdle=0
the select blocks on the recv channel alone (fills up to MaxItems or
EOF). When MaxIdle>0 the timer fires as before.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
unified-storage: improve error handling and improve test coverage (#121814)

This PR cleans up error handling in the two backends and verify we get expected errors from the resource server. The main changes are:

* server stops trying to identify optimistic locking errors, as the storage backend is the one that performs the authoritative checks. RV validation and conflict detection moved to the storage backend.
* Server stops setting RV to `latest` in update and delete, and storage backend enforces that RV was passed by client
* optimistic lock checks in the KV backend now return a 409 (conflict) instead of a 500, allowing clients to easily identify the situation and retry the operation if desired.

commit.message:
InteractiveTable: Support specific column widths (#121384)

* InteractiveTable: support specific column widths

Add width, minWidth, and maxWidth properties to the Column interface
for InteractiveTable, allowing consumers to control column sizing
explicitly.

Previously the only width control was disableGrow (boolean), which
prevented a column from flexing beyond its content but offered no way
to set a specific width. This caused confusing spacing in tables where
some columns (like "Port") wasted horizontal space.

Changes:
- types.ts: add width, minWidth, maxWidth optional number props
- utils.ts: pass width/minWidth/maxWidth to react-table column config
  (width falls back to disableGrow behavior when not specified)

commit.message:
Zanzana: deduplicate folder batch checks and fix ensuredNamespaces cache (#121834)

Zanzana: deduplicate folder batch checks in phases 2 and 3

BatchCheck phases 2 (folder permission) and 3 (folder subresource) were
sending one OpenFGA check per batch item even when many items shared the
same folder+relation. For example, 20 dashboards in the same folder would
produce 20 identical (user, can_get, folder:1) checks.

This introduces a dedupBatcher that groups identical folder checks so only
one round-trip is issued per unique (relation, folderIdent, groupResource)
tuple, with results fanned out to all matching correlation IDs.

QueryEditor: Multi-selection with ctrl/shift modifiers (2/3) (#120139)

* Refactor(qev2): extract UI toggles hook + migrate selection state to arrays

- Extracts useQueryEditorUIToggles: pulls isQueryOptionsOpen, focusedField,
  showingDatasourceHelp, and transformTogglesState out of QueryEditorContextWrapper
  into a dedicated hook, reducing the size of the wrapper component.

- Migrates selection model from scalar string|null to string[] arrays:
  selectedQueryRefIds and selectedTransformationIds. The "primary" card is
  always the last element, so single-select behaviour is unchanged. This
  prepares the context for multi-selection in the next PR.

- Updates useSelectedCard, QueryEditorContextWrapper, testUtils, and all
  related tests accordingly. Pure refactor — no user-visible behaviour change.

Made-with: Cursor

* Feat(qev2): multi-selection on sidebar cards with Ctrl/Shift modifiers

Adds multi-select support to the query/transformation sidebar so users
can select multiple cards before applying a bulk action.

- useMultiSelection hook: manages ordered multi-selection state for
  queries and transformations. Supports plain click (replace selection),
  Ctrl/Cmd click (toggle card), and Shift click (range-select). Query and
  transformation selections are mutually exclusive.

- SidebarCard: renames onClick → onSelect, passes { multi, range } modifiers
  derived from the click event. Shift+mousedown prevents native text selection.
  Adds isPartOfSelection prop for a subtle tint on non-primary selected cards.
  Exposes aria-pressed for both primary and part-of-selection cards.

- QueryCard / TransformationCard / AlertCard / GhostSidebarCard: switch
  from setSelectedQuery/setSelectedTransformation to toggleQuerySelection /
  toggleTransformationSelection.

- EditableQueryName: new readOnly mode (renders plain text) used when
  multiple queries are selected, preventing accidental rename.

- Wires toggleQuerySelection, toggleTransformationSelection, and
  clearSelection through QueryEditorContext and QueryEditorContextWrapper.

Made-with: Cursor

* fix: multi selection logic

* fix: improve selection state management with refs for queries and transformations

* chore: other PR feedback

feat: index snapshot configuration settings (#121333)

* feat: index snapshot configuration settings (#719)

Add 9 index_snapshot_* settings under [unified_storage] ini section
for configuring remote index snapshot behavior.

Settings: index_snapshot_enabled (bool), index_snapshot_bucket_url (string),
index_snapshot_remote_threshold (int), index_snapshot_upload_interval (duration),
index_snapshot_upload_doc_threshold (int), index_snapshot_cleanup_interval (duration),
index_snapshot_max_age (duration), index_snapshot_lock_ttl (duration),
index_snapshot_min_keep (int).

- Parsed in setting_unified_storage.go, stored on Cfg struct
- Uses config option (not feature toggle) — instance-level, not tenant-level
- Wired through NewSearchOptions into SearchOptions
- Bucket URL supports mem://, file:///, s3://, gs://, azblob://
- All settings documented with defaults in conf/defaults.ini

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: reduce snapshot config to essential options only

Per review feedback, remove all advanced snapshot config options from
public config surface. Keep only index_snapshot_enabled and
index_snapshot_bucket_url as configurable. Other parameters (thresholds,
intervals, TTLs) will use sensible hardcoded defaults internally.

Also remove all snapshot entries from defaults.ini since this is an
experimental feature not yet ready for public documentation.

commit.message:
feat(connections): derive landing page cards from nav tree (#122017)

* feat(connections): derive landing page cards from nav tree

The Connections landing page previously used a hardcoded card list
(CardData.ts) that was not aware of which plugins were actually enabled
or whether the current user had RBAC access to them.

Cards are now derived directly from the navIndex 'connections' children,
which are already built by the backend with full plugin availability and
RBAC checks applied. A URL-keyed CardMetadata map provides icons and
descriptions for well-known items, taking priority over nav tree values
(which are written for nav tooltip context, not landing page cards).

This means:
- Cards appear only when the backend decides the user can see them
- The flat nav mode from grafana-collector-app PR #1047 is automatically
  reflected: Alloy Configuration / Collector Setup, Instrumentation Hub,
  Fleet Management appear as individual cards when collectorFlattenedNav
  is enabled, without any changes needed here
- Any future plugin registering pages under Connections gets a card for free

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(connections): restore OSS/Cloud subtitle distinction

The subtitle on the Connections landing page was OSS/Cloud conditional
in the original code. The nav-tree refactor accidentally always showed
the Cloud copy. Restored the isOnPrem check so OSS instances continue
to see their original subtitle.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(connections): restore OSS card description for Add new connection

The original CardData.ts had OSS-specific text for the Add new connection
card ('Connect to a new data source' vs 'Connect data to Grafana through
data sources, integrations and apps' for Cloud). CardMetadata now accepts
isOnPrem and returns the correct subtitle per edition.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(connections): restore OSS title and description parity with original CardData

CardMetadata now also supports an optional text override so the Data
sources card shows 'View configured data sources' on OSS (matching the
original getOssCardData behaviour). Config is reset to Cloud defaults in
beforeEach to prevent test state bleed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(connections): address Copilot review comments and sync locale file

- Use nullish coalescing (??) instead of || for subTitle/text merging
  to avoid overwriting intentionally empty strings
- cardMetadata is computed inside the component (already the case after
  isOnPrem was introduced as a parameter) so translations resolve at
  render time, not at import time
- Sync mock: standalone navIndex entry for infrastructure now says
  'Integrations' to match the children entry
- Update CardMetadata comment to accurately describe that core nav items
  are also intentionally overridden for landing-page card copy
- Sync en-US locale file: remove deleted title keys, add new
  collector-setup, fleet-management and instrumentation-hub subtitle keys

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(i18n): remove unused OSS data-sources subtitle key from locale file

The OSS data-sources card now uses the cloud subtitle key directly;
the oss-specific subtitle is no longer referenced in code.

* Unified: fix write delay cancelled too early during shutdown (#121985)

* Resource server: fix write delay cancelled too early during shutdown

The sleepAfterSuccessfulWriteOperation select included a case on
s.ctx.Done(), which is cancelled by s.cancel() in Stop() before
inflight.Wait(). This meant in-flight write delays were cut short
during shutdown, breaking the search-after-write consistency guarantee.

Remove the s.ctx.Done() case so in-flight writes complete their full
artificial delay. The request context still provides cancellation if
the client disconnects, and Stop()'s inflight.Wait() (bounded by the
stop context deadline) ensures graceful shutdown.

Also remove the goleak ignore for runtimeconfig.Manager.loop and add
the missing service.stop() cleanup in quotas_test.go.

* Storage: fix race in batchRunner when MaxIdle is zero (#122016)

* Storage: fix race in batchRunner when MaxIdle is zero

When MaxIdle was set to 0 (no idle timeout), NextBatch used a
non-blocking select with a default branch to drain additional items
from the channel. This created a race: after the first item was
consumed, the recvLoop goroutine often hadn't placed the next item
into the channel yet, causing the default branch to fire and return
an under-full batch.

Fix by replacing the non-blocking select with a blocking channel read,
matching the intended semantics of MaxIdle=0 (fill up to MaxItems with
no timeout). All termination paths (channel close, EOF, error) are
still handled correctly.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Storage: remove dead MaxIdle<=0 branch in batchRunner

Replace the duplicate MaxIdle<=0 / MaxIdle>0 code paths with a single
loop. A nil timer channel is never selected in Go, so when MaxIdle=0
the select blocks on the recv channel alone (fills up to MaxItems or
EOF). When MaxIdle>0 the timer fires as before.

* Unified: fix write delay cancelled too early during shutdown (#121985)

* Resource server: fix write delay cancelled too early during shutdown

The sleepAfterSuccessfulWriteOperation select included a case on
s.ctx.Done(), which is cancelled by s.cancel() in Stop() before
inflight.Wait(). This meant in-flight write delays were cut short
during shutdown, breaking the search-after-write consistency guarantee.

Remove the s.ctx.Done() case so in-flight writes complete their full
artificial delay. The request context still provides cancellation if
the client disconnects, and Stop()'s inflight.Wait() (bounded by the
stop context deadline) ensures graceful shutdown.

Also remove the goleak ignore for runtimeconfig.Manager.loop and add
the missing service.stop() cleanup in quotas_test.go.

* Storage: fix race in batchRunner when MaxIdle is zero (#122016)

* Storage: fix race in batchRunner when MaxIdle is zero

When MaxIdle was set to 0 (no idle timeout), NextBatch used a
non-blocking select with a default branch to drain additional items
from the channel. This created a race: after the first item was
consumed, the recvLoop goroutine often hadn't placed the next item
into the channel yet, causing the default branch to fire and return
an under-full batch.

Fix by replacing the non-blocking select with a blocking channel read,
matching the intended semantics of MaxIdle=0 (fill up to MaxItems with
no timeout). All termination paths (channel close, EOF, error) are
still handled correctly.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Storage: remove dead MaxIdle<=0 branch in batchRunner

Replace the duplicate MaxIdle<=0 / MaxIdle>0 code paths with a single
loop. A nil timer channel is never selected in Go, so when MaxIdle=0
the select blocks on the recv channel alone (fills up to MaxItems or
EOF). When MaxIdle>0 the timer fires as before.

Alerting: Alert activity groupBy not filtering by environment (#121952)

* Alerting: fix scope alert rule instances to parent group labels

The method alertRuleInstancesQuery(ruleUID, filter) only added matchers for the global filter string plust grafana_rule_uid, and there were no parent group matchers in the expression, causing PromQL to not restrict instances to the expanded row's group.

The fix was to thread those parent group label values from the Workbench compoentn down to AlertRuleInstances, and including those labels as PromQL matchers in alertRuleInstacesQuery so that expanding a rule under a specific group only shows instances belonging to that group.

* Address code review comments

- Removed redundant String() call
- Added missing assertions in test
- Refactored arrow function expression AlertRuleRow to function declaration

commit.message:
IAM: increase observability in TestIntegrationTeamBindings (#121751)

* IAM: fix flaky TestIntegrationTeamBindings under Postgres/MySQL

The test was intermittently failing in CI with:
  pq: canceling statement due to user request

Root cause: the shared HTTP test client has a 30s timeout. In CI,
mode_0 runs first (~280s). By the time mode_1 starts, the basicRoleCache
(30s TTL) has expired. The GetBasicRoles DB query on cache miss takes
long enough under Postgres load that the client-side timeout fires,
closes the connection, cancels the server-side request context, and
database/sql sends pg_cancel_backend() to Postgres.

Fix: use context.WithoutCancel for the GetBasicRoles DB query in
getUserBasicRole. RBAC lookups should not be interruptible by a client
disconnect — the query must complete for correct authorization.

Also split TestIntegrationTeamBindings into TestIntegrationTeamBindingsMode0
and TestIntegrationTeamBindingsMode1 so each mode has an independent
lifecycle. The original broad t.Skip was incorrectly skipping mode_0
as collateral damage.

* IAM: apply context.WithoutCancel at getUserPermissions entry point

The previous fix only covered GetBasicRoles, but getUserTeams and
GetUserIdentifiers have the same vulnerability. Apply context.WithoutCancel
once at the getUserPermissions entry point so all downstream DB lookups
are covered.

* revert: remove context.WithoutCancel from getUserPermissions

The context detach hid the flakiness rather than exposing it — removing it so the timeout surfaces visibly in logs and can be properly diagnosed.

* test: add per-helper HTTP timeout override to K8sTestHelper

Adds HTTPClientTimeout field to K8sTestHelperOpts that clones the shared client with a custom timeout, leaving other tests unaffected.

* test(iam): increase observability in TestIntegrationTeamBindings

Merge Mode0/Mode1 back into a single test with table-driven subtests, enable Grafana logger output, and raise the HTTP client timeout to 60s so slow authz checks are logged rather than silently timed out.

* fixup: restore test structure in TestIntegrationTeamBindings

The previous commit deviated from main by dropping the subtest name, inline comments, and the if mode < 3 guard on legacy API tests. This restores those to match the original, keeping only the intended additions: EnableLog and HTTPClientTimeout.

* tests: replace HTTPClientTimeout with CustomHTTPClient field

commit.message:
PieChartPanel: Add gradient color scheme with WCAG-aware slice labels (#121303)

Adds a new 'Gradient' option to the standard Color scheme picker (positioned
after 'Shades of a color'). When selected, two inline color pickers appear —
identical layout to 'Single color' — where the start color is assigned to the
largest slice and the end color to the smallest. All intermediate slices receive
linearly interpolated RGB fills ordered by value.

On-slice labels (name, value, percent) automatically switch between black and
white text using tinycolor.mostReadable() so they remain readable at any point
in the gradient. Legend item colors are kept in sync by computing the fills once
in PieChartPanel and sharing the same Map with both the chart and the legend.

Changes:
- @grafana/data: add FieldColorModeId.Gradient; add FieldColor.gradientColorTo
- fieldColorModeRegistry: register Gradient mode after Shades in the initializer
- FieldColorEditor: render two inline ColorValueEditor pickers for Gradient;
  seed fixedColor and gradientColorTo defaults on mode switch
- PieChart: accept pre-computed gradientFills map; pick WCAG-contrasting label
  color per slice using tinycolor.mostReadable
- PieChartPanel: compute gradient fills once, share with chart and legend
- module: seed fixedColor default so Single color / Shades / Gradient never
  open with an empty (gray) picker on a fresh panel
- Add 11 unit tests for computeGradientFills (N=1/2/5, edge cases, monotonicity)
- Add 10 RTL tests for FieldColorEditor gradient UI branch

Fixes #121301

Zanzana: Add sync hooks for service account basic role assignments (#122082)

* Zanzana: Add sync hooks for service account basic role assignments

Add real-time sync hooks that write service account basic role assignments
to Zanzana immediately on create/update/delete, rather than waiting for
batch reconciliation. This mirrors the existing user org role hooks pattern.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* IAM: Revoke role on None downgrade, deduplicate org role tuple logic

When a service account's role is downgraded to None, only delete the
old role assignment instead of writing a new None role. Also extract
shared getOrgRoleUpdateTuples helper to eliminate duplication between
user and service account update tuple functions.

commit.message:
unified-storage: retry on creation conflict in resource client (#122078)

Previously, when multiple concurrent clients attempted to create the same resource, they could all fail and the resource would not be created due to optimistic lock checks.

In #121814, optimistic lock checks started returning a conflict (409) error when a concurrent modification was detected. In this PR, the resource client is updated to detect this kind of error and return an `Aborted` response code in the corresponding grpc call:

> `ABORTED`: The operation was aborted, typically due to a concurrency issue such as a sequencer check failure or transaction abort.

https://grpc.io/docs/guides/status-codes/

When attempting to perform a `Create`, the resource client will retry failed attempts after applying a backoff and jitter. In a scenario with multiple concurrent writers, one writer should succeed -- not as a guarantee, but as a high probability event.

commit.message:
IAM: Skip propagating None role to Zanzana for user hooks (#122156)

Align user hooks with service account behavior: when a user's role is
set to None, only revoke the previous role assignment instead of writing
a None role to Zanzana. Also skip Zanzana sync on create/delete when
the user has a None role.

commit.message:
Search: Fix title search scoring and add DoubleEquals exact match operator (#122226)

* Search: Fix title search scoring and add DoubleEquals exact match operator

Fix broken title search query construction and add support for exact
title matching via the == operator in field requirements.

Phase 1 search query fixes:
- Target title_phrase (pre-lowered keyword field) for exact match boost
  instead of title (mixed analyzer field with original case)
- Use TermQuery + ToLower instead of MatchQuery + keyword analyzer,
  giving case-insensitive exact matching that actually fires
- Remove dead boost=5 TEXT query on title_phrase — standard analyzer
  splits the query into word tokens, but title_phrase only has a single
  keyword term (the full title), so multi-word titles never matched
- Update duplicate QueryFields in dashboard search.go

DoubleEquals operator:
- Split selection.Equals and selection.DoubleEquals into separate cases
  in requirementQuery — previously treated identically
- == always does exact matching via TermQuery. For title, routes to
  title_phrase with lowered values. For keyword fields (tags, folder),
  behaves same as = (already exact)
- = keeps current fuzzy/word match behavior unchanged

* Update search test snapshots for new score values

The query changes (3 disjunction queries → 2) change BM25 scoring
internals: coord factor goes from 1/3 to 1/2, queryNorm changes
accordingly. Same documents matched in same order, only absolute
score values differ.

* Simplify DoubleEquals to single-value only, add error tests

Handle only len(values) == 1 for DoubleEquals; 0 or >1 values fall
through to BadRequestError. Add tests verifying the error response
for both cases.

commit.message:
Alerting: Fix crash when MultiCombobox value contains duplicates (#122180)

* Alerting: Fix crash when MultiCombobox value contains duplicates

getSelectedItemsFromValue used a Map keyed by value to build the selected items array.
When the value prop contained duplicates (e.g. ['a', 'a', 'b']),
Map deduplication kept the last index, leaving earlier indices unassigned,
creating a sparse array with undefined holes. Downstream iteration in useMeasureMulti then
crashed accessing .label on undefined. Deduplicate the value array before building the Map so the result
 is always dense. Also add optional chaining in useMeasureMulti as a defensive guard.

* Refctor map & dedup into single loop

commit.message:
CI: Add endpoint migration feature toggle check (#122183)

* CI: Add endpoint migration feature toggle check

Add a GitHub Actions workflow that detects frontend-only PRs migrating
API endpoints (replacing old calls with new K8s API clients from
@grafana/api-clients/rtkq/) without gating behind config.featureToggles.

Frontend deploys uniformly to all users while backend rolls out through
release channels. Without a feature toggle, users on slower channels may
hit errors when their backend doesn't yet serve the new endpoints.

The check uses a two-signal detection approach:
- Signal 1: New @grafana/api-clients/rtkq/ imports adde
- Signal 2: Old API code removed (getBackendSrv, old client imports, or
data-fetching hooks)

Only when both signals are present is it treated as a migration. A
config.featureToggles.* reference on an added line satisfies the check.

Bypass with the 'no-check-endpoint-feature-toggle' label.

* Extract script for easier testing

* Cleanup script

* Update codeowners with new workflow

* Add new workflow to the required checks list in policy.yml

Create a simple counter-based uniqueId utility and replace all 9 lodash
uniqueId imports across grafana-ui components:
- Switch, CollapsableSection, MenuGroup, InteractiveTable
- RadioButtonList, RadioButtonGroup, Legacy Switch
- CustomHeadersSettings, FileDropzone (keeps isString from lodash)

* chore(grafana-ui): replace uniqueId with React useId hook for DOM element linking

- Replace uniqueId with useId in Switch component
- Replace uniqueId with useId in Collapse/CollapsableSection component
- Replace uniqueId with useId in Menu/MenuGroup component
- Replace uniqueId with useId in Forms/RadioButtonList component
- Replace uniqueId with useId in Forms/RadioButtonGroup component
- Replace uniqueId with useId in InteractiveTable component

useId is the recommended React hook for generating stable IDs for linking DOM elements
and is better suited for SSR scenarios.

Note: Components that generate IDs for internal data objects (FileDropzone, CustomHeadersSettings)
and the legacy PureComponent-based Switch continue using the internal uniqueId utility.

commit.message:
Import: Library panel missing DS when imported in v1 and classic  (#119980)

* fix(import): preserve library panel UIDs and interpolate datasources on import

When importing a classic/V1 dashboard with library panels through the
K8s path, two issues caused library panels to appear broken:

1. addLibraryPanel did not pass the original UID to the API, so the
   backend generated a new random UID while dashboard panels still
   referenced the original — breaking the link.

2. Library panel models from __elements still contained ${DS_...}
   placeholders. Unlike the legacy backend path which ran a full
   recursive interpolation, the K8s frontend path only interpolated
   panels/annotations/variables but never touched __elements models.

This fix:
- Passes the original UID when creating library elements during import
- Interpolates ${DS_...} placeholders in library panel models before
  creating them, using the same datasource mappings from the import form

Fixes #119494

* fix(import): extract shared datasource placeholder resolution and handle legacy string format

Address PR feedback:
- Extract `extractDatasourcePlaceholder` and `resolveDatasource` helpers
  to deduplicate datasource placeholder detection across
  `interpolateLibraryPanelDatasources`, `processPanel`, and
  `processAnnotation`.
- Handle the legacy string datasource format (`"${DS_PROMETHEUS}"`)
  in addition to the object form (`{ uid: "${DS_PROMETHEUS}" }`),
  fixing imports of very old community dashboards.
- Add tests for legacy string datasource placeholders in both
  library panel interpolation and V1 dashboard import.

Fixes #117859

* Apply missing fix to variables

---------

Co-authored-by: alexandra vargas <alexa1866@gmail.com>

commit.message:
Search: add dedicated title_ngram index field (#122330)

search: add dedicated title_ngram index field for ngram search

Add a separate title_ngram index mapping with the ngram analyzer,
and include it in the default QueryFields (boost=1). This is the
first step toward separating ngram analysis from the title field.

The existing triple-mapping on title (standard + ngram + keyword)
is kept for backward compatibility — indexers deploy before clients,
with a gap up to a month. A follow-up will remove the redundant
ngram + keyword from title once all clients include title_ngram.

Changes:
- Add SEARCH_FIELD_TITLE_NGRAM constant and title_ngram index mapping
- Add title_ngram (TEXT, boost=1) to default and dashboard QueryFields
- Rename EDGE_NGRAM_MIN_TOKEN to NGRAM_MIN_TOKEN (the analyzer uses
  full ngrams, not edge ngrams)
- Add index_server_search_legacy_query_fields_total metric to track
  when old clients stop sending QueryFields without title_ngram
- Add tests for title_ngram field independently and scoring hierarchy
- Update integration test snapshots (score changes from 2→3 member
  disjunction)

Zanzana: merge legacy and Zanzana permissions in searchUsersPermissions (#121258)

* Zanzana: merge legacy and Zanzana permissions in searchUsersPermissions

During migration, permissions live in both the legacy RBAC store and
Zanzana. The previous fallback logic (use Zanzana, fall back to legacy
only on error) silently returned an empty set for any action not yet
migrated to Zanzana.

This change always queries the legacy store as a baseline and, when the
`zanzanaSearchUsersPermissions` feature flag is enabled, merges in
results from Zanzana on top. Permissions are deduplicated by
action+scope per user so neither source wins over the other — the
result is the union.

Key changes:
- Add `mergePermissions` helper and wiring in `api.go`
- Add `zanzanaSearchUsersPermissions` feature flag (experimental, off by default)
- New `zanzanaPermissionResolver` in `zanzana_resolver.go` that resolves
  permissions via Zanzana's `List` RPC, translating scopes back to
  legacy RBAC format for proper deduplication
- Extend `zanzana.Client` interface with a `List` method
- Centralise action→Zanzana params mapping in `translations.go` via new
  `SupportedActions()` and `TranslateActionToListParams` (now returns
  group/resource/verb); remove hardcoded action list in resolver
- Fix N+1 in `searchAllUsers`: paginate user fetches (500/page) and
  fan-out with bounded concurrency (16 workers via errgroup)
- Wire `zanzanaClient` into `acimpl.ProvideService` and reorder
  dependency init in `wire_gen.go`

* accesscontrol: resolve Zanzana permissions from search hits without per-user GetByID

searchAllUsers already receives id and uid from user.Search; use that identity
to build the Zanzana subject instead of calling GetByID for every user.
Fall back to GetByID when uid is empty.

* accesscontrol: add debug logging for user permissions search request

Enhance the searchUsersPermissions function by adding detailed debug logging. This includes logging the organization ID, caller user ID, namespaced ID, user ID, action, action prefix, and scope to aid in troubleshooting and monitoring user permissions search requests.

* accesscontrol: add unit tests for Zanzana permission resolver

Introduce unit tests for the Zanzana permission resolver to validate the mapping of Zanzana folders to legacy folder scopes, inclusion of wildcards for dashboard actions, and the application of scope filters to folder scopes. These tests ensure the correct functionality of the listPermissions method in various scenarios.

* accesscontrol: add List method to mock Zanzana client in tests

Enhance the mock Zanzana client implementations in both collectors_test.go and resource_reconciler_orphan_test.go by adding a List method. This addition allows for better testing of interactions with the Zanzana API, specifically for handling List requests in unit tests.

* accesscontrol: update user context access in searchUsersPermissions

Refactor the searchUsersPermissions function to utilize the updated context model. Replace direct calls to SignedInUser methods with context methods for retrieving organization ID and user ID, improving code clarity and consistency.

* make update-workspace

* address comments

* Enhance zanzanaPermissionResolver to support wildcard scope filtering in listPermissions. Add comprehensive unit tests to validate behavior for various scope scenarios, ensuring correct inclusion and exclusion of permissions based on wildcards.

* Refactor zanzanaPermissionResolver to enhance wildcard scope handling in listPermissions. Introduce capturingZanzanaClient for improved test assertions and add legacy filtering functions to ensure accurate permission matching. Update unit tests to cover new edge cases and scenarios for scope filtering.

* Enhance AccessControlAPI: Integrate actionResolver into zanzanaPermissionResolver and improve permission merging logic. This update allows for better handling of action sets and ensures permissions are correctly appended without altering the original slices.

* Zanzana: memoize SupportedActions slice at package init

Build the action list once from resourceTranslations via an immediately
invoked function and return the same slice from SupportedActions(), per
review feedback.

* wire gen

* chore: sync go.sum after make update-workspace

* fix(featuremgmt): set Generate for zanzanaSearchUsersPermissions

Legacy Go/frontend generation is required for this flag name and keeps
make gen-feature-toggles / CI feature toggle checks passing.

* Fix typo: rename actionMappig to actionMapping

commit.message:
Provisioning: Add integration tests for cross-namespace isolation with folder sync (#122431)

* Fix: Use repository namespace instead of object namespace in provisioning

## Problem

Resources from different repositories in different organizations/namespaces
were all being created in the default organization, causing ownership conflicts.

The error manifested as:
"resource 'X' is managed by repo 'repository-A' and cannot be modified by
repo 'repository-B'"

## Root Cause

In `parser.go`, both the `Run()` and `DryRun()` methods used:
```go
identity.WithProvisioningIdentity(ctx, f.Obj.GetNamespace())
```

This attempted to get the namespace from the resource object itself, which
is often empty or not set in the JSON files. When empty, it defaults to
the default organization.

## Solution

Changed to use the repository's namespace instead:
```go
identity.WithProvisioningIdentity(ctx, f.Repo.Namespace)
```

The `f.Repo.Namespace` field contains the correct namespace from the
repository configuration, ensuring resources are created in the proper
organization/namespace.

## Impact

- Resources from repository A (in org X) will now correctly be created in org X
- Resources from repository B (in org Y) will now correctly be created in org Y
- No more ownership conflicts between repositories in different namespaces

Fixes: https://github.com/grafana/git-ui-sync-project/issues/1055

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Add integration tests for provisioning namespace isolation

Tests verify that:
1. Resources from different repositories are created with correct namespace
2. The provisioning identity is derived from f.Repo.Namespace (not f.Obj.GetNamespace())
3. No ownership conflicts occur between repositories
4. Repository metadata is correctly preserved across syncs

These tests cover the bug fix where f.Obj.GetNamespace() was incorrectly
used instead of f.Repo.Namespace, causing resources to be created in the
wrong namespace/organization.

Test package: pkg/tests/apis/provisioning/orgs

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Add comprehensive CRUD and security isolation tests for provisioning files

**Files CRUD Tests** (`files_crud_test.go`):
- TestFilesCreate_NamespaceIsolation - Verify file creation respects namespace boundaries
- TestFilesRead_NamespaceIsolation - Verify file reads are properly scoped
- TestFilesUpdate_NamespaceIsolation - Verify updates maintain namespace/ownership
- TestFilesDelete_NamespaceIsolation - Verify deletions are repository-scoped
- TestFilesCRUD_CrossRepositoryIsolation - Verify ops in one repo don't affect another
- TestFilesNamespaceConsistency - Verify namespace maintained through full lifecycle

**Security/Attack Tests** (`security_isolation_test.go`):
- TestAttack_CrossRepositoryFileAccess - Attempt to read/modify files from other repos
- TestAttack_ResourceOwnershipHijacking - Attempt to claim resources owned by others
- TestAttack_NamespaceLeakage - Verify resources don't leak across namespaces
- TestAttack_MaliciousFileOperations - Test path traversal and malicious paths
- TestAttack_SyncJobManipulation - Verify sync jobs are properly scoped
- TestAttack_ResourceNameCollision - Test UID collision scenarios

These tests verify the namespace isolation fix works correctly by:
1. Testing normal CRUD operations maintain proper isolation
2. Simulating attacker scenarios that try to break isolation
3. Ensuring the bug (using f.Obj.GetNamespace() instead of f.Repo.Namespace) is fixed

All tests should PASS with the fix and FAIL before the fix.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Fix namespace isolation bug in dualwriter file operations

Found 3 additional instances of the same namespace bug in dualwriter.go:

**Line 133 - Delete() method**
- BEFORE: `identity.WithProvisioningIdentity(ctx, parsed.Obj.GetNamespace())`
- AFTER: `identity.WithProvisioningIdentity(ctx, r.repo.Config().Namespace)`

**Line 393 - createOrUpdate() method**
- BEFORE: `identity.WithProvisioningIdentity(ctx, parsed.Obj.GetNamespace())`
- AFTER: `identity.WithProvisioningIdentity(ctx, r.repo.Config().Namespace)`

**Line 589 - moveFile() method**
- BEFORE: `identity.WithProvisioningIdentity(ctx, newParsed.Obj.GetNamespace())`
- AFTER: `identity.WithProvisioningIdentity(ctx, r.repo.Config().Namespace)`

## Impact

These bugs affected the Files API endpoints:
- DELETE /api/v1/provisioning/repositories/{name}/files/{path}
- POST /api/v1/provisioning/repositories/{name}/files/{path} (create)
- POST /api/v1/provisioning/repositories/{name}/files/{path} (update)
- POST /api/v1/provisioning/repositories/{name}/files/{path} (move)

All file operations were creating/modifying resources in the wrong namespace,
just like the sync operations bug we fixed in parser.go.

## Audit Results

Comprehensive audit of the codebase found:
- ✅ parser.go: 2 bugs (DryRun, Run) - Fixed
- ✅ dualwriter.go: 3 bugs (Delete, createOrUpdate, moveFile) - Fixed
- ✅ folders.go: Already using correct pattern
- ✅ resources.go: Already using correct pattern
- ✅ jobs/persistentstore.go: Correct (uses existing K8s object namespace)
- ✅ Frontend: No issues (test files only)

All namespace isolation bugs in provisioning are now fixed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Revert code changes - no actual bug existed

After investigation, confirmed that:
- The parser correctly sets obj.SetNamespace(repo.Namespace)
- All code paths call Parse() before Run()
- The code works correctly in production (cloud environments)
- Repositories were created in the same org
- No actual namespace isolation vulnerability exists

The original code was working as intended. This PR now only adds
comprehensive integration tests to verify namespace isolation works correctly.

Reverts commits:
- c740602f540 (parser.go changes)
- 7aa02c0b66c (dualwriter.go changes)

Keeps:
- All integration test files (namespace, CRUD, security tests)

* Provisioning: Simplify integration tests to focus on cross-namespace isolation with folder sync

- Rewrote namespace_isolation_test.go to test repositories in different organizations (Org1 and OrgB)
- All repositories now use folder sync target instead of instance target
- Tests verify successful sync completion and cross-org isolation
- Removed files_crud_test.go and security_isolation_test.go (overly complex, tested same-namespace scenarios)
- Updated helper_test.go with copyToPath function
- Simplified test coverage: one focused test file instead of three

Test now verifies:
1. Repository creation in different namespaces
2. Successful folder sync completion
3. Cross-namespace isolation (folders in correct namespaces)
4. Cross-namespace access denial
5. Dashboard isolation
6. Re-sync consistency

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Refactor tests to use org-aware helpers

Created OrgHelper wrapper that makes it easy to create repositories and run operations
in different organizations/namespaces:

Benefits:
- Much cleaner test code - no manual client creation for each resource
- Reusable helpers: CreateRepo(), SyncAndWait(), GetFolders(), GetDashboards()
- Encapsulates org-specific context (user, namespace)
- Makes cross-org testing straightforward

Example usage:
```go
org1Helper := GetOrgHelper(helper, helper.Org1)
org1Helper.CreateRepo(t, common.TestRepo{...})
org1Helper.SyncAndWait(t, "repo-name", nil)
folders := org1Helper.GetFolders(t)
```

This follows the suggestion to improve helpers instead of duplicating
resource client creation logic in tests.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Move org-aware test helpers to common package

Refactored org-aware helper functionality to the common package to make
it reusable across all provisioning integration tests.

Changes:
- Added OrgContext struct to encapsulate org-specific context (user, namespace, orgID)
- Added helper methods to common package:
  - OrgContextFor() / DefaultOrgContext() - create org contexts
  - CreateRepoWithOrg() - create repo in specific org
  - SyncAndWaitWithOrg() - sync repo in specific org
  - WaitForHealthyRepositoryWithOrg() - wait for repo health
  - AwaitJobsWithOrg() - wait for jobs in specific org
  - GetFoldersWithOrg() - list folders in specific org
  - GetDashboardsWithOrg() - list dashboards in specific org
- All *WithOrg() methods accept nil orgCtx for backwards compatibility
- Simplified namespace_isolation_test.go to use common helpers
- Simplified orgs/helper_test.go to basic setup only

This makes it easy to write multi-org tests across the provisioning
test suite without duplicating org-aware logic.

* Provisioning: Refactor to WithNamespace() pattern for multi-org testing

Simplified the multi-org testing architecture by replacing OrgContext
and *WithOrg() methods with a cleaner scoped helper pattern.

Changes:
- Added WithNamespace(namespace, user) method that returns a new
  ProvisioningTestHelper scoped to that namespace
- Added Cleanup(t) method to delete all resources in a namespace
- Removed OrgContext struct and all *WithOrg() methods
- Tests now use scoped helpers with regular method names:
  orgAHelper := helper.WithNamespace(ns, user)
  orgAHelper.CreateRepo(t, repo)
  orgAHelper.SyncAndWait(t, repo, nil)
  defer orgAHelper.Cleanup(t)
- Renamed Org1/OrgB to orgA/orgB for consistency

This pattern is cleaner, more intuitive, and eliminates the need
to pass org context to every method call.

* Fix goimports formatting

* Add Namespace field to ProvisioningTestHelper for better usability

Instead of accessing namespace via orgHelper.Repositories.Args.Namespace,
tests can now use the more intuitive orgHelper.Namespace.

Changes:
- Added Namespace field to ProvisioningTestHelper struct
- Set in WithNamespace() method and buildProvisioningHelper()
- Updated SyncAndWait() to use h.Namespace
- Updated test to use orgAHelper.Namespace and orgBHelper.Namespace

* Add tests to verify namespace in parsed files is ignored

Added two critical security tests to ensure namespace isolation:

1. **Full sync test**: Verifies that when a dashboard YAML file specifies
   a different namespace in metadata.namespace, it is ignored and the
   dashboard is created in the repository's namespace.

2. **Files endpoint test**: Verifies that the files endpoint also ignores
   namespace specified in JSON/YAML files and uses the repository's
   namespace instead.

These tests ensure that users cannot break namespace isolation by
specifying a different namespace in their resource files. The repository's
namespace is always enforced as the security boundary.

Test scenarios:
- Create dashboard with namespace: orgB in file
- Sync in orgA repository
- Verify dashboard created in orgA namespace (not orgB)
- Verify orgB cannot access the dashboard

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Sonnet 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

- The code works correctly in production (cloud environments)
- Repositories were created in the same org
- No actual namespace isolation vulnerability exists

comprehensive integration tests to verify namespace isolation works correctly.

1. Repository creation in different namespaces

in different organizations/namespaces:

- Much cleaner test code - no manual client creation for each resource
- Reusable helpers: CreateRepo(), SyncAndWait(), GetFolders(), GetDashboards()
- Encapsulates org-specific context (user, namespace)
- Makes cross-org testing straightforward

```go
org1Helper := GetOrgHelper(helper, helper.Org1)
org1Helper.CreateRepo(t, common.TestRepo{...})

resource client creation logic in tests.

  - OrgContextFor() / DefaultOrgContext() - create org contexts
  - CreateRepoWithOrg() - create repo in specific org
  - SyncAndWaitWithOrg() - sync repo in specific org
  - WaitForHealthyRepositoryWithOrg() - wait for repo health
  - AwaitJobsWithOrg() - wait for jobs in specific org
  - GetFoldersWithOrg() - list folders in specific org

test suite without duplicating org-aware logic.

Simplified the multi-org testing architecture by replacing OrgContext
and *WithOrg() methods with a cleaner scoped helper pattern.

  ProvisioningTestHelper scoped to that namespace
- Added Cleanup(t) method to delete all resources in a namespace

to pass org context to every method call.

Instead of accessing namespace via orgHelper.Repositories.Args.Namespace,
tests can now use the more intuitive orgHelper.Namespace.

Added two critical security tests to ensure namespace isolation:

1. **Full sync test**: Verifies that when a dashboard YAML file specifies
   a different namespace in metadata.namespace, it is ignored and the
   dashboard is created in the repository's namespace.

2. **Files endpoint test**: Verifies that the files endpoint also ignores
   namespace specified in JSON/YAML files and uses the repository's
   namespace instead.

These tests ensure that users cannot break namespace isolation by
specifying a different namespace in their resource files. The repository's
namespace is always enforced as the security boundary.

commit.message:
Alerting: Add scheduler plumbing for rule chain evaluation (#121352)

* Alerting: Add scheduler plumbing for rule chain evaluation

Enable sequential evaluation of rule chain members by enriching rules
with synthetic group names, ordering, and intervals during registry set().
Includes RuleChainStore interface, change detection, and tests.

* Alerting: Extract chain enrichment and types to models package

Move SchedulableRuleChain, EnrichRulesWithChainMembership, and
RuleChainGroupPrefix from the schedule package to ngalert/models so
they can be shared across packages. Required for the upcoming
RuleChain entity PR which needs these types outside of scheduler
internals.

* Alerting: Use padded sentinel for chain group names to prevent user collision

The chain group name used a simple prefix check that a user could
satisfy by naming their rule group with the same prefix. Replace the
bare prefix with a padded sentinel (prefix + chainUID + '*' padding
to 200 chars), mirroring the NoGroupRuleGroup pattern. Because the
storage layer rejects group names longer than 190 characters, no
user-created group can match the sentinel.

commit.message:
Auth: URL-encode redirectTo cookie value in OAuth login flow (#121953)

Go's net/http silently strips double-quote characters from cookie
values because they are not valid per RFC 6265. This causes redirectTo
URLs containing quotes (e.g. PromQL label matchers like {label="value"})
to be corrupted during the OAuth login redirect flow.

URL-encode the redirectTo value before writing it to the cookie, pairing
with the existing url.QueryUnescape on the read side in handleLogin.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
Scopes: Fix defaultPath not loading on initial page load (#121614)

When a page loads with scopes in the URL but without scope_node,
the scope selector badge and tree fail to show the correct path.

This happens because resolvePathToRoot only runs when scope_node
is present in the URL, and appliedScopes.scopeNodeId is never
backfilled from defaultPath after the scope metadata is fetched.

Fix:
- Derive scopeNodeId from defaultPath after changeScopes resolves
  and call resolvePathToRoot to populate the node cache and tree
- Backfill scopeNodeId into appliedScopes/selectedScopes so open()
  can expand the tree to the correct node

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
Tempo: Fix trace rendering failure when span attributes contain NaN or Infinity (#122504)

fix(tempo): serialize NaN/Inf double attributes as strings

json.Marshal rejects NaN and Inf, causing traces with OTel-valid
floating point attributes to fail rendering entirely.

OTel spec explicitly permits NaN, Infinity, -Infinity as attribute
values. Serialize them as strings to preserve the value without
breaking JSON encoding.

Closes #122378

commit.message:
Dashboards: Fix collapse/expand all rows keyboard shortcuts (#122524)

* Dashboards: Fix collapse/expand all rows keyboard shortcuts

The `d shift+c` and `d shift+e` shortcuts were broken in two ways:

1. They were registered inside the `if (canEdit)` block, so they never
   fired for users without edit permissions. Collapsing/expanding rows
   is a view-mode operation that doesn't mutate the dashboard.

2. They didn't handle `TabsLayoutManager` - on tabbed dashboards the
   `instanceof` checks silently failed. Added `getRowCollapseTarget()`
   that resolves the correct layout by delegating to the current tab's
   inner layout when the body is a `TabsLayoutManager`.

Fixes #100622

commit.message:
Search: remote index storage with per-file upload/download (#121331)

* feat: remote index storage interface with per-file upload/download (#717)

Add RemoteIndexStore for uploading/downloading search index snapshots
to/from object storage via Go CDK's blob.Bucket abstraction.

Key design:
- meta.json uploaded last as completion signal, deleted first on removal
- Index keys are immutable; callers must hold a distributed lock
- Upload rejects symlinks (Lstat + SameFile inode check for TOCTOU)
- Download validates path traversal, resolves symlinks in parent dirs,
  and rejects symlinked leaf files before writing
- Partial files cleaned up on download failure

Extends CDKBucket interface with Upload/Download streaming methods
and adds InstrumentedBucket wrappers measuring full transfer latency.

---------

commit.message:
Storage: Fix watch latency metric and timestamp for KV backend (#122558)

* Storage: Fix watch latency metric and timestamp for KV backend

The watch_latency_seconds metric assumed ResourceVersion is always a
unix microsecond timestamp, but the KV backend stores snowflake-encoded
IDs. Use resourceVersionTime() which handles both formats.

Also fix WatchEvent.Timestamp in the KV backend's WatchWriteEvents,
which was dividing a snowflake ID by 1e9 as if it were nanoseconds.

* Remove rvmanager dependency from resourceVersionTime

Extract timestamp from snowflake ID directly using bit shifting
instead of calling rvmanager.RVFromSnowflake. This removes the
dependency on the rvmanager package from server.go.

commit.message:
Unified storage: add query cache config migration (#121962)

* Unified storage: add query cache config migration

Migrate querycacheconfigs from the legacy data_source_cache table to
unified storage (querycaching.grafana.app). The migrator joins
data_source_cache with data_source to resolve org_id and plugin type,
then streams QueryCacheConfig objects via BulkProcess.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Fix querycacheconfigs test: handle missing API group gracefully

The querycaching API requires an enterprise license to register. When
the API isn't available, List returns "not found". The Verify step now
treats this as acceptable when shouldExist is false, instead of failing.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Remove querycacheconfigs integration test cases

The count validator already covers the most likely migration failure.
The enterprise-only K8s API makes the test setup fragile without
adding meaningful coverage over the existing framework tests.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Register querycacheconfigs test case in defaultMigrationTestCases

Export the struct and register it directly as &QueryCacheConfigsTestCase{}
following the standard test case pattern.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Fix migrator: use int64 for SQLite bool columns, string for datetime

SQLite stores booleans as integers and datetimes as strings. Scanning
into Go bool/time.Time fails silently. Also add missing NOT NULL
columns (basic_auth, is_default, json_data, secure_json_data) to the
test data_source inserts, and create data_source_cache table in
AddLegacySQLMigrations since it's only in the enterprise migration
snapshot.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Remove querycacheconfigs integration test case

The querycaching API group is enterprise-only, so the test can't verify
data via K8s API in OSS builds. The migrator itself is validated by
the count validator at runtime.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Add querycacheconfigs unified storage migration with tests

- Fix migrator SQL join and JSON serialization issues
- Add unit tests with SQL snapshot coverage for all dialects
- Add enterprise integration test case verifying full migration lifecycle
- Update migration test harness to support enterprise-only migration IDs

Made-with: Cursor

* Address review feedback on querycacheconfigs migration

- Handle time.Parse error explicitly instead of silently ignoring
- Remove unused `updated` column from SQL query and scan
- Add sync comment on queryCacheConfigSpec referencing the source type
- Use metav1.TypeMeta directly instead of custom typeMeta struct
- Add comment to AddLegacySQLMigrations explaining table provenance

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Use Unix epoch integer for created timestamp instead of time.Parse

Convert DATETIME to Unix epoch in SQL (dialect-specific: UNIX_TIMESTAMP
for MySQL, EXTRACT(EPOCH) for Postgres, strftime for SQLite) and scan
as int64. Avoids string parsing entirely, matching the pattern used by
other migrators.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Use DialectName from SQLTemplate instead of separate field

Access .DialectName directly in the SQL template via the embedded
SQLTemplate interface. This ensures snapshot tests work correctly
since the test framework calls SetDialect per iteration.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Gate querycacheconfigs migration behind cacheConfigUnifiedStorageMigration feature toggle

Only register the migration when the feature toggle is enabled.
This prevents the migration from running in deployments where the
querycaching API group is not available.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Remove feature toggle gate from migration registration

The migration is already gated by enableMigration config (opt-in,
false by default). No additional feature toggle check needed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Rename data_source_cache table after migration

Set RenameTables to rename data_source_cache to data_source_cache_legacy
after successful migration, preventing stale writes from old pods.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Update test case RenameTables to match migration registrar

The registrar now renames data_source_cache after migration. Update
the test case to return the same table name from RenameTables().

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Fix test case Postgres compatibility

Use bool params for basic_auth/is_default instead of integer literals,
and use xorm session for queries to handle dialect-specific placeholder
conversion (? → $1/$2 on Postgres).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Fix data_source_cache test inserts for Postgres boolean columns

Parameterize enabled and use_default_ttl values in INSERT...SELECT
so xorm converts bool args correctly for Postgres (which uses BOOL
instead of tinyint).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Use bool for enabled/useDefaultTTL to fix Postgres scan

Postgres returns native bool for tinyint(1) columns. Scanning into
int64 fails with "converting driver.Value type bool to int64". Using
bool works for both SQLite (auto-converts 0/1) and Postgres.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
Dashboard: Preserve timezone user-preference when converting V1 → V2 (#122267)

fix(dashboard): preserve timezone user-preference when converting V1 → V2

In V1/V0 dashboards, `timezone: ""` is the sentinel value meaning
"fall back to the user's profile preference". The V1→V2alpha1 converter
was initialising TimeSettings.Timezone from the spec default ("browser")
and then, for `timezone: ""`, leaving that default in place rather than
clearing it. As a result, every V0/V1 dashboard whose timezone was unset
would resolve to browser time in V2 instead of honouring the user's
profile setting.

Fix: when the V1 payload contains `timezone: ""` explicitly, set
TimeSettings.Timezone to nil so the serving layer can apply the
user-preference fallback, matching the V1 semantics. An absent timezone
key continues to use the "browser" default.

Regenerate golden checksums to reflect the corrected output (timezone
field omitted instead of being set to "").

Fix: when the V1 payload contains `timezone: ""` explicitly, set

field omitted instead of being set to "").

commit.message:
Dashboard: Skip folder tree build during schema conversion (#122666)

* LibraryElements: Skip folder tree fetch for admin during schema conversion

The dashboard DTO endpoint (v2beta1) triggers schema version conversion
which calls GetAllElements to resolve library panel repeat options. This
fetched ALL folders via unified storage (k8s List with limit=100000 →
BatchGet in chunks of 50), causing ~37s latency on large orgs.

Add SkipFolderTreeForAdmin to SearchLibraryElementsQuery to skip the
folder tree fetch when the caller is admin, since admins can see all
folders and don't need permission filtering. The conversion path already
uses a StaticRequester with RoleAdmin.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* LibraryElements: Add tests for SkipFolderTreeForAdmin

Tests verify:
- Admin with SkipFolderTreeForAdmin skips GetFolders call
- Admin without the flag still fetches folder tree and populates FolderName
- Non-admin with the flag still fetches folder tree for permission filtering

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* LibraryElements: Use empty FolderName when folder tree is skipped

When SkipFolderTreeForAdmin is set, FolderName should be empty rather
than defaulting to "General" (RootFolderName). The previous code
incorrectly labeled all elements as root folder elements.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

commit.message:
Build: Upgrade TypeScript to 6.0 (#118528)

* Build: Upgrade TypeScript to 6.0 beta

Update typescript from 5.9.2 to 6.0.0-beta across all packages. Configure tsconfig to handle TS 6.0 breaking changes: add `ignoreDeprecations: "6.0"` to suppress warnings for deprecated options, disable `noUncheckedSideEffectImports` to allow CSS side-effect imports, explicitly configure `types` field since TS 6.0 no longer auto-includes all @types packages, set appropriate `rootDir` in packages that include files outside their directory, and update `@ts-ignore` comment placement in Table utils to match where TS 6.0 now reports the type error.

All typecheck tests pass with 0 errors.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Add explicit rootDir to root tsconfig for ts-jest compatibility

TS 6.0 requires rootDir to be explicitly set when it differs from the
inferred common source directory. Without this, ts-jest fails with
TS5011 when running unit tests.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Fix package builds: add rootDir and jquery types for TS 6.0

TS 6.0 requires explicit rootDir in tsconfigs that emit output. Add
rootDir to all package build configs that were missing it. Also add
jquery to the base types array since @types/jquery is no longer
auto-included.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Fix TS 6.0 errors in e2e and plugin tsconfigs

- e2e/tsconfig.json: Add moduleResolution: "bundler" to fix TS5098
  (customConditions requires bundler/node16/nodenext moduleResolution)
- packages/grafana-plugin-configs/tsconfig.json: Add ignoreDeprecations: "6.0"
  to fix TS5101 (downlevelIteration deprecated) inherited from @grafana/tsconfig,
  cascading to all 15 datasource plugins and 3 e2e-playwright test plugins

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Fix package build output: use rootDir: "./src" instead of "."

rootDir: "." caused type declarations to emit to dist/types/src/
instead of dist/types/, breaking the published package types paths.
Using rootDir: "./src" preserves the correct output structure while
satisfying TS 6.0's requirement for an explicit rootDir.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Align TS 6.0 changes with tsgo PR (#114643)

- Remove baseUrl in favor of path mapping ("*": ["./public/*"])
- Add rootDir: "./src" to grafana-sql and grafana-test-utils tsconfigs
- Add explicit Size type annotations to AutoSizer callbacks
- Add explicit type params to MultiSelect<string> in LokiContextUi
- Update @ts-ignore comments for TS5/TS6/TS7 compatibility
- Switch JS files to @ts-nocheck (eslint.config.js, env-util.js)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Build: Upgrade TypeScript from 6.0.0-beta to 6.0.1-rc

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Build: Upgrade TypeScript from 6.0.1-rc to 6.0.2 stable

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Fix o11y-ds-frontend package build: add rootDir to build config

Same fix as other packages — the build config was inheriting
rootDir: "../../" from tsconfig.json, causing type declarations
to emit to the wrong path.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Dashboards: Strip BOM characters in admission mutation hook (#122677)

* Dashboard: Strip BOM characters in admission mutation hook (Layer 2)

## Problem

PR #117984 only implemented Layer 1 (file parsing) of the BOM fix, leaving
dashboards vulnerable to validation errors during PATCH operations. When
provisioning repositories are deleted, the finalizer PATCHes dashboards to
remove ownership annotations, which triggers validation on the entire object.
If the dashboard spec contains BOMs, validation fails with:

```
Dashboard.dashboard.grafana.app "<uid>" is invalid: []: Invalid value: illegal byte order mark
```

## Root Cause

Layer 2 (admission mutation) was described in PR #117984 but never implemented.
Without the mutation hook stripping BOMs, Kubernetes PATCH operations fail
validation when the dashboard spec contains BOMs (even if only annotations
are being modified).

## Solution: Implement Layer 2

This PR implements the missing Layer 2 by adding BOM stripping to the dashboard
admission mutation hook:

### Changes

- **pkg/registry/apis/dashboard/mutate.go**: Strip BOMs during CREATE/UPDATE/PATCH
  - v0alpha1/v1: Strip BOMs from all strings in `Spec.Object` (map[string]any)
  - v2alpha1/v2beta1/v2: Strip BOMs from Title and Description fields
  - Handles pointer types correctly for v2 Description fields

### How PATCH Operations Work with Mutation Hooks

1. Finalizer calls `client.Patch()` to remove annotations
2. Kubernetes applies the JSON patch to the current object
3. **Mutation hook runs with `admission.Update` operation**
4. **Mutation hook strips BOMs from the dashboard spec**
5. Validation passes (no BOMs present)
6. Both changes are persisted (annotations removed + BOMs stripped)

This is the key insight: Kubernetes internally treats PATCH as UPDATE for
admission hooks, so our mutation hook runs and cleans up BOMs automatically.

### Testing

**Unit tests** (`pkg/registry/apis/dashboard/mutation_test.go`):
- BOM stripping for v0alpha1, v1, v2alpha1, v2beta1 dashboards
- Verifies BOMs are removed from titles, descriptions, and panel titles
- Tests both CREATE and UPDATE operations (PATCH uses UPDATE internally)

**Integration tests** (`pkg/tests/apis/dashboard/bom_test.go`):
- End-to-end CREATE/UPDATE/PATCH with BOMs
- Simulates provisioning finalizer scenario (PATCH to remove annotations)
- Verifies no "illegal byte order mark" errors during PATCH
- Tests all dashboard API versions (v0alpha1, v1, v2alpha1, v2beta1)

## Benefits

- ✅ Fixes provisioning repository deletion failures
- ✅ Prevents BOM validation errors during any PATCH operation
- ✅ Works for all dashboard API versions
- ✅ No changes required to provisioning finalizer code
- ✅ Defense-in-depth: complements Layer 1 file parsing fix

## Related

- Completes the fix started in PR #117984
- Resolves the original error from provisioning repository controller

* Optimize BOM stripping performance using reflection

Performance optimization: Replace JSON marshal/unmarshal approach with
direct reflection-based BOM stripping for v2 dashboard specs.

**Performance Improvements:**
- Small dashboards: 49x faster (8,078ns → 165ns), 0 allocations
- Medium dashboards: 45x faster (46,950ns → 1,040ns), 0 allocations
- Large dashboards: 41x faster (262,626ns → 6,425ns), 0 allocations

**Overall Mutation Performance:**
- Small: 239ns baseline → 424-527ns with BOM stripping (1.7-2.2x vs 46x)
- Medium: 429ns baseline → 1,500-3,196ns (3.4-7.3x vs 118x)
- Large: 4,308ns baseline → 10,930-19,855ns (2.5-4.6x vs 64x)

The reflection approach eliminates JSON encoding overhead by walking
struct fields directly, resulting in dramatic performance gains and
zero heap allocations.

Changes:
- Added util.StripBOMFromStruct() using reflection for typed structs
- Added comprehensive unit tests for struct BOM stripping
- Added performance benchmarks comparing both approaches
- Reduced cyclomatic complexity with stripBOMIfEnabled helper
- Kept JSON-based implementation for comparison/benchmarking

- Unused encoding/json import

- Benchmarks for util package showing performance on various struct sizes

Results:
- Small struct: 51.73 ns/op, 0 allocations
- Medium struct: 571.3 ns/op, 96 B/op, 6 allocs
- Large nested: 1,307 ns/op, 240 B/op, 15 allocs
- Dashboard small: 301.7 ns/op, 0 allocations

* Add batch dashboard mutation benchmarks for throughput testing

Added benchmarks to measure performance when processing multiple dashboards,
useful for understanding admission webhook throughput.

Results (time per dashboard remains constant - linear scaling):
- 10/100/1000 small dashboards: ~350-400 ns/dashboard
- 10/100/1000 medium dashboards: ~1.3-1.4 µs/dashboard
- 10/100/1000 large dashboards: ~7.3-8.0 µs/dashboard

Throughput estimates:
- Small dashboards: ~2.5M dashboards/second
- Medium dashboards: ~700K dashboards/second
- Large dashboards: ~125K dashboards/second

The linear scaling shows the reflection-based BOM stripping has
no hidden performance cliffs or contention issues.

commit.message:
Unified Storage: Allow Terraform manager identity transitions (#122719)

* Unified Storage: Allow Terraform manager identity transitions

Relaxes manager identity validation to allow Terraform managers to
change their identity string across provider versions, while still
enforcing that the manager kind remains the same.

Problem:
- Terraform provider uses manager IDs like "Terraform/crossTF000" or
  "terraform-provider-grafana/crossplane" that change based on version
- Current code blocks ANY identity change, preventing Terraform updates
- This breaks Terraform workflows when the provider version changes

Solution:
- For Terraform managers: only validate that the Kind stays "terraform"
- For other managers: continue to validate both Kind and Identity
- This allows seamless Terraform provider version upgrades without
  requiring users to manually remove and re-add manager annotations

The change is backward compatible:
- Existing non-Terraform managers maintain strict validation
- Terraform resources can now transition between provider versions
- Tests verify both legacy IDs and new version-specific IDs work

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Fix comments to reflect actual Terraform manager ID format

The manager identity is the full User-Agent string, not separate parts.
Example: 'Terraform/crossTF000 (+https://www.terraform.io) terraform-provider-grafana/crossplane'

Updated test cases to use realistic user-agent based identities.

* Prevent reverting from new Terraform IDs back to legacy placeholders

Enhances Terraform manager identity validation to allow one-way migration:
- Legacy (crossTF000/crossplane) → New (version-based): ALLOWED
- New → New (version updates): ALLOWED
- Legacy → Legacy: ALLOWED
- New → Legacy (reverting): BLOCKED

Legacy IDs use placeholders like 'crossTF000' or 'crossplane' instead of
actual Terraform/provider versions. Once migrated to version-specific IDs,
reverting back to placeholders is prevented to ensure proper version tracking.

* Correct legacy detection: User-Agent strings vs simple IDs

Updates Terraform manager ID validation to properly distinguish:
- Legacy: User-Agent strings (e.g., 'Terraform/... +https://www.terraform.io ...')
- New: Simple IDs (e.g., 'grafana-terraform-provider', 'my-terraform-provider')

Changes:
- isLegacyTerraformID now detects User-Agent strings by looking for
  'Terraform/' and '+https://www.terraform.io' patterns
- Test cases updated to show realistic transitions:
  * User-Agent → simple ID (migration)
  * Simple ID → different simple ID (updates)
  * User-Agent → different User-Agent (legacy updates)
  * Simple ID → User-Agent (blocked)

* Document Terraform identity hack and add stricter validation

Adds comprehensive documentation explaining why Terraform managers get
special treatment for identity changes:

Why this is a HACK:
- Terraform provider historically used HTTP User-Agent as manager identity
- User-Agent changes with every version (not a stable identifier)
- Was never intended to be used this way (design mistake)
- Special-casing violates principle of immutable manager identities
- Necessary to fix original design and enable migration to stable IDs

Stricter legacy detection:
- Now requires all three patterns:

Fix usage stats error when Amazon/Azure Prometheus plugins are not installed (#120283)

When collecting Prometheus flavor stats, GetDataSourcesByType returns an
error if the plugin is not found in the plugin store. For optional plugins
like grafana-amazonprometheus-datasource and grafana-azureprometheus-datasource,
treat "plugin not found" as an expected condition (log at debug level and
continue with an empty list) instead of aborting the entire collection.

commit.message:
Search: disable unnecessary DocValues to reduce index size (#122798)

Disable bleve DocValues on all fields except `folder` (used by authz
DocValueReader) and `title_phrase` (used for default sort). DocValues
are columnar per-document stored values for sorting and faceting that
account for ~3.3 MB per 10K-document segment (~10.4% of index size),
but only these two fields actually consume them.

Changes:
- Set DocValuesDynamic=false on IndexMappingImpl to prevent dynamic
  fields (labels.*, reference.*, non-filterable fields.*) from getting
  DocValues
- Explicitly set DocValues=false on factory-created field mappings
  (title_ngram, titleSearch, titleWord, source.timestampMillis,
  filterable fields.* keyword mappings) which default to true
- Stop sharing titlePhraseMapping between title_phrase and title fields
  so that title gets no DocValues while title_phrase keeps them

Trade-off: 4 enterprise-only sort fields (views_total,
views_last_30_days, errors_total, errors_last_30_days) will use
bleve's inverted-index fallback instead of DocValues for sorting.
Sorting still works correctly but is slower for large result sets.
The default alphabetical sort (title_phrase) is not affected.

Savings realized through natural index rebuilds on upgrade.

Ref: grafana/search-and-storage-team#744

commit.message:
RBAC: Share folder tree getter across BatchCheck groups (#122749)

The RBAC BatchCheck was creating a new folderTreeGetter per action group,
causing redundant folder list calls. With 7 check items grouped into
separate actions, this resulted in 7 folder tree fetches (each listing
all folders via k8s API) per BatchCheck call.

Share a single folder tree getter at the BatchCheck level. When any group
requires fresh data, use a fresh getter and process those groups first so
the fetched tree populates the cache. Non-fresh groups then reuse the

Pyroscope: Add support for heatmap query API (#120995)

* feat: Add heatmap support to Pyroscope datasource

Adds backend support for heatmap queries in the Pyroscope datasource:
- New heatmap package with gap-filling and bucket normalization logic
- New exemplar package for creating profile/span exemplar data frames
- Updated pyroscopeClient and query handling to support heatmap requests
- Adds profilesHeatmap feature toggle to the registry
- Updates pyroscope/api dependency to v1.3.0 (adds heatmap RPC support)
- Updates generated CUE types with includeHeatmap, heatmapType, profileIdSelector fields
- New heatmapType query option in the CUE schema and generated types
- Updated QueryOptions UI to expose heatmap controls
- Datasource updated to request heatmap data when enabled
- SpanFlameGraph updated for Query type compatibility
- profilesHeatmap feature toggle TypeScript type added

* Switch to a sparse heatmap

In order for a sparse heatmap to work, the heatmap panel, does a panel calibration between the first different xMax
element. It assumes the gap is constant for all other buckets. Therefor we need to insert a zero value, if there is no
point for firstTs+step.

I also renamed `Point` to `Slot` to be consistent with the Pyroscope API.

* Limit bucket width to 64

* Pass through the data source UID

* pyroscope: filter private labels from exemplar frame

Filters out labels with a `__` prefix (e.g. `__name__`, `__profile_type__`)
when building the exemplar data frame, so they don't appear as annotation
columns in the panel.

This filtering should be moved to the frontend — tracked in
https://github.com/grafana/grafana/issues/122786

commit.message:
IAM: Skip hidden users filtering for service identities (#122793)

Service identities (e.g. Zanzana) need full visibility into all users,
including hidden ones, to properly manage authorization tuples. This adds
an early return in all StoreWrapper methods (AfterGet, FilterList,
BeforeCreate, BeforeUpdate, BeforeDelete) that bypasses hidden user
filtering when the caller is a service identity, consistent with the
IAM authorizer which already grants service identities full access.

commit.message:
Search: Fix data race in TestConcurrentIndexUpdateSearchAndRebuild (#122827)

The test used `_, err =` (assignment to outer-scope variable) instead of
`_, err :=` (local declaration) for the UpdateIndex call inside goroutine
closures. All 25 goroutines shared the same `err` variable, causing a
data race where one goroutine could overwrite `err` between another's
assignment and its `errors.Is` check, bypassing the ErrorIndexClosed
guard and hitting `require.NoError` with a stale error value.
