commit.message:
Search: disable bleve _all composite field to reduce index size (#122727)

* Search: disable bleve _all composite field to reduce index size

The _all composite field merges terms from all indexed fields into a
single synthetic field. We never query it — all searches target explicit
fields. Disabling it significantly reduces index size.

- Add disabled sub-document mapping for bleve's internal "_all" field
- Set IncludeInAll: false on all explicit field mappings
- Route wildcard queries to explicit fields instead of relying on _all
- Introduce SEARCH_FIELD_ALL_FIELDS sentinel to decouple the "return all
  columns" convention from bleve's _all composite field
- Simplify default field selection logic

Ref: grafana/search-and-storage-team#743

* Search: support wildcard queries across multiple fields via QueryFields

The _all composite field removal restricted wildcard queries to the title
field only. This broke IAM user search which needs to match against email
and login fields too.

When QueryFields is set, wildcard queries now create a disjunction across
all named fields. Only Name is used (Type and Boost are ignored since bleve
wildcards don't support analyzers or relevance scoring).

* Search: use title+title_phrase disjunction for default wildcard queries

The legacy dashboard search service wraps queries as "*<lowered title>*".
With title restricted to standard-analyzed (word tokens), multi-word
wildcards fail because no single token matches the full phrase.

Search both title (word-level prefix wildcards like "hell*") and
title_phrase (keyword-analyzed full title for "*grafana dev overview*").

* Search: add test for multi-word wildcard matching via title_phrase

Verify that legacy dashboard search pattern "*grafana dev overview*"
matches the keyword-analyzed title_phrase field, since multi-word
wildcards can't match individual word tokens in the standard-analyzed
title field.

* Search: default wildcard searches email/login, expand title to title_phrase

Two improvements to wildcard query handling:

1. Default wildcard path (no QueryFields) now searches email and login
   fields in addition to title/title_phrase. This provides backward
   compatibility for older IAM clients that don't set QueryFields during
   the deployment gap.

2. When QueryFields includes "title", automatically expand to search both
   title (standard-analyzed, word tokens) and title_phrase (keyword-
   analyzed, full phrase). Callers shouldn't need to know about the
   internal field split to get correct multi-word wildcard matching.

* Search: use keyword-analyzed fields in wildcard email/login test

Use newTestIndexWithFields helper to create an index with keyword-
analyzed email/login fields matching production IAM configuration.
This allows testing wildcard queries against full email addresses
(e.g. *alice@grafana.com*) which require keyword analysis to avoid
tokenization by the standard analyzer.

* Replace code reference with Github URL.

commit.message:
AccessControl: add configurable ScopeAttribute and AllowsKind to ResourcePermission mapper (#122684)

* AccessControl: unify mapper struct with configurable ScopeAttribute

Merge `mapper` and `idMapper` into a single configurable struct.
Add `ScopeAttribute` typed constant (`ScopeAttributeUID` / `ScopeAttributeID`)
so the scope attribute is explicit and compile-time safe instead of an
arbitrary string.

`NewMapper` is unchanged for existing callers (uid-scoped resources).
`NewIDScopedMapper` becomes a thin wrapper — this also fixes a latent
bug where `idMapper.Scope()` was returning `:uid:` instead of `:id:`.
`NewMapperWithAttribute` exposes the full constructor for callers that
need an explicit scope attribute and kind restrictions.

Closes sub-task: add attribute + NewMapperWithAttribute (issue #1997)

* AccessControl: add AllowsKind to Mapper interface

Resources can restrict which assignment kinds they permit. Service accounts,
for example, do not support BasicRole assignments. When allowedKinds is nil
(the default for all existing mappers), all kinds continue to be allowed.

Closes sub-task: AllowsKind interface + implementation (issue #1997)

* AccessControl: restrict SA ResourcePermission mapper to allowed kinds

Service accounts do not support BasicRole assignments — built-in roles
already cover all service accounts globally, so per-resource grants to
BasicRole would be semantically wrong and inconsistent with the legacy
path which enforces the same constraint.

Closes sub-task: wire up SA mapper with allowedKinds (issue #1997)

* AccessControl: add unit tests for ScopeAttribute and AllowsKind

Covers uid vs id scope attribute paths (Scope/ScopePattern), and
AllowsKind with nil allowedKinds (all permitted) and a restricted
list (BasicRole excluded for service accounts).

Closes sub-task: unit tests (issue #1997)

commit.message:
AccessControl: backfill SA action set tokens to managed roles (#122718)

* AccessControl: backfill SA action set tokens to managed roles

Adds a SQL migration that scans managed roles with SA granular actions
(serviceaccounts:read/write/delete on serviceaccounts:id:* scopes) and
inserts the corresponding action set token (serviceaccounts:edit or
serviceaccounts:admin) if not already present.

This is required for existing SA permissions to be visible to the K8s
ResourcePermission API, which queries by action set token rather than
individual actions.

The migration runs unconditionally on the first restart after deployment
— no feature flag required. It is purely additive: no existing rows are
modified or deleted. Rolling back the code after deployment is safe;
old code ignores the extra rows. Removing the backfilled data would
require a manual SQL cleanup (no automatic down migration, consistent
with Grafana's migration system).

FlagOnlyStoreServiceAccountActionSets (from the companion PR) should
only be enabled after this migration has run in production and the
backfilled data has been validated.

* AccessControl: drop serviceaccounts:read from SA action set migration query

serviceaccounts:read does not map to any action set, so querying for it
was unnecessary. Remove it from the IN clause and clean up the now-dead
level == "" guard that existed only to handle read-only cases.

commit.message:
AccessControl: write SA action set token on permission grant, gated by feature flag (#122698)

* AccessControl: add FlagOnlyStoreServiceAccountActionSets feature flag

Separate flag from FlagOnlyStoreActionSets (which is permanently true)
so service accounts can safely start writing action set tokens alongside
granular actions without immediately breaking the legacy read path.

The flag starts false. It should only be enabled after the SQL migration
(#1999) has backfilled action set tokens on existing SA permissions in
production.

Closes sub-task: add feature flag (issue #1998)

* AccessControl: add SA action set token to mapPermission, gated by flag

When setting service account resource permissions, emit the action set
token (e.g. serviceaccounts:edit) alongside the existing granular actions
(serviceaccounts:read, serviceaccounts:write) so the K8s ResourcePermission
API can find and list these permissions by action set.

The dual-write is gated by FlagOnlyStoreServiceAccountActionSets: when off
(default), both are written for backward compatibility; when on, only the
action set token is written. The flag is safe to enable only after the
backfill migration in #1999 has run.

Also adds ScopeServiceAccountRoot constant to the serviceaccounts package,
matching the pattern of folder.ScopeFoldersRoot and dashboards.ScopeDashboardsRoot.

* AccessControl: add tests for service account permission mapping

Covers the SA changes added in the previous commit:
- mapPermission: dual-write (action set + granular) when flag is off,
  action-set-only when FlagOnlyStoreServiceAccountActionSets is on
- isActionSetEnabledResource: SA action prefixes are recognised

* fix linter

* AccessControl: migrate SA action-set flag evaluation to OpenFeature

Replaces the legacy IsEnabledGlobally call for FlagOnlyStoreServiceAccountActionSets
with openfeature.NewDefaultClient().BooleanValue, adds ctx to mapPermission, and
updates the test to use the static OpenFeature provider instead of featuremgmt.WithFeatures.

commit.message:
Candlestick: add e2e tests (#122742)

* Candlestick: add e2e tests

Add comprehensive E2E test coverage for the candlestick panel:
- renders successfully (all panel variations, no errors)
- no data handling with "No value" option override
- tooltip interactions (hover, pin, unpin, X close, Escape, Cmd+C persist, disable mode)
- legend visibility toggle
- panel editor options (mode, candle style, color strategy, colors)
- data links in pinned tooltip

New test dashboard (panel-tests-candlestick) with purpose-built panels
covering candles+volume, OHLC bars, close-close color strategy, volume
only, no-data, and data link configurations. Existing panning test and
its dashboard are preserved unchanged.

Closes #112989

* fix: remove no-data panel, candlestick renders empty chart instead

Candlestick panel wraps TimeSeries which renders uplot even with empty
data, unlike simpler panels that show PanelDataErrorView. Remove the
no-data panel and test, renumber data link panel to id 5.

* fix: tooltip/legend/data-link test positioning

- Use .u-over center for hover/click instead of hardcoded offsets
- Set includeAllFields: true so legend has visible items

* fix: match state-timeline tooltip hover pattern

- Hover on .uplot at {x:100,y:50} like state-timeline does
- Add explicit tooltip config to panel JSON

* fix: drop data link test, use force hover, fix uplot count

- Remove fragile data link test and its dashboard panel
- Use force:true on hover/click to handle overlay elements
- Use .first() for uplot locator in edit mode
- Fix panel count to 4

* add data links test on panel 1

Move data link config to panel 1 where tooltip already works.

* split data links into dedicated panel

Panel 1 (no data links) for tooltip/legend/options tests.
Panel 5 (with data links) for data links test.

* split candlestick e2e tests into separate file

Original candlestick.spec.ts (panning only) restored unchanged.
New candlestick-panels.spec.ts with renders, tooltip, legend,
panel options, and data links tests against a dedicated dashboard.

* split candlestick e2e tests into separate files

- candlestick.spec.ts: x-axis panning (unchanged from main)
- candlestick-render.spec.ts: dashboard renders all panels
- candlestick-editor.spec.ts: panel options in edit mode
- candlestick-tooltips.spec.ts: tooltip hover/pin/close interactions
- candlestick-legend.spec.ts: legend visibility toggle
- candlestick-datalinks.spec.ts: data links in pinned tooltip

* add no-data test and panel

New panel 6 with no_data_points scenario. Test verifies no chart
renders and "No data" message appears, scoped to the panel title.

* add golden file checksum for candlestick_tests dashboard

* add candlestick_tests to jsonnet dev-dashboards config

* cleanup: consistent tooltip config, remove redundant comment

* use computed positions from u-over boundingBox instead of hardcoded offsets

* add editor option toggle smoke tests

Toggle mode, candle style, and color strategy options in edit mode
and verify the chart re-renders without errors.

* add tooltip All mode toggle to tooltip interactions test

* add legend mode and placement toggle test

* add action button assertion to data links test

* update golden checksum for candlestick_tests dashboard with action

* add step comments to editor and legend toggle tests

commit.message:
Search: enable SkipFreqNorm and disable IncludeTermVectors on bleve fields (#122838)

Reduce bleve index overhead by disabling unnecessary freq/norm data and
term vectors on fields that don't need them.

- Add SkipFreqNorm=true to all keyword/exact-match fields and other
  fields not used for BM25 scoring (name, title_phrase, folder, tags,
  description, createdBy, ownerReferences, managedBy, manager.*, source.*,
  filterable fields, selectable fields)
- Add IncludeTermVectors=false to fields created via NewKeywordFieldMapping()
  and NewTextFieldMapping() helpers which default to true. No field uses
  phrase queries or highlighting.
- Keep SkipFreqNorm=false on title (standard), title_ngram, and
  title_search fields that need BM25 scoring for relevance ranking.
- Add TestTermVectorsAndFreqNorm regression test to catch future fields
  added via helper functions without overriding defaults.

Ref: grafana/search-and-storage-team#746

commit.message:
TimeRangePicker: Fix calendar reverting when clicking a date range (#122897)

Use react-hook-form's `watch` instead of `getValues` so the calendar
receives updated from/to props when the user picks a date. `getValues`
is not reactive, so `setValue` from the calendar's onChange did not
trigger a re-render, leaving the `value` prop stale and causing the
calendar to revert to the previously selected range.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

CLI: Fix reset-admin-password failing on PostgreSQL due to boolean = integer comparison (#122507)

fix(cli): use bool param in adminFilter to fix PostgreSQL reset-admin-password

Hardcoded `is_admin = 1` is invalid on PostgreSQL where is_admin is a
boolean column — the engine rejects boolean = integer comparison with
"operator does not exist". Use a parameterized condition so xorm emits
the correct value for each database dialect.

Closes #122206

commit.message:
AccessControl: backfill SA action set tokens to managed roles (#122940)

* AccessControl: backfill SA action set tokens to managed roles

Adds a SQL migration that scans managed roles with SA granular actions
(serviceaccounts:read/write/delete on serviceaccounts:id:* scopes) and
inserts the corresponding action set token (serviceaccounts:edit or
serviceaccounts:admin) if not already present.

This is required for existing SA permissions to be visible to the K8s
ResourcePermission API, which queries by action set token rather than
individual actions.

The migration runs unconditionally on the first restart after deployment
— no feature flag required. It is purely additive: no existing rows are
modified or deleted. Rolling back the code after deployment is safe;
old code ignores the extra rows. Removing the backfilled data would
require a manual SQL cleanup (no automatic down migration, consistent
with Grafana's migration system).

FlagOnlyStoreServiceAccountActionSets (from the companion PR) should
only be enabled after this migration has run in production and the
backfilled data has been validated.

* AccessControl: drop serviceaccounts:read from SA action set migration query

serviceaccounts:read does not map to any action set, so querying for it
was unnecessary. Remove it from the IN clause and clean up the now-dead
level == "" guard that existed only to handle read-only cases.

These bookmarks serve the purpose of indicating to the client that no new events are expected _after_ the RV included in the bookmark. This allows reconnecting clients to use that RV instead of starting from scratch or requesting to `SendInitialEvents`, or sending unnecessarily outdated RVs.

In particular, if the client is using an informer (which automatically reconnects after ~5-10mins), the bookmark allows the server to help the client update its "last known" RV even if no events reach the caller. This is particularly useful for cases where the caller is watching for resources based on some predicate (such as a label filter, for example), as that filtering currently happens on the client.

Without this change the `watch_latency_seconds` metric we collect can look like we're sending events with huge delays, when in reality we are just sending repeated events due to outdated RVs.
* test fix

commit.message:
IAM/Zanzana: inject MT reconciler GVR list via Wire (#122873)

* IAM/Zanzana: inject MT reconciler GVR list via Wire

Promote the hardcoded `reconcileGVRs` package global to a `Config.GVRs`
field on the reconciler and wire it through `NewEmbeddedZanzanaServer` /
`newServer`. The OSS list (folders, resourcepermissions, teambindings,
users, serviceaccounts) is provided by `ProvideReconcileGVRs`; enterprise
can rebind this to include Role/RoleBinding (and any other
enterprise-only resources) without touching the reconciler package.

Split `authz.WireSet` into `authz.WireSetBase` (reusable) and
`authz.WireSet` (base + OSS `ProvideReconcileGVRs`) so enterprise's
wireset can swap in its own list by importing `WireSetBase` and binding
its own provider.

Why: Role and RoleBinding are noop-implemented in OSS
(pkg/registry/apis/iam/api_installer.go). Listing them in the reconciler
fails the whole namespace reconcile. Rather than teach the reconciler to
detect and skip noop APIs at runtime, pick the GVR list at wire time so
the reconciler only sees resources it can actually read.

This PR is pure DI plumbing — no behavior change for enterprise (which
will land the override on its matching branch) and no change to the set
of GVRs the OSS MT reconciler is currently expected to handle.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* IAM/Zanzana: move ReconcileGVRs out of shared wireSet

The shared wireSet in wire.go previously bundled authz.WireSet, which
included authz.ProvideReconcileGVRs. Because wireSet is composed into
both OSS and enterprise graphs, enterprise would silently pull in the
OSS default provider and conflict with (or shadow) its own override.

- pkg/server/wire.go: use authz.WireSetBase instead of authz.WireSet in
  the shared wireSet.
- pkg/server/wireexts_oss.go: add authz.ProvideReconcileGVRs to the OSS
  wireExtsBasicSet so OSS still binds the default list.

Enterprise supplies extauthz.ProvideEnterpriseReconcileGVRs in its own
wireExtsBasicSet (lives in grafana-enterprise).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
Nav: Add access to Connections section for plugin routes (#121002)

* Nav: Add access to Connections section for plugin routes

* Nav: Fix whitespace lint in hasConnectionsPluginItems

* refactor(navtree): extract hasAccessibleInclude method

* Nav: create Connections section before addAppLinks

* fix(connections): show section to users with plugin children, not only datasource admins

Previously the Connections section was only added to the nav tree when
the user had ConfigurationPageAccess (datasources:create or read+write).
This meant plugin pages registered under the "connections" section ID
(e.g. grafana-collector-app, grafana-pdc-app) were invisible to viewers
who lacked datasource write permissions, even when they had access to
those plugins.

Changes:
- buildDataConnectionsNavLink now always returns the Connections section
  so that addAppLinks can attach plugin children regardless of the
  caller's datasource permissions. Core items (add-new-connection,
  datasources) remain gated by ConfigurationPageAccess.
- NavTreeRoot.RemoveEmptyConnectionsSection prunes the section after all
  app links and enterprise hooks have run if no children were registered.
  Called from setIndexViewData alongside RemoveEmptyAdminSections.
- /connections landing page route relaxed to reqSignedIn. The page
  derives its cards from the nav tree (grafana/grafana#122017), so any
  signed-in user who has nav children can view it; sub-pages retain their
  own per-route authorization.
- Tests added covering: admin sees core items, viewer gets empty section,
  viewer with plugin attachment sees the section, and empty pruning.

* fix: resolve cherry-pick conflicts remove duplicated test

commit.message:
PostgreSQL: Allow sql_engine to return results for EXPLAIN queries (#122739)

Allow sql_engine to return results for explain queries

In the switch to pgx library, a filter for select queries was added as
an indicator of fields with rows. This meant that explain analyze
stopped working (this worked in previous versions through the explore
panels). This is a nice feature to have as it allows understanding the
cost of various queries being used in grafana and how they could be
optimized for better dashboard experiences.

This changes the filtering to instead work with anything that provides

TimePicker: Show label for fiscal-quarter relative ranges (#122384)

* TimePicker: Show label for fiscal-quarter relative ranges

The trigger button label was blank when using relative expressions like
`now-1fQ/fQ`, `now-2Q`, or `now-1fy`. `describeTextRange` used the regex
`/^now([-+])(\d+)(\w)/` which only captures a single word character, so
for `now-1fQ/fQ` it extracted `unit='f'` — and the `spans` table was
missing `Q`, `fQ`, and `fy` entries anyway.

Extend the regex to capture the fiscal-prefixed units and add the
missing entries to `spans`, matching the units already recognized by
`datemath.parse`.

Fixes #111628

* TimePicker: Document fQ/fy as display-only lookup keys

commit.message:
Zanzana: ListObjects path when folder batch checks exceed threshold (#122465)

* Zanzana: use ListObjects when folder batch checks exceed threshold

When a batch check involves many unique folder tuples, evaluating each one
with BatchCheck can be costly. Above a configurable threshold, resolve folder
permission and subresource phases by listing accessible folders (ListObjects),
grouped by relation and resource context.

Adds [zanzana.server] folder_check_batch_threshold (default 20) and integration
tests that force the list path.

* Zanzana: list path uses streamed ListObjects deadline helper; drop unused flag

- Extract withListObjectsClientDeadline so client cancels before server stream deadline
  (deadline-1s when possible; tighter margins for sub-second deadlines)
- Remove UseStreamedListObjects / use_streamed_list_objects (unused; list always streams)

commit.message:
folder: remove redundant validations from Update in unified storage (#122984)

* folder: remove redundant UID validation from Update in unified storage

The Kubernetes API server enforces that the object name (which maps to
the folder UID) is immutable on update, making the IsValidShortUID /
IsShortUIDTooLong checks in the folder service Update method redundant.
Removed those checks and added a comment in validateOnCreate explaining
why they are only needed at creation time.

Made-with: Cursor

* folder: remove no-op TrimSpace on UID in Update

Valid UIDs only contain [a-zA-Z0-9\-\_] (enforced by IsValidShortUID at
creation time), so whitespace can never be present on an existing UID.
The TrimSpace call is a no-op in practice.

Made-with: Cursor

* folder: remove redundant empty title check from Update in unified storage

The validateOnUpdate function in the folder API server already enforces
that the title cannot be empty, making this check in the service layer
redundant.

Made-with: Cursor

* Remove unnecessary variable

Signed-off-by: Maicon Costa <maiconscosta@gmail.com>

commit.message:
Search: object storage distributed lock for index snapshots  (#121332)

* feat: distributed locking via conditional object storage writes (#718)

Implement distributed locking for index snapshots using conditional
object storage writes (S3/GCS/Azure), avoiding the need for external
coordination services like etcd or Redis.

Lock protocol:
- Atomic create via If-None-Match / ifGenerationMatch:0
- Atomic update/delete via If-Match / ifGenerationMatch
- Server-side mtime-based expiry (avoids clock skew between instances)
- Heartbeat with transient failure tolerance before declaring loss
- Immediate loss detection on ownership errors (ErrLockHeld/ErrLockNotFound)

CDK lock backend:
- ConditionalWriteFunc/ConditionalDeleteFunc for provider-specific operations
- Provider auto-detection via (*blob.Bucket).As() at wiring time
- Prefix-aware conditional deletes for ?prefix= bucket URLs
- Native SDK error mapping (HTTP 412, gRPC FailedPrecondition, 404)

ObjectStorageLock:
- Acquire/Release/Lost() API for callers
- Background heartbeat goroutine with configurable interval
- Graceful shutdown (context cancellation not treated as loss)
- Validates HeartbeatInterval < TTL at construction time

Tests:
- Unit tests with conditional bucket simulation (memblob + ETag tracking)
- Integration tests against fileblob (always) and real buckets (via env var)
- Tested against GCS (gs://unified-storage-index-snapshot-integration-test)

Closes grafana/search-and-storage-team#718
Parent epic: grafana/search-and-storage-team#715

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: CI lint and workspace check failures

- Add //nolint:exhaustive to gRPC codes.Code switch (only FailedPrecondition
  and NotFound are relevant)
- Run go mod tidy to mark azblob and s3 as direct deps (no longer indirect)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: move azblob and s3 to direct deps with modowner annotation

These are now direct imports from the lock providers file. Move them
from the indirect block to the direct require block with
@grafana/grafana-search-and-storage ownership.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* chore: unify integration test env var to CDK_TEST_BUCKET_URL

Rename CDK_LOCK_TEST_BUCKET_URL to CDK_TEST_BUCKET_URL so both
the lock and remote index store integration tests use the same
env var for the remote bucket.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: harden distributed lock correctness and test coverage

- Clock skew: add configurable ClockSkewAllowance (default 30s) to
  expiry check, preventing premature takeover when clocks diverge
- Lease expiry: reject Update from owners whose lease has expired
  (ErrLeaseExpired), preventing paused holders from reviving stale locks
- Heartbeat: enforce TTL >= 2*HeartbeatInterval at construction,
  use math.Ceil for maxFailures, dedicated write context to prevent
  orphaned server-side writes during Release
- S3 409: handle ConditionalRequestConflict in Create, retryCreate,
  and conditionalWrite via isObjectExistsErr helper
- Key validation: reject unsafe characters (CDK escaping mismatch)
  via validateObjectKey on every operation
- Provider check: fail fast for non-conditional blob providers
- Constructor: return error instead of panic, validate Owner/TTL/HB
- Tests: unified test infrastructure (conditionalBucket or real
  provider based on CDK_TEST_BUCKET_URL), concurrent takeover test,
  verified against S3, GCS, and Azure Blob Storage

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: simplify validateObjectKey and correct expired-lock comment

Replace multi-branch character validation with a single regex and
a contains check. Correct the Create godoc to include clockSkewAllowance
in the expiry condition.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: harden lock correctness, size validation, and test infrastructure

- Fix Release retry deadlock: only clear cancelHB/hbDone when held is
  also cleared, preventing nil-channel block on retry after transient
  delete errors
- Validate serialized lock size on write (Create/Update) to match the
  read-side cap, preventing locks that can be written but not read back
- Extract LimitedWriter to resource package, reuse in both search and
  lock packages instead of duplicating
- Use readLockData (Download + unmarshal) instead of ReadAll to enforce
  size limits before buffering the full object
- Simplify Delete error handling, test fake infrastructure, and remove
  dead nil guards in Release
- Clarify mutex discipline with struct field grouping comments
- Remove unused ctx parameter from Release()

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor: deduplicate lock tests, unexport backend options, reorganize code

Extract testBucketAndOpts to share setup between testBackend and
testBackendPair. Add expiredFakeLock helper for repeated expired-lock
test pattern. Convert ClockSkewAllowance and CorruptData tests to
table-driven. Unexport CDKLockBackendOptions fields (package-internal).
Reorganize cdk_lock_backend.go: move helpers to bottom, consolidate
comments.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: close heartbeat loss detection gap and empty-key panic

- Use floor instead of ceil for maxFailures so loss is detected no
  later than the TTL boundary (ceil could leave the lock appearing
  healthy after the lease expired).
- Tighten Update lease check from > to >= (now.After → !now.Before)
  so renewal at exactly mtime+TTL is rejected, closing the tick race
  when TTL is an exact multiple of HeartbeatInterval.
- Guard validateObjectKey against empty strings to prevent index
  out-of-bounds panic.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: cancel in-flight heartbeat update on release, move options to dedicated file

Derive heartbeat Update context from the heartbeat loop context instead
of context.Background(), so Release() cancelling the loop also cancels
any in-flight Update call. Previously Release could block up to 30s on
<-hbDone waiting for a slow Update to complete.

Move conditionalWriteFunc, conditionalDeleteFunc, CDKLockBackendOptions,
and errPreconditionFailed to cdk_lock_backend_options.go.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: remove unused azure-storage-blob-go dependency

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: address lint-go CI failures (errcheck, staticcheck QF1008)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor: unexport all types, split Release into stop+delete, fix heartbeat race

- Unexport all package types (objectStorageLock, cdkLockBackend, etc.)
  since the package is internal to the search layer
- Replace conditionalWrite/conditionalDelete function fields with
  conditionalOps interface grouping BeforeWrite+Delete per provider
- Split Release into idempotent stopHeartbeat (via sync.Once closure
  set by Acquire) and retryable Delete, eliminating cancelHB/hbDone fields
- Fix sporadic GCS test failure: use context.Background() for heartbeat
  Update so in-flight writes complete before Release's conditional delete
- Remove key validation from per-call backend methods (validated in constructor)
- Inline tryTakeover into Create, add validatePrefix helper
- Add comment on Lost() documenting Release-after-loss contract

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: restore per-call key validation in cdkLockBackend methods

The backend is general-purpose and may receive arbitrary keys, so each
public method re-validates. TestCDKLockBackend_RejectsInvalidKeys guards
this contract.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor: deduplicate lock package helpers

Extract shared helpers in the lock package:

Production:
- fetchAttrsAndData: consolidates the attrs+read+NotFound pattern
  previously repeated in Create, Update, and Delete
- marshalLockInfo: wraps json.Marshal + maxLockDataSize check
- mapDeleteStatus: maps HTTP 412/404 to sentinel errors, shared by
  S3, GCS-REST, and Azure Delete paths

Tests:
- newTestLock: replaces objectStorageLockConfig boilerplate
- createLockForTest: creates a lock and registers cleanup
- injectETagMismatch: single helper for interceptOps ETag-mismatch
  injection across Create/Update/Delete tests

Net -96 lines, behavior unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor: simplify objectStorageLock concurrency contract

Drop mu + sync.Once in favor of a "not safe for concurrent caller use"
contract. Replace the sync.Once-wrapped closure with plain hbCancel +
hbDone fields — cancel() and receiving from a closed channel are both
idempotent. Promote the heartbeat body to a named runHeartbeat method
so the goroutine shows up under a real symbol in stack traces.

Also add constructor-validation test coverage for newObjectStorageLock
and fix a pre-existing race in the failingUpdateBackend test double.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor: address round-3 review on lock package

- Drop b.ops != nil fallbacks in conditionalWrite/Delete and remove the
  TestCDKLockBackend_NoConditionalFuncs test. cdkLockOptionsFromBucket
  rejects unsupported providers, so ops is always non-nil in production;
  the branches were dead code that read like a supported fallback.
- Add test coverage for the errLockNotFound retry path in Create
  (object deleted between our IfNotExist-exists signal and the
  subsequent Attributes read).
- Add TestObjectStorageLock_ReleaseWaitsForInFlightUpdate, which locks
  in the design decision that heartbeat Update uses context.Background():
  Release must wait for an in-flight Update before Delete, without
  firing Lost. A future rewire to hbCtx would fail this test.
- Assert Create with the current owner also returns errLockHeld on an
  already-held lock.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: drop redundant embedded field qualifier in lock test helper

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
Settings: Fix GF_UNIFIED_STORAGE_* env overrides for bare section keys (#123060)

The generic second-pass env override logic skips all GF_UNIFIED_STORAGE_*
vars to avoid clobbering camelCase resource keys, and the unified-storage
handler only recognized _DUALWRITERMODE/_ENABLEMIGRATION suffixes, so env
vars targeting the bare [unified_storage] section (e.g.
GF_UNIFIED_STORAGE_MIGRATION_CACHE_SIZE_KB,
GF_UNIFIED_STORAGE_MIGRATION_PARQUET_BUFFER) were silently dropped.

Fall back to writing those to the bare [unified_storage] section with a
lowercased snake_case key.

Fixes #122993

commit.message:
IAM: Add read-only in-memory GlobalRole API for OSS (#122853)

* IAM: Add read-only in-memory GlobalRole API for OSS

Implement InMemoryGlobalRoleApiInstaller that serves basic roles
(Admin, Editor, Viewer, None, Grafana Admin) from accesscontrol.Service
as v0alpha1.GlobalRole objects through the k8s apiserver storage interface.
This enables the reconciler to read basic role permissions into Zanzana
without requiring a database backend.

Key changes:
- Add RoleNameAnnotation/RoleHiddenAnnotation constants to OSS
- Create ReadOnlyGlobalRoleREST implementing grafanarest.Storage (read-only)
- Create model translation from RoleDTO to v0alpha1.GlobalRole
- Move GlobalRoleIdentityWrapper from enterprise to OSS for shared use
- Wire the new provider to replace ProvideNoopGlobalRoleApiInstaller
- Feature-gated behind FlagKubernetesAuthzGlobalRolesApi (unchanged)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* IAM: Tighten in-memory GlobalRole API authorizer and align models to enterprise

Restrict the in-memory GlobalRole authorizer to access-policy identities
(the MT reconciler), skipping the per-request RBAC round-trip. Align model
translation with the enterprise legacy builder so basic roles' timestamps
are stable across apiserver restarts.

Changes:
- Authorizer now allows only TypeAccessPolicy on get/list; rejects writes
  and all other identities without calling accessClient.Check
- Drop accessClient field and provider argument (no longer needed)
- roleDTOToV0GlobalRole uses dto.Created/dto.Updated instead of a per-REST
  startTime snapshot (matches enterprise toV0GlobalRole behavior)
- MutateOn{Create,Update,Delete} return errReadOnly to match Validate
- Remove utils.VerbWatch from readVerbs (storage doesn't implement Watcher)
- Tighten GlobalRoleIdentityWrapper doc to describe Get/List only

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* IAM: Simplify GlobalRole authorizer and drop Wire-time flag gate

Authorizer now denies by default and only allows reads from access-policy
identities. Also removes the feature-flag check in the Wire provider — the
same gate already exists in register.go where storage is registered.

Adds table-driven tests for GetAuthorizer covering unauthenticated,
access-policy read/write, and non-access-policy identity cases.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* IAM: Inline GlobalRole service identity swap into rest.go

Moves the service identity context swap from the GlobalRoleIdentityWrapper
decorator directly into ReadOnlyGlobalRoleREST.Get/List, and drops the
now-unused wrapper package. Fewer files to maintain and the swap lives
next to the storage code that needs it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* IAM: Require matching token permission on GlobalRole access policy reads

The in-memory GlobalRole authorizer previously accepted any access-policy
identity for get/list. Now it also verifies the access token carries a
matching permission of the form `iam.grafana.app/globalroles:<verb>` (or
`iam.grafana.app/globalroles:*`), so callers that happen to authenticate
as an access policy but lack the specific permission are denied.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix lint

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
ToolbarButton: fix text overflow causing overlap with adjacent elements (#121269)

ToolbarButton: fix text overflow in buttons with icons

When a ToolbarButton has a fixed width (e.g. the Refresh button in
dashboard scenes), longer translations like German "Aktualisieren"
overflow and overlap adjacent elements.

Add overflow: hidden, textOverflow: ellipsis, and minWidth: 0 to the
contentWithIcon style so that text is properly truncated with an
ellipsis instead of overflowing into neighboring controls.

Fixes #119789

Signed-off-by: Pierluigi Lenoci <pierluigi.lenoci@gmail.com>

commit.message:
Zanzana: Fix mt-reconciler Unauthenticated error by adding internal ReadTuples (#123180)

The mt-reconciler runs as a background worker without end-user claims
in its context. #123030 routed its reads through Server.Read, which
calls authorize() and fails every reconcile with
"rpc error: code = Unauthenticated desc = unauthenticated".

Mirror the WriteTuples pattern: add an internal ReadTuples(store, req)
on Server that uses a pre-resolved StoreInfo and calls the OpenFGA
client directly, skipping the public-API auth check. computeDiffStreaming
now resolves the store once up front and iterates via ReadTuples with
openfgav1 types (dropping the authzextv1 conversion).

commit.message:
Storage: Move lock package into search package (#123231)

The lock package under pkg/storage/unified/search/lock/ has no external
importers and is only intended to be used by RemoteIndexStore. Moving it
into the parent search package is a precursor to exposing locking via
RemoteIndexStore.

All identifiers in the lock package were already unexported and there
are no name collisions with the search package, so this is a mechanical
move: rename files with a 'lock_' prefix and change 'package lock' to
'package search'.

commit.message:
Search: download remote index snapshot on startup (#123238)

* Search: download remote index snapshot on startup

Extend bleveBackend.BuildIndex to try downloading a prebuilt bleve
snapshot from remote object storage before falling back to a full
rebuild. Gated by the index_snapshot_enabled config and a per-resource
MinDocCount so small indexes are still built in-process.

Selection picks the best snapshot by tiered preference:
  - tier 0: MinBuildVersion <= version <= running Grafana version
  - tier 1: version below MinBuildVersion (still usable)
  - tier 2: version newer than running (last resort)
Within each tier, sort by version desc -> RV desc -> upload time desc.
Snapshots older than MaxIndexAge or with unparseable build versions
are dropped outright. On any download / open / validate failure the
partial destDir is cleaned up and BuildIndex falls through to the
existing build-from-scratch path.

Adds two metrics (index_server_snapshot_downloads_total{status} and
index_server_snapshot_download_duration_seconds) and wires the CDK
bucket + RemoteIndexStore in NewSearchOptions when the feature is
enabled.

Upload of a freshly built snapshot is intentionally out of scope for
this PR and will land with the periodic-upload work in #721.

Part of grafana/search-and-storage-team#720.

* Search: clarify snapshot download metric help and drop stale design-doc reference

Review feedback: the histogram help read as if it contradicted the
counter (which has download_error / validate_error statuses), and the
tryDownloadRemoteSnapshot comment referenced a design doc that isn't
linked here. The tiers are already documented inline in pickBestSnapshot.

* Search: simplify snapshot download duration metric help

* Search: merge snapshot integration test into bleve_snapshot_test.go

Grafana's convention is to identify integration tests by the
TestIntegration prefix, not by a separate _integration_test.go file.
Renamed TestBleveBackend_SnapshotRoundTrip to
TestIntegrationBleveSnapshotRoundTrip and folded it + its helpers
into the unit test file.

* Search: simplify snapshot integration test

Seed the bucket via writeFakeSnapshot + store.UploadIndex instead of
building a real index, stopping the backend, and locating the on-disk
dir. The unique signal of this test is that BuildIndex chooses the
download path when configured; the real-build round-trip is already
covered by TestRemoteIndexStore_UploadDownloadBleveIndex.

Drops makeDocs, onlyIndexSubdir, and strconv+resourcepb imports.

* Search: isolate RV-desc tiebreaker in snapshot selection test

Split the "within tier" case into two assertions: first without d
proves RV-desc wins over upload-desc (200 beats 50 despite older
upload); then d is added to prove upload-desc is the next tiebreaker
when version + RV are equal. Before this, the single-assertion test
couldn't distinguish RV-desc from upload-desc winning.

* Search: drop redundant nil-store check, log snapshot candidates at debug

Review feedback: BuildIndex already guards tryDownloadRemoteSnapshot
with Snapshot.Store != nil, so the internal nil check (and its test)
was dead. Also add per-candidate + selection-summary debug logs in
pickBestSnapshot so operators can see why a snapshot was picked
(counts of dropped-by-age, dropped-unparseable, and which tier won).

this PR and will land with the periodic-upload work in #721.

Part of grafana/search-and-storage-team#720.

* Search: clarify snapshot download metric help and drop stale design-doc reference

Review feedback: the histogram help read as if it contradicted the
counter (which has download_error / validate_error statuses), and the
tryDownloadRemoteSnapshot comment referenced a design doc that isn't
linked here. The tiers are already documented inline in pickBestSnapshot.

* Search: simplify snapshot download duration metric help

* Search: merge snapshot integration test into bleve_snapshot_test.go

Grafana's convention is to identify integration tests by the
TestIntegration prefix, not by a separate _integration_test.go file.
Renamed TestBleveBackend_SnapshotRoundTrip to
TestIntegrationBleveSnapshotRoundTrip and folded it + its helpers
into the unit test file.

* Search: simplify snapshot integration test

Seed the bucket via writeFakeSnapshot + store.UploadIndex instead of
building a real index, stopping the backend, and locating the on-disk
dir. The unique signal of this test is that BuildIndex chooses the
download path when configured; the real-build round-trip is already
covered by TestRemoteIndexStore_UploadDownloadBleveIndex.

Drops makeDocs, onlyIndexSubdir, and strconv+resourcepb imports.

* Search: isolate RV-desc tiebreaker in snapshot selection test

Split the "within tier" case into two assertions: first without d
proves RV-desc wins over upload-desc (200 beats 50 despite older
upload); then d is added to prove upload-desc is the next tiebreaker
when version + RV are equal. Before this, the single-assertion test
couldn't distinguish RV-desc from upload-desc winning.

* Search: drop redundant nil-store check, log snapshot candidates at debug

Review feedback: BuildIndex already guards tryDownloadRemoteSnapshot
with Snapshot.Store != nil, so the internal nil check (and its test)
was dead. Also add per-candidate + selection-summary debug logs in
pickBestSnapshot so operators can see why a snapshot was picked
(counts of dropped-by-age, dropped-unparseable, and which tier won).

Provisioning: Fix flaky TestIntegrationProvisioning_CreatingGitHubRepository delete wait (#123334)

Provisioning: Raise repository-delete wait to default timeout in GitHub test

The post-Delete EventuallyWithT used a 10s/50ms bound, but the repository
controller must run three finalizers (cleanup, release, remove) before the
API object disappears. Under CI load that regularly exceeds 10s, leaving
the repo around and cascading into the next test's CleanupAllResources.
Switch to the suite-wide defaults (60s/100ms) that every other wait uses.

Refs grafana/git-ui-sync-project#1104

Provisioning: Use default wait timeouts for finalizer-driven deletions (#123336)

Follow-up to #123334. Replace bespoke EventuallyWithT timeouts in the
provisioning integration tests with the package-wide defaults
(common.WaitTimeoutDefault = 60s, common.WaitIntervalDefault = 100ms).
These waits all follow a repository Delete() and poll for the
finalizer chain (cleanup → release/remove orphan resources) to complete;
on loaded CI runners the chain can exceed the old 5s–20s bounds and
cascades into failures in the next test via CleanupAllResources.

commit.message:
Provisioning: Fix v1beta1 CRUD test flake by disabling sync (#123340)

The TestIntegrationV1Beta1RepositoryCRUD test enabled sync with
target=folder, which races with the repo's remove-orphan-resources
finalizer: if the root folder is created by sync but not yet indexed
when the finalizer lists managed resources, the folder is leaked.
Subsequent tests then fail cleanup with "managed resource is missing
source path annotation" because the root folder has no source path
(it lives at the repo root).

The test only exercises v1beta1 API CRUD serialization; it does not
need sync. Disable it to match the pattern used in apiversion/version_test.go.

Fixes https://github.com/grafana/git-ui-sync-project/issues/1103

commit.message:
Provisioning: Unify finalizer-driven cleanup waits in integration tests (#123343)

Introduce three helpers in pkg/tests/apis/provisioning/common to replace
the repeated EventuallyWithT blocks that follow a repository Delete() and
wait for the finalizer chain (cleanup -> release/remove orphan resources)
to drain:

- ProvisioningTestHelper.WaitForRepositoryDeleted polls until the named
  repository reports NotFound.
- WaitForResourcesReleased lists a dynamic client and waits for the
  provisioning-manager annotations (manager kind/identity, source
  path/checksum) to be stripped from every item.
- WaitForResourcesDeleted lists a dynamic client and waits for zero items.

Refactors the six test files touched by #123336 onto the new helpers so
every wait uses WaitTimeoutDefault / WaitIntervalDefault consistently.

commit.message:
Provisioning: Fix flake in IncrementalDiffThreshold integration test (#123342)

The RepositoryController only re-processes a repo when its informer
re-emits the object. The SharedInformerFactory's resync period is 60s,
which sits right at the test's WaitTimeoutDefault=60s, making the test
flake at the boundary. Nudge the controller inside the polling loop
(throttled, and only once syncAge ≥ syncInterval) so we don't depend on
the 60s informer tick to observe an interval-scheduled sync.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
Search: trigger background rebuild for indexes built by newer Grafana version (#123344)

When the periodic scan detects an index that was built by a Grafana
version newer than the currently running one, enqueue a background
rebuild. This ensures indexes converge to match the running version
after a downgrade scenario.

The check is added to shouldRebuildIndex via a new maxBuildVersion
parameter (the running Grafana version). The existing rebuild queue
and periodic scan (every 5 minutes) handle the actual rebuild.

Follow-up to #123238.

commit.message:
Provisioning: Fix race in PullStatus condition with controller patches (#123358)

* Provisioning: Fix flaky PullStatus condition race with controller patches

The sync worker and RepositoryController both patched /status/conditions
with a whole-array replace built from their own view of the conditions.
When either actor held a stale snapshot, its patch could silently clobber
conditions the other had just written — most visibly the PullStatus
condition set by the sync worker, which the controller never includes
in its own view.

Switch BuildConditionPatchOpsFromExisting to emit per-condition JSON
Patch ops (add /status/conditions/- for new types, replace /<index> for
changed existing types) so unrelated condition types are left untouched.
The whole-array replace is still used when the conditions array is
empty, since `add /-` requires the target array to exist.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Add integration tests for per-condition patch ops

Exercises the JSON Patch shape the repository controller and sync worker
use to write /status/conditions: `add /-` for brand-new condition types
and `replace /<index>` for existing ones. The concurrent-adds test covers
the no-clobber guarantee that motivated switching away from whole-array
replaces.

* Provisioning: Harden condition-patch integration tests against controller race

Wait for Ready + NamespaceQuota before snapshotting so the initial
reconcile has landed and the informer cache has caught up. Wrap the
apply-and-assert blocks in idempotent EventuallyWithT loops so the
narrow empty-cache fallback in BuildConditionPatchOpsFromExisting
cannot flake the tests if the controller reruns with a stale view.
Move require.NoError calls off the concurrent worker goroutines.

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
Unified Storage: use batch transaction context in ResourceVersionManager writes to fix SQLite integration tests (#122241)

* fix(storage): use batch transaction context in ResourceVersionManager writes

WriteEventFunc now receives the WithTx context; sql backend and kv datastore
paths use it for ExecContext on the batch transaction. Prevents a canceled
request context from invalidating *sql.Tx mid-batch (flaky resource_history
inserts: transaction already committed or rolled back).

Fixes provisioning incremental sync flakes (e.g. graceful folder rename).

Made-with: Cursor

* Commit changes

* docs: add HACK notes for RV batch txn test timeout override

Document the process-wide rvmanager default and k8s test helper wiring so
future readers know the tradeoffs and preferred explicit configuration.

Made-with: Cursor

* test(provisioning): re-enable non-metadata folder rename subtest

The "non-metadata folder rename still works via delete and create" subtest
in TestIntegrationProvisioning_IncrementalSync_GracefulFolderRename was
skipped because of flaky "context deadline exceeded" errors during resource
insertion — the exact symptom of the batch-txn context bug fixed by this PR.

Re-enable it now that WriteEventFunc uses the transaction context.

* refactor(storage): wire batch transaction timeout via [unified_storage] ini

Replace the process-wide atomic override (SetDefaultBatchTransactionTimeout /
ClearDefaultBatchTransactionTimeout) with the conventional Grafana pattern:
ini key → setting.Cfg → BackendOptions → ResourceManagerOptions.

New ini key:
  [unified_storage]
  resource_version_batch_transaction_timeout = 5s    ; default

Mirrors the existing NotifierSettleDelay wiring. Integration tests set the
value by writing the ini key via testinfra GrafanaOpts instead of mutating a
global — works with parallel test servers in one process, no Set/Clear dance.

Provisioning: Fix flaky inline secrets test by polling for secret cleanup (#123373)

Inline secrets are cleaned up asynchronously after a repository is
deleted (via owner-reference GC and the secret garbage-collection
worker), so the test could race the cleanup and still decrypt a secret
after WaitForRepositoryDeleted returned. Wrap the post-deletion decrypt
check in EventuallyWithT so it tolerates the async cleanup lag.

commit.message:
Provisioning: Fix TestIntegrationProvisioning_BlockManagerChange flake (#123382)

Provisioning: Fix BlockManagerChange flake by retrying SyncAndWait on IsAlreadyExists

When a repository becomes healthy, the controller auto-triggers a full resync.
If that in-flight sync races with SyncAndWait, the old behavior only waited
for the controller's pre-setup sync to drain, so state changes made after
WaitForHealthyRepository (e.g. file copies to the provisioning path) were
never observed. The retry drains in-flight jobs and posts again so a sync
is guaranteed to run against current state.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
E2E: fix perf-test flakiness caused by unhandled response.body() error (#123323)

When `response.body()` throws a Protocol error (e.g. for cached or
redirect responses where CDP has no body data), the `#requestsInFlight`
counter was never decremented, causing `stopListening()` to hang
indefinitely and the test to time out.

Wrap the async body read and sizes call in a try/finally so
`#requestsInFlight` is always decremented. Also move `stopListening()`
before metrics collection so all responses are captured, and await
`page.close()`.

QueryEditor: Bulk actions bar (3/3) (#120140)

* Refactor(qev2): extract UI toggles hook + migrate selection state to arrays

- Extracts useQueryEditorUIToggles: pulls isQueryOptionsOpen, focusedField,
  showingDatasourceHelp, and transformTogglesState out of QueryEditorContextWrapper
  into a dedicated hook, reducing the size of the wrapper component.

- Migrates selection model from scalar string|null to string[] arrays:
  selectedQueryRefIds and selectedTransformationIds. The "primary" card is
  always the last element, so single-select behaviour is unchanged. This
  prepares the context for multi-selection in the next PR.

- Updates useSelectedCard, QueryEditorContextWrapper, testUtils, and all
  related tests accordingly. Pure refactor — no user-visible behaviour change.

Made-with: Cursor

* Feat(qev2): multi-selection on sidebar cards with Ctrl/Shift modifiers

Adds multi-select support to the query/transformation sidebar so users
can select multiple cards before applying a bulk action.

- useMultiSelection hook: manages ordered multi-selection state for
  queries and transformations. Supports plain click (replace selection),
  Ctrl/Cmd click (toggle card), and Shift click (range-select). Query and
  transformation selections are mutually exclusive.

- SidebarCard: renames onClick → onSelect, passes { multi, range } modifiers
  derived from the click event. Shift+mousedown prevents native text selection.
  Adds isPartOfSelection prop for a subtle tint on non-primary selected cards.
  Exposes aria-pressed for both primary and part-of-selection cards.

- QueryCard / TransformationCard / AlertCard / GhostSidebarCard: switch
  from setSelectedQuery/setSelectedTransformation to toggleQuerySelection /
  toggleTransformationSelection.

- EditableQueryName: new readOnly mode (renders plain text) used when
  multiple queries are selected, preventing accidental rename.

- Wires toggleQuerySelection, toggleTransformationSelection, and
  clearSelection through QueryEditorContext and QueryEditorContextWrapper.

Made-with: Cursor

* Feat(qev2): bulk actions bar for queries and transformations

When 2+ queries or transformations are selected (via Ctrl/Shift click from
the previous PR), a BulkActionsBar appears in the sidebar with contextual
actions for the selection.

Query bulk actions:
- Delete (with confirmation modal)
- Hide / Show toggle
- Change data source (via DataSourceModal picker)

Transformation bulk actions:
- Delete (with confirmation modal)
- Enable all / Disable all toggle

Backend (PanelDataPaneNext):
- bulkDeleteQueries, bulkToggleQueriesHide, bulkChangeDataSource
- bulkDeleteTransformations, bulkToggleTransformationsDisabled

The BulkActionsBar is responsive — action labels are hidden and only icons
shown when the bar is narrower than 280 px.

* chore: bulk actions bar polish — clear selection after DS change, compact mode for transformations, align styling tokens

* chore: fix fallback logic

* chore: cleanup

commit.message:
Fix flaky stars migration test with eventual consistency (#123383)

The stars migration test was flaky because each Add() operation uses its
own transaction, and the subsequent GetByUser() query may run on a different
database connection that doesn't immediately see the committed data due to
PostgreSQL connection pooling.

Replace the immediate assertion with require.Eventually() to handle the
read-your-own-writes delay, giving up to 5 seconds for the data to become
visible.

Signed-off-by: Maicon Costa <maiconscosta@gmail.com>

* unified storage: add permission check tests for server.read()

Test that Read enforces access control correctly: denied when the user
lacks get permission, allowed when permitted, error propagated when the
authz service fails, and the resource's parent folder is forwarded to
the access check for hierarchy-aware resolution.

Made-with: Cursor

are excluded, and passing nil access bypasses filtering entirely.

The accesscontrol.Evaluate() check for folders:read was redundant because
user-level RBAC is already enforced in the unified storage layer via

centralized in the storage layer where the parent folder context is known.

Plugins: Introduce internal datasource plugin metadata lookup API (#121479)

* Plugins: Introduce internal datasource plugin metadata lookup API

Adds getDatasourcePluginMetas() as an internal API for fetching
datasource plugin metadata independently of datasource instance data.
This follows the existing pattern established for panels and apps,
creating a single deduplicated source of truth for datasource plugin
metadata keyed by plugin type ID.

This is Phase 1 of decoupling datasources from bootdata. It does not
change DataSourceSrv APIs or remove meta from bootdata — it introduces
the metadata lookup as a parallel source of truth and wires it into
plugin loading paths (sandbox codeLoader).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* pluginImporter: resolve datasource plugin meta internally via getDatasourcePluginMeta

Change importDataSource to accept a pluginId string instead of a DataSourcePluginMeta
object, resolving the metadata internally through getDatasourcePluginMeta. This removes
the dependency on DatasourceSrv providing meta to the importer, preparing for Phase 2
where DatasourceSrv APIs become async-aware.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Plugins: Gate datasource plugin meta lookup behind datasourcePluginMetaLookup feature toggle

Add a new feature toggle `datasourcePluginMetaLookup` that controls whether the
plugin importer resolves datasource metadata internally via getDatasourcePluginMeta
(new path) or falls back to looking it up from config.datasources (legacy path).
This allows safely shipping the new behavior behind a flag.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Revert "Plugins: Gate datasource plugin meta lookup behind datasourcePluginMetaLookup feature toggle"

This reverts commit 6e042e09d8a26a310fe17c9d8efaeecd182e7ea7.

* Plugins: Use enableDatasourceMetaApiPluginLoading toggle for datasource plugin meta

Switch datasources.ts from useMTPlugins to the dedicated
enableDatasourceMetaApiPluginLoading feature toggle introduced in #121640.
Also adopt the fallback pattern from panels.ts/apps.ts — when the API
returns empty items, fall back to bootdata and log a warning.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Plugins: Remove unused getDatasourcePluginMetasMapSync

Address review feedback from @hugohaggmark — the sync variant was an ugly
workaround needed only for panels (dashboard-scene code). Datasources have
no callers of the sync function, so remove it entirely.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Plugins: Fix datasource mapper import path and angular test expectation

Fix TS2307 build error — the import path for Spec type was missing the
'meta/' directory segment. Also update angular mapper test expectations
to match the updated shared angularMapper output.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Plugins: Revert importDataSource to accept DataSourcePluginMeta instead of pluginId

Address PR review feedback to keep importDataSource consistent with
importPanel and importApp by accepting a meta object parameter. The
getDatasourcePluginMeta lookup now happens at caller sites instead of
inside the importer.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Plugins: Use plugin meta API for datasource loading, remove unused toggle

Resolve datasource plugin meta via getDatasourcePluginMeta() in
DatasourceSrv.loadDatasource() instead of relying on bootdata. Remove
the enableDatasourceMetaApiPluginLoading toggle and use useMTPlugins
to align with panels and apps. Remove unused getDatasourcePluginMetasMap.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Datasources: reject when plugin meta missing and fill test gaps

Reject in DatasourceSrv.loadDatasource when getDatasourcePluginMeta
returns null, update tests to match the new per-type meta semantics,
and cover setMetas non-empty paths plus the bootdata fallback warning.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Datasources: avoid duplicate /api/frontend/settings fetch in reload

Accept optional pre-fetched settings in refetchDatasourcePluginMetas and
pass the settings already loaded by DatasourceSrv.reload() to skip the
redundant request when useMTPlugins is off.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Datasources: resolve plugin meta by aliasIDs

Mirror the panels.ts approach: maintain a datasourcesByAliasIDs index
updated alongside the main map so getDatasourcePluginMeta can resolve
legacy plugin ids via aliasIDs before returning null.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* DatasourceSrv: fall back to instanceSettings.meta on null meta lookup

When getDatasourcePluginMeta returns null (e.g. a partial Meta API
response missing an installed datasource), fall back to the bootdata
meta from instanceSettings instead of rejecting. Include the plugin
type in the error when both sources are missing.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Potential fix for pull request finding

Co-authored-by: Copilot Autofix powered by AI <175728472+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Datasources: move FrontendSettings type and add hook tests

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* DatasourceSrv: log warning and document instanceSettings.meta fallback

* DatasourceSrv: use logPluginMetaError and cover reload() with tests

commit.message:
Provisioning: Fix flaky reconciliation trigger helpers (#123361)

The Trigger{Repository,Connection}Reconciliation helpers used Get +
UpdateStatus wrapped in EventuallyWithT to touch status.health.checked.
On SQLite the controller reconciler concurrently updates the object on
every tick and wins the optimistic-lock race every iteration, so the
wrapper never escapes and times out.

Replace with a merge patch on the status subresource. Merge patches
carry no resourceVersion, so they cannot conflict. Same approach as
PR #121164 (step 4 of the same test).

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
Stars: Fix silent data loss from colliding synthetic dashboard_id values (#123476)

Replace time.Now().UnixMicro() + rand.Int63n(5000) with a UnixMicro +
atomic counter in starimpl.Insert, guaranteeing uniqueness within a
process. The old formula produced duplicate values ~0.01% of the time for
back-to-back Add() calls, which silently violated the legacy
UNIQUE (user_id, dashboard_id) index and got swallowed by Add()'s
idempotency path, causing silent data loss.

Also revert the require.Eventually workaround from #123383 now that the
root cause is fixed.

commit.message:
Provisioning: fix memory leak in repository controller work queue (#123359)

* Provisioning: fix memory leak in repository controller work queue

Switch the queue item type from *queueItem to string to enable proper
deduplication. With pointer keys, every Add call bypassed the workqueue
dirty set and pushed a distinct item holding a full *Repository reference,
causing unbounded queue growth under the status-patch feedback loop
described in git-ui-sync-project#1087.

With string keys, repeated enqueues of the same namespace/name key collapse
to a single dirty entry, bounding queue depth at O(number of repositories).
The queueItem struct is removed entirely: obj was never read in process
(it fetches from the lister), and attempts is replaced by NumRequeues.

Fixes: grafana/git-ui-sync-project#1088

* fixing new tests using string key

* formatting

commit.message:
Provisioning: Allow file rename on dashboard save (#123103)

* Provisioning: Allow file rename on dashboard save

When saving an existing dashboard via Git Sync, the file path is now
editable. The save form shows split Folder + Filename inputs (same as
new dashboards) instead of a read-only Path field.

When the path changes, the frontend switches from PUT (update) to POST
with originalPath (move+update), using the backend's existing move API.
The Save button also enables when only the path changes.

No backend changes required — the move API already supports content
changes during moves.

* format

* Provisioning: Fix dashboard changed prompt after provisioned save

* Provisioning: Clear dashboardWatcher suppression on save error

Wrap the onError handler passed to useProvisionedRequestHandler so it
calls dashboardWatcher.clearIgnoreSave() before delegating to showError.
Previously, a failed provisioned save left ignoreSave at Infinity until
the drawer unmounted, hiding later live save/conflict events from other
sessions while the user retried.

Also correct the unmount-effect comment: success clears via
handleDismiss, error clears via the new onError handler, and the effect
itself only covers cancel/navigation-away.

* format

commit.message:
Provisioning: retry Repository patches on RV conflict (#123497)

The unified storage layer translates every JSON Patch into a
read-modify-write with PreviousRV set to the value it just read, so
concurrent writes legitimately race with our patches and surface as
"Operation cannot be fulfilled on repositories.provisioning.grafana.app
...: requested RV does not match current RV". Two call sites on the
repository object have no retry and fail outright today:

  - RepositoryStatusPatcher.Patch — shared helper behind every status
    patch (status patch operations, post-hook status updates, delete-
    status writes).
  - handleDelete — the JSON Patch that strips /metadata/finalizers
    after finalizer processing completes.

Wrap both in retry.RetryOnConflict with the default backoff (5 steps,
~50ms). Conflicts are transient by nature here, so a re-read + re-apply
will succeed on the next attempt in almost every real case, and the
retry budget is bounded so persistent conflicts still surface.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
IAM: Persist team members on the Team resource (step 1) (#123468)

* IAM: Persist team members on the Team resource (step 1)

* Add shared CUE TeamMember + TeamPermission types and expose
  TeamSpec.Members as a list of those.
* team LegacyStore: hydrate spec.members on Get/List and reconcile
  add/update/delete deltas on Create/Update against the legacy team
  tables. Reconciliation runs in the same SQL transaction as the team
  row update; team-internal-ID resolution happens before BEGIN to avoid
  a SQLite self-deadlock when the write tx holds the file lock.
* Admission rejects duplicate members and flips of the immutable
  `external` flag so the error is consistent regardless of dual-write
  mode.
* Legacy CreateTeam now returns apierrors.NewAlreadyExists on a unique
  constraint violation so clients see a proper 409 instead of a 500
  wrapping the raw SQL error.
* Index member UIDs on the Team search document.
* Integration tests cover CRUD with members, hydration, and the new
  admission rules.

Scope of this commit is the data model + legacy store + index path.
The user-teams / team-members subresources, the enterprise team-group
synchronizer, and the legacy member-search adapter land in follow-up
steps on this branch.

* Regenerate openapi spec

* IAM: fix testdata path in team integration subtests

The team integration test file lives in `pkg/tests/apis/iam/team/`
while the shared testdata fixtures live one level up in
`pkg/tests/apis/iam/testdata/`. The new members/AlreadyExists subtests
referenced `testdata/…` instead of `../testdata/…`, so CI failed with
"no such file or directory" when loading the fixture. Use the correct
relative path and switch the helper deletions from `defer` to
`t.Cleanup` for consistency with the rest of the file.

* Fix frontend

* IAM: address review on team members path

* Create is now transactional. CreateTeamCommand gained MemberCreates
  and legacy.CreateTeam inserts the team row and all seed members in
  one WithTransaction; a failing member rolls back the team too,
  matching Update's atomicity.
* Update now maps team.ErrTeamMemberAlreadyAdded → apierrors.NewConflict
  so the concurrent-add race returns 409 instead of 500, matching the
  Create path.
* buildCreateCommand / buildUpdateCommand translate GetUserInternalID
  failures into apierrors.NewBadRequest so an unknown user UID in
  spec.members returns 400 rather than a 500.
* Replace the per-team hydration on List with a single bulk query via
  a new ListTeamBindingsQuery.TeamUIDs + ArgList in team_bindings_query.sql,
  backed by listTeamMembersForTeams. Drops the N+1.
* mapTeamPermission / toLegacyPermission use explicit switches with a
  default panic so adding a new permission variant upstream without
  updating the mapping fails loud instead of silently collapsing to
  "member".
* Clarify comments on CreateTeamCommand.MemberCreates and
  UpdateTeamCommand.Member{Deletes,Updates,Creates} to spell out the
  atomicity guarantee and which fields the caller must pre-resolve.
* Document the remaining TOCTOU gap between listAllTeamMembers and the
  write tx in Update, and why the race that matters (add-add) is
  covered by the unique-constraint → 409 path.

* IAM: integration test for Update 409 on concurrent member adds

Exercises the ErrTeamMemberAlreadyAdded → apierrors.NewConflict mapping
on the team Update path by racing 10 goroutines that each add the same
user to an empty team. The test asserts no goroutine ever receives a
500 (the pre-fix failure mode), at least one succeeds, and the final
team state contains the user exactly once — i.e. the race converges
through the 409/retry path rather than duplicating or corrupting rows.

* IAM: propagate permission-mapping errors and bulk team-member writes

* mapTeamPermission / toLegacyPermission / mapToTeamMember / toTeamObject
  now return (value, error) instead of panicking on unknown variants.
  diffMembers, buildCreateCommand, buildUpdateCommand, and the Get /
  List / Create / Update flows in team/store.go propagate the error so
  a corrupt SQL row or a new upstream variant surfaces as a 500 at the
  HTTP boundary instead of crashing the apiserver.
* legacy.CreateTeam and legacy.UpdateTeam now issue one bulk INSERT
  (multi-row VALUES) for MemberCreates and one bulk DELETE (… WHERE
  uid IN (...)) for MemberDeletes, replacing the per-row loops.
  DeleteTeamMembersBulkCommand is scoped by OrgID so a UID collision
  across orgs cannot remove the wrong row. Permission UPDATEs stay as
  one statement per row — each has a distinct target value and a
  CASE-WHEN bulk isn't worth the complexity today.
* New golden-SQL tests (single + many variants) cover the two bulk
  templates across mysql/postgres/sqlite.

commit.message:
Alerting: fix UpdateAdminConfiguration updating wrong rows when multiple orgs exist (#123425)

alerting: fix UpdateAdminConfiguration updating wrong rows when multiple orgs exist

The UPDATE used a WHERE-clause filter on org_id via xorm's fluent API, but
xorm resolves the target row by primary key when a struct is passed to Update.
Without an explicit ID, the WHERE condition was silently ignored and all rows
could be affected.

Fix: fetch the existing row first to obtain its PK, then use .ID() so the
UPDATE is scoped to exactly that one record. Also guard against a no-op update
when no columns are changed.

Adds an integration test that verifies updates to one org do not touch others.

Co-authored-by: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
Provisioning: Enrich worker logs and fix finalizer version field duplication (#123500)

* Provisioning: Log worker_id in repository and connection controllers

Attach a worker_id to the per-goroutine logger context in
RepositoryController and ConnectionController so the worker handling
each queue item is identifiable in logs. ConcurrentJobDriver already
logs driver_id for the same purpose.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Fix version log field duplication in finalizer item processor

newItemProcessor captured the logger from its outer scope and reassigned
it on every folder item via `logger = logger.With("version", version)`.
Each subsequent invocation appended another "version" field, producing
log lines with "version=v1beta1" repeated dozens of times. Because
processResourceItems invokes this closure concurrently, the shared
reassignment was also a data race.

Copy the base logger into a local variable per invocation so each item
gets a clean logger.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
Provisioning: retry finalizer ops on RV conflict (#123493)

* Provisioning: retry finalizer ops on RV conflict

Transient optimistic-concurrency conflicts from the unified storage
backend ("requested RV does not match current RV") currently fail an
entire repository finalizer run. The finalizer races with other
reconciles/syncs that legitimately mutate the same folder/dashboard, so
a conflict on one item should be retried rather than aborting cleanup.

Wrap the per-item Patch/Delete callback in retry.RetryOnConflict with
the default backoff (5 steps, ~50ms).

Also fix a logger bug in newItemProcessor: the closure reassigned the
captured `logger` variable with `logger.With("version", ...)`, causing
`version=v1beta1` to accumulate on every folder item processed. Use a
per-item logger instead.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Revert logger fix in finalizers item processor

Keep only the retry-on-conflict change in this PR. The logger
accumulation fix will be handled separately.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Provisioning: Nested folders for Dashboards (#119852)

* Backend: Provisioning Nested folders for Dashboards

Add support for nested folder hierarchies when using `foldersFromFilesStructure`.

The folder structure on disk (e.g. `level1/level2/dashboard.json`) is now correctly reflected in **Grafana** with proper parent-child relationships.

Changes:

- Refactor `getOrCreateFolder` into `getOrCreateFolderInternal` with unified logic
- Add `parentUID` parameter to `getOrCreateFolderByTitle` for nested folders
- `getOrCreateFolderFullpath` creates folders level by level, passing parent UID
- Use `identity.WithServiceIdentity` for provisioning operations

Backward compatibility:

- Single folder and flat structures unchanged (`parentUID = nil`)
- Explicit FolderUID lookup unchanged
- All existing tests pass

commit.message:
Provisioning: Fix flaky webhook rotation tests racing with reconciler (#123506)

The status merge-patches in TestIntegrationProvisioning_GithubRepoWebhookRecreatedWhenMissing
and TestIntegrationProvisioning_WebhookSecretRotatedWhenExpired occasionally
failed with "secure value not found" when a concurrent reconcile rotated
secure.webhookSecret between the apistore's optimistic read and the resource
server's re-read — canReferenceSecureValues saw the stale name and rejected
the update even though the patch itself never touched secure.

Wrap the patches in EventuallyWithT to retry the transient error, matching
the existing pattern used for spec updates in the same tests.

commit.message:
Alerting: Fix flake TestReceiverTestingService_TestNewReceiverIntegration (#123524)

The default `integration` in the "integration is tested successfully
(receiverUID empty)" subtest was built with `IntegrationGen(WithUID(""))`,
which picks a random integration type. After #123173 added email-address
validation that runs only for `schema.EmailType`, whenever the RNG picked
Email the test's FakeEmailValidator rejected the integration because the
generator's random Name did not match validEmailIntegration's hardcoded
"valid" name, surfacing as 'email address is not allowed'.

Pin the default integration to `schema.SlackType` so it cannot fall into
the email-validation path.

commit.message:
Stat: Fix percent change E2E tests racing panel render (#123548)

The zero-change and NaN percent-change tests asserted toBeHidden() on
directional arrow icons immediately after navigation. toBeHidden() passes
when the element is not attached to the DOM, so the assertions resolved
before the panel rendered — producing a false positive that would not
catch a regression adding an arrow. Wait for the stat panel content to
render before checking arrow absence.

commit.message:
Azure Monitor: Pool gzip writers in Log Analytics deep-link encoder (#123555)

encodeQuery builds the gzip+base64-encoded ChartDefinition segment of
the Azure Portal deep-link embedded in Log Analytics frame metadata. It
allocated a fresh *gzip.Writer (with its ~32 KB flate state) on every
call, even though the writer is discarded immediately after use.

Introduce a package-level sync.Pool of *gzip.Writer and rebind the
output buffer with Reset on each call. Output is byte-identical, no API
change.
