commit.message:
Provisioning: Add selective dashboard export via Resources field (#123381)

* Provisioning: Add selective dashboard export via Resources field

Adds an optional Resources []ResourceRef field to ExportJobOptions so an
export job can target a specific list of dashboards instead of the full
instance. An empty Resources list preserves the existing whole-namespace
export behavior.

The admission validator rejects refs missing Name/Kind, non-Dashboard
kinds, and non-dashboard.grafana.app groups so a misconfigured request
fails fast. The worker resolves each ref via ForKind+Get, reuses the
shared exportItem helper so the conversion shim and UID regeneration
stay in lockstep with the bulk path, and records a per-resource warning
when an explicitly named dashboard is skipped because it is managed by
another repository.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Use constants for dashboard kind/group in selective export

Replaces the string literals "Dashboard" and "dashboard.grafana.app" in
the admission validator and the ExportSpecificResources worker with
package constants so a rename or GVK change only has to land in one
place.

Adds a DashboardResourceKind/DashboardResourceGroup constant pair to the
provisioning API package (apps/provisioning cannot import apps/dashboard
across module boundaries) and a DashboardKind GVK to the existing
pkg/registry/apis/provisioning/resources var block alongside FolderKind.

Also adds admission integration cases for non-Dashboard kind, non-
dashboard group, and missing resource name, plus a worker-path
integration test covering the not-found warning scenario where a present
dashboard is exported while an absent sibling is recorded as a warning.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Expand admission integration cases for selective export

Adds five more push-with-resources validation cases: resource missing
kind, empty ref, index reporting for a mixed valid/invalid list,
lowercase dashboard kind, and LibraryPanel kind. These nail down the
boundary behavior of the new ResourceRef validation so regressions in
the field-path indices or the case-sensitivity of the Dashboard kind
check surface as a test failure rather than a runtime surprise.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Move dashboard kind/group constants into apps/provisioning/pkg/resources

The Dashboard kind and group strings were parked in the v0alpha1 API
package next to ResourceRef as a short-term shim. Promotes them into a
dedicated resources package at apps/provisioning/pkg/resources where
future provisioning-owned resource identifiers can live alongside them.

The typed GVR/GVK vars stay in pkg/registry/apis/provisioning/resources
because they depend on apps/dashboard/apps/folder/apps/iam, which
apps/provisioning does not import. A pointer comment in client.go
documents the intentional split so future readers see why the same
strings appear in both places.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Use typed dashboard GVR/GVK and fail explicit export misses

Pull apps/dashboard into apps/provisioning so apps/provisioning/pkg/resources
can re-derive Dashboard GVR/GVK directly from DashboardResourceInfo instead
of mirroring strings. pkg/registry/apis/provisioning/resources now re-exports
those vars so there is a single source of truth.

When ExportSpecificResources cannot fulfil a caller-named ref — wrong kind,
already managed by another repository, or not found — record the result as
an error rather than a warning so the job surfaces the failure.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Cover v2 stable and v2beta1 in selective export integration test

Extend TestIntegrationProvisioning_ExportSpecificResources to select
dashboards across every supported stored version (v0, v1, v2, v2beta1).
v2alpha1 becomes the non-selected case that proves filtering still
excludes unnamed dashboards.

Add DashboardsV2 to the provisioning test helper and DashboardResourceV2
to apps/provisioning/pkg/resources so the typed GVR is available
alongside the existing v2alpha1 and v2beta1 entries.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Escalate explicit-export failures to job-level error state

jobProgressRecorder.Record silently drops per-resource errors when the
result carries FileActionIgnored (progress.go:94), so the previous
selective-export error paths were local-only and the job finished as
success even when the caller-named dashboard could not be exported.

Clear the action on the explicit-request failure paths (wrong kind,
managed, not-found, get-error) so the recorder counts the error, appends
it to JobStatus.Errors, and escalates the final state to Error. The
bulk-export path keeps the Ignored action since encountering managed or
write-skipped resources there is expected and shouldn't fail the job.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
KV: retry-aware kvListIterator for BatchGet failures (#123197)

* unified-storage: retry-aware KVListIterator for BatchGet failures

The bleve index builder and other ListIterator consumers abort with
a top-level error on any transient BatchGet failure, even when a retry
would recover. Observed under 5% fault-injection on the unified-storage
KV backend:

    err="rpc error: code = Internal desc = error in batch get: readfail: simulated read failure"
    msg="Failed to build index"

kvListIterator and history now transparently recovers:

- Holds ctx, dataStore, the original []DataKey, and a first-occurrence
  keyIdx map for resumption.
- On retryable BatchGet failures (Unavailable / ResourceExhausted /
  Internal) — whether surfaced via the pull's next() or via
  readAndClose on a partially-read value — closes the current pull,
  re-opens dataStore.BatchGet(ctx, keys[currentIdx:]), and continues
  iteration.
- Bounded by maxKvListIteratorConsecutiveFailures (3, resets on
  progress) and maxKvListIteratorTotalAttempts (20) with exponential
  backoff via dskit/backoff.
- Backoff config exposed as a package var so tests can inject fast
  values.

Mid-stream buffering is intentionally kept at the consumer layer
(readAndClose already drains into a byte slice) rather than at the
transport layer — kvGRPC.BatchGet stays a true streaming interface.
A companion change in grafana-enterprise's kvGRPC.BatchGet adds a thin
stream-open retry only.

Tests in storage_backend_list_retry_test.go cover: retryable
Unavailable / Internal mid-stream, non-retryable InvalidArgument
propagation, consecutive-failure budget exhaustion.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* KV: use p.nextIdx instead of keyIdx map

- reduce min/max backoff

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* KV: remove redundant retry checks

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
Search: require BuildVersion when snapshot store is configured (#123503)

Snapshot selection compares against runningBuildVersion, so require it
to be set when the feature is enabled. This lets snapshotTier drop its
nil check on running.

Also drop the m == nil guard in pickBestSnapshot — the store is assumed
to return a non-nil IndexMeta. The unparseable-version hard filter stays
because the store does not (and should not) validate metadata semantics:
different Grafana versions may write different fields.

commit.message:
Provisioning: Compute test base64 PEM at runtime to silence TruffleHog (#123602)

The literal base64-encoded PEM in TestGithubPrivateKeyBase64 triggered
TruffleHog's PrivateKey detector via its base64-decoding pass. The
detector matches against the decoded chunk, where source-line
`trufflehog:ignore` directives cannot reach, so the existing inline
ignore was being bypassed.

Encode from TestGithubPrivateKeyPEM at runtime instead. The output is
byte-identical to the prior literal (trailing newline preserved). The
underlying PEM constant keeps its own ignore directives.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
Combobox: fix onBlur prop being overridden by downshift's getInputProps (#121179)

The `onBlur` prop was passed as a direct prop to `InputComponent`
  before spreading `getInputProps(...)`. Since downshift's `getInputProps`
  always returns its own `onBlur` handler, the spread overwrote the
  consumer's callback, making `onBlur` silently non-functional.

  Fix by passing `onBlur` into `getInputProps()` so that downshift merges
  both handlers via `callAllEventHandlers`.

commit.message:
Provisioning: Surface unmanaged-root collision as a pull job warning (#123598)

* Provisioning: Surface unmanaged-root collision as a pull job warning

When "Delete and keep resources" strips manager annotations from the
root folder and a new repository is created with the same name, the
folder's UID collides with the new repo's RootFolder. The previous
behavior failed FullSync with a bare error, hiding the actual cause
from operators reading pull job output. Return ResourceUnmanagedConflictError
from EnsureFolderExists and record it as a folder-level warning so it
surfaces with ReasonResourceInvalid in the job results.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Add integration test for unmanaged-root-folder conflict

Reproduces the "Delete and keep resources" + reconnect-with-same-name
flow end-to-end against a running Grafana: the release-orphan-resources
finalizer strips manager annotations from the root folder, and a new
folder-target repository created with the same name surfaces the
collision as a per-resource validation warning instead of a hard
failure. Also asserts the orphan is not silently adopted.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
Azure Monitor: Stream-decode responses and typed structs for portal deep link (#123565)

* Azure Monitor: Stream-decode HTTP response bodies

The three unmarshalResponse helpers (metrics, Log Analytics, Resource
Graph) and retrieveSubscriptionDetails all buffered the entire response
body into a []byte via io.ReadAll before decoding. For large Azure
Monitor metric and Log Analytics responses this produces a transient
per-query allocation proportional to response size, held live for the
duration of the decode.

Replace the read+unmarshal pattern with json.NewDecoder(res.Body) so
the decoder streams directly from the response body, and only buffer
the body on non-2xx responses where the bytes are needed for the error
message. UseNumber is preserved on Log Analytics and Resource Graph
responses because downstream converters type-assert cells to
json.Number and fail on any other numeric type.

Error messages no longer embed the raw response body on decode failure;
the HTTP status remains sufficient for diagnosing the common cases
(4xx/5xx are handled separately above, and the decoder's own error
already describes the parse failure site).

* Azure Monitor: Replace map[string]any with typed structs in portal deep link

getQueryUrl assembled the Azure Portal Metrics Explorer deep link by
nesting four map[string]any literals and passing them to json.Marshal.
Reflect-based encoding of map[string]any boxes every value and looks
up keys dynamically on each Marshal call; on a busy query path this
shows up as a measurable allocation cost.

Introduce a small set of unexported typed structs mirroring the Azure
Portal schema (portalTimeContext, portalChartDefinition, portalV2Chart,
portalFilterCollection, portalGrouping) and marshal those directly.
Field order is chosen so the resulting JSON is byte-identical to the
previous map[string]any output - map keys serialise alphabetically, so
the struct fields are declared in alphabetical order where the prior
code relied on that.

The existing round-trip tests in TestAzureMonitorBuildQueries compare
fully expanded expectedPortalURL strings, so any ordering or formatting
drift would be caught immediately.

* Azure Monitor: Address review feedback on stream-decode

Two changes in response to review:

1. retrieveSubscriptionDetails: revert to its prior buffer-then-decode
   pattern. Subscription detail responses are tiny (a few hundred
   bytes), so the per-call allocation savings from streaming this
   particular site are negligible, and keeping the body in the decode
   error message is useful for debugging unexpected response shapes.
   The other three response sites (metrics, Log Analytics, Resource
   Graph) keep streaming.

2. metrics.unmarshalResponse, loganalytics.unmarshalResponse,
   resourcegraph.unmarshalResponse: stop discarding the io.ReadAll
   error in the non-2xx branch. If the body read itself fails, return
   an error that wraps the read failure together with the HTTP status,
   instead of swallowing the read error and surfacing only the status.

commit.message:
IAM/Zanzana: integration tests target the MT reconciler (#123076)

Adds a ZanzanaReconcilerMode option to testinfra and switches the
single-org Zanzana dashboard suite and the folder tree suite onto the MT
reconciler path. The multi-org dashboard cases stay on the legacy
reconciler in a new TestIntegrationDashboardAPIZanzanaCrossOrg suite
because the k8s users API is single-org only.

AwaitZanzanaReconcileNext now branches on the configured reconciler mode
and polls the MT histogram count (status=success) under MT mode,
keeping the legacy timestamp poll otherwise.

testinfra also enables zanzana.server.allow_insecure=true when MT mode
is selected. The MT reconciler's background loop calls Server.Read
without populating an auth identity, which Zanzana's authorizer rejects
unless allow_insecure is set; without it the histogram count never
increments and the reconcile wait times out.

Enterprise compatibility: the MT tests enable KubernetesAuthzRolesApi and
KubernetesAuthzRoleBindingsApi so the Role/RoleBinding kinds are
registered in the scheme, and testinfra wires the bundled enterprise
test license fixture when MT mode runs on an enterprise build. Without
the license the enterprise RBAC storage backends (GlobalRole, Role,
RoleBinding) short-circuit to 'unavailable functionality' and every
reconcile fails. OSS is unaffected (extensions.IsEnterprise=false
skips the license wiring, and the OSS reconciler CRD set omits
Roles/RoleBindings).

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
Lazy transform editors and operators (#122326)

* Dashboard: Lazy-load transformation editors via React.lazy

Rewrite standardTransformers.ts to construct registry items inline with
React.lazy editors instead of importing getXxxTransformRegistryItem functions
from each editor file. This breaks the coupling between registry metadata and
editor components, allowing webpack to code-split all 34 editors into
separate async chunks loaded only when a user opens a transformation editor.

Add Suspense + ErrorBoundary at the Scenes editor render site so lazy-loaded
editors show a loading state and gracefully handle import failures.

Export editor components that were previously file-scoped (OrganizeFields,
FormatString, GroupBy) so React.lazy can import them.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Dashboard: Remove standardTransformers namespace from @grafana/data public API

Remove the standardTransformers export from @grafana/data's index.ts so
the import * in sharedDependencies.ts no longer pulls all 29 transformer
implementations into the plugin-facing shared chunk.

Migrate the 3 core consumers (explore decorators, annotation support,
CalculateFieldTransformerEditor) from direct standardTransformers access
to standardTransformersRegistry.get().

Bump @grafana/scenes and @grafana/scenes-react to canary
7.3.13--canary.1425.24205906579.0 which contains the matching Scenes-side
migration (grafana/scenes#1425).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Dashboard: Lazy-load transformation operators on demand

Change TransformerRegistryItem.transformation from a DataTransformerInfo
value to () => Promise<DataTransformerInfo>. All transformers now use a
resolver function:
- Tier 1 (from @grafana/data): () => Promise.resolve(transformer)
- App-level (12 transforms): () => import('./path').then(m => m.getter())

This removes heavy app-level dependencies (ml-regression, geo/gazetteer,
heatmap calculations) from the initial bundle - they load only when a
panel with that specific transform type renders.

Hoist defaultOptions to TransformerRegistryItem so the editor render site
can access it synchronously without resolving the transformation promise.

Update transformDataFrame's getOperator to resolve the async transformation
within the Observable pipeline, with caching for subsequent calls.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Dashboard: Clean up dead registry item factories from transformer editors

Removes the getXxxTransformRegistryItem() functions from individual
editor files - these are dead code after Phase 1 moved all registration
to standardTransformers.ts. Updates test imports to use @grafana/data/internal
instead of the removed standardTransformers namespace. Adds 3 missing
transformer exports to the internal API surface.

Also removes an accidentally committed .yarn symlink.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Dashboard: Fix remaining TS errors from transformation cleanup

- Remove stale getReduceTransformRegistryItem import in
  transformSceneToSaveModel.test.ts, use mockTransformationsRegistry
- Export reduceTransformer from @grafana/data/internal for test use
- Remove unused GroupByTransformerOptions import

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Dashboard: Review fixes for lazy-loading transformations

- Replace custom ErrorBoundaryWithRetry with ErrorBoundaryAlert from
  @grafana/ui (Faro reporting, no fake retry)
- Use DataTransformerID enum instead of string literals in registry
  lookups
- Clean up stale comment and unnecessary eslint-disable in
  standardTransformers.ts
- Restore isApplicable support in TransformationCard by hoisting
  isApplicable and isApplicableDescription to TransformerRegistryItem,
  with lightweight applicability functions extracted into separate files
  to avoid pulling heavy deps into the initial bundle
- Fix i18n for heatmap isApplicableDescription

commit.message:
unified-storage: watch delay only reported for events emitted after Watch (#123574)

Following up from the investigation done for #122886: in this PR, we start recording the watch delay metric only for events that happened after the Watch stream is created. This avoids reporting very high delays for clients that pass a value for `Since` RV that is old enough to inflate the metrics, but recent enough that the broadcaster still has cached events for it.

The metric is now only tracking the watcher's "reaction" time to track the delay for recently produced events, which should reduce confusing outliers when analyzing metrics.

commit.message:
Restore dashboards: Add Deleted by column and sort to Recently Deleted view (#123364)

* Dashboards: Add Deleted by column and sort to Recently Deleted view

* Dashboards: Test resolveDeletedByDisplayMap helper in trash cache

* Dashboards: Resolve typed numeric user annotations in trash display map

* Dashboards: Avoid leaking RTK Query subscriptions in trash display lookup

* Dashboards: Surface IAM display lookup errors and stabilize RTKQ cache key

* Dashboards: Show "Deleted account" when the deleter was removed

Previously, when a user (or service account, API key, etc.) who deleted a dashboard was themselves deleted, the trash page's "Deleted by" column rendered the raw UID annotation (e.g. `user:5`) because the IAM display endpoint has no entry for deleted identities.

Introduce two sentinel values in the deletedBy display map:

  - DELETED_BY_REMOVED: IAM lookup succeeded for this UID but returned no entry (account deleted)

  - DELETED_BY_UNKNOWN: IAM batch containing this UID failed (network/timeout/server error)

The trash table now renders "Deleted account" and "Unknown account" respectively via formatDeletedByDisplayValue(). The deletedby sort treats both sentinels as missing so rows sort to the end in both directions.

Raw UIDs no longer leak to the UI.

* Dashboards: Chunk IAM display lookup to avoid oversize URLs

resolveDeletedByDisplayMap previously dispatched a single `getDisplayMapping` request with up to 1000 `?key=` query parameters, producing ~27 KB query strings that exceeded nginx's default 8 KB header buffer for large trash pages.

Split UID lookup into batches of IAM_DISPLAY_BATCH_SIZE (200) keys dispatched in parallel via Promise.allSettled so a single failing batch does not blank out every row.

The resolver now owns sentinel ownership: on success it returns a map whose value for every requested UID is one of

  - a real display name (IAM hit)

  - DELETED_BY_REMOVED (successful batch, no entry for this UID)

  - DELETED_BY_UNKNOWN (batch for this UID failed)

Subscriptions are built inside `try` so `finally` always cleans up whatever was created before any synchronous throw. Error messages are routed through getMessageFromError for consistent logging.

* Dashboards: Strengthen deletedby sort tests with Unicode and sentinel coverage

The previous deletedby sort tests covered only ASCII names and a simple "ascending reverses descending" invariant, which is too weak: it would pass even if the sort function ignored Intl.Collator rules.

Add tests that compute expected order from the same `new Intl.Collator()` the production code uses, then assert the sort output matches, for:

  - Diacritic names (e.g. Ëmïlÿ, Öskar)

  - Japanese names

  - Arabic names

Also add a test that verifies both DELETED_BY_REMOVED and DELETED_BY_UNKNOWN sentinel values sort to the end of the result in both ascending and descending directions.

* add class-level cache, remove unknown user

* remove duplicate cache

* simplify

* fix tests

* Search: fall back to DELETED_BY_UNKNOWN instead of raw UID in resourceToSearchResult

resourceToSearchResult is exported and can be called with an incomplete
or undefined display map. Previously it fell back to the raw annotated
UID (e.g. "user:ffkf6bh837z0ga") which would leak into the UI.
Now it falls back to DELETED_BY_UNKNOWN so the UI shows a placeholder
with a warning icon instead of a raw identifier.

* Search: use Trans component instead of t() for deleted-by-unknown label

The label contains an embedded <Icon/> component, so Trans is the
correct i18n primitive — it preserves the JSX tree as indexed
placeholders in the translation string.

Build: Refactor Webpack config to TS (#121181)

* build(webpack): add tsconfig.json for Node strip-types compliance

* build(webpack): extract shared esbuild options to esbuild.ts

* build(webpack): add package.json to declare ESM module type

* build(webpack): convert sass.rule to TypeScript

* build(webpack): convert CorsWorkerPlugin to TypeScript

* build(webpack): convert FeatureFlaggedSriPlugin to TypeScript

* build(webpack): convert webpack.common to TypeScript, add theme entries

* build(webpack): convert webpack.dev to TypeScript, remove esbuild duplication

* build(webpack): convert webpack.prod to TypeScript, remove esbuild duplication

* build(webpack): fix TypeScript types in webpack.prod transform callback

* build(webpack): convert webpack.stats to TypeScript

* build(webpack): update scripts to use TypeScript webpack configs

* build(webpack): simplify env-util to use import.meta.dirname directly

* build(webpack): tidy up plugins

* build(webpack): move rules for ts and sass into single module

* build(webpack): consolidate shared config into common, move splitChunks to prod

- Move MiniCssExtractPlugin, esbuildRule and sassRule into common so both
  dev and prod configs share them without duplication
- Move splitChunks/runtimeChunk optimisation to webpack.prod only (not
  needed in dev)
- Use require() for SubresourceIntegrityPlugin to work around broken ESM
  build (waysact/webpack-subresource-integrity#236)
- Refactor conditional plugin logic in dev from ternary to if-blocks

* build(webpack): remove dead import and clarify webpack destructure pattern

- Remove unused MiniCssExtractPlugin import from webpack.prod (moved to common)
- Add comment explaining why DefinePlugin/EnvironmentPlugin are destructured
  from the default webpack import rather than using named ESM imports

* style(webpack): reorder consts

* chore(env-util): fix up env-util and webpack configs so tests continue to run

* refactor(env-util): accept grafanaRoot param instead of relying on __dirname

Removes the global.__dirname mutation hack in webpack.common.ts by making
the grafana root path an explicit argument to getEnvConfig. Each caller
resolves its own root and passes it in, removing the implicit path-depth
contract and the CJS/ESM compatibility workaround.

* build(webpack): remove unused angular chunk group

commit.message:
Add periodic snapshot upload background task (#123724)

* Add periodic snapshot upload background task

Adds a background goroutine that periodically uploads file-based index snapshots to remote storage, plus upload metrics.

The runner ticks every 5 minutes, checks each open file index against the upload policy, and uploads under the distributed build lock. After a successful upload it advances the persisted mutation baseline by subtracting the value read before the upload, preserving any mutations that arrived during the upload. Upload timing is updated only on success; lock contention and policy skips leave both the timing and mutation count untouched.

Adds index_server_snapshot_uploads_total (success, skip_no_changes, skip_lock_contention, error) and index_server_snapshot_upload_duration_seconds.

* Fix periodic upload to not block eviction or use stale time

The periodic upload scan called getCachedIndex on every open index, which refreshed lastFetchedFromCache and prevented runEvictExpiredOrUnownedIndexes from evicting unowned indexes when the upload tick (5m) is shorter than IndexCacheTTL (default 10m).

Switch the scan to a peekCachedIndex helper that does not refresh the timestamp, and refresh time.Now() per iteration so shouldUpload's interval check is not skewed by long-running uploads earlier in the sweep.

commit.message:
Alerting: Fix 500 on external Alertmanager config GET when upstream returns empty config (#123175)

ExternalAlertmanagerConfig.UnmarshalYAML/UnmarshalJSON left the unexported
amSimple field as nil when the upstream Mimir/Cortex-compat AM returned an
empty, null, or missing alertmanager_config — yaml/json unmarshal on empty
input is a no-op and does not populate the target map. MarshalJSON/YAML
then errored because amSimple == nil, returning a 500 on
GET /api/alertmanager/{dsUID}/config/api/v1/alerts and blocking customers
from creating contact points on freshly provisioned stacks where no AM
config has ever been saved upstream.

Initialize amSimple to an empty map if still nil after unmarshal so
legitimately empty upstream configs round-trip, while preserving the
Marshal nil-check that catches zero-value structs that were never decoded.

Regression from #121484.

commit.message:
Folders: Make GetDescendants scale with subtree size, not org size (#123663)

* Folders: Make GetDescendants scale with subtree size, not org size

Replace FolderUnifiedStoreImpl.GetDescendants so it walks the subtree
level by level via k8sclient.Search instead of listing every folder in
the org and recursing in memory.

GetChildren is split into the existing public method (which keeps the
parent-existence check) and a new private searchChildren helper. The
new walk uses searchChildren so it doesn't re-validate nodes it just
discovered.

Cost scales with the size of the subtree (1 Get + (subtreeSize + 1)
Search) rather than the total folder count. The sole production caller
is Service.Delete, which uses only the UID and ParentUID fields.

Returned folders are now minimal (UID, ID, OrgID, ParentUID, Title,
ManagedBy). Documented on the function. The traversal is bounded by
ss.maxDepth, mirroring GetHeight's loop shape.

* Address comment.

* go fmt

* Ignore ref.ID linter check.

* Folders: Batch parents in GetDescendants Search calls

Replace one Search per parent with one Search per group of up to 100
parents using a multi-value `In` filter on the folder field. Total
calls per GetDescendants drop from O(subtree size) to roughly
O(subtree size / 100), which is enough to make GetDescendants strictly
faster than the previous List-all-and-walk-in-memory approach across
all subtree sizes — removes the very-large-subtree regression noted in
the function doc comment.

Also moves pagination inside searchChildren itself: each Search call
fetches at most searchPageSize=10000 hits per round-trip and loops
until the requested slice is exhausted. This keeps every gRPC response
well under the default 4 MiB max message size, regardless of fan-out.
GetChildren benefits too: previously, a folder with more than ~40k
direct children would have returned a ResourceExhausted error.

searchChildren now takes parents as []string (one path serves both
GetChildren with []string{q.UID} and GetDescendants with chunked
batches), and drops the legacy-search post-filter and the obsolete
`Page` field on the request — folders are served exclusively by the
unified bleve backend (#121806), which honours Offset and ignores
Page.

* Folders: Address review feedback on GetDescendants

Split the merged searchChildren back into two:

- GetChildren (public, user-facing) builds its own request inline and
  performs a single Search call. The k6 visibility filter and the
  caller-controlled q.Limit/q.Page semantics live here.

- searchChildren (internal, used only by GetDescendants) does no
  filtering and paginates to exhaustion. Each round-trip is bounded by
  searchPageSize hits to stay under the 4 MiB gRPC max receive size.

A small doSearchPage helper does the shared 'one Search round-trip,
parse, map' work for both.

This addresses three review concerns:

1. GetDescendants no longer silently truncates wide levels at
   folderSearchLimit. searchChildren paginates until the search backend
   has returned every match.

2. Hitting the depth cap with descendants still queued returns
   ErrMaximumDepthReached instead of logging a warning and returning a
   partial subtree (which could let Service.Delete leave orphans
   behind). Genuine cycles are still caught earlier by the visited
   check, so this branch only fires for trees deeper than maxDepth.

3. GetDescendants no longer inherits the public k6-folder visibility
   filter. The filter is a UI concern for end-user folder listings, not
   an internal-traversal concern; in practice k6 only lives at the root
   so the filter never excluded anything from a real subtree walk
   anyway.

* Folders: Tighten searchChildren tests

Add coverage for two GetDescendants/searchChildren behaviours that were
asked about in review:

1. Level-2 chunking when a level has more parents than
   descendantsBatchSize. Builds 150 root children and asserts the walk
   issues two batched Search calls with 100 + 50 parent slices.

2. Inner page-loop pagination when a single batched Search returns more
   than searchPageSize hits. Builds searchPageSize+1 children at one
   level and asserts two Search round-trips at offsets 0 and
   searchPageSize.

Also tighten the expectSearchChildren matcher to require exactly one
Fields entry on the request \u2014 the internal searchChildren path applies
no visibility filters, so any extra entry is a regression.

* Folders: Update GetDescendants doc comment for ErrMaximumDepthReached

The doc comment still described the original 'log a warning and return
the partial result' behaviour. Update to match the implementation
(returns ErrMaximumDepthReached when the depth cap is hit with items
still queued).

discovered.

Cost scales with the size of the subtree (1 Get + (subtreeSize + 1)
Search) rather than the total folder count. The sole production caller
is Service.Delete, which uses only the UID and ParentUID fields.

Returned folders are now minimal (UID, ID, OrgID, ParentUID, Title,
ManagedBy). Documented on the function. The traversal is bounded by
ss.maxDepth, mirroring GetHeight's loop shape.

* Address comment.

* go fmt

* Ignore ref.ID linter check.

* Folders: Batch parents in GetDescendants Search calls

Replace one Search per parent with one Search per group of up to 100
parents using a multi-value `In` filter on the folder field. Total
calls per GetDescendants drop from O(subtree size) to roughly
O(subtree size / 100), which is enough to make GetDescendants strictly
faster than the previous List-all-and-walk-in-memory approach across
all subtree sizes — removes the very-large-subtree regression noted in
the function doc comment.

Also moves pagination inside searchChildren itself: each Search call
fetches at most searchPageSize=10000 hits per round-trip and loops
until the requested slice is exhausted. This keeps every gRPC response
well under the default 4 MiB max message size, regardless of fan-out.
GetChildren benefits too: previously, a folder with more than ~40k
direct children would have returned a ResourceExhausted error.

searchChildren now takes parents as []string (one path serves both
GetChildren with []string{q.UID} and GetDescendants with chunked
batches), and drops the legacy-search post-filter and the obsolete
`Page` field on the request — folders are served exclusively by the
unified bleve backend (#121806), which honours Offset and ignores
Page.

* Folders: Address review feedback on GetDescendants

Split the merged searchChildren back into two:

- GetChildren (public, user-facing) builds its own request inline and
  performs a single Search call. The k6 visibility filter and the
  caller-controlled q.Limit/q.Page semantics live here.

- searchChildren (internal, used only by GetDescendants) does no
  filtering and paginates to exhaustion. Each round-trip is bounded by
  searchPageSize hits to stay under the 4 MiB gRPC max receive size.

A small doSearchPage helper does the shared 'one Search round-trip,
parse, map' work for both.

This addresses three review concerns:

1. GetDescendants no longer silently truncates wide levels at
   folderSearchLimit. searchChildren paginates until the search backend
   has returned every match.

2. Hitting the depth cap with descendants still queued returns
   ErrMaximumDepthReached instead of logging a warning and returning a
   partial subtree (which could let Service.Delete leave orphans
   behind). Genuine cycles are still caught earlier by the visited
   check, so this branch only fires for trees deeper than maxDepth.

3. GetDescendants no longer inherits the public k6-folder visibility
   filter. The filter is a UI concern for end-user folder listings, not
   an internal-traversal concern; in practice k6 only lives at the root
   so the filter never excluded anything from a real subtree walk
   anyway.

* Folders: Tighten searchChildren tests

Add coverage for two GetDescendants/searchChildren behaviours that were
asked about in review:

1. Level-2 chunking when a level has more parents than
   descendantsBatchSize. Builds 150 root children and asserts the walk
   issues two batched Search calls with 100 + 50 parent slices.

2. Inner page-loop pagination when a single batched Search returns more
   than searchPageSize hits. Builds searchPageSize+1 children at one
   level and asserts two Search round-trips at offsets 0 and
   searchPageSize.

Also tighten the expectSearchChildren matcher to require exactly one
Fields entry on the request \u2014 the internal searchChildren path applies
no visibility filters, so any extra entry is a regression.

* Folders: Update GetDescendants doc comment for ErrMaximumDepthReached

The doc comment still described the original 'log a warning and return
the partial result' behaviour. Update to match the implementation
(returns ErrMaximumDepthReached when the depth cap is hit with items
still queued).

commit.message:
Folder: Wrap validation errors in metav1.Status (#123709)

* Folder: Wrap validation errors in metav1.Status

The folder admission validator returned bare errors that the k8s apiserver
could not convert to a structured response, surfacing them as "Unhandled
Error" 500s instead of proper 4xx responses (alert #1782995). The bulk of
the SLO budget burn came from the max-depth check; the same pattern also
affected invalid-uid, title-empty, parent-of-itself, and cyclic-reference.

Wrap each one with errutil so they implement the APIStatus interface and
the apiserver renders them as structured 4xx. The legacy /api routes keep
their original errors.New sentinels and unchanged err.Error() strings;
new ErrAPIxxx variants in pkg/services/folder/model.go are pre-wrapped via
%w so errors.Is keeps matching the legacy sentinels for the existing
ToFolderErrorResponse handler.

Also moved the cyclic-reference sentinel from a local var in parents.go
into model.go for consistency, and retyped TestValidateCreate.expectedErr
from substring to typed error so assertions go through errors.Is.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Folder: Integration test for max-depth returning 400 not 500

Boots the folder apiserver via apis.NewK8sTestHelper, creates the
maximum allowed nesting (default depth 4), then attempts one more
folder and asserts the response is HTTP 400 BadRequest, not 500
InternalError. Guards the regression that fired alert #1782995.

Note: placed in pkg/tests/apis/folder/ rather than provisioning
because the bug is in the folder apiserver itself; provisioning is
just one of many consumers of that error path.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Folder: Assert exact error message format for max-depth in integration test

Provisioning and external observability tooling consume the message
returned by the apiserver. Pin the full string ("[folder.maximum-depth-reached]
folder max depth exceeded, max depth is 4") so any change to the messageID
or the depth log message format fails this test.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Folder: gofmt fix

* Folder: add validation tests for other scenarios
- title-empty, invalid-uid, cannot-be-parent-of-itself
- fix TestIntegrationFoldersCreateAPIEndpointK8S

commit.message:
Provisioning: Return test results instead of HTTP 500 when GetDefaultBranch fails (#123725)

Provisioning: Surface GetDefaultBranch failures via TestResults instead of HTTP 500

When the test endpoint built a temporary GitHub repository whose branch was empty,
a failure in GetDefaultBranch (e.g. GitHub returning 404 for an unreachable repo or
401/403 for a token without access) propagated as a Go error and was returned to the
client as "failed to get repository metadata: file not found" with HTTP 500. This is
the onboarding entry point, so the user has no way to act on the message.

Classify the underlying repository error and return a TestResults with a
field-targeted ErrorDetails, mirroring the existing URL-parse and branch-protection
handling. The connector remains responsible for serializing the result.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Provisioning: Folder max depth problems should be surface as warnings (#123726)

* bug: folder too depth problems should be a job warning

* bug: add integration test for max depth and other integration test

* Provisioning: Detect folder depth violations on Update/move path

The previous matcher only recognized the Create-path error string
("folder max depth exceeded"). Folder move/update validation in
pkg/registry/apis/folders/validate.go returns folder.ErrMaximumDepthReached
("Maximum nested folder depth reached"), so a managed folder being moved
deeper than the limit surfaced as a hard error and triggered the same
retry loop the warning was meant to prevent.

Broaden detection to also match the structured errutil sentinel, the K8s
status details message ID, and the public-message substring. Apply the
same FolderDepthExceededError wrapping on the Update path of
EnsureFolderExists so moves into too-deep paths are surfaced as warnings
too.

Unified Storage: Vector storage db setup and migrations (#122751)

* feat(unified-storage): add vector-storage database config section

* feat(unified-storage): add VectorBackend interface and types

* feat(unified-storage): add pgvector schema DDL and init

* feat(unified-storage): add vector SQL templates and request structs

Add 5 SQL template files (upsert, delete, search, get_latest_rv,
create_partition) and queries.go with typed request/response structs
following the sqltemplate pattern used in unified storage.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(unified-storage): add vector SQL template snapshot tests

Add snapshot tests for all 5 SQL templates (upsert, delete, search,
get_latest_rv, create_partition) using PostgreSQL dialect only via the
mocks.CheckQuerySnapshots framework.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(unified-storage): add pgvectorBackend implementation

Implements the VectorBackend interface using pgvector-go for half-vector
similarity search, the Grafana db.DB/db.Tx abstractions for dbutil
compatibility, and a sync.Map partition cache for idempotent DDL.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(unified-storage): add pgvectorBackend unit tests

Tests cover sanitizePartitionName, Upsert no-op with empty/nil slice,
Delete (all and stale), and GetLatestRV (value and no-rows cases)
using the existing sqlmock test infrastructure.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor(unified-storage): make vector search metadata filters generic

Replace hardcoded datasource_uids/query_languages filters with a generic
MetadataFilterEntry that works for any JSONB key. The SQL template now
uses {{ range .MetadataFilters }} instead of dashboard-specific conditionals.

* refactor(unified-storage): use migrator pattern for vector schema

Replace raw schema.sql DDL with Grafana's migrator pattern (same as
MigrateResourceStore). Each DDL statement is a tracked migration against
the separate vector database, enabling incremental schema evolution.

* devenv: add pgvector docker block for vector search integration tests

PostgreSQL with pgvector extension on port 5433. Usage:
  make devenv sources=pgvector

* feat(unified-storage): add vector database provider wiring

ProvideVectorBackend connects [database_vector] config to a working
pgvectorBackend: builds connection string, creates xorm engine, runs
migrations, wraps as db.DB. Returns (nil, nil) if not configured.

* test(unified-storage): add pgvector integration tests

Tests run against real PostgreSQL+pgvector via devenv block:
  make devenv sources=pgvector
  PGVECTOR_TEST_DB="..." go test -run TestIntegration ...

Covers: upsert, search with filters, GetLatestRV, delete stale,
upsert overwrite. Skips when PGVECTOR_TEST_DB is not set.

* chore: remove planning docs from repo

* chore: remove trivial vector config tests

* get tests passing

* partition on namespace + model so we dont mix embeddings

* wire up VectorBackend and feature flag

* fix wiring

* gofmt and provider func name change

* docs: spec for tenant watcher/deleter tracing

Performance-oriented tracing design: spans around labelling and
deletion to identify slow tenants/group-resources.

* chore: remove superpowers spec accidentally merged from local main

The docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-20-tenant-tracing-design.md was
committed to local main and came along during a merge-back into this
branch. Per repo convention, superpowers planning docs stay outside
the repo.

* gofmt

* fix codeowners for pgvector docker block

* fix CI make gen-apps

* make update-workspace

* fix bad comment and modowners

* fix linter errors

* rename ff to vector_backend

* shard by table. Create tables on write. Remove rv dep for embeddings and track it globally in one table until we have a persistent queue

* use halfvec(1024) for embeddings to match what GA uses. Fix some comments.

* add some vector validation

* gofmt

* update partitioning strategy... again. One table per resource, tenants with many resources get their own dedicated partition created dynamically that has hnsw index, all other tenants share a single partition with no hnsw index

* add gin index to metadata when creating new partition

* move promoter into vector backend

* make gen-jsonnet

* use partitioning for resource tables instead. Makes things simpler and makes cross resource search easier

* remove top level default partition - not used

Provisioning: Add commitMessageTemplate field to Repository spec (#123166)

* Provisioning: Add commitMessageTemplate field to Repository spec

Adds an optional `commitMessageTemplate` field to the RepositorySpec and
the RepositoryView so that provisioned-resource save flows can pre-populate
the commit/comment field from a per-repo template (e.g. conventional commits).

The template supports three variables — {{action}} (create/update/delete/
move/rename), {{resource}} (dashboard/folder), and {{title}} — which the
frontend interpolates at save time. When the field is empty, existing
hardcoded fallback messages ("Save dashboard: <title>", etc.) continue to
apply, so current behaviour is preserved.

Frontend wiring lives in a follow-up PR.

commit.message:
Provisioning: Add raw .md read support to the files API (#123744)

Lets the provisioning files API serve README.md (and other raw markdown)
from a Git Sync repository without trying to parse it as a Kubernetes
resource. Authorization is folder-scoped: callers need folders:get on
the file's containing folder, mirroring how parsed-resource reads
inherit folder permissions.

- IsReadablePath / IsRawFile helpers separate read-only extensions from
  the parseable resource extensions.
- handleGet short-circuits raw files to handleGetRawFile, which auths
  via the new Authorizer.AuthorizeReadRawFile and returns the bytes
  under resource.file.content.
- Write operations on .md (POST/PUT/DELETE) remain rejected with 400.

Companion frontend PR will gate the actual UI behind a feature toggle.

commit.message:
Storage: make badgerKV Keys/BatchGet/BatchDelete honor ctx cancellation (#123748)

* Storage: make badgerKV Keys/BatchGet/BatchDelete honor ctx cancellation

The ctx parameter on these methods was effectively unused for cancellation:
the iter.Seq2 closures and the BatchDelete loop ran to completion regardless
of cancellation, so cancelling a gRPC stream context did not actually stop
the badger scan.

This contributed to a TestKVGRPC flake where GracefulStop had nothing to
drain quickly, fell back to Stop() after its 5s timeout, and the still-
running handler raced db.Close() panicking inside NewIterator.

Failing run: https://github.com/grafana/grafana/actions/runs/25041595286/job/73345999559
Earlier test-only fix: https://github.com/grafana/grafana-enterprise/pull/11798

* Storage: add TestBadgerKV_ContextCancellation

Covers Keys, BatchGet, and BatchDelete with both pre-cancelled ctx and
mid-iteration cancellation. Also documents the deliberate empty-keys
no-op behavior of BatchDelete and guards errors.Is(context.Canceled)
for callers like the kvGRPC retry logic.

commit.message:
Alerting: Surface save and bulk-delete errors to the user (#123690)

Two destructive operations were silently swallowing errors, leaving the UI in an inconsistent state with no actionable feedback:

  - AlertRuleForm.submit awaited the upsert hooks but never validated the
    result. With useAsync swallowing rejections, a failed save produced
    no toast and the form fell through to a silent logWarning. The
    submit body is now wrapped in try/catch and a "Failed to save alert
    rule" notification is surfaced via getMessageFromError before
    returning early, so redirectToDetailsPage only runs on a real
    response.

  - DeleteModal's catch block called only trackFolderBulkActionsDeleteFail,
    so the modal stayed open with no error UI after a failed bulk delete.
    It now surfaces a notifyApp.error and dismisses the modal, mirroring
    the PauseUnpauseActionMenuItem precedent in the same folder.

commit.message:
Add background cleanup of obsolete remote index snapshots (#123796)

* Add background cleanup of obsolete remote index snapshots

Run a periodic per-namespace cleanup pass that deletes obsolete remote
index snapshots and stale partial uploads, so the snapshot bucket
doesn't grow unboundedly as #123745's primitives accumulate uploads.

The cleanup loop is started from NewBleveBackend alongside the existing
upload goroutine when Snapshot.Store is configured and CleanupInterval
is positive. The first run is jittered uniformly in [0, CleanupInterval)
to spread listings across replicas deployed together; subsequent runs
fire on a fixed ticker. Each pass:

- lists namespaces, randomises order, then per namespace:
- filters by ownership via ownsIndexFn (namespace-level only — Group and
  Resource are intentionally empty, matching the production OwnsIndex
  contract);
- acquires the namespace cleanup lock (distinct key from the build lock
  so cleanup never blocks uploads);
- ties a per-namespace context to the lock via context.WithCancelCause
  so a lost lock cancels in-flight bucket calls immediately rather than
  waiting for the next resource boundary;
- applies the retention rules (rule A: age cutoff at MaxIndexAge,
  rule B: per-Grafana-version-group, keep newest, delete predecessors
  once newest is past CleanupGracePeriod), and sweeps incomplete
  uploads.

Snapshot metrics (downloads, uploads, cleanups, deleted) are now
zero-initialised in NewBleveBackend rather than ProvideIndexMetrics, so
instances that never enable the snapshot feature don't emit
permanently-zero `index_server_snapshot_*` series.

Part of grafana/search-and-storage-team#722.

* Address review comments

- Drop "per namespace" from index_server_snapshot_cleanups_total help
  (it's only labelled by status).
- Record incomplete-upload metric counts before returning the error from
  CleanupIncompleteUploads, so a partial run with a transient error
  still reflects the deletes that did succeed.
- Drop the duplicated CleanupInterval > 0 guard inside
  cleanupSnapshotsPeriodically; the only caller (NewBleveBackend)
  already gates on it.
- Fix typo in cross-reference comment to
  TestRunCleanup_OwnershipFilter_NamespaceLevel.
- Extract v.String() to a local in selectSnapshotsToDelete grouping.
- Clarify the test comment in
  TestSelectSnapshotsToDelete_NewestInGroupAlwaysKept that overriding
  UploadTimestamp makes keys[4] the oldest, not the newest \u2014 the test
  still asserts the right thing because RV-desc beats UploadTimestamp-desc
  in the per-group sort.

* Surface per-snapshot delete failures and split deleted metric

Per-snapshot DeleteIndex failures inside runResourceCleanup are now
recorded under index_server_snapshot_deleted_total{outcome="error"}
and surfaced as a non-canceled error so the namespace-level cleanup
status flips to "error" instead of being recorded as "success".

Treat CleanupIncompleteUploads errors symmetrically: log a warning,
keep going, aggregate the failure into the resource's return value
via errors.Join, instead of short-circuiting the resource.

Split index_server_snapshot_deleted_total into two metrics so the
labels are orthogonal:

- index_server_snapshot_deleted_total{outcome="success|error"} \u2014
  full snapshot delete attempts only.
- index_server_snapshot_incomplete_uploads_cleaned_total \u2014 plain
  counter, one increment per partial-upload prefix removed by
  CleanupIncompleteUploads (no error series by construction).

Rename to clarify aggregation level:

- IndexSnapshotCleanups \u2192 IndexSnapshotNamespaceCleanups
- index_server_snapshot_cleanups_total \u2192
  index_server_snapshot_namespace_cleanups_total
- recordSnapshotCleanupStatus \u2192 recordSnapshotNamespaceCleanupStatus
- snapshotCleanupStatus* \u2192 snapshotNamespaceCleanupStatus*

The metric is incremented once per (namespace, outcome) tuple per
cleanup pass; the new names make that scope explicit at the call site
and on the wire, since there's no namespace label.

Also drop two stale TODOs on RemoteIndexStore.UploadIndex and
CleanupIncompleteUploads in favour of doc comments stating the lock
contract callers are expected to hold.

* Address test review comments

Replace defensive vacuous-pass branch in
TestSelectSnapshotsToDelete_NeverDeletesDownloadPick with
require.True(ok). None of the current cases produce no-pick, so the
fall-through was dead code that would silently bypass the
cross-check assertion if a future case ever did.

Simplify the TestRunCleanup_ReplicaVersionAgnostic doc comment per
review suggestion.

* Fix typo.

commit.message:
Restore dashboards: Separate localStorage keys for main-page and recently-deleted sort (#123675)

* fix: separate localStorage keys for main and recently-deleted sort
The main dashboards page and recently-deleted page shared one
localStorage key (grafana.search.sort) but use mutually exclusive
sort vocabularies. Picking a sort on the recently-deleted page would
persist a value the main page's SortPicker couldn't recognise,
leaving the main page in an unexpected list view with no sort displayed.
Changes:
- Add SEARCH_SELECTED_SORT_DELETED and RECENTLY_DELETED_SORT_VALUES
  constants to constants.ts (single source of truth for the
  recently-deleted vocabulary).
- Make SearchStateManager.sortStorageKey a protected overridable
  property (defaults to SEARCH_SELECTED_SORT). Replace the four
  direct SEARCH_SELECTED_SORT references inside initStateFromUrl,
  setStateAndDoSearch, and onSortChange with this.sortStorageKey.
- Add a one-time stale-value guard in initStateFromUrl: when running
  as the main-page manager (sortStorageKey === SEARCH_SELECTED_SORT),
  if the persisted value is in the recently-deleted vocabulary it is
  cleared from localStorage so legacy pollution is cleaned up on
  first visit.
- Override sortStorageKey = SEARCH_SELECTED_SORT_DELETED in
  TrashStateManager so its sort is persisted to a separate key and
  never bleeds into main-page state.
- Use store.get/set/delete from @grafana/data for all new
  localStorage accesses (satisfies @grafana/no-direct-local-storage-access).
- Update eslint-suppressions.json to reflect fewer violations in
  SearchStateManager.ts.
Tests:
- New useRecentlyDeletedStateManager.test.ts: verifies TrashStateManager
  writes to the recently-deleted key and not the main key.
- Extended SearchStateManager.test.ts: verifies stale recently-deleted
  values are cleared, and valid main-page values are preserved.

Co-authored-by: Cursor Agent <cursoragent@cursor.com>

* fix: remove type assertion from jest.spyOn in test

Co-authored-by: Cursor Agent <cursoragent@cursor.com>

* style: fix prettier formatting in test files

Co-authored-by: Alex Khomenko <Clarity-89@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix: isolate recently-deleted layout from main browse layout

- Add SEARCH_SELECTED_LAYOUT_DELETED and override layoutStorageKey in TrashStateManager so sort on trash does not set grafana.search.layout for dashboards.
- Persist main/trash layout via store API instead of direct localStorage; rename helper to getMainLayoutFromStore.
- Remove obsolete eslint suppressions for SearchStateManager.
- Extend tests for layout key isolation.

* fix: read persisted layout from layoutStorageKey in initStateFromUrl

TrashStateManager was calling getMainLayoutFromStore() which always used
the main page key, so folder layout on dashboards discarded trash sort on init.

- Add protected getPersistedLayout() using this.layoutStorageKey
- Use it in initStateFromUrl; keep getMainLayoutFromStore for getSearchStateManager
- Tests for trash vs main layout key behavior

* refactor: consolidate getLayoutFromStore helper

Replace getMainLayoutFromStore and getPersistedLayout with a single
getLayoutFromStore(key); drop redundant : string on protected keys.

* test: use search constants in SearchStateManager tests

Use RECENTLY_DELETED_SORT_VALUES and SEARCH_SELECTED_LAYOUT in stale-sort guard tests per review feedback.

---------

Co-authored-by: Cursor Agent <cursoragent@cursor.com>

commit.message:
Search: scale retry budget for streaming index builds (#123830)

* unified-storage: scale retry budget for streaming index builds

The hardcoded 10-failure cap in the BatchGet retry pull aborts a 1M-row
index build at ~1% in under realistic transient KV noise (5% read
failure rate). Replace the constants with a BatchGetRetryPolicy whose
total budget scales as max(floor, rate * len(keys)).

Two policies are hardcoded:
- defaultBatchGetRetryPolicy for sync list/history/trash paths keeps
  the legacy small budget so a stuck KV surfaces as a quick error.
- defaultRebuildBatchGetRetryPolicy absorbs ~5% noise on million-key
  rebuilds with 2x headroom.

Callers opt into the rebuild budget via WithIndexBuildRetryBudget(ctx).
Only init (buildIndexes) and the background rebuilder
(runIndexRebuilder) opt in; getOrCreateIndex deliberately does not, so
a flaky build at request time can't stall search requests for hours
under context.WithoutCancel.

Add tests pinning ctx propagation through the init and request-time
paths, plus the policy math.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* unified-storage: scale retry budget by BatchGet chunks, not raw keys

The total-failures counter increments per retryable BatchGet/stream
error, which is a chunk-level event (50 keys per chunk by default), but
totalBudget was scaling by raw key count. For 1M keys with rate 0.10
that produced a 100k budget against ~20k first-pass chunks — under the
500ms minimum backoff an unhealthy KV could keep a rebuild running for
many hours before exhausting it.

Divide numKeys by dataBatchSize inside totalBudget so the unit matches.
1M keys at rate 0.10 now yields a budget of 2000 (vs. 100000), bounding
the worst case to ~17 minutes while keeping 2x headroom over the
expected ~1000 chunk failures at 5% noise.

Tests updated to use the new chunk-based math.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
Dashboards: Tighten panel ID types in v2 schema to integers (#123139)

* Dashboards: Tighten panel ID types in v2 schema to integers

Change `PanelSpec.id`, `LibraryPanelKindSpec.id`, and `AnnotationPanelFilter.ids`
from CUE `number`/`uint32` to `uint16` across v2alpha1, v2beta1, and v2.

Why: kube-openapi maps `uint32` to `format: int64`, and CUE `number` to
`type: number, format: double`. Consumer codegens that follow the int64-as-string
convention (to avoid JS precision loss past 2^53) then serialise panel IDs as
strings, breaking wire compatibility with Grafana's typed Go decoders. Panel IDs
are integers in practice and always have been; `uint16` narrows the advertised
range to match reality and renders cleanly as `format: int32` in OpenAPI.

Fixes grafana/hyperion-planning#588.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Dashboards: Widen v2 panel ID types from uint16 to int32 & >=0

uint16 caps panel IDs at 65,535. Fine for UI-created dashboards,
but dashboards-as-code (Terraform, jsonnet, k8s controllers) can
emit timestamps or arbitrary numerics as IDs. The v1 -> v2alpha1
converter then silently drops those.

uint16 also leaves a contract mismatch: CUE uint16 emits
format: int32 in OpenAPI, so the wire spec advertises int32 range
while the Go decoder rejects anything > 65535. Same class of
loose-contract bug as the original int64-with-string issue, just
inverted.

int32 & >=0 emits the same OpenAPI shape (format: int32, no
string coercion), widens the range to ~2.1B, and aligns the Go
runtime exactly with the wire. Migration silent-drop path tightened
to MaxInt32 -- unreachable in practice.

Per @kristinademeshchik's review on the original PR.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Dashboards: regen v2 OpenAPI snapshots and gofmt codegen

Two CI-driven fixups for the int32 schema change:

- OpenAPI v2 stable: regenerate dashboard.grafana.app-v2.json
  (snapshot + package mirror). Previous commit only updated the
  v2alpha1 / v2beta1 specs because the wrong gen entrypoint was
  used; CI's "Verify OpenAPI specs" caught the v2 stable drift.

- gofmt: drop stray blank lines from v0alpha1 / v1
  dashboard_object_gen.go. They were introduced by running
  `make generate` from apps/dashboard instead of the canonical
  `make gen-apps` from repo root, which CI uses.

Folder: Wrap remaining validation errors in metav1.Status (#123843)

* Folder: Wrap remaining validation errors in metav1.Status (follow-up)

Continues #123709 by extending APIStatus coverage to the remaining folder
admission validator paths that surfaced as 500 in production:

- Dashboard UID errors: validate.go now returns ErrAPIInvalidUID/ErrAPIUIDTooLong
  (errutil wrappers around the legacy dashboards sentinels) so they implement
  APIStatus and render as 400 instead of "Unhandled Error" 500.
- ErrNameExists: both call sites use .Errorf(...) so the apiserver gets an
  APIStatus error instead of a raw Base value.
- New ErrFolderCannotBeMovedToK6 for the k6 move rejection.
- ErrCircularReference reused for the move-under-descendant case.

ToFolderStatusError now copies errutil.Error.Status().Details into the
returned metav1.Status so downstream consumers can match on the structured
messageID via Status.Details.UID without parsing the human message.

ToFolderErrorResponse: dashboard branch only strips the errutil prefix when
the chain contains an errutil.Error AND the underlying matches one of
stableDashboardErrSentinels — keeps legacy /api/folders messages
byte-stable without dropping custom context from non-errutil callers.

Tests: TestIntegrationFolderValidationReturns400 is now a 9-row table
covering all create + update validation paths, each asserting Code=400,
exact message, and the messageID via Status.Details.UID.
doCreateCircularReferenceFolderTest fixed (broken JSON was silently
passing) and extended with a create-then-move circular flow.
TestToFolderErrorResponse moved to apierrors_test package so it can
reference the production folders.ErrAPI* wrappers directly.

commit.message:
Provisioning: Surface folder uid-too-long and other validation 4xx as sync warnings (#123797)

* Provisioning: Surface folder uid-too-long as a sync warning

When the folder API rejects a write because the UID exceeds 40
characters, provisioning treats it as a retryable hard error today and
the sync job is requeued every 5 minutes — the same retry-loop bug that
#123726 fixed for max-depth violations, just for a different validation
rule. Path-derived UIDs always fit (resources.appendHashSuffix
truncates to 40), so the rejection only fires when _folder.json declares
a stable UID over the limit; the user must fix the repository, not wait
for a retry.

Mirror the FolderDepthExceeded pattern: ErrFolderUIDTooLong sentinel,
FolderUIDTooLongError type, IsFolderUIDTooLongAPIError matcher (sentinel
+ Status.Details.UID == "folder.uid-too-long" + substring fallback for
the pre-fix legacy 500 form and the post-fix bracketed message-id form).
EnsureFolderExists wraps the rejection on both Create and Update/move
paths. classifyWarning maps it to the new ReasonFolderUIDTooLong, so
the sync surfaces as a warning instead of an error and downstream
resources under the offending folder are short-circuited via the
existing failedCreations machinery.

Integration test in pkg/tests/apis/provisioning/foldermetadata/
(env has folder metadata enabled) writes _folder.json with a 41-char
UID, runs a pull job, asserts JobStateWarning, no errors, exactly one
uid-too-long warning, the dashboard under the bad folder is silently
skipped, the shallow folder still gets created, condition reason is
CompletedWithWarnings, and a re-run reproduces the same warning state
without state corruption.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Surface generic folder validation 4xx as a sync warning

Extends the depth-exceeded and uid-too-long handling to cover any
folder-API validation rejection the more specific matchers don't claim
(illegal-uid-chars, reserved-uid, future folder validations). Same
retry-loop bug, same fix shape: typed warning, generic reason.

resources.IsFolderValidationAPIError matches anything a depth or
uid-too-long check would catch, plus any K8s StatusError whose code is
400 and whose Status.Details.UID has the "folder." messageID prefix.
That covers every existing folder errutil sentinel post-#123709 and any

commit.message:
Provisioning: Retry SQLITE_BUSY on repository status patch (#123873)

Provisioning: Retry SQLITE_BUSY on repo status patch

The repository status patcher only retried K8s optimistic-concurrency
conflicts. When the unified storage SQL backend bubbles a transient
SQLITE_BUSY through the apiserver (as a 500 InternalError carrying the
"database is locked"/"SQLITE_BUSY" text), the patch failed instead of
retrying. This surfaced as flakes such as
TestIntegrationProvisioning_FullSync_FolderMetadataTitle on the SQLite
shards.

Switch to retry.OnError with a predicate that retries both K8s conflicts
and SQLite lock contention, and add a unit test for the new path.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
Provisioning: Per-verb fallback for the files subresource (#123867)

The files connector handles GET/POST/PUT/DELETE in a single place but was
wired with a single static fallback role (accessWithAdmin), so any role
fallback was wrong for at least one verb family — reads should fall back
to Viewer, writes to Editor; an Admin-only fallback over-restricts both.

Introduce auth.NewVerbAwareAccessChecker(read, write AccessChecker) which
dispatches Check by req.Verb (get/list/watch -> read, everything else ->
write), and compose accessWithViewer + accessWithEditor for the files
connector. Inner checkers retain their fallback configuration; the
wrapper's WithFallbackRole is intentionally a no-op (per-verb fallbacks
are decided at construction).

This does not by itself resolve the customer regression where MT-side
authz denies dashboards:create for Editors on non-General folders — that
denial originates in the MT authz service and the role fallback is a
no-op in token mode regardless. Filed separately for the I&A team. This
PR removes the static-fallback-role footgun on the files connector so
the eventual MT fix surfaces correctly here.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
Provisioning: Fix flaky folder-count assertion in quota sync test (#123872)

* Provisioning: Fix flaky folder-count assertion in quota sync test

TestIntegrationProvisioning_SyncQuotaHandling/full_sync_with_nested_folders_counts_folders_toward_quota_and_skips_resources
listed folders once via Folders.Resource.List right after SyncAndWait
and counted those whose grafana.app/managerId matched the repo. The
folders-list API can lag behind sync-job completion, occasionally
returning 0 managed folders and failing the assertion.

Mirror the fix used for dashboards in #123362: add a
RequireRepoFolderCount helper that polls with EventuallyWithT, and
replace both direct list-and-count blocks in the test with it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Restore folder breakdown in quota sync test comments

Spell out which folders make up the expected count, so a future reader
debugging a failure does not have to reconstruct the breakdown from the
surrounding sync logic.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
Provisioning: Fix TestIntegrationProvisioning_BlockManagerChange cleanup flake (#123902)

Provisioning: Bump CleanupAllResources timeout to handle search index lag

Folder admission validates "folder is empty" against the resource search
index, which is eventually consistent with respect to dashboard deletes.
Under SQLite write contention that lag has been observed to exceed the
60s WaitTimeoutDefault, causing TestIntegrationProvisioning_BlockManagerChange
to fail in cleanup with "folder is not empty" on leftovers from the
preceding TestIntegrationFolderManagerConsistency test.

Introduce a dedicated waitTimeoutCleanup (2x WaitTimeoutDefault) so each
cleanup step has a longer budget than the default per-operation wait.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Under SQLite write contention that lag has been observed to exceed the
60s WaitTimeoutDefault, causing TestIntegrationProvisioning_BlockManagerChange
to fail in cleanup with "folder is not empty" on leftovers from the
preceding TestIntegrationFolderManagerConsistency test.

Introduce a dedicated waitTimeoutCleanup (2x WaitTimeoutDefault) so each
cleanup step has a longer budget than the default per-operation wait.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Add selective resource migration via Resources field

Mirrors the selective Export support (#123381) for the Migrate job:
MigrateJobOptions now accepts a Resources []ResourceRef list. When empty
the legacy "migrate everything" behavior is preserved; when non-empty the
inner Export pushes only the listed dashboards (folder hierarchy is still
emitted). For instance-target repos we skip the namespace cleanup phase
in selective mode, since deleting every other unmanaged resource would be
destructive when the user only asked to take over specific dashboards.

Alerting: consolidate rule status and alert state mutators into single RuleMutator (#120876)

* Alerting: consolidate rule status and alert state mutators into single RuleMutator

In HA single-node evaluation mode, the Prometheus API made two separate
GetStatesForRuleUID calls per rule — one for status, one for alert
states. Since both derive from the same DB query, merge them into a
single RuleMutator type with two implementations:

- NewInMemoryRuleMutator: non-HA, reads status from scheduler and
  states from state manager (same behavior as before)
- NewDBRuleMutator: HA mode, single DB fetch per rule

* fix comment

commit.message:
Search: defensive fixes for RemoteIndexStore and lock heartbeat (#123951)

Three small, independent hardening fixes to pkg/storage/unified/search:

- objectStorageLock heartbeat: declare loss one tick before TTL boundary
  (maxFailures = ttl/hbi - 1) so another replica can't take the lock at the
  same instant we declare loss. With defaults (180s / 60s) loss is now
  detected at ~120s instead of ~180s.

- BucketRemoteIndexStore.DownloadIndex: cap each per-file download at
  expectedSize+1 via LimitedWriter, mirroring the meta.json pattern. A
  misadvertised manifest size or a bucket object that has grown out of band
  now fails fast instead of streaming unbounded bytes to disk.

- validateManifestPaths: stop rejecting filenames that legitimately start
  with '..' (e.g. '..foo/bar.zap'). Still rejects '..', '../escape', etc.

- BucketRemoteIndexStore.DownloadIndex: cap each per-file download at

commit.message:
Search: split build vs cleanup lock options, make timeouts configurable (#123954)

NewBucketRemoteIndexStore now takes a BucketRemoteIndexStoreConfig struct
with separate BuildLock and CleanupLock options, replacing five positional
args. Build locks are per-snapshot while cleanup runs on a 6h cadence, so
the two have different natural durations.

objectStorageLockConfig gains HeartbeatUpdateTimeout and ReleaseDeleteTimeout,
both defaulting to 30s. The previous hardcoded 30s for the heartbeat Update
context made Release block up to 30s on shutdown, bypassing the codebase's
shutdown budget; operators can now tune this per lock kind.

No production behaviour change: defaults preserve the previous timings, and
buildSnapshotOptions wires the same LockOptions into both BuildLock and
CleanupLock for now.

commit.message:
Search: log per-snapshot deletes and unify wording to "index snapshot" (#123957)

Add an Info log line for each successful retention-driven snapshot delete
in runResourceCleanup, mirroring the existing failure log. Includes the
snapshot's upload timestamp and age so operators can distinguish max-age
deletes from supersede deletes without re-checking the bucket.

Also normalise log messages across the snapshot code paths to consistently
say "index snapshot" instead of bare "snapshot" / "index":

- bleve_snapshot.go: snapshot candidate / no snapshot candidates / selected snapshot
- bleve_snapshot_upload.go: releasing snapshot upload lock
- remote_index_cleanup.go: deleting snapshot (failure log)
- remote_index_store.go: skipping index with non-ULID key / invalid manifest

commit.message:
BugFix: RandomWalk multi-query key collision (#123492)

Grafana: Fix RandomWalk multi-query key collision

When using the -- Grafana -- datasource with multiple RandomWalk
queries, only the last query's data appeared because all response
packets fell back to the same key ('A') in processResponsePacket.

Fix by setting refId on generated frames in randomWalk.ts and an
explicit key on each response packet in datasource.ts, matching
the pattern used by other frontend datasources.

commit.message:
Provisioning: Fix flaky EmptyPath multi-repo resource-count assertions (#124028)

TestIntegrationProvisioning_EmptyPath/multiple_repositories_with_empty_path
listed dashboards and folders once via DashboardsV1.Resource.List and
Folders.Resource.List immediately after CreateLocalRepo returned for
repo2. Because repo2 uses SkipResourceAssertions=true, the helper does
not poll for resource visibility, and the list endpoints can lag behind
sync-job completion — occasionally returning 0 folders even though the
sync produced 12.

Wrap both checks in require.EventuallyWithT with the standard
common.WaitTimeoutDefault / common.WaitIntervalDefault, mirroring the
pattern used for the other assertions in this package.

commit.message:
Unified Storage: retry batched RV transaction on SQLITE_BUSY (#124026)

The provisioning incremental sync flake surfaces as
"writing resource from file ...: transactional operation: insert into resource:
... database is locked (5) (SQLITE_BUSY)" because rvmanager.execBatch wraps
all writes in a single WithTx but never retries when SQLite returns BUSY.
The transaction is rolled back, so the whole batch is safe to retry.

Wrap WithTx in a bounded backoff that fires only on sqlite.IsBusyOrLocked
(50ms->500ms, max 5 attempts), reset per-attempt state so a rolled-back
attempt cannot leak guids/rvs into the next one, and abort early if the
batch context is cancelled. Non-busy errors and non-SQLite drivers fall
through unchanged.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
search: add BuildStartTimestamp to IndexMeta (#124035)

Records when the bleve index was originally created (start of the
from-scratch build), as distinct from the snapshot upload time.
Sourced from the bleve index's internal buildInfo, which is preserved
across reopens and snapshot round-trips, so periodic re-uploads of a
long-lived index re-emit the original build-start time.

Snapshots produced before this change have a zero-value field;
readers must treat zero as "unknown" and fall back to other criteria.

Plumbing only — no reader uses the field yet.

commit.message:
fix: never include enterprise imports (#124044)

* fix: never include enterprise imports

The imports only need to exist for tooling's sake. It doesn't actually help the binary at all: the code that actually needs it will import it already, and thus bring it into the binary. This means we can persist all the import usage locations' build tags and similar by simply never using the actual imports files in OSS.

* fix: include Grafana imports as well

In some cases, Grafana Enterprise depends on code from apps in Grafana.
This means we need to keep imports from Grafana as well, otherwise go.mod will be inconsistent depending on whether you
have Enterprise linked.

commit.message:
search: add ListIndexKeys and GetIndexMeta to RemoteIndexStore (#124039)

* search: add ListIndexKeys and GetIndexMeta to RemoteIndexStore

Adds two cheap metadata primitives to the RemoteIndexStore interface:

- ListIndexKeys returns the ULID keys of all snapshots under a namespaced resource, without reading manifest bodies. May include incomplete uploads.

- GetIndexMeta returns the manifest for a single snapshot, or ErrSnapshotNotFound if missing.

Also refactors DownloadIndex and ListIndexes to use GetIndexMeta, removing duplicated manifest fetch/parse/validate logic. DownloadIndex now returns ErrSnapshotNotFound (sentinel) when the manifest is missing instead of a wrapped fmt.Errorf.

* search: add ErrInvalidManifest, fold isValidManifest into GetIndexMeta

GetIndexMeta now wraps ErrInvalidManifest for structural errors (oversized, unparseable, empty file list, or non-canonical paths). ErrSnapshotNotFound and other download errors unchanged.

isValidManifest is removed: its single caller in CleanupIncompleteUploads inlines the switch on the two sentinels, which is more direct than the (bool, error) three-way contract.

* search: drop redundant doc comment on BucketRemoteIndexStore.GetIndexMeta

The interface already documents the contract (ErrSnapshotNotFound and ErrInvalidManifest). The duplicated impl-level doc only said half of it and would drift.

* fmt

commit.message:
search: skip periodic snapshot upload when same-version remote is fresh (#124051)

Adds a cross-instance dedup probe to the periodic snapshot upload path.
Before acquiring the build lock, uploadSnapshot lists snapshots for the
namespace and walks them newest-first by ULID time (which equals upload
time), looking for a same-version snapshot uploaded within UploadInterval.
If found, the upload is skipped; lastUploadTime is bumped to now so this
replica's local rate limit also applies, and the mutation baseline is
preserved.

Walking (rather than checking only the newest) is necessary in
mixed-version clusters \u2014 either transiently during rolling upgrades, or
as a deliberate steady-state configuration. V1 and V2 replicas may
interleave uploads, so the newest snapshot can be the wrong version
while a same-version match lives a few keys back.

The probe is an optimisation, not a correctness check: probe failures
fall through to today's upload path. ULIDs guarantee unique snapshot
keys, so duplicate uploads remain safe; cleanup reaps the loser.

Disabled when UploadInterval == 0, mirroring the local logic.
New metric label: skip_recent_remote.
