commit.message:
Provisioning: fix SyncAndWait race causing folder metadata test flake (#124048)

SyncAndWait POSTs a sync job and then calls AwaitJobs(repo), which lists
active jobs for the repo. If the just-queued job has already moved to the
historic subresource before the list call, waitUntilComplete is empty and
the success check (successCount >= len(waitUntilComplete)) trivially
passes (0 >= 0), so SyncAndWait returns without ever having waited for
the sync. Callers that immediately list provisioned resources then race
against the actual sync, producing flakes such as
TestIntegrationProvisioning_FullSync_FolderMetadataTitle.

Wait for the specific job we queued by UID via the historic subresource,
and assert the resulting state is not JobStateError (Warning is still
allowed, matching the prior semantics). Also include the folders we did
see in requireRepoFolderTitle's error message so future flakes
distinguish "missing entirely" from "wrong title".

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
storage/unified/search: add findFreshSnapshotByBuildStart probe and align IndexMeta field names (#124061)

* search: add findFreshSnapshotByBuildStart probe and align IndexMeta field names

Adds a backend-agnostic probe that walks namespace snapshots newest-first
and returns the first one whose BuildVersion matches the running version
and whose BuildTime falls within [now-maxAge, now]. Mirrors the existing
findFreshSnapshotByUploadTime, but uses build-start time so periodic
re-uploads of long-lived indexes are correctly rejected when their
underlying data ages past maxAge, even though their ULID (= upload time)
is recent.

Also renames IndexMeta fields to match the existing IndexBuildInfo
naming used elsewhere in the package:

  BuildStartTimestamp -> BuildTime  (json: build_time)
  GrafanaBuildVersion -> BuildVersion  (json: build_version)

These fields were introduced recently and are not deployed; no compat
shim needed.

The probe tests are table-driven and share a small runProbeCases helper,
so the upload-time and build-start variants stay parallel.

No call sites for the new probe yet; wiring into BuildIndex follows in
a separate change.

* gofmt

commit.message:
Provisioning: Scope repository uniqueness by (URL, branch, path) (#123498)

* fix(FD-009): reject duplicate repos with empty paths and scope uniqueness by branch

The Repository admission validator had two related defects in the
(URL, path) identity-key logic:

1. Two Repositories with the same URL and both paths empty were
   admitted as non-duplicates, even though empty path means "repository
   root" — the worst case of overlap.

2. Branch was not part of the identity key, so two Repositories
   pointing at the same URL and path but different branches were
   incorrectly rejected as duplicates.

The fix changes the identity rule to (URL, branch, path) with literal
equality on all three components. The empty-path exception is removed.

Closes grafana/git-ui-sync-project#1080
Closes grafana/git-ui-sync-project#1081

commit.message:
Table: Fix width bi-directional updates for nested tables (#123986)

* TableNG: sync nested table column widths via controlled columnWidths state

Fixes #118893. Each nested DataGrid instance had independent internal
width state, so resizing one nested table had no effect on the others.

Move nested tables to react-data-grid's controlled column-width API:
a shared ColumnWidths map is held in parent state and passed to every
nested DataGrid via `columnWidths`/`onColumnWidthsChange`. Any resize in
one nested table updates the shared state, propagating immediately to all
others. The map is re-initialised when field names or panel-configured
widths change so that override-panel edits stay reactive.

commit.message:
Provisioning: Honor ruleset bypass for write workflow validation (#123893)

GetRulesets returned a hard block whenever a branch had any active
pull_request rule, even when the configured GitHub App was in the
parent ruleset's bypass_actors with bypass_mode=always. Direct push
actually succeeds at runtime in that case, so the preflight produced
a false positive that blocked legitimate Repository configurations.

Fetch each unique parent ruleset and consult CurrentUserCanBypass;
GitHub evaluates the bypass match server-side for the calling actor,
so we don't need the App installation ID. Treat only "always" and
"exempt" as non-blocking — "pull_request" only bypasses on PR merge.
Fail-closed when the parent fetch errors so configs that would fail
at push time don't silently save.

Fixes #123877

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
Provisioning: Negotiate receive-pack capabilities for git pushes (#124122)

Some GitLab servers wrap receive-pack responses in side-band-64k, which
caused pushes that the server actually rejected (e.g. pre-receive hook
declined) to surface as silent success. Enabling nanogit's capability
negotiation makes the client advertise only the intersection with what
the server announces, avoiding the wrapping path on those servers and
keeping the default set on servers that already advertise it.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
Provisioning: Don't mark folders pending due to _folder.json metadata (#124118)

* Provisioning: Don't mark folders pending due to _folder.json metadata

The Git Sync Resources tree was showing a pending sync icon on folders
whose only "pending" child was the _folder.json metadata file. _folder.json
has no matching Kubernetes resource (the folder resource lives at the
parent path), so getStatus always returned 'pending' for it, and that
status propagated up to the folder.

Treat _folder.json as folder metadata: don't assign it a row-level sync
status, and skip it when aggregating folder status from children.

Fixes grafana/git-ui-sync-project#1130

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Compare _folder.json hash against parent folder resource hash

The folder resource exposes a hash that represents its synced metadata
(empty when no metadata is present). _folder.json has no resource of its
own, so its sync state must be derived from the parent folder's resource
hash. With this comparison in place, the file row and the parent folder
correctly reflect added, updated, and removed metadata transitions.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Mark folder pending when _folder.json is removed locally

When a provisioned folder's resource has a non-empty metadata hash but the
_folder.json file is no longer present in the repo, the metadata file was
deleted between syncs. Reflect this on the parent folder by marking it
pending until the next sync reconciles the resource.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Reword "locally" as "remotely" in metadata sync tests

The metadata file changes happen in the remote git repository (the source
of truth) and Grafana detects the drift on its next sync. The previous
wording made it sound like the user changed the file in their working tree.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Cover remaining sync-status matrix rows in tree tests

Add unit tests for matrix rows that were previously covered only implicitly:
inferred parent folder with _folder.json present (parent has no resource),
synced metadata alongside a pending dashboard sibling, and sibling folder
independence (a pending folder must not bleed into a synced sibling).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
Pyroscope: Support UTF-8 label names in label selectors (frontend) (#121863)

* Pyroscope: Support UTF-8 label names in label selectors (frontend)

Label names containing characters outside [a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]* are now
double-quoted when serialised into selector strings, e.g. {"k8s.namespace"="prod"}.
Backslashes and double quotes within label names are escaped.

The Prism grammar, extractLabelMatchers, and Monaco autocomplete are updated to
parse and insert them correctly, enabling full round-trip support.

Also fixes a preexisting bug in autocomplete where existingLabels were parsed
incorrectly (destructuring match[1] string instead of the match array).

* Pyroscope: Remove unused labelSelector file

Removes labelSelector.ts and its test file which were added but never
imported or wired up.

* Pyroscope: Fix UTF-8 label names not filtering from autocomplete suggestions

The labelSelectorRegex in createSelector used \w+ which only matches
ASCII word characters, so quoted UTF-8 label names (e.g. "k8s.namespace")
were silently dropped when building the API selector. This meant the API
returned them as available labels even after they were already selected.

* Pyroscope: Fix missing Query properties in UTF-8 label names tests

were silently dropped when building the API selector. This meant the API
returned them as available labels even after they were already selected.

* Pyroscope: Fix missing Query properties in UTF-8 label names tests

commit.message:
search: download fresh same-version snapshot instead of rebuilding (#124110)

On the rebuild path, BuildIndex now probes the remote index store for
a same-version snapshot whose BuildTime is fresh enough (within 10%
of the per-resource rebuild interval) and strictly newer than
lastImportTime. On hit, downloads it instead of rebuilding from
scratch. On miss, falls through to a from-scratch rebuild — no
tiered fallback (we already have a working index).

Built on top of the findFreshSnapshotByBuildStart helper landed in
#124061.

Adds a policy label to index_server_snapshot_downloads_total with
values "tiered" (existing initial-startup path via pickBestSnapshot)
and "same_version" (new rebuild-path probe).

Refactors tryDownloadRemoteSnapshot and tryDownloadFreshSnapshot to
share a downloadSelectedSnapshot template that owns the trace span,
log lines, outcome metric, and the reserve-download-open-validate
flow. Each policy supplies its selection logic via a snapshotSelectFn
closure.

commit.message:
Zanzana: Fix flaky TestIntegrationFolderTreeZanzana (#124146)

IAM/Zanzana: Fix flaky TestIntegrationFolderTreeZanzana

AwaitZanzanaReconcileNext under MT mode polls the per-namespace
reconcile-success histogram, which never increments until the reconciler's
ListAllStores returns a non-empty set. At start-of-test there is a window
where no OpenFGA store exists for any org, so the 30s wait can time out
with "0 > 0".

Prime the store for org-1 by issuing a single authenticated GET /api/folders
before sampling the baseline. This routes through Server.Check ->
EnsureNamespace -> GetOrCreateStore, after which the reconciler's next tick
reliably bumps the histogram. Subsequent calls are no-ops via the
ensuredNamespaces cache.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
Alerting: add RBAC authorization for alertmanager import API (#124151)

* Alerting: define RBAC actions and scope for alertmanager imports

Introduces four scoped actions under notifications.alerting.grafana.app:
- alertmanagerimports:create
- alertmanagerimports:get
- alertmanagerimports:update
- alertmanagerimports:delete

Adds ScopeAlertmanagerImportsProvider and ScopeAlertmanagerImportsAll
for scoping permissions to specific import identifiers.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Alerting: add ExtraConfigAuthz interface and enforce in notifier

Defines ExtraConfigAuthz with AuthorizeCreate, AuthorizeUpdate, and
AuthorizeDelete methods. SaveAndApplyExtraConfiguration and
DeleteExtraConfiguration now accept a user and authz parameter and
call the appropriate check before mutating state.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Alerting: implement AlertmanagerImportsAccess RBAC service

Implements ExtraConfigAuthz using RBAC. AuthorizeCreate requires the
explicit create action (no legacy fallback). AuthorizeUpdate and
AuthorizeDelete accept either the scoped import action or legacy
notifications:write.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Alerting: register alertmanager-imports admin role, gated by feature flag

Adds fixed:alerting.alertmanager-imports:writer role with all four
import actions scoped to alertmanagerimports:*, granted to Org Admins.
Role is only registered when FlagAlertingImportAlertmanagerAPI is
enabled. Threads FeatureToggles into DeclareFixedRoles.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Alerting: wire alertmanager imports authorization into convert API

Threads AlertmanagerImportsAccess through the convert API. The
Alertmanager interface now accepts user and authz on Save and Delete
so authorization is enforced inside the notifier. Existing
notifications:read/write permissions remain as legacy fallback on
GET/POST/DELETE via EvalAny.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Alerting: register alertmanagerimports kind in RBAC permission registry

Adds AlertingAlertmanagerImportsKind to the default kind→scope-prefix
map so the permission registry accepts scoped permissions for the
convert API import endpoints.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

commit.message:
Alerting: batch InsertMulti in default notification policy migration (#124237)

The "grant basic roles access to default notification policy" migration
builds a single bulk INSERT for every editor/viewer managed role across
every org. On instances with many orgs the placeholder count exceeds
modernc.org/sqlite's SQLITE_MAX_VARIABLE_NUMBER (32766), and the upgrade
fails with "too many SQL variables (1)".

Wrap the InsertMulti in the existing batch helper (batchSize = 500),
matching every other bulk-insert migration in this package.

Fixes #124016

commit.message: Provisioning: GitHub-style README panel inline on the folder page (#123755) * Provisioning: GitHub-style README panel below the dashboards list Render the folder's README inline below the dashboards list, like GitHub does for repository directories. A small one-line hint above the list ("Looking for an overview of this folder? See the README") scrolls users to the panel via #folder-readme. Behind the new provisioningReadmes feature toggle (frontend-only, off by default). Frontend pieces: - useFolderReadme — resolves the README path from the source-path annotation, fetches via the provisioning files API, gates on the toggle. - FolderReadmePanel — GitHub-style: header bar with the README.md filename + Edit pencil that opens the host editor; body renders markdown when one exists, otherwise an "Add README" CTA that opens the host's new-file editor pre-filled with a structure scaffold. - FolderReadmeHint — one-line, anchor-link version that only renders when a README is present. - New URL helpers in utils/git.ts: getRepoEditFileUrl and getRepoNewFileUrl. Both honor repository.path so the URL points at the actual file inside the host repo. Analytics (reportInteraction): - grafana_provisioning_readme_hint_clicked (carries repositoryType) - grafana_provisioning_readme_edit_clicked - grafana_provisioning_readme_create_clicked Depends on the backend support for raw .md reads (provisioning files API) — see the companion backend PR. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 * Provisioning: Stop the README panel getting squeezed by the page flex layout The panel sits at the bottom of Page.Contents, which is a height: 100% flex column. The previous sibling (the AutoSizer-driven dashboards list) claims height: 100%, leaving the panel as a shrinkable flex child — its overflow: hidden then crops the markdown body. Add flex-shrink: 0 so the panel always takes its natural content height and the page scrolls past the dashboards list to reveal it intact. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 * Provisioning: Remove the README hint above the dashboards list The inline README panel below the dashboards is the discoverability mechanism on its own, GitHub-style. The hint above the list became redundant. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 * Provisioning: Shrink the dashboards list to its content height GitHub-style: the file list takes (rowCount * rowHeight) rather than the full available page height, so the README panel below sits right after the last row instead of below a stretch of empty AutoSizer space. Compute the natural height in BrowseDashboardsPage from useFlatTreeState and the DashboardsTree row constants (36px). Cap at 70vh so very long folders stay manageable — react-window will virtualize internally as before once the list exceeds the cap. Search mode and empty folders fall back to a 480px default. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 * Provisioning: Use a pencil icon for the README edit action The external-link-alt icon read as "open in a new tab" rather than "edit", which made the panel's icon-only edit button ambiguous. Switch to the standard pencil (matches GitHub's per-file edit affordance); target="_blank" still opens the host editor in a new tab. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 * Provisioning: Rewrite relative URLs in the rendered README Markdown READMEs use relative paths to other files in the repo (e.g. [CODEOWNERS](../../../.github/CODEOWNERS)). When rendered inside Grafana those resolve against /dashboards/f/... and 404. Post-process the rendered HTML so they land back on the host repo: - new getRepoLinkUrl helper that picks blob/tree per provider and preserves trailing-slash directory targets; - new rewriteRelativeMarkdownLinks utility: walks , leaves schemed/protocol-relative/anchor URLs alone, resolves the rest against the README's directory inside the repo, replaces with an absolute host URL, and adds target=_blank + rel=noopener; - the panel passes repository + readmePath through so the resolver knows the README's location. Local repos (no host link pattern) get the relative href stripped so the text doesn't render as a clickable but broken link. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 * Provisioning: Rewrite relative in the rendered README too Markdown screenshots referenced with relative paths (e.g. ![diagram](./diagram.png)) used to point inside the Grafana app and 404. Resolve them against the README's directory and swap to the host's raw file URL so the images render inline. - new getRepoRawFileUrl helper: GitHub: /raw/{branch}/{path} (redirects to raw.githubusercontent.com) GitLab: /-/raw/{branch}/{path} Bitbucket: /raw/{branch}/{path} - rewriteRelativeMarkdownLinks now also walks ; absolute and protocol-relative URLs are left alone. - For repos without a raw URL pattern (local), the broken relative src is stripped so the alt text falls back instead of a broken-image icon pointing at the Grafana app. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 * Provisioning: Show a README hint above long dashboards lists When a folder has many dashboards the README at the bottom is unlikely to be discovered without a nudge. Bring the hint back as a single-line inline pointer above the list, but only when the dashboards list is at least 15 items long — short folders don't need the help, the README is already in view. The hint uses the same #folder-readme anchor as before, so clicking just scrolls down inside the page. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 * Provisioning: Tweak README hint copy from "and" to "or" "Lots of dashboards or new to this folder?" reads more accurately — either condition on its own is enough reason to point users at the README; "and" implied both had to be true. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 * Provisioning: Bump README hint threshold from 15 to 20 items Anything under ~20 dashboards still leaves the README close to the fold on a normal viewport — only fire the hint past that point. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 * Provisioning: Drop README hint threshold to 18 items Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 * Provisioning: Drive README hint scroll explicitly with scrollIntoView Native `#folder-readme` hash navigation only updates the URL when Grafana's Page component owns the scroll container — the page doesn't actually scroll on click. Call scrollIntoView ourselves with behavior=smooth/block=start so the panel comes into view regardless of which ancestor handles scroll. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 * separate components * Fix link text size * Provisioning: render folder README inline in browse-dashboards tree - Add 'readme' UI kind to DashboardsTreeItem type union - Append README row to flat tree when folder is provisioned - Render FolderReadmePanel inside DashboardsTree with dynamic height - Fix isItemLoaded to close over flatTreeWithReadme (prevents spurious root fetch when InfiniteLoader checks the appended readme row) - Refactor FolderReadmePanel: remove InlineFolderReadmeLayout wrapper, render directly with markdown link rewriting - Fix markdown link rewriting for query strings, fragments, and encoded characters - Remove FolderReadmeHint and InlineFolderReadmeLayout (replaced by inline tree row) - Remove useBrowseFolderItemCount hook (no longer needed) - Add BrowseView tests for README injection conditions (5 cases) - Update FolderReadmePanel and markdownLinks tests * Browse dashboards: full-width README row with top spacing * remove height calcs * refactor: consolidate getRepoLinkUrl into getRepoFileUrl Extend getRepoFileUrl with trailing-slash directory detection so it picks tree/blob per provider, then delete the duplicated getRepoLinkUrl. Route markdownLinks.ts through the consolidated function. Add direct unit tests for directory-path URL generation (GitHub tree, GitLab tree, Bitbucket src). * Conditional rendering * chore: simplify README_ROW_HEIGHT comment * Provisioning: Add experiment telemetry to README panel * Switch to analytics framework * chore: re-trigger CI Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 --------- Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.7 Co-authored-by: Clarity-89

Provisioning: add public_root_url instance setting for external URLs (#123613)

* Provisioning: add public_app_url instance setting for external URLs

Introduces the [provisioning] public_app_url setting to expose a
publicly-reachable URL for instances whose [server] root_url points at an
internal/cluster host. Both webhook callbacks registered with the Git
provider and screenshot images embedded in PR comments fall back through
this setting when set, so a single instance-level knob fixes both the
unreachable-webhook and broken-PR-image-render cases without overloading
the per-repository spec.webhook.baseUrl contract.

Resolution chains:
- Webhook URL: spec.webhook.baseUrl -> public_app_url -> AppURL
- Screenshot URL: public_app_url -> AppURL

Screenshots intentionally do not consult spec.webhook.baseUrl — per-repo
webhook overrides remain a webhook-only concern, keeping the two
contracts independent at the consumer layer.

Alternative to #123004.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: rename public_app_url to public_root_url

The setting shadows [server] root_url as a fallback, so naming it
public_root_url makes the relationship obvious — operators searching
docs for "root_url" will land on the correct setting.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: keep clickable links on AppURL even when public_root_url is set

The previous revision flipped the entire urlProvider closure to public_root_url,
which also moved the GrafanaURL and PreviewURL clickable links in PR comments
onto the public URL. That's wrong for the common reviewer scenario: clicks
travel from a human's browser on the corp network, and the public URL is often
firewalled to the Git provider's CIDRs only — internal reviewers would 403 on
their own preview links.

Split into two closures: internalURLProvider (returns AppURL, fed to the
evaluator's urlProvider for clickable links) and publicURLProvider (returns
public_root_url || AppURL, fed to the webhook builder and as screenshotBaseURL
for image embeds). Webhooks and screenshots stay public-reachable; clickable
links stay corp-network-friendly.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: fall back to public_root_url for operator webhook registration

The operator runs as a separate process and previously needed
[operator] provisioning_server_public_url to be set explicitly to register
webhooks. With public_root_url now defined at the instance level, fall back
to it when the operator-specific knob is unset, so a single config drives
both the in-process and operator deployments.

If neither is set, behavior is unchanged (no webhook registered).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: scope public_root_url to on-prem only

The operator deployment path runs in a different topology and is not the
target audience for the on-prem dual-network use case that motivates
public_root_url. Reverting the operator-side wiring so the setting stays
purely an on-prem concern; can revisit if/when operator deployments grow
the same need.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: trim operator jobs.go to minimal NewEvaluator signature change

Operator path doesn't consume public_root_url; only the new screenshotBaseURL
argument is wired (passing AppURL, unused at runtime due to NoOp renderer).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: replace evaluator's split URL args with URLProvider struct

NewEvaluator previously took urlProvider and screenshotBaseURL as separate
arguments, which forced the operator path to invent a screenshotBaseURL
value (cfg.AppURL) it didn't actually need. Wrap both into a URLProvider
struct with Internal and Public fields — each caller fills in what it knows:

- In-process Grafana: Internal=AppURL, Public=public_root_url||AppURL.
- Operator (NoOp renderer, no public/internal split): Internal=Public=
  the existing per-tenant urlProvider from controllerCfg.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
DashboardLibrary: Fix template card thumbnail collapsing to half width (#124271)

Card.Heading from @grafana/ui sets `gridColumnEnd: 'Tags'`, which
created an implicit column in DashboardCard's overridden grid template
and shrunk the thumbnail/bottom rows to ~half the card width.

Declare a `[Tags]` named line at the end of `gridTemplateColumns` so
the upstream rule resolves to an existing line instead of creating an
implicit column.

commit.message:
Provisioning: Fix ConditionsPatch_AppendDoesNotClobber cleanup flake (#124124)

Provisioning: Clean up released resources in admin-release-patch test

TestIntegrationProvisioning_AdminCanReleaseManagedResourceViaPatch
releases its folder and dashboard (removes manager annotations) but
leaves them as unmanaged resources, dumping the cleanup cost onto the
next test's CleanupAllResources. The folder step there has to absorb
the Bleve search-index lag between the dashboard delete and folder
admission's "is empty" check, which has flaked
TestIntegrationProvisioning_ConditionsPatch_AppendDoesNotClobber under
SQLite write contention.

Add a t.Cleanup to delete the dashboard and retry the folder delete
until the search index lets it through, so the lag is paid in the test
that owns the leak. Failures are logged only; the next test's
CleanupAllResources (with its larger folder budget) remains the safety
net.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
ImageUpload: Add presigned URL support for S3 external image storage (#119002)

* feat(imageupload): 🔗 add presigned URL support for S3 external image storage

Add `enable_presigned_urls` and `presigned_url_expiration` config options
to `[external_image_storage.s3]`, bringing S3 to parity with GCS and Azure.

When enabled, objects are uploaded without an ACL header (compatible with
BucketOwnerEnforced buckets that disable ACLs) and a time-limited
presigned GET URL is returned instead of a direct S3 URL.

Closes #82707

Co-Authored-By: Claude <svc-devxp-claude@slack-corp.com>

* refactor(imageupload): 🔧 address PR review feedback for S3 presigned URLs

- Refactor NewS3Uploader to accept S3UploaderOptions struct instead of
  positional parameters
- Remove dead ACL override (ACL was set to "private" but never used
  since upload skips ACL when presigned URLs are enabled)
- Add validation that presigned_url_expiration is >= 0
- Remove tautological constructor tests
- Add S3 client interface (s3ifaces) with stubbable newS3Client for
  testability, mirroring the existing GCS pattern
- Add unit tests for both upload paths: regular (with ACL) and presigned
  URL (without ACL)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude <svc-devxp-claude@slack-corp.com>
Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
search: cold-start coordination for index snapshot builds (#124252)

* search: cold-start coordination for index snapshot builds

When multiple replicas of the same Grafana version start at once with no
local index, today they each run a from-scratch build independently --
wasted CPU and IO that scales with replica count.

This adds coordination via the existing build lock: the first replica
becomes the leader, builds, and uploads its snapshot. Other replicas
wait and download what the leader publishes. If the leader dies without
uploading, one of the waiters promotes itself. Wait timeout falls back
to building alone -- coordination is best-effort, not a correctness
primitive.

Each iteration of the wait loop probes the remote index store for a
same-version snapshot, then tries to acquire the lock. Probe-before-
acquire is intentional: the leader uploads before releasing the lock,
so a probe hit is preferable to becoming a duplicate leader after the
leader's release.

Cold-start coordination runs only on the initial-startup path (no
cached index, not a rebuild) and only when the index snapshot store is
configured. It's decoupled from maxFreshSnapshotAge (the rebuild-path
knob): cold-start uses Snapshot.MaxIndexAge for its probe window since
any same-version snapshot beats rebuilding from scratch.

BuildIndex now propagates context cancellation from all three remote-
download fallbacks (tiered selection, cold-start coordination, fresh-
same-version rebuild probe) instead of swallowing it and continuing.

Epic: grafana/search-and-storage-team#715
Issue: grafana/search-and-storage-team#766

* Fix linter issues.

* search: propagate context cancellation from cold-start lock acquire

LockBuildIndex can return context.Canceled / context.DeadlineExceeded if
the context is cancelled mid-acquire. The wait-loop default branch
treated these as build-alone fallbacks, so a cancelled BuildIndex would
still kick off a from-scratch build instead of aborting cleanly.

Mirror the ctx.Err() propagation already used in
tryDownloadColdStartSnapshot and in BuildIndex's three remote-download
call sites.

* search: address PR review

- Skip cold-start coordination when MaxIndexAge=0. With no probe window,
  the lock+wait would only serialise N replicas' duplicate from-scratch
  builds without snapshot-reuse upside. Filed as a follow-up to revisit
  MaxIndexAge=0 semantics across all use sites.

- Add coldStartOutcomeContextCanceled metric label ("context_canceled")
  and assign it on the three ctx-error propagation paths in
  coordinateColdStartBuild. Previously these recorded wait_timed_out by
  default, which was misleading.

- Reuse b.recordSnapshotUploadStatus(...) for the cold-start leader's
  immediate-upload metric updates instead of inlining
  IndexSnapshotUploads.WithLabelValues(...).Inc().

commit.message:
storage/unified: simplify BatchGet by moving retries into the gRPC client (#124210)

storage/unified: buffer BatchGet values in gRPC client, remove storage-layer retry

BatchGet previously streamed values lazily to callers, requiring each
KeyValue.Value to be consumed before advancing to the next key and
delegating retry logic to batchGetRetryPull in the storage backend.

In practice every caller immediately calls io.ReadAll on the value
(via readAndClose in kvListIterator/kvHistoryIterator), so the
streaming contract bought nothing but complexity.

This commit removes batchGetRetryPull, BatchGetRetryPolicy,
WithIndexBuildRetryBudget, and the associated iterator retry loops
from the storage backend. Retries are now handled entirely inside the
gRPC client (see companion enterprise commit).

kvListIterator and kvHistoryIterator are simplified to drive
dataStore.BatchGet directly via iter.Pull2, with no retry plumbing.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

commit.message:
Alerting: Fix provisioning API returning 500 for non-admin alert rule deletes (#124331)

HasAccessOrError returned raw errors from ac.Evaluate (e.g., scope
resolution failures) which are not errutil.Error. Handlers using
ErrOrFallback only extract status codes from errutil.Error, so these
fell through to the 500 default. Wrap the internal error alongside an
errutil.Forbidden so callers can detect a proper status code.

Also fixes a copy-paste bug in TestDeleteAlertRule that was calling
UpdateAlertRule instead of DeleteAlertRule.

HasAccessOrError returned raw errors from ac.Evaluate (e.g., scope
resolution failures) which are not errutil.Error. Handlers using

fell through to the 500 default. Wrap the internal error alongside an

Also fixes a copy-paste bug in TestDeleteAlertRule that was calling

commit.message:
Migration: Widen team.updated to DATETIME(3) on MySQL (#124314)

SQLStore: widen team.updated to DATETIME(3) on MySQL

The team.updated column is used as the resourceVersion when an
apiserver-style write goes through legacy.UpdateTeam. The DBTime wire
format already sends millisecond precision, but MySQL DATETIME(0)
silently truncates the fractional part on storage, so the in-memory
timestamp diverges from what's on disk.

ALTER team MODIFY updated DATETIME(3) NOT NULL aligns the column
precision with the wire format on MySQL. SQLite stores DATETIME as
TEXT verbatim and Postgres TIMESTAMP already preserves sub-second
precision, so neither needs a change.

commit.message:
Search snapshots: MaxIndexAge=0 means "no age limit" (#124381)

Make Snapshot.MaxIndexAge=0 mean "no age limit" everywhere it's checked,
matching the idiomatic Go reading of a zero-valued duration. Today the
tiered-selection and cleanup paths already do this; the rebuild /
cold-start freshness check treats 0 as "reject everything", and
cold-start coordination has a workaround that skips the lock entirely

commit.message:
unified-storage: don't share BeginTx deadline with fixture setup in incident 2144 regression test (#124399)

TestReproIncident2144UsingGrafanaDB is flaky on slow CI runners. The
subtests create a 2s-deadline context and pass it to both
setupDBForGrafana (cfg load + sqlite + default org/admin) and the
BeginTx call that's actually under test. On a slow runner the fixture
setup alone can take ~2s, so BeginTx is hit with an already-expired
context and fails with 'context deadline exceeded'.

PR #120483 previously bumped this timeout from 1s to 2s for the same
reason. This change addresses the cause instead: setup now runs with
t.Context() (no deadline, canceled on test cleanup), and the 2s
deadline is created fresh just before BeginTx. The hang guard around
BeginTx is preserved.

* feat(annotations): add kubernetesAnnotations FF and wire k8s app installer

Adds the kubernetesAnnotations feature toggle (experimental, off by default)
that routes manual annotation create/update/delete and tag autocomplete from
/api/annotations to the /apis/annotation.grafana.app endpoint.

Wires the annotation app installer to the FF: previously only
cfg.AnnotationAppPlatform.Enabled triggered registration, leaving all routes
as 404 when only the FF was set.

Frontend changes that consume this FF live in a separate PR.

client-side routing flag from any future server-side annotation k8s flags.

to kubernetesAnnotationsClient perpetuated that. Restore the tombstone
verbatim from main and add kubernetesAnnotationsClient as its own fresh
entry. Run make gen-feature-toggles before push if a more
deterministic metadata block is desired.

commit.message:
Pyroscope: Signal UTF-8 label name support to backend API (#121864)

* Pyroscope: Signal UTF-8 label name support to backend API

Pyroscope is adopting UTF-8 label names (e.g. `k8s.namespace`,
`http/url`). The backend needs to opt in by setting
`allow-utf8-labelnames=true` in the Accept header so that the
Pyroscope API returns these names unescaped.

This commit:
- Adds a `pyroscopeUTF8LabelNames` feature toggle (public preview,
  on by default) so the behaviour can be disabled if needed.
- Appends the opt-in Accept parameter on LabelNames and SelectSeries
  connect requests when the toggle is enabled.
- Introduces `labelNameNeedsQuoting` / `formatLabelName` helpers that
  will be used by future backend selector-assembly code to correctly
  quote non-traditional label names.

* Clean up unused functions

output) were not highlighted at all because the trailing `\b` failed
between the unit character and the following digit.

Closes #124307

commit.message:
search: serialize concurrent index rebuilds and protect in-flight build directories (#124472)

* search: serialize concurrent index rebuilds for the same key

Previously, multiple workers picking up rebuild requests for the same
{namespace, group, resource} could run concurrently. Each finishing
rebuild called bleve's cleanOldIndexes, which removed every sibling
directory under the resource folder except its own — so concurrent
rebuilds deleted each other's working directories, leaving the cached
index unable to persist new segments and breaking writes until pod
restart.

This change adds an in-flight tracker on searchServer. When a worker
enters rebuildIndex and another worker is already rebuilding the same
key, the new request is stashed as a follow-up and the worker returns
immediately. When the in-flight rebuild finishes, the stashed follow-up
is re-enqueued so its conditions (e.g. a newer lastImportTime) are
re-evaluated against the just-built index, and either trigger another
rebuild or close the deferred completion channels as a no-op.

Properties:
- At most one rebuild per key runs at a time.
- Workers don't park, so a hot key can't starve other keys.
- Stricter conditions arriving during a rebuild are preserved via
  combineRebuildRequests and re-evaluated on the follow-up.

Also consolidates the existing slowSearchBackendWithCache test helper
into a new blockingSearchBackend that uses a channel for deterministic
unblocking, and adds tests covering the dedup and follow-up paths.

Refs grafana/search-and-storage-team#783

* search: protect in-flight build directories from cleanOldIndexes

cleanOldIndexes deletes every subdirectory of a resource directory except
the caller's own. Two BuildIndex calls running for the same key (e.g. a
concurrent rebuild and a snapshot download, or two rebuilds racing each
other) write into separate timestamped subdirectories; whichever finishes
first wipes out the other's working directory, leaving the still-running
build unable to persist segments and writes failing with ENOENT until the
pod is restarted.

Track the absolute paths of directories that belong to in-flight
BuildIndex calls (or their helpers) in a refcounted set on bleveBackend.
Helpers register the path right when the directory becomes visible on
disk:
  - createEmptyFileIndex registers after the bleve index is created.
  - findPreviousFileBasedIndex registers before returning a reused dir.
  - downloadSelectedSnapshot registers right after reserveSnapshotDir,
    so the entire (potentially multi-minute) download window is covered.
BuildIndex unregisters via a single deferred call after prepareIndex
returns, regardless of success or failure path. cleanOldIndexes consults
this set and skips any registered directory in addition to its existing
skipName.

Add a maintainer note on cleanOldIndexes documenting the contract for
future helpers that allocate or open directories under a resource's
directory.

* search: address review feedback on in-flight build dir tracking

- tryReuseFileIndex: unregister the directory when rejecting a stale
  reused index. Without this, a cold-start path where lastImportTime
  postdates the persisted index's BuildTime leaves the rejected dir
  registered for the lifetime of the process, and cleanOldIndexes
  silently skips it forever.
- unregisterInFlightBuildDir: log an error when called with an unknown
  path. A missing entry indicates a missing register or a double
  unregister; logging surfaces the bug without crashing production.
- rebuildIndex: switch the stash to &req per review.
- Tests: assert inFlightBuildDirs is empty at the end of the concurrent
  rebuild test, and add a focused test for the cold-start reuse
  rejection leak that fails without the tryReuseFileIndex fix.

* search: revert deferred rebuild stash to new(req)

Switching to &req earlier introduced a race: &req aliases the (heap-
escaped) parameter, and the function nils req.completeChannels two lines
later, so the next deferring goroutine merged from a nil slice and lost
the previous goroutine's completion channel. CI flagged this as 3
channels collected instead of 4.

new(req) (Go 1.26+ allocate-from-value) makes a heap copy at the time
of the stash, so the subsequent mutation is invisible to the stash.
Comment added so a future reviewer doesn't 'fix' it back.

Alerting: refactor merge package — inline, simplify, fix bugs (#124327)

* refactor: move GetMergedAlertmanagerConfig to merge package

* add context to merge function

* make merge return definitions.PostableUserConfig

* merge GetMergedAlertmanagerConfig into MergeExtraConfig

* rename Merge function to mergeConfigs for consistency

* Updated tests and references to use the renamed function.
* Enhanced clarity and alignment with naming conventions.

* replace TestMerge by  TestMergeExtraConfig

* refactor: simplify merge logic in alertmanager configurations

* Removed redundant code and streamlined error handling.
* Improved struct assignments for better clarity and maintainability.
* Enhanced merge functions for routes, receivers, and time intervals.

* remove MergeOpts

* clean up merge package slop

- Hoist RenameResourceUsagesInRoutes before the matchers guard,
  eliminating a redundant no-op call when SubtreeMatchers is set
- Remove vestigial error return from DeduplicateResources; it never
  erred, and the dead error check in imported.go is gone with it
- Fix stale doc comment on MergeResult referencing the old function name

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix nil route dereference before nil guard in MergeExtraConfig

Move the nil-route check before checkIfMatchersUsed so accessing
cfg.AlertmanagerConfig.Route.Routes cannot panic. Remove the now-dead
mcfg.Route == nil guard (the mimir parser rejects configs without a
route, so it can never be nil here). Add a test locking the nil-base-route
error path.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix slice aliasing in MergeRoutes and MergeInhibitRules

Both functions took value copies of structs but still shared the
backing arrays of their Matchers slices. An append with spare capacity
would silently overwrite the caller's data. Use slices.Clone before
appending to guarantee a fresh allocation.

commit.message:
Unified Storage: Allow ':' in KV key regex for user-storage names (#124471)

* Unified Storage: Encode ':' in resource Names before they reach the KV layer

The Grafana resource-name validator allows ':' (e.g. user-storage's
"<service>:<userUID>" convention), but the unified storage KV layer's
validKeyRegex does not. The kvtest cell crash-looped because a
"grafana-splash-screen:<uid>" object produced a KV key the server rejected
on every iterator scan, failing resource server init.

Encode disallowed bytes in the Name segment as ~XX hex (and decode on
parse) in DataKey.String / StringWithGUID / ParseDataKeyParts and in
ListRequestKey.Prefix / GetRequestKey.Prefix, so on-disk keys stay within
the KV-safe character set while DataKey.Name keeps its original form.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Replace encode/decode with one-line regex change

Drop the EncodeKeyName / DecodeKeyName helpers and the encoding calls in
DataKey.String / StringWithGUID / ParseDataKeyParts and Prefix(). Instead,
add ':' to validKeyRegex so the KV layer accepts keys for resource Names
that already pass the Grafana name validator (which permits ':' for the
user-storage <service>:<userUID> convention).

The regex change is a strict superset, requires no migration, recovers
the existing kvtest data without manual cleanup, and avoids any runtime
encode/decode cost. Tests: positive cases for ':' in IsValidKey, the
kvtest reproduction, and the badger+sqlkv integration test all assert
the literal colon survives end-to-end.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test: clean up userstorage colon subtest, drop standalone reproduction

- Drop TestDataKey_KvtestSplashScreenReproduction; it duplicated coverage
  the table-driven TestParseDataKeyParts_ResourceVersionMetadata already
  has.
- Rewrite the "userstorage format with colon" subtest to match the
  surrounding subtest style: 5-part key (no section prefix), full field
  assertions in the same order as the namespaced subtest, expected/actual
  argument order corrected.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test: pin kv.validKeyRegex as a superset of grafana name validators

Add TestKeyRegexCoversValidationCharSets to pkg/storage/unified/resource —
a package that already imports both validation and kv, so neither package
gains a dependency on the other.

The test sweeps every ASCII byte in the middle of an alphanumeric-padded
sample and asserts: for every byte upstream (IsValidGrafanaName /
IsValidNamespace / IsValidGroup / IsValidResource) accepts in the sample,
kv.IsValidKey must also accept the sample. Anchors in qualifiedNameFmt
(start/end alphanumeric) and resourceFmt (start alpha) are sidestepped by
fixing the probe byte at position 2.

This catches the next regression of the kvtest crash class: silently
widening grafanaNameFmt without widening kv.validKeyRegex.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
IAM: Add team /addmember and /removemember subresources (#124094)

* IAM: Add /teams/{name}/addmember and /removemember subresources

Cross-instance team-sync used to converge a user's membership by
PUT'ing the entire Team object: each instance Get'd, appended a member
to Spec.Members, and submitted the full list back. When two instances
synced different users on the same team from the same baseline, the
second writer's full-replace silently dropped the first writer's
just-added member because the diff treats the submitted list as
authoritative.

The new subresources move the single-member operation server-side. The
client posts {name, permission, external} (or {name} to remove), and
the apiserver expands that into a Get + Spec.Members mutation + Update
through the team resource's dual-writer storage — so the same handler
works under any dual-writer mode (legacy primary, unified primary, or
both). retry.RetryOnConflict around the Update absorbs the
unified-storage resourceVersion check; the synchronizer no longer
keeps a stale Spec.Members snapshot in memory at all, which is what
made the cross-instance race possible in the first place.

HTTP semantics:
  - POST /addmember   → 201 Created on a fresh insert,
                        200 OK on an idempotent re-add.
  - POST /removemember → 200 OK whether or not a row existed; the
                         request is idempotent so the synchronizer
                         doesn't have to distinguish "already gone"
                         from "just deleted".

Request/response shapes are defined in apps/iam/kinds/team.cue and
generated via the App SDK; the handlers consume the generated types
(CreateTeamMember{RequestBody,Body,Response} and the Delete*
counterparts) and emit them with TypeMeta filled in by the framework.

Authorization mirrors the parent Team resource's RBAC: members/groups
keep their existing get_permissions check; addmember/removemember are
gated on team `update` — same bar as a full PUT teams/{name}, since
the effective change is the same shape. No new feature toggle —
registration of these storage map entries is itself gated on the team
API being enabled.

Integration tests cover the happy path, the idempotent re-add (200 vs
the fresh-insert 201), the idempotent re-remove, and a concurrent
addMember of two different users on the same team that exercises the
race the full PUT path could not handle.

* IAM: Reject stale Team Update via resourceVersion precondition

Two Grafana instances running team-sync would race on the same Team and
silently drop each other's just-added members: each Get'd at the same
resourceVersion, each appended a different user to its own Spec.Members
snapshot, and both submitted Update. The IAM team store didn't enforce
the submitted resourceVersion, so the second writer's full-replace list
(which never saw the first writer's append) overwrote the row and
deleted the just-added member with no error and no log line.

Gate the SQL UPDATE in legacy.UpdateTeam on `updated = ?` using the RV
the caller observed at Get time. 0 rows affected after the gate fires
yields ErrTeamUpdateConflict, which the apiserver maps to 409 Conflict;
synchronizer.addUserToTeam's retry.RetryOnConflict re-reads the team
and re-submits with the merged member set, so both members end up
present and the original silent-loss path is closed.

DBTime now serialises with millisecond precision when the value carries
sub-second nanos (so concurrent writes within a second can be told
apart). On-second values keep emitting the legacy second-only format
so the gated UPDATE still text-matches rows xorm wrote at second
precision (e.g. teams created via /api/teams).

* Add retry on MySQL and Postgres deadlock

(cherry picked from commit bd594b70409d5ed1469e5760a7c3f9f6a2b3b9a1)

* Add custom backoff

* Revert "Add retry on MySQL and Postgres deadlock"

This reverts commit 4420f6b91debe854d2dba4276e11374503bfdc45.

* Address review feedback

* wip

* IAM: convert SQL deadlocks on /addmember and /removemember to 409

Map MySQL deadlock / lock-wait timeout, Postgres deadlock_detected /
serialization_failure, and SQLite busy/locked to apierrors.NewConflict
in the addmember/removemember handlers so the synchronizer's
retry.RetryOnConflict reissues against fresh state instead of leaking
the deadlock as a 500.

Adds a string-match fallback because the unified-storage resource
server stringifies its error into a proto Message field, so errors.As
can't reach the original *mysql.MySQLError / *pq.Error type by the
time it arrives at the REST handler.

Also trims verbose comments in store.go and the two REST handlers.

* IAM: tighten comments and fix rest_members test feature flag

Trim verbose comments across the team subresource changeset so each one
describes the current behaviour rather than past iterations. Also fix
the rest_members test to enable FlagKubernetesTeamsApi to match the
production handler. apps/iam/kinds/team.cue picks up cue fmt alignment.

* Format

* IAM: bounds-check members[i] in concurrent addmember test

gosec G602 flagged indexing into members from a `range results` loop
even though both slices have the same length by construction. Add an
explicit `i < len(members)` guard to make the bounds proof local.

* IAM: address review feedback on team subresources

- Apply isRetryableTxnError conversion to LegacyStore.Update so the full
  PUT path also returns 409 on transient SQL deadlocks instead of 500.
- Make NewTeamAddMemberREST / NewTeamRemoveMemberREST panic at
  registration if the storage doesn't satisfy rest.Getter / rest.Updater,
  surfacing wiring bugs at startup instead of as a deferred 503.
- Tolerate unknown fields in the request body to match the apiserver's
  forward-compatible decoding convention.
- Wrap the unexpected-type guard in apierrors.NewInternalError for
  consistent k8s-style error handling.
- Update isRetryableTxnError string fallbacks to substrings the actual
  drivers emit (Error 1213/1205, SQLSTATE 40P01/40001, "deadlock
  detected", "could not serialize"); the previous deadlock_detected /
  serialization_failure substrings never matched any driver output.
- Add retryable_test.go covering structured matches for mysql / pgx v5 /
  lib/pq, wrapped chains, and a stringified-fallback suite that fails if
  a future dependency bump changes a driver's error format.

* IAM: re-read team.updated after UPDATE to fix MySQL RV gating

MySQL's DATETIME(0) silently truncates the millisecond fraction the
DBTime wire format sends, so the in-memory cmd.Updated.Time we returned
to the caller didn't match the value stored on disk. The next caller's
PreviousUpdated comparison then mismatched, surfacing as a spurious
ErrTeamUpdateConflict.

Add a SELECT updated FROM team after the UPDATE inside the same
transaction and return that value, so the resourceVersion the caller
sees always matches what's actually stored regardless of dialect.

Also refresh the iam.grafana.app v0alpha1 OpenAPI snapshot to include
the new addmember/removemember subresource paths.

* IAM: widen team.updated to DATETIME(3) for ms-precision RV gating

MySQL DATETIME(0) silently truncated the millisecond fraction the
DBTime wire format sends, so cmd.Updated.Time didn't match the value
stored on disk and the next Update's PreviousUpdated comparison
mismatched. SQLite stores DATETIME values as TEXT verbatim and Postgres
TIMESTAMP already preserves sub-second precision, so only MySQL needs
the schema bump.

ALTER team MODIFY updated DATETIME(3) NOT NULL on MySQL aligns the
column precision with what the code actually sends, lets the RV gate
distinguish concurrent writes within the same second on MySQL too, and
makes the legacy.UpdateTeam re-read of the stored value unnecessary
(reverted in this commit).

Also picks up the regenerated iam.grafana.app v0alpha1 OpenAPI spec
and TS API client for the new addmember/removemember subresources.

* IAM: Tighten team member loops and document /addmember external semantics

Simplify add/remove loop logic; note in CUE that re-add preserves external.

commit.message:
`iam`: Add metrics and traces to the Storage Wrapper (#124418)

* storewrapper: add tracing spans and metrics observer

Adds opt-in observability hooks to the storage wrapper and its
filteredWatcher. No-op defaults are provided so all existing callers
continue to work without changes.

New surface:
- Observer interface with Observe(layer, op, resource, dur, status)
- WithTracer(trace.Tracer) and WithObserver(Observer) options on New()
- LayerAuthz / LayerInner constants to distinguish timing slices
- Op* constants for each operation (OpCreate, OpGet, …, OpFilterWatchEvents, …)
- statusFromError() maps k8s API errors to stable status label strings

Every CRUD method and the filteredWatcher's filterEvents / sendAllowed
now records a span and an observer call for both the authz hook and the
inner store call.

The New() signature gains a schema.GroupResource parameter (needed to
label spans and metrics); appinstaller/server.go is updated accordingly.

commit.message:
AuthN: Separate external IdP groups from team UIDs on Identity (#124406)

* Authn: Separate external IdP groups from team UIDs on Identity

Add Identity.ExternalGroups (and GetExternalGroups) for groups asserted
by the external IdP (SAML/OIDC/LDAP/auth-proxy/JWT). Identity.Groups now
carries team UIDs synced from the SignedInUser, so GetGroups behaves like
the k8s user.Info contract. AuthInfo (authlib) is unchanged.

* Authn: Migrate LDAP API to ExternalGroups + add regression tests

Switches identityFromLDAPUser to write the IdP groups onto
Identity.ExternalGroups instead of Identity.Groups, and adds tests that
pin the contract:

- Identity.GetGroups returns team UIDs, GetExternalGroups returns IdP groups
- syncSignedInUserToIdentity sources Groups from usr.TeamUIDs and preserves
  ExternalGroups
- per-client checks that IdP groups don't leak into Identity.Groups

commit.message:
search: replace ad-hoc remote-store fakes with a single hookable wrapper (#124555)

Test-only refactor. No production code or interface changes.

Replaces three ad-hoc RemoteIndexStore fakes (fakeRemoteIndexStore, coldStartFakeStore, uploadTestStore) with a single hookableStore that wraps the real BucketRemoteIndexStore over gocloud's in-memory memblob bucket. Tests now run against the same code path that runs in production, including the real lock backend.

The wrapper carries the test instrumentation the old fakes had: per-method error injection, call counters, controllable lock loss, and mid-call callbacks.

Groundwork for a follow-up PR that reshapes the RemoteIndexStore interface -- doing it separately keeps that diff focused on the interface change.

commit.message:
TracesPanel: resolve datasource from panel options when data.request is unavailable (#121215)

When a VizPanel with pluginId 'traces' uses SceneDataNode (pre-fetched
data), PanelData.request is undefined because no query pipeline ran.
The traces panel previously resolved the datasource exclusively from
data.request.targets[0].datasource.uid, so TraceView received no
datasource context and extension points like
grafana/traceview/header/actions were hidden.

Add datasource?: DataSourceRef to TracesPanelOptions as a fallback.
Consumers using SceneDataNode can set options.datasource on the VizPanel
to provide datasource identity explicitly.

commit.message:
search: shrink RemoteIndexStore to per-file primitives + helper free functions (#124564)

* search: shrink RemoteIndexStore to per-file primitives + helper free functions

RemoteIndexStore shrinks from 11 methods to 8 by moving high-level operations into package-level helper free functions. Backends now implement only the per-file primitives (WriteSnapshotFile, ReadSnapshotFile, ListIndexKeys) plus listing, locks, and delete.

The new helpers (UploadIndexSnapshot, DownloadIndexSnapshot, ReadIndexSnapshotManifest, ListIndexSnapshots, CleanupIncompleteIndexSnapshots, ValidateIndexSnapshotManifest) carry the backend-agnostic logic -- directory walking, manifest build / validate, staging-dir + atomic rename, size verification, cleanup classification -- in one place. A future second backend reuses them.

Also renames ListNamespaceIndexes to ListNamespaceResources (it returns resources, not indexes).

No behaviour change.

Notes worth flagging during review:

- ReadSnapshotFile takes io.Writer (not io.ReadCloser) -- matches gocloud's bucket.Download and avoids extending the CDKBucket interface.

- The logging helpers take a log.Logger parameter. Production callers pass their existing context-rich loggers, so cleanup/upload logs now inherit the namespace/resource context they previously lost when going through a package-level logger.

- CleanupIncompleteIndexSnapshots takes a time.Time cutoff (olderThan) rather than a time.Duration (minAge). No internal time.Now() call; tests pin the cutoff explicitly.

* search: address review on ListIndexSnapshots error handling

ListIndexSnapshots now matches the old bucket-impl behaviour: one bad snapshot does not fail the whole listing. Any manifest read error is warned and skipped, so snapshot selection and cleanup continue with the remaining snapshots.

ErrSnapshotNotFound is logged silently. After the move to ListIndexKeys + per-key manifest reads, in-progress uploads (data files written, manifest not yet) and snapshots deleted by a concurrent cleanup are visible to the listing. Both are expected and should not produce a warning.

Also: gofmt fixes.

* search: drop orphaned ListIndexKeys godoc above listSubdirs

When ListIndexKeys was converted into a one-line wrapper around listSubdirs, its old godoc block was left in place above the new helper. The interface declaration carries the equivalent contract.

* search: clarify why UploadIndexSnapshot wants a build lock

The lock is not about avoiding upload conflicts (each upload generates its own ULID, so they can't conflict in the bucket). It's about avoiding multiple Grafana instances redundantly building and uploading the same index.

* search: drop history reference from ListIndexSnapshots godoc

The comment described the new behaviour in terms of how the old bucket impl behaved, which doesn't make sense to a reader without that context. Replaced with a self-contained description of what gets logged vs silenced.

commit.message:
Unified Storage: support cross-namespace ListModifiedSince (#124572)

Allows StorageBackend.ListModifiedSince to be called with an empty
namespace, returning rows across all namespaces for a given
(group, resource). Single-namespace callers are unchanged; the SQL
template keeps namespace first when present so existing query plans
are preserved.

SQL backend uses a conditional template clause; KV backend reuses
the underlying dataStore.Keys empty-namespace support. Both backends
dedup by (namespace, name) so same-named resources in different
namespaces each yield once. Adds a shared integration subtest and
snapshot coverage across all three SQL dialects.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
Provisioning: Skip strict validation on in-place resource renames (#124027)

* Provisioning: Skip strict validation on in-place resource renames

When a rename is processed as an in-place UPDATE (same name + group +
kind), the spec is not changing. Sending the unchanged spec through
strict server-side validation can fail for resources persisted before
the current schema was enforced — most visibly, dashboards saved long
before the CUE-based admission validator was wired up.

This adds SkipStrictValidation on ParsedResource and sets it from
RenameResourceFile in the same-identity branch so the in-place UPDATE
goes out with FieldValidation=Ignore. The DELETE+CREATE branch
(different identity) is untouched — fresh creates still validate
strictly. The pre-existing v1-dashboard exemption is preserved.

Includes a unit test that asserts FieldValidation=Ignore is sent on
the in-place rename, using a synthetic GVR so the assertion is not
masked by the dashboard exemption.

* Provisioning: Limit rename validation skip to pure path-only renames

The previous commit set SkipStrictValidation on every same-identity
rename, but FileActionRenamed in the incremental sync path comes from
git's similarity-based detection (~50% threshold) and can carry real
content changes. That meant a rename-with-edits could silently bypass
strict admission validation and let new bad data into the cluster.

Tighten the bypass: only skip strict validation when the git blob hash
of the old and new files matches (and both are non-empty). Pure
path-only renames keep the FieldValidation=Ignore behaviour for legacy
data; rename-with-edits keeps strict validation so any failure is
surfaced. Empty hashes fall back to strict to be safe.

Adds two new sub-tests for the strict cases (changed hash, empty hash)
and renames the existing one to make the hash-equal precondition
explicit.

* Provisioning: Add integration tests for rename validation discriminator

Adds two end-to-end tests in pkg/tests/apis/provisioning/git/incremental_test.go
that exercise both branches of the hash-based rename discriminator:

- PureRename_PreservesContent: a git mv with no body change leaves the
  spec untouched and only updates sourcePath. Companion to the unit
  tests that assert FieldValidation=Ignore on hash-equal renames.
- RenameWithEdit_AppliesNewContent: a git mv combined with a body edit
  in the same commit applies the new content at the new path. Confirms
  the rename-with-edits branch is not silently short-circuited.

Both tests run in ~17-20s each. All existing rename/move integration
tests continue to pass (9 tests, 102s combined).

Note: end-to-end coverage of the strict-validation rejection path
(rename-with-invalid-edit) is masked by the pre-existing v1 dashboard
exemption at parser.go (FIXME: f.GVR == DashboardResource always sends
Ignore). The unit tests in resources_remove_test.go assert the wire-
level behavior using a synthetic GVR to bypass the exemption.

* skipping strict validation only when hash didn't change

* removing unuseful test

* improving unit tests

---------

Co-authored-by: Daniele Ferru <daniele.ferru@grafana.com>

commit.message:
Alerting: auto-sync Mimir Alertmanager config into Grafana ExtraConfiguration (#119910)

* Alerting: Add syncExternalAlertmanager feature flag

* Alerting: Add external Alertmanager config sync

Background sync routine on MultiOrgAlertmanager that polls configured
Mimir/Cortex Alertmanager datasources per org and mirrors their config
into Grafana as an ExtraConfiguration, removing the need to manually
import every change.

Squashed from 28 commits of iterative review feedback (rounds 1-3 plus
follow-up cleanups). Highlights:

- admin_config API gains an external_alertmanager_uid field, gated by
  the alertingSyncExternalAlertmanager feature flag. POST validates the
  datasource as a mimir/cortex Alertmanager; GET surfaces the ini
  override; sync-disabled and ini-set states are rejected with the
  appropriate status code.
- ExternalAMSyncer encapsulates the sync state, HTTP transport, and
  per-tick dedup against the previous response-body hash held in
  process memory. Uses the same DataSourceRequestValidator the
  user-driven datasource proxy runs.
- Per-org metrics: external_alertmanager_config_sync_total,
  external_alertmanager_config_sync_failures_total (with reason label),
  external_alertmanager_config_sync_duration_seconds (per org), and
  external_alertmanager_config_sync_hash gauge.
- Convert API refuses imports for orgs where sync is configured, to
  avoid sync overwriting the imported config on its next tick.
- SaveAndApplyExtraConfiguration is the entry point shared by convert
  and sync; identifier-collision errors are surfaced as
  identifier_mismatch on the failures metric.

* Alerting: Move external AM sync into MAM per-org sync flow

Restructures external Alertmanager sync along yuri's review feedback:
the syncer's responsibility is now fetch-only; MAM owns the save+apply
path via its existing per-org sync loop. Eliminates the standalone
init-time Sync call that wrote to DB before MAM's Alertmanager
instances were initialised.

- ExternalAMSyncer exposes FetchExtraConfig(orgID) → (*ExtraConfig, hash)
  and MarkSaved(orgID, hash); the standalone Sync(orgIDs) method is gone.
  Hash gauge is set in MarkSaved so the metric reflects the last
  persisted config (not the last fetched one).
- MultiOrgAlertmanager.SyncAlertmanagersForOrgs runs the external
  fetch+save as a pre-pass before acquiring alertmanagersMtx (the lock
  would conflict with SaveAndApplyExtraConfiguration's RLock). The
  pre-pass skips orgs whose Alertmanager instance has not been created
  yet; the locked loop creates them and the next tick picks up the
  sync.
- getLatestConfigs reads after the pre-pass so the snapshot reflects
  any saves; no in-place mutation of the dbConfigs map.
- ExternalAMConfigSyncTotal docstring clarifies that it counts
  successful fetches (including no-op same-hash ticks), per yuri's nit.

commit.message:
Unified Storage: vector embedding reconciler (#124568)

* add vector write-path reconciler

Keeps the vector index in sync with ongoing dashboard writes via a
periodic reconciler that drains an in-memory dedup queue. Watch events
(via the resource server's broadcaster) and a startup catch-up that
replays ListModifiedSince since the stored cursor both feed the queue.

Key pieces:
- pkg/storage/unified/search/embed/reconciler: new package owning the
  per-(group,resource,namespace,name) dedup queue, broadcaster
  subscription, startup catch-up, per-cycle drain, and per-event retry
  cap. Coordinated across replicas via a per-pod-lifetime advisory lock
  (TryAcquireReconcilerLock) so only one replica reconciles at a time.
- pkg/storage/unified/search/vector: extends VectorBackend with
  SetLatestRV, TryAcquireReconcilerLock, and UpsertReplaceSubresources
  (atomic stale-subresource cleanup + upsert in one tx).
- pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go: hosts the backfiller and
  reconciler as VectorIndexer / VectorWriteReconciler interfaces, joins
  them in Stop via indexersWG. Resource package stays free of the
  concrete imports (would cycle).
- pkg/storage/unified/sql: cross-namespace ListModifiedSince
  (group/resource only; empty namespace = all namespaces). Adds
  conditional clause to the SQL template and a per-dialect snapshot
  test; KV backend gets matching behavior.
- pkg/setting: new vector_embedder.interval ini (default 60s) threads
  through to the reconciler's tick.

Backfiller refactor folded in:
- backfill.NewVectorBackfiller takes a *embedder.BatchEmbedder
  directly (drops the Embedder + Log option fields).
- embedder.BatchEmbedder.Model() exposes the model name to callers.
- sql/server.go::withVectorIndexers builds both the backfiller and
  the reconciler inline; the duplicate provider.go wrapper and the
  goroutine in sql/service.go::running are gone (the resource server
  owns the lifecycle).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix startup reconcile DESC-order data loss; rename indexer interfaces

reconcileSince previously flushed each batch via processBatch, which
advances the cursor. With the real SQL backend yielding rows ORDER BY
resource_version DESC, the first batch holds the highest RVs; advancing
after it pushes every later (lower-RV) batch below the freshly-bumped
cursor and silently drops those events. On a pgvector deploy, any
catch-up window > startupBatchSize (1000) embedded only the top 1000
resources by RV. The unit test masked it because the fake yielded in
ascending order.

Extract processEvents (no cursor advance) from processBatch. reconcileSince
now reads sinceRv once at start, accumulates max RV / lowest failed RV
across all batches, advances the cursor exactly once at the end.

Also rename:
- VectorIndexer -> Runnable
- VectorWriteReconciler (interface) -> BroadcasterConsumer

The ResourceServerOptions field name VectorWriteReconciler stays; only
the type was renamed so the abstractions no longer pretend to be
vector-domain types when they're really shape-only.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix linters: gofmt + drop unused currentBroadcaster

* drop stale comment about indexer construction in client.go

* requeue successful startup events on checkpoint write failure

Previously reconcileSince only re-enqueued failed events when
SetLatestRV errored. In the common case where every event embedded
successfully but the checkpoint write hit a transient failure, the
cursor stayed at its stale value and the queue was left empty — the
steady-state loop had nothing to retry against, so the cursor sat
behind real progress until a new write arrived and triggered another
advance. On restarts that meant repeated full catch-up over the same
range.

Track the successful events alongside the failed ones and re-enqueue
both on cursor-write failure. Re-enqueueing already-embedded events
is idempotent — UpsertReplaceSubresources just rewrites the same rows.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* rename remaining 'scanner' / 'write-path' refs to reconciler

* add go-mysql-server/sql/analyzer to enterprise_imports

* reconciler review follow-ups: setting rename, validation, tests

- Rename VectorBackfillerEnabled -> VectorIndexingEnabled
  (vector_backfiller_enabled -> vector_indexing_enabled). Single
  toggle on purpose: enabling embeddings without a reconciler would
  leave the index stale after every write.
- Move the reconciler tick interval out of [vector_embedder] and
  into [unified_storage] as vector_reconciler_interval. The embedder
  section is now provider-only.
- Logger label: log.New("embeddings_reconciler") (the per-line
  "reconciler:" prefix stays as a message namespace).
- New() rejects nil Storage/VectorBackend/BatchEmbedder up front to
  match NewVectorBackfiller.
- Tighten the New() doc: without a broadcaster the reconciler does
  startup catch-up and then ticks over an empty queue (no fallback
  poll of storage).
- Tests:
  * Run lifecycle: ExitsOnContextCancel, BlocksUntilLockAvailable,
    ContextCancelDuringLockWait, RunsStartupAndCycles.
  * Broadcaster path: DeliversWatchEvents (with a fakeBroadcaster),
    SubscribeErrorContinues.
  * processBatch requeue paths: GetLatestRV failure and SetLatestRV
    failure.
  * fakeVector gains getLatestRVErr / setLatestRVErr hooks; fakes_test
    gains fakeBroadcaster.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* add tests for pgvectorBackend.UpsertReplaceSubresources

Integration: atomic replace + delete-missing on a single UID, cross-UID
isolation, multi-UID single-tx, empty-input no-op, atomic rollback on
validation error.

Unit (sqlmock): empty-slice no-op, invalid-vector rejected before any
DB work, unknown-resource Begin+Rollback.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* review feedback: WaitGroup.Go, builder key by group/resource, pending naming

Addresses three review comments:

- server.go: use s.indexersWG.Go(...) (Go 1.25+) instead of the
  Add(1)/defer Done() boilerplate around each indexer goroutine.

- reconciler: key builders by group/resource (via a small builderKey
  helper) so multiple builders can share a group, and drop the
  redundant builder.Group() != ev.group check in enqueue — the lookup
  itself now enforces both.

- reconciler: rename the dedup map from "queue" to "pending" and
  thread the rename through methods (drainQueue -> drainPending,
  processQueue -> processPending, queueLen -> pendingLen,
  queueSupersedes -> supersedesPending, eventQueueKey -> pendingKey,
  queueMu -> pendingMu) and comments. Calling a map "queue" was
  misleading — there's no FIFO ordering, it's just a dedup buffer.
  Slice parameters that used "pending" as a local name are renamed
  to "batch" to keep s.pending vs a local "batch" unambiguous.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* gofmt: realign pending field

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

cursor stayed at its stale value and the queue was left empty — the
steady-state loop had nothing to retry against, so the cursor sat
behind real progress until a new write arrived and triggered another
advance. On restarts that meant repeated full catch-up over the same
range.

Track the successful events alongside the failed ones and re-enqueue
both on cursor-write failure. Re-enqueueing already-embedded events
is idempotent — UpsertReplaceSubresources just rewrites the same rows.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* rename remaining 'scanner' / 'write-path' refs to reconciler

* add go-mysql-server/sql/analyzer to enterprise_imports

* reconciler review follow-ups: setting rename, validation, tests

- Rename VectorBackfillerEnabled -> VectorIndexingEnabled
  (vector_backfiller_enabled -> vector_indexing_enabled). Single
  toggle on purpose: enabling embeddings without a reconciler would
  leave the index stale after every write.
- Move the reconciler tick interval out of [vector_embedder] and
  into [unified_storage] as vector_reconciler_interval. The embedder
  section is now provider-only.
- Logger label: log.New("embeddings_reconciler") (the per-line
  "reconciler:" prefix stays as a message namespace).
- New() rejects nil Storage/VectorBackend/BatchEmbedder up front to
  match NewVectorBackfiller.
- Tighten the New() doc: without a broadcaster the reconciler does
  startup catch-up and then ticks over an empty queue (no fallback
  poll of storage).
- Tests:
  * Run lifecycle: ExitsOnContextCancel, BlocksUntilLockAvailable,
    ContextCancelDuringLockWait, RunsStartupAndCycles.
  * Broadcaster path: DeliversWatchEvents (with a fakeBroadcaster),
    SubscribeErrorContinues.
  * processBatch requeue paths: GetLatestRV failure and SetLatestRV
    failure.
  * fakeVector gains getLatestRVErr / setLatestRVErr hooks; fakes_test
    gains fakeBroadcaster.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* add tests for pgvectorBackend.UpsertReplaceSubresources

Integration: atomic replace + delete-missing on a single UID, cross-UID
isolation, multi-UID single-tx, empty-input no-op, atomic rollback on
validation error.

Unit (sqlmock): empty-slice no-op, invalid-vector rejected before any
DB work, unknown-resource Begin+Rollback.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* review feedback: WaitGroup.Go, builder key by group/resource, pending naming

Addresses three review comments:

- server.go: use s.indexersWG.Go(...) (Go 1.25+) instead of the
  Add(1)/defer Done() boilerplate around each indexer goroutine.

- reconciler: key builders by group/resource (via a small builderKey
  helper) so multiple builders can share a group, and drop the
  redundant builder.Group() != ev.group check in enqueue — the lookup
  itself now enforces both.

- reconciler: rename the dedup map from "queue" to "pending" and
  thread the rename through methods (drainQueue -> drainPending,
  processQueue -> processPending, queueLen -> pendingLen,
  queueSupersedes -> supersedesPending, eventQueueKey -> pendingKey,
  queueMu -> pendingMu) and comments. Calling a map "queue" was
  misleading — there's no FIFO ordering, it's just a dedup buffer.
  Slice parameters that used "pending" as a local name are renamed
  to "batch" to keep s.pending vs a local "batch" unambiguous.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
