commit.message:
Scopes: Refactor recent scopes (#123823)

* Refactor recent scopes

* Fix import path for ScopesSelectorServiceState and refactor useRecentScopes

- Fix TS2305: import ScopesSelectorServiceState from ScopesSelectorService (not types)
- Refactor: extract resolveParentNodeTitle helper to eliminate duplicated defaultPath logic
- Refactor: replace .map().filter() with .flatMap() throughout

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* E2E: handle RTK cache hits in selectScope helper

When a scope has been selected previously in the same session, its data
is kept in the RTK Query cache via the useRecentScopesApi subscription.
Subsequent selections of the same scope return from cache without making
an HTTP request, causing waitForResponse to time out.

Race against the checkbox/radio becoming checked so the helper works
correctly whether data comes from the network or the cache.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Scopes: address code review findings in recent scopes refactor

- Sort names before joining as namesKey in useScopesById/useScopeNodesByName
  so that order-insensitive name sets produce the same cache key
- Remove spurious async from validateStoredRecentScopes (body is synchronous)
- Use jest.requireActual for storage constants in tests so they don't
  diverge silently if the real constant values change

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(scopes): wrap store I/O in try/catch in recentScopesStorage

Move store.get inside the try block so sandboxed-iframe SecurityErrors
are caught, and wrap store.set + dispatchEvent in their own try/catch
for the same reason.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(scopes): subscribe to native storage event for cross-tab sync

The custom RECENT_SCOPES_CHANGED_EVENT only fires in the same tab.
Add a native 'storage' listener so changes from other open Grafana
tabs are picked up immediately, keeping recent-scope lists in sync
across windows.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(e2e): race applyScopes response against drawer-close for RTK cache hits

When scope data is already cached in RTK Query, applyScopes makes no
HTTP request and waitForResponse times out. Apply the same Promise.race
pattern used in selectScope: race the network response against the
drawer closing, then confirm with a final waitForSelector.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor(scopes): remove redundant recentScopesValidation and lazy effect

The manual validation in readStoredRecentScopes already filters invalid
entries synchronously at read time, making the async Zod layer
redundant. Remove recentScopesValidation.ts, the lazy useEffect, and
its test mock. Zod is not statically imported to avoid adding it to the
bundle.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(scopes): add unit tests for recentScopesStorage

Add direct test coverage for readStoredRecentScopes and writeRecentScope,
including: empty/null/malformed store values, invalid entry shapes,
version-mismatch stripping of scopeNodeId, deduplication by fingerprint,
max-entry cap, defaultPath-based scopeNodeId omission, and sandboxed-
iframe error handling (SecurityError on get/set).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(scopes): fix import order in useRecentScopesApi

Move createSelector import from @reduxjs/toolkit before react to satisfy
the import/order ESLint rule.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(scopes): fix ScopeNode type import in useRecentScopes test

ScopeNode from @grafana/data has disableMultiSelect as optional
(boolean | undefined), but useScopeNodesByName returns the stricter
type from endpoints.gen where it is required (boolean). Import ScopeNode
from the correct module and add the missing field to the mock factory.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(e2e): handle RTK cache hits in openScopesSelector, expandScopesSelection, searchScopes

When scope node children are already in the RTK Query cache from a prior interaction, no HTTP request fires and waitForResponse times out. Apply the same Promise.race pattern used in selectScope and applyScopes to race against a UI-settled check.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(e2e): revert searchScopes race and suppress dangling responsePromise

Two problems with the previous Promise.race additions:

1. searchScopes raced against any existing tree item, which resolved
   immediately with stale content before new search results loaded.
   Reverted to the original 'await responsePromise'.

2. On the cache-hit path, the losing responsePromise outlived the
   Promise.race and was rejected by Playwright teardown, surfacing as
   a spurious 'Test timeout exceeded' error. Added responsePromise.catch
   to suppress it in selectScope, applyScopes, openScopesSelector, and
   expandScopesSelection.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor(scopes): rename useRecentScopesApi → useScopesApi, fix selector memoization

- Rename: the hook contains generic RTK Query helpers (useScopesById,
  useScopeNodesByName), not recent-scopes-specific logic
- Fix createSelector(state => state) pattern that defeated memoization;
  replace with useMemo + inline selector + shallowEqual
- Fix defaultPath.length gate: use <= 1 (not === 0) so leaf nodes are
  fetched when defaultPath has exactly one segment
- Add useScopesApi.test.ts covering selector stability and subscription
- Update useRecentScopes.test.ts: remove dead mocks, add edge-case test

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(scopes): dispatch event outside try, retry write on QuotaExceededError

- Move window.dispatchEvent() outside the try block so a throwing event
  listener is not silently swallowed
- On QuotaExceededError retry once with the oldest entry dropped; if the
  retry also fails, give up silently (storage unavailable)
- Add tests for all three QuotaExceededError paths: retry succeeds,
  retry fails, single-entry list (no retry attempted)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(scopes): remove dead parentNodeId fallback in ScopesInput

parentNodeId on SelectedScope is never populated in production code and
is never read back by any service method. Remove the dead fallback in
ScopesInput (prefer scopeNode.spec.parentName) and add a TODO comment
on the type for eventual removal.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(e2e): attach .catch() before Promise.race in scope helpers

Attaching .catch() after an awaited Promise does not prevent an
unhandled rejection — the rejection fires at await time. Move .catch()
onto the promise before passing it to Promise.race so cache-hit paths
that never receive an HTTP response don't leave a dangling rejection.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(scopes): extract EMPTY_OBSERVABLE to module level in recentScopesActions

new Observable() constructed inline as the useObservable fallback creates
a new instance on every render when services is undefined, causing
useObservable to tear down and resubscribe on every render cycle.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(e2e): attach .catch() before Promise.race in openScopesSelector and expandScopesSelection

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(e2e): increase Navigate between dashboards timeout to 90s

Test takes ~30s locally; CI shard resource pressure pushes it past the default 30s limit.

HTTP request and waitForResponse times out. Apply the same Promise.race
pattern used in selectScope: race the network response against the
drawer closing, then confirm with a final waitForSelector.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

redundant. Remove recentScopesValidation.ts, the lazy useEffect, and
its test mock. Zod is not statically imported to avoid adding it to the
bundle.

including: empty/null/malformed store values, invalid entry shapes,
version-mismatch stripping of scopeNodeId, deduplication by fingerprint,

Authn: Enrich gRPC log fields with client, code, namespace, and header names (#124411)

* Authn: Enrich gRPC log fields with client, code, namespace, and header names

Add grpclog.AddFields calls to Service.Authenticate so the existing
gRPC logging interceptor's "finished call" line includes which authn
client handled the request, the response code, the request namespace,
and the names of HTTP headers sent (values excluded).

This makes it possible to filter and correlate authn requests in Loki
without adding new log lines.

commit.message:
GrafanaUI: Add stable container data-testids for plugin-e2e fixtures (#124120)

* GrafanaUI: Add stable container data-testids for plugin-e2e

Adds container data-testids to Select, MultiSelect, RadioGroup, Switch,
InlineSwitch, ColorPicker and UnitPicker so plugin-e2e tests can locate
each control by its first occurrence on the page without scoping
through implementation-detail DOM queries.

Refs grafana/plugin-tools#2583, fixes #124091.

* GrafanaUI: Update cloud-monitoring snapshot for Select container testid

The new default `data-testid` on Select/SelectBase is now rendered into
the cloud-monitoring VariableQueryEditor snapshot.

* GrafanaUI: Stop duplicating Switch testid inside InlineSwitch

Switch now accepts a `data-testid` prop that overrides the default
`Switch.container` testid. InlineSwitch passes its own
`InlineSwitch.container` into the inner Switch instead of adding a
second testid on an outer wrapper, so each instance carries exactly
one container testid and the Switch / InlineSwitch selectors return
disjoint sets.

* GrafanaUI: Remove InlineSwitch selector — not needed by plugin-e2e

InlineSwitch wraps Switch internally, so both carry the Switch.container
testid. Plugin-e2e does not differentiate them, so the separate
InlineSwitch selector and the data-testid override machinery were
unnecessary. Reverts to a simple hardcoded testid on the Switch wrapper.

* GrafanaUI: Remove ColorPicker container selector — existing colorswatch testid is sufficient

ColorSwatch already has data-testid="data-testid-colorswatch" across
all Grafana versions. Adding a second testid via ColorPicker.container
is redundant and risks breaking external consumers that depend on the
existing testid.

* GrafanaUI: Add versioned fallback selectors for older Grafana versions

Adds fallback CSS selectors for Select, MultiSelect, RadioGroup, Switch
and UnitPicker so plugin-e2e tests can find these components on Grafana
versions older than 13.1.0 (where our new data-testid selectors were
introduced).

Fallback strategies by component:
- Select: CSS class label grafana-select-value-container (8.5.0+)
- MultiSelect: CSS class label grafana-select-value-container-multi (8.5.0+)
- RadioGroup: role="radiogroup" (10.0+), :has() with name pattern (8.5+)
- Switch: role="switch" (12.0+), :has() with sibling pattern (8.5+)
- UnitPicker: :has() with Cascader nesting pattern (8.5.0+)

Also adds VersionedStringOrCssSelector type to support mixing string
(data-testid) and function (CSS selector) entries in the same versioned
selector.

* Revert "GrafanaUI: Add versioned fallback selectors for older Grafana versions"

This reverts commit 6716d2a22257abbab16a277829bb72b50fe5cace.

* GrafanaUI: Address PR review feedback from joshhunt

RadioButtonGroup: destructure data-testid from props so consumer-
provided values override the default (matching the Select pattern).

UnitPicker: remove the wrapper div, extend Cascader to accept a
data-testid prop and apply it to its existing root div. UnitPicker
now passes the testid through as a Cascader prop instead.

* GrafanaUI: Add tests for custom data-testid override on Select and RadioGroup

Adds override tests for MultiSelect, AsyncMultiSelect, and
RadioButtonGroup — verifying that a consumer-provided data-testid
replaces the default selector value.

SelectBase already had this test.

* GrafanaUI: Add test for custom data-testid on Cascader

commit.message:
IAM: Add spec.externalGroups to Team API (#124679)

* wip

* Move validate to the reconciler, change registration

* Address Claude's review findings

* Team API: make spec.externalGroups optional

Regenerate Go/TS/OpenAPI artifacts for the optional `?:` field, drop the
nil→[]string{} coercion in toTeamObject, remove the field from the
integration-test JSON expectation, and switch validate_test type
assertions to errors.As (errorlint).

* Team API: trim OSS externalGroups round-trip test

Mode<5 hydration depends on which ExternalGroupReconciler is bound; the
OSS test had baked in a noop-only assumption that doesn't hold when the
enterprise reconciler is in scope. Round-trip coverage already lives in
the enterprise suite (doExternalGroupsReconcileTests); keep only the
universal dup-validation case here.

* Sorted externalGroups with mutation + legacy support

* Team API: cascade team_group cleanup on Delete; tighten reconciler interface

- Add DeleteAll to ExternalGroupReconciler so deleting a Team also removes
  its team_group rows in the same SQL transaction as the team row.
- Drop NormalizeExternalGroups: admission Mutate canonicalizes the spec
  before storage, and the reconciler does its own normalization.
- Simplify validateExternalGroups by dropping the redundant early-return
  branch on empty input.
- Tighten ExternalGroupReconciler godoc and document the lexicographic-
  order contract on ListByTeams.

* Team API: hoist GetTeamInternalID out of DeleteTeam tx; doc polish

- DeleteTeam: resolve team_id before opening WithTransaction, mirroring
  UpdateTeam's SQLite-deadlock-avoidance pattern; collapse redundant
  pre-tx + in-tx Validate() calls.
- ExternalGroupReconciler.Reconcile godoc: document that `desired` is the
  post-admission spec and implementations should treat duplicates and
  whitespace defensively.
- MutateOnCreateAndUpdate godoc: replace the storage-backend parenthetical
  with the cleaner "consistent across dual-writer modes" framing.
- Stub-test assertion message: drop the misleading "un-normalized" wording
  now that admission Mutate canonicalizes upstream.

commit.message:
Tracing: Fix span duration handling in tracing loops for grafana queries (#123456)

fix(tracing): replace defer span.End() inside loops with direct calls

In Go, defer executes when the enclosing function returns, not at the
end of a loop iteration. Using defer span.End() inside a loop causes
all spans to close simultaneously when the function exits, making
per-iteration span durations incorrect.

Fixed in two places:
- pkg/expr/graph.go: execute() — each SSE.ExecuteNode span now ends
  immediately after the node finishes, including the early-return path
- pkg/tsdb/graphite/query.go: query loop — each graphite query span
  now ends at the correct point including error paths

Fixes #123419

commit.message:
Alerting: Support creating Grafana-managed rules without a group (#120228)

* Alerting: Allow creating rules without an evaluation group

This lets users create rules by directly specifying an evaluation interval, without needing to create an evaluation group. This uses the new app-platform rules apis to create rules without groups, and adds a new "No group" option in the UI that opens the rule form with the evaluation group section hidden and the evaluate every field shown.

* Alerting: Clean up ungrouped rule handling in view and edit

Ungrouped rules don't have a group name and should be treated accordingly in the edit page and in the breadcrumbs. Breadcrumbs now all say `{Rule Title} (Ungrouped)` instead of the uid mask. Same for the edit page.

* Update to use radio button for evaluation mode selection

* fix lints and i18n

* adjust i18n label

* fix tests

Co-authored-by: Copilot <copilot@github.com>

* Hide virtual groups from evaluation groupd dropdown

* Fix missing translations

* Fix tests

* Refactor tests and cleanup changes

- Moved collator + sortByLabel above namespaceToGroupOptions so the function reference is in scope at module init time
- Added unit tests for missing cases in GrafanaEvaluationBehaviour.test.ts
- Added setCreateGrafanaRuleResolver test helper
- Refactored groupOptions in GrafanaEvaluationBehavior

* Fix error when migrating grouped rule to ungrouped

- Fixed error when trying to update grouped rule to ungrouped
- Fixed duplicated translation string
- Added regression tests for AlertRuleForm.test.tsx to address different grouped / ungrouped use cases

* Hide ungrouped creation / edit behind alerting.rulesAPIV2 feature flag

* Fix tests

* Address code review comments

* Update translations

* Alerting: address review feedback on ungrouped rule editor

- Encapsulate ungrouped rule create/replace mutations behind useSaveUngroupedGrafanaRule
- Rename EvaluationMode literals to rule-based/group-based and use watched isUngroupedRule directly
- Drop synthetic (Ungrouped) breadcrumb label in RuleViewer and GroupDetailsPage

* Alerting: restore empty-group short-circuit in groupOptions memo

Without it, group-based mode with no group selected injects a synthetic
option with an empty name and the current interval into the dropdown.

* Alerting: fix duplicate None pills and add evaluateEvery integration tests

Fix duplicate "None" pills in pending period and keep-firing-for quick-pick
rows when typing an incomplete evaluation interval (e.g. "3" mid-keystroke).
safeParsePrometheusDuration returns 0 for unparseable strings, causing all
five multiples to collapse to 0s and render as identical "None" buttons.

Add integration tests for evaluateEvery validation in both rule-based mode
and the group creation modal, replacing the standalone validator unit tests.

* Update translations

* Remove unnecessary exports and consts

* Get rule type from form values

* Simplify api adapter

* Rename useSaveUngroupedGrafanaRule to useUpsertUngroupedGrafanaRule

commit.message:
Alerting: Support history and trash list selectors in legacy storage (#124349)

* Alerting: Support history and trash list selectors in legacy storage

Plumb the grafana.app/get-history and grafana.app/get-trash label selectors
through the AlertRule and RecordingRule legacy storage so the resources behave
consistently with unified storage (pkg/storage/unified/apistore/util.go).

History requests use the metadata.name field selector to identify the rule and
return its revision history; trash requests return tombstones for soft-deleted
rules with a deletion timestamp set. Each path filters by rule type so the two
resources only surface their own kind. Adds a shared ParseListMode helper, new
provisioning service methods (GetAlertRuleVersions, GetDeletedAlertRules), and
conversion APIs for AlertRuleVersion -> k8s resources.

* Alerting: Add e2e tests for history and trash list selectors

Cover the grafana.app/get-history and grafana.app/get-trash label selectors
end-to-end for AlertRule and RecordingRule. The tests exercise version listing
across multiple updates, rule-type isolation between alerting and recording
rules, soft-delete tombstones with deletion timestamps, and selector input
validation (missing metadata.name, unknown rules, mixed labels, non-true
values).

commit.message:
AnnotationListPlugin: rebuild row layout to stop heading + timestamp overlap (#124398)

* fix(annolist): rebuild row layout to stop heading + timestamp overlap

The Card component is built for a multi-row layout: Card.Heading and
Card.Description both default to gridColumnEnd: 'Tags' so each spans the
middle column horizontally. AnnoListPanel rendered them in a custom
single-row grid where that span made the heading and timestamp cells
visually overlap.

Card's internal styles couldn't be overridden cleanly — @emotion/css
cx() merges the className we pass with the internal class into one,
where neither selector-doubling (&&) nor !important reliably won the
cascade. Replacing Card with a plain-div CSS grid we own removes the
fight entirely. Visual styling (background, hover, padding, radius)
mirrors the previous Card look.

* fix(annolist): rebuild row layout to stop heading + timestamp overlap

The Card component is built for a multi-row layout: Card.Heading and
Card.Description both default to gridColumnEnd: 'Tags' so each spans the
middle column horizontally. AnnoListPanel rendered them in a custom
single-row grid where that span made the heading and timestamp cells
visually overlap.

Card's internal styles couldn't be overridden cleanly — @emotion/css
cx() merges the className we pass with the internal class into one,
where neither selector-doubling (&&) nor !important reliably won the
cascade. Replacing Card with a plain-div CSS grid we own removes the
fight entirely. Visual styling (background, hover, padding, radius)
mirrors the previous Card look.

commit.message:
DashboardDS: Fix Mixed panels not updating on time-range change with stale upstreams (#124665)

* DashboardDS: Fix Mixed panels not updating on time-range change with stale upstreams

In a Mixed datasource panel where each subquery uses the "-- Dashboard --"
datasource, a time-range change can leave the chain panel rendering data from
the previous range. The upstream `SceneQueryRunner` exposes its results via a
ReplaySubject(1) that retains the previous Done state. On time-range change
the dashboard datasource subscribes to that stream and immediately receives
the stale Done; `emitFirstLoadedDataIfMixedDS` then matches that stale Done
with `first(Done || Error)` and completes the substream before the upstream
re-runs for the new range. With a slow upstream, the real Done lands after the
substream is already closed, so the chain never re-renders.

Drop terminal emissions whose upstream request range does not match the
chain's request range before the Mixed-DS operator chain runs. This catches
the stale ReplaySubject replay on time-range change without affecting refresh
or editor-add flows (same range in both cases).

* DashboardDS: Restrict range filter to Mixed-DS and harden regression test

Self-review follow-up to the prior commit:

- Gate the new range-mismatch filter to the Mixed-DS path
  (`requestId.includes(MIXED_REQUEST_PREFIX)`). The bug only fires there
  because `emitFirstLoadedDataIfMixedDS` uses `first(Done || Error)` to
  complete the substream; the non-Mixed path stays open and naturally
  re-emits when the fresh Done arrives. Applying the filter outside that
  path was dropping legitimate Done emissions for chain panels that have
  a `PanelTimeRange` override (timeFrom, timeShift), which leaves them
  hanging in Loading forever.
- Add a regression test covering the non-Mixed override case so the
  scope of the filter stays locked in.
- Switch the test helper to `ReplaySubject(1)` and push the stale Done
  BEFORE subscribing. The earlier `Subject` mock did not exercise the
  synchronous-on-subscribe replay that is the heart of the production
  bug.
- Extract the range equality check to a small `isSameRange` helper for
  readability.

* DashboardDS: Drop internal tracker reference from test comment

commit.message:
K8s Dashboards: Fix folder permission check to use dashboards:create (#124612)

* K8s Dashboards: Fix folder permission check to use dashboards:create

The verifyFolderAccessPermissions method was checking CanEdit on the
folder access subresource, which maps to folders:write. This meant
enterprise users with custom RBAC roles granting only dashboards:create
+ dashboards:write on a folder were denied dashboard creation, because
they lacked folders:write.

Replace the folder access subresource fetch with a direct
accessClient.Check() call for VerbCreate on the dashboards resource
scoped to the target folder. This checks the semantically correct
permission (dashboards:create) and works for both enterprise custom
roles and OSS resource permission levels (Edit grants the folders:edit
action set which includes dashboards:create).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* K8s Dashboards: Simplify verifyFolderAccessPermissions signature

Both call sites pass a single folder UID, so the variadic parameter is
unnecessary. Take a single folderID string instead.

commit.message:
Scopes: Skip scope_node URL write when defaultPath is source of truth (#124054)

* Scopes: Skip scope_node URL write when defaultPath is source of truth

When a scope has spec.defaultPath, the URL was redundantly carrying
scope_node alongside scopes — exposing implementation-detail IDs that
change across versions and making URLs non-portable.

Re-applies #123130 (reverted in #123626) with one added safeguard:
setEnabled defers its URL write when scope metadata has not loaded yet,
closing the race window where @grafana/scenes' ScopesVariable.setContext
could write a stale fallback during the gap between applyScopes' two
updateState calls.

Also adds defaultPath to gdev-app1, gdev-app2, and defines gdev-cluster1
in the devenv config so the local scope tree has multiple defaultPath
scopes available for testing transitions (cluster1 was referenced in
the tree but undefined, returning 404 from fetchMultipleScopes).

Refs grafana/hyperion-planning#542

* Scopes: Cover setReadOnly, cleanUp, and setEnabled edge cases

Adds tests for previously-uncovered code paths in ScopesService:
- setEnabled with empty appliedScopes (firstScope-falsy short-circuit
  in the defer guard introduced earlier in this PR)
- setEnabled called with the current enabled state (no-op early return)
- setReadOnly state changes and selector close-and-reset side effect
- cleanUp does not throw on subscriber teardown

Brings file-level line coverage from 85.84% to 91.15% and addresses
the @grafana/grafana-operator-experience-squad coverage check that
flagged a 0.03% drop on the prior commit.

Refs grafana/hyperion-planning#542

* chore: trigger fresh CI run

Empty commit to trigger a full re-run of squad-level coverage workflows
on the same content as 0517f9ff0c0.

* Scopes: Pin setEnabled URL write test; simplify devenv titles

Add a test asserting setEnabled writes scope_node when scopes are
unchanged at navigation time, since applyScopes can't fire in that
path. Without this assertion, the URL write inside setEnabled reads
as redundant to the location subscription's write and could be
removed as cleanup.

Update devenv scope titles for app1, app2, and shared-service to
include "(defaultPath)" — the marker is then visible in the scope
selector UI without requiring YAML-comment archaeology. Drops the
now-redundant inline comments on app1 and app2.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Update title for cluster1 scope definition

commit.message:
unified-storage: fix lease and sqlkv logging (#125009)

By referencing `grafana-app-sdk`'s `DefaultLogger` in a package-level variable,
the underlying logger depends on package import order (as it's updated by
`pkg/infra/log` at `init()` time). This commit initializes the `lease` and
`sqlkv` loggers in constructors, at which point it's safe to assume that the
SDK logger points to the application logger.

commit.message:
Dashboard: Add annotation CRUD to mutation API (#123939)

* Dashboard: Add annotation CRUD to mutation API

Add ADD_ANNOTATION, UPDATE_ANNOTATION, REMOVE_ANNOTATION, and
LIST_ANNOTATIONS commands to the Dashboard Mutation API so external
tooling (e.g. the Assistant) can manage dashboard annotation layers
without manipulating the scene tree directly.

Annotations are keyed by name (matches variable command semantics).
The built-in Grafana annotation cannot be removed and a second
built-in cannot be added; the v2 load path auto-injects it on next
save/load anyway.

* fix: remove duplicate schema re-exports, use payloads directly for types

* fix: reject UPDATE_ANNOTATION rename when target name already exists

* feat: UPDATE_ANNOTATION accepts partial AnnotationQueryKind with deep-merge

Mirrors UPDATE_PANEL semantics: only provided fields are applied, object
fields are deep-merged, arrays (filter.ids) are replaced wholesale. Lets
the LLM say "change just iconColor" without re-emitting the full kind.

- New partialAnnotationQueryKindSchema makes every spec field optional and
  threads partial query/filter sub-schemas through.
- updateAnnotation handler reads existing kind via annotationLayerToKind,
  merges the partial input via local mergeReplacingArrays helper (kept
  inline to avoid touching shipped updatePanel.ts), and rebuilds the
  layer in place.
- Rename gated on payload.annotation.spec.name being defined.
- Tests cover partial preservation, nested query.spec merge, array
  replacement, rename via partial, and empty-spec no-op.

commit.message:
Alerting: remove MergeMatchers from ExtraConfiguration (#124856)

* alerting: remove MergeMatchers from ExtraConfiguration struct

Remove the MergeMatchers field and its equality-type validation from
ExtraConfiguration. Remove the corresponding parameter from the Prometheus
import API params struct and fix the orphaned comment that was attached to
the Replace field after the removal. Drop the field from the stored JSON
test fixture.

* alerting: remove merge matchers routing logic

Remove ValidateSubtreeMatchers, MergeRoutes, MergeInhibitRules, and
checkIfMatchersUsed from the merge package along with the associated error
variables (ErrInvalidMatchers, ErrDuplicateMatchers, ErrSubtreeMatchersConflict).
Remove ErrRouteConflictingMatchers and MakeErrRouteConflictingMatchers from
models/errors.go. Drop the conflict-check branches in UpdatePolicyTree and
UpdateManagedRoute that returned those errors.

* alerting: remove X-Grafana-Alerting-Merge-Matchers HTTP header

Remove the mergeMatchersHeader constant, parseMergeMatchersHeader, and
formatMergeMatchers from the Prometheus import API handler. Stop reading
the header on POST and stop echoing it back on GET.

* alerting: update tests after MergeMatchers removal

Remove MergeMatchers from all test fixtures and helper functions. Drop
tests that existed solely to cover merge-matchers validation
(TestValidateSubtreeMatchers, TestCheckIfMatchersUsed,
TestParseMergeMatchersHeader, TestFormatMergeMatchers,
ErrRouteConflictingMatchers scenario). Remove the now-obsolete
"cannot be fully merged" test case in TestConfigRevisionImported.
Collapse the duplicate TestApplyConfigWithExtraConfigsConvertsMimirReceivers
into TestApplyConfigWithExtraConfigs and update its assertions to reflect
that Mimir receivers are always converted regardless of any flag.
Add TestApplyConfigWithExtraConfigs and
TestCompareAndSendConfigurationConvertsMimirReceivers to cover the
receiver-conversion path.

Update TestIntegrationExtraConfigsConflicts to test the conflict that
still exists: creating a managed route whose name matches an imported
route's identifier returns a Conflict error.

* alerting: remove dead MergeExtraConfig calls from UpdateManagedRoute and DeleteManagedRoute

The calls were either no-ops (Update: error silently logged and ignored)
or guarding against scenarios that no longer exist (Delete: merge
matchers conflict was the only way MergeExtraConfig could fail on a
valid config). Neither call has tests covering them.

docs(alerting): document inhibition rules toggle and managed routes (#124373)

Inhibition rules only take effect when the alertingMultiplePolicies feature
toggle is enabled, but the API has no gating, so users can create rules that
silently never apply. Document the requirement up front, update the API
version reference from v0alpha1 to v1beta1, and add a section describing how
Grafana-managed rules differ from imported rules in their interaction with
managed routes.

Alerting: External Alertmanager sender to use stable fingerprint for Alert (#125161)

* ngalert/sender: use stable FNV fingerprint in Alert.Hash()

Replace Labels.Hash() (xxhash, non-stable across runs) with
model.LabelSet.Fingerprint() (FNV-1A over sorted label pairs).
This matches the fingerprint Prometheus Alertmanager uses for alerts,
so the 7-char hash in "Sending alert" ruler logs can be directly
correlated with alertmanager-side logs.

commit.message:
Alerting: Create PostableUserConfig domain layer model AMConfigV1 (#125154)

This pull request contains prep work needed to eventually have separate, distinct types for Alertmanager config in the DB, domain, and API layers.

This PR does not tackle adding UIDs to the domain layer or any structural changes we want to make there. It also does not include separating the DB layer from the API PostableUserConfig.

Included in this PR is is the separation of the API layer from the domain layer. done by creating a copy of PostableUserConfig, named AMConfigV1, as well as some nested types.

These are placed in a new package pkg/services/ngalert/notifier/legacy_storage/v1 to avoid cycles for now, but can eventually live in pkg/services/ngalert/models.

The types are copied verbatim and should not include any functional changes, the intent here is not to start defining our domain layer but to untangle how the codebase references DB/API definitions in places it shouldn't and give us a domain layer type that we can refactor in small iterations without worrying about DB/API serialization.

References to PostableUserConfig and the above nested types and replaced with the domain layer types in as many places as is reasonable, ensuring the boundary between DB <-> Domain <-> API is crossed using newly created compat functions.

commit.message:
unified-storage: add garbage collection to leases (#124862)

The `lease` package, as is currently being used by the KV storage backend, creates one entry in the `LeasesSection` of the underlying KV store for every resource update (create, update, delete). To avoid unbounded growth of this section, this PR introduces a self-contained garbage collection mechanism that periodically scans the leases section and deletes entries that have expired or been released for longer than a grace period (currently 1 minute).

The implementation does a best-effort attempt at avoiding duplicated work: before starting the GC scan, the process will read a private key to see if any other instance is currently already running it. It does not use the same mechanism as the lease manager itself for a couple of reasons: 1) to avoid having the GC process create more keys for itself to clean up later; and 2) to avoid circular dependencies, where the lease manager relies on GC to cleanup its keys, and GC uses the manager to perform that job.

An important change from now on is that lease generations are now _not_ monotonically increasing: the GC process may delete entries that have long expired, which would cause the generation to be reset the next time a client attempts to acquire that lease. To deal with the inherent race between lease acquisition and a concurrent run of garbage collection, the `Acquire` function was updated to also perform a `BatchOpUpdate` operation on the previous generation when attempting to create the next one: in other words, creating generation `N` (where `N > 1`) should only succeed if generation `N-1` still exists. Without that, another client could observe an emtpy lease history, create a lease with `generation=1`, and two clients would believe they hold the same lease at the same time.

The garbage collection goroutine is created by default when a manager is instantiated. The KV backend was updated to stop the GC goroutine in its `Stop()` function.

Part of: https://github.com/grafana/hyperion-planning/issues/608

IAM: Authorize teams resource for access-policy identities (#125118)

The standalone IAM apiserver's authorizer in NewAPIService had no case
for the teams resource, so access-policy callers (e.g. the zanzana MT
reconciler) listing teams fell through to the default deny.

Mirror the users pattern: require an access-policy identity, then defer
to the access-checker so the token's permissions decide the outcome.

commit.message:
Grafana CLI: add admin db-migrate subcommand (#125182)

* Grafana CLI: add admin db-migrate subcommand

Wraps server.InitializeForCLI through runDbCommand so a paused tenant's
schema can be advanced without booting the full Grafana process. The
runner init drives the migration as a side effect; logLastMigration then
reports the most recent migration_log row.

Enterprise builds (e.g. hosted-grafana-pro) automatically pick up
*EnterpriseMigrations via the existing wireexts overlay — verified
empirically on grafana-pro 13.1.0: a single `cli admin db-migrate`
invocation applies all 863 OSS + enterprise migrations, with no second
`grafana server` boot needed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Grafana CLI: use dialect-aware boolean in migration_log query

Pass `dialect.BooleanValue(true)` instead of a literal `true` so the
comparison binds correctly on every dialect (MySQL/SQLite store success
as 0/1, Postgres as native bool).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Datasource Proxy: Restrict full access to setting.Cfg (#125180)

Plugin Proxy: Narrow data source config to DataSourceProxySettings

The data source proxy only needs a handful of fields from setting.Cfg.
Introduce a focused DataSourceProxySettings struct that exposes only
those fields, load Azure settings lazily via a resolver callback so the
proxy avoids touching Azure configuration unless an Azure-authenticated
route is matched, and pass the new struct through the datasource proxy
service in place of *setting.Cfg.

sidebar sections addressable by name in the accessibility tree.

Render the rule name as <h1> (was a styled <span>) so screen readers and
automated tests can locate the page heading by role.

Three happy-path specs covering the new rulesAPIV2 flows:
- rule-based evaluation interval (ungrouped)
- group-based interval with a new group created via modal
- group-based interval with an existing group

Each test asserts the post-save rule viewer shows the correct name,
evaluation interval, and contact point.

Adds AlertRuleEditPage and AlertRuleViewPage POMs with accessibility-first
selectors.

* Alerting: strengthen GMA rule e2e tests with full viewer assertions

- Switch feature toggle from URL params to test.use({ featureToggles })
- Add label and annotation to creation flow; assert both on viewer
- Add folder and group breadcrumb assertions
- Seed rule-based interval rule via k8s alertrule API; exercise edit flow
- Fix label Combobox: use pressSequentially so createCustomValue fires
- Add breadcrumbLink and annotationValue locators to AlertRuleViewPage POM

- Use resolved datasource UID (not the name) in the k8s alertrules seed

- Switch beforeAll/afterAll to beforeEach/afterEach for per-test isolation

- Move seedRuleGroup helper below tests (top-down organization)
- Exercise 7m evaluation interval and 14m pending period in the
  happy-path test, with corresponding viewer assertions

* Alerting: address code review issues in rule form E2E tests

- Remove banned `as GrafanaConfig` type assertion; destructure settings.json() directly
- Rename switchEvaluationMode → setEvaluationMode (idempotent setter, not toggle)
- Move inline group-picker locator from spec into POM as selectedGroupText()
- Replace hardcoded labelsInSubform index-1 testids with prefix selector + .last()
- Replace annotation-value-0/1 testids with getByLabel(/summary|description \(optional\)/i)
- Scope evaluationIntervalText to the Evaluation interval info item parent div
- Guard aria-label={title || undefined} in DetailGroup to prevent empty-string emission

commit.message:
IAM: Add member count to GET /api/teams/{team_id} (#125153)

* IAM: Fix GET /api/teams/{id} returning memberCount=0

Bug surfaced by the May 2026 Teams K8s Migration bug bash. With
kubernetesTeamsRedirect on, GET /api/teams/{id} returned memberCount=0 even
when the team had real members and /api/teams/search reported the correct
count.

Root cause: teamk8s/team.go GetTeamByID's response mapping built team.TeamDTO
without setting MemberCount, defaulting it to zero. The SearchTeams path in
the same file populates it correctly, which is why the two endpoints
disagreed.

Fix: populate MemberCount from len(fetched.Spec.Members) in the GetTeamByID
response mapping. Mirrors the precedent set by PR #124903 (which made the
same shape of fix for the searchTeams memberCount enrichment) — Spec.Members
is the source of truth for membership across both endpoints.

Regression coverage is a subtest inside the existing
TestIntegrationGetTeamByIDAPI rather than a sibling test — same fixture,
same setup, and the cross-mode equivalence test for GET is the natural home
for the memberCount contract.

* better test comments

* better test case

---------

commit.message:
i18n: move plural defaults of t() calls into options object (#125312)

For every key in grafana.json that has both _one and _other forms and is
used via t(), move the plural defaults from the positional defaultValue
into defaultValue_one and defaultValue_other inside the options object.

i18next selects the plural suffix from count + CLDR rules at runtime and
i18next-cli emits the matching <key>_<suffix> entries on extract, so the
translation JSON stays byte-identical.

Trans component usages are out of scope and tracked separately.

commit.message:
Unified Storage: extract KV and resource DB construction into Wire providers (#124842)

* Unified Storage: extract KV and resource DB construction into Wire providers

Add sql.ProvideKV(cfg, eDB) as the single instantiation point for the
unified-storage kv.KV (Badger for storage_type=file, SQL KV for
storage_type=unified when EnableSQLKVBackend=true, nil otherwise). Add
sql.ProvideResourceDB(cfg, grafanaDB) so the resource-DB wrapper is a
Wire output shared between ProvideKV and NewStorageBackend — keeping
one eDB instance per process.

NewStorageBackend and NewFileBackend now take eDB and kvStore as
parameters instead of constructing them internally. unified.Options
gains KV and EDB fields; populated by Wire. ModuleServer.NewModule
also takes both, stored on the struct and reused in the UnifiedBackend
module callback.

This enables future DI-time consumers (e.g. a KV-lease-based leader
elector) to depend on kv.KV directly without going through the
storage backend's deferred construction.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* make update-workspace

* regen wire

* Remove KV provider from module server wire

* Unified Storage: skip resource DB init when storage_type doesn't use it

ProvideResourceDB now returns nil for storage_type=file, unified-grpc,
and unified-kv-grpc so Wire DI doesn't open an unused xorm engine /
connection pool at startup. Only storage_type=unified consumes eDB
(legacy SQL backend or SQLKV).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Unified Storage: tighten ProvideResourceDB doc comment

Drop the "single eDB instance per process" wording — the guarantee is
per Wire graph, not per process.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Unified Storage: provide resource DB for legacy and etcd storage types

ProvideResourceDB previously returned nil for every storage_type other
than `unified`, but `legacy`, `etcd`, and unspecified types fall through
to the SQL backend in newClient. That left NewBackend with a nil
DBProvider and broke startup. Skip the resource DB only for the storage
types that genuinely do not consume it (file, unified-grpc,
unified-kv-grpc).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Unified Storage: satisfy exhaustive linter in ProvideResourceDB

Move the dbimpl.ProvideResourceDB call into a default branch so the
switch covers every StorageType variant.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Dashboards: skip flaky tabs scroll Playwright test

Introduced in #123251 (merged the same day this branch was rebased onto
main). The "scroll tabs left" button intermittently stays visible after
the test scrolls all the way to the start, failing the toPass() block
that waits for it to hide.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

DashboardTemplate: Wire dashboard-scene support for dashboard template flow (#125015)

* DashboardTemplate: Wire dashboard-scene support for template edit/save flows

Adds the dashboard-scene plumbing needed by the dashboard template feature
without including the template gallery UI (modal/card/filters) or the
in-page banners — those ship in a separate PR.

- New Template route handling in the V2 state manager (loadDashboardTemplate
  via the DashboardTemplateExtension hook, V2-only schema, edit vs use flows)
- Save drawer gains saveAsDashboardTemplate / saveDashboardTemplate modes
  backed by extension form stubs
- Toolbar Save button: edit-mode save for templates and "Save as template"
  menu item, gated by extension registration
- Versions view: history listing/restore for templates via extension hook
- General settings: hide Folder field for templates
- Settings nav: surface Versions entry for templates
- DashboardScene.onRestore: delegate to the template extension when the
  scene is a template
- DashboardScenePage / route types: forward dashboardTemplateUid and
  editTemplate query params to the state manager
- DashboardMeta: add isDashboardTemplate and dashboardTemplateUid

* DashboardTemplate: Tests for dashboard-scene template flows

- New unit test for transformTemplateToSaveModelSchemaV2 (envelope shape,
  resource version default, access flag defaults)
- New toolbar SaveDashboard test covering template edit mode, save-as-template
  menu item gating (flag + canSave + extension form), and save-as-copy
- DashboardScene tests for the onRestore template path and openSaveDrawer
  with saveAs/save template flags
- SaveDashboardDrawer tests for the save-as-template / save-template flows
  and graceful fallback when no extension form is registered
- GeneralSettingsEditView tests asserting the Folder field is hidden for
  templates and rendered otherwise
- VersionsEditView tests for fetching history via the template extension,
  embedded-dashboard diff data, and the no-op early return
- V2 state manager tests for the Template route (edit/use flows + flag gate)
  and Unified manager activation of V2 when dashboardTemplateUid is set
- DashboardControls.test.tsx renderInGrafanaContext now wraps in
  OpenFeatureProvider so the toolbar's useFlagGrafanaOrgDashboardTemplates
  call has a client during tests

* DashboardTemplate: Migrate new tests to test-utils render

Use the centralized render/userEvent from public/test/test-utils.tsx
instead of bare @testing-library/react + manual provider wrappers. The
test-utils render already wraps components in Redux, Router,
OpenFeatureProvider, GrafanaContext, ModalsContextProvider, and
LocationServiceProvider — matching the convention in CLAUDE.md.

- SaveDashboard.test.tsx (new file): drop OpenFeatureProvider wrapper
  and userEvent import; use the user instance returned by render
- GeneralSettingsEditView.test.tsx: drop TestProvider wrapper around
  the new Folder field cases
- DashboardControls.test.tsx: drop the OpenFeatureProvider wrap from
  the renderInGrafanaContext helper; inner GrafanaContext.Provider
  override still wins for kiosk mode tests; mock contextSrv.user since
  test-utils' configureStore reads it at module load

* little improvements in tests and save drawer changes tab

* import fix

* more restriction based on FF

* tests fixed'

* latest improvements

* dashboard restore changed back

* tests fixed

* DashboardTemplate: Wire drawer prop to template save form

- Pass drawer={model} to SaveDashboardTemplateForm so the enterprise
  form can invoke drawer.state.onSaveSuccess?.() after a successful save
  (matches SaveDashboardForm).
- SaveAsTemplateFormExtension props no longer require changeInfo; create
  flow doesn't need diff info.
- Hide diff tabs when rendering the save-as-template flow.

* DashboardTemplate: Always render diff tabs in save drawer

Reverts the saveAsDashboardTemplate ? undefined : tabs conditional so
tabs are always shown, including in the save-as-template flow.

  via the DashboardTemplateExtension hook, V2-only schema, edit vs use flows)
- Save drawer gains saveAsDashboardTemplate / saveDashboardTemplate modes
  backed by extension form stubs
- Toolbar Save button: edit-mode save for templates and "Save as template"
  menu item, gated by extension registration
- Versions view: history listing/restore for templates via extension hook
- General settings: hide Folder field for templates
- Settings nav: surface Versions entry for templates
- DashboardScene.onRestore: delegate to the template extension when the
  scene is a template
- DashboardScenePage / route types: forward dashboardTemplateUid and
  editTemplate query params to the state manager
- DashboardMeta: add isDashboardTemplate and dashboardTemplateUid

* DashboardTemplate: Tests for dashboard-scene template flows

- New unit test for transformTemplateToSaveModelSchemaV2 (envelope shape,
  resource version default, access flag defaults)
- New toolbar SaveDashboard test covering template edit mode, save-as-template
  menu item gating (flag + canSave + extension form), and save-as-copy
- DashboardScene tests for the onRestore template path and openSaveDrawer
  with saveAs/save template flags
- SaveDashboardDrawer tests for the save-as-template / save-template flows
  and graceful fallback when no extension form is registered
- GeneralSettingsEditView tests asserting the Folder field is hidden for
  templates and rendered otherwise
- VersionsEditView tests for fetching history via the template extension,
  embedded-dashboard diff data, and the no-op early return
- V2 state manager tests for the Template route (edit/use flows + flag gate)
  and Unified manager activation of V2 when dashboardTemplateUid is set
- DashboardControls.test.tsx renderInGrafanaContext now wraps in
  OpenFeatureProvider so the toolbar's useFlagGrafanaOrgDashboardTemplates
  call has a client during tests

* DashboardTemplate: Migrate new tests to test-utils render

Use the centralized render/userEvent from public/test/test-utils.tsx
instead of bare @testing-library/react + manual provider wrappers. The
test-utils render already wraps components in Redux, Router,
OpenFeatureProvider, GrafanaContext, ModalsContextProvider, and
LocationServiceProvider — matching the convention in CLAUDE.md.

- SaveDashboard.test.tsx (new file): drop OpenFeatureProvider wrapper
  and userEvent import; use the user instance returned by render
- GeneralSettingsEditView.test.tsx: drop TestProvider wrapper around
  the new Folder field cases
- DashboardControls.test.tsx: drop the OpenFeatureProvider wrap from
  the renderInGrafanaContext helper; inner GrafanaContext.Provider
  override still wins for kiosk mode tests; mock contextSrv.user since
  test-utils' configureStore reads it at module load

* little improvements in tests and save drawer changes tab

* import fix

* more restriction based on FF

* tests fixed'

* latest improvements

* dashboard restore changed back

* tests fixed

* DashboardTemplate: Wire drawer prop to template save form

- Pass drawer={model} to SaveDashboardTemplateForm so the enterprise
  form can invoke drawer.state.onSaveSuccess?.() after a successful save
  (matches SaveDashboardForm).
- SaveAsTemplateFormExtension props no longer require changeInfo; create
  flow doesn't need diff info.
- Hide diff tabs when rendering the save-as-template flow.

* DashboardTemplate: Always render diff tabs in save drawer

Reverts the saveAsDashboardTemplate ? undefined : tabs conditional so
tabs are always shown, including in the save-as-template flow.

Home: Fix flaky DashboardTabs extension tabs test (#125355)

The "renders extension tabs from plugins" test relies on the auto-switch
effect promoting the first extension tab to active once recent/starred
data finishes loading. The synchronous aria-selected assertion could fire
before that effect runs, causing intermittent failures. Wrap the
assertion in waitFor so it retries until the auto-switch has taken effect.

commit.message:
Unified Storage: VectorSearch query-embedding cache and per-tenant rate limit (#125284)

* Unified Storage: Add VectorSearch query cache + per-tenant rate limit

Adds a pgvector-backed query embedding cache (FIFO eviction by created_at)
and a DB-backed per-tenant tumbling-window rate limiter for VectorSearch.
Both are always on when the backend supports them; limits are fixed in
code (1000 entries/tenant; 60 requests/min/tenant). Includes background
sweeper for rate-bucket housekeeping and Prometheus counters that avoid
unbounded namespace cardinality.

* Unified Storage: Simplify VectorSearch query cache and metrics

Refinements on top of the initial implementation:

- Switch cache eviction from LRU to FIFO by created_at — keeps Get as
  a pure SELECT so hot rows don't contend on per-hit UPDATEs.
- Drop the stored query_text column; only (namespace, model, hash) ->
  embedding is needed.
- Rename EvictLRU -> EvictOldest to match the new policy.
- Trim implementation details from QueryEmbeddingCache / RateLimiter
  interface docs; document the contract instead.
- Collapse per-namespace cache metric labels to per-model where
  cardinality matters, and split rate-limit metrics into "rejected"
  vs "limiter errors" so fail-closed and over-quota stay distinguishable.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Unified Storage: Tidy VectorSearch handler and rate-bucket schema

- Extract rate-limit check and query-embed/cache flow into helper
  methods so VectorSearch sits comfortably under the gocyclo limit.
- Switch sweeper goroutine to sync.WaitGroup.Go (Go 1.25).
- Define vector_search_rate_buckets via migrator.Table now that no
  pgvector-specific column types are involved; the cache table stays
  raw SQL for halfvec(1024).
- Drop a misleading comment about non-pgvector backends in withSearch.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Unified Storage: Address VectorSearch cache + rate-limit review

- Make cache cap, rate limit threshold and rate limit window
  configurable via [database_vector] (defaults: enabled, 1000, 60, 1m).
  Both can be disabled independently via *_enabled = false.
- Evict the query cache down to 80% of the per-tenant cap in one pass
  instead of trimming one row per miss, so we don't DELETE on every
  cache miss at steady state.
- Add a standalone window_start index on vector_search_rate_buckets so
  the periodic sweep can use it (composite PK leads with namespace and
  can't satisfy a window_start-only predicate).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Annotations: Route manual annotation writes through annotation.grafana.app k8s API (#124104)

* wip

* fix(annotations): optional AnnotationTagList.items, tighten comments, add scope tests

- AnnotationTagList.items is now optional (defensive ?? [] implies it can be absent)
- Replace multi-line comment blocks with single-line inline comments per codebase style
- Add scope-forwarding tests to setDashboardPanelContext: verify scopes from
  sceneGraph.getScopes() are included in k8s create/update request spec

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(annotations): wire k8s app installer to FF, fix tags shape, fix ID normalisation

- Register annotation app installer when kubernetesAnnotations FF is on
  (previously only cfg.AnnotationAppPlatform.Enabled=true triggered it,
  leaving all routes as 404 when only the FF was set)
- Fix AnnotationTagList/AnnotationTagItem to match backend shape
  ({tags:[{tag,count}]} not {items:[{name,count}]}) and update the
  term mapping in K8sAnnotationServer.tags()
- Add toK8sName(id: string|number) to normalise legacy numeric IDs
  (e.g. 23 or "23") to the k8s "a-{id}" prefix required by parseAnnotationID;
  apply it to both update (GET fetch-then-merge) and remove (DELETE)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(annotations): route dashboard query through k8s /search sub-resource

When kubernetesAnnotations is on, dashboard annotation queries now hit
/apis/annotation.grafana.app/v0alpha1/namespaces/{ns}/search instead of
the legacy /api/annotations endpoint:

- Add annotationK8sClient.search() with param translation (matchAny → tagsMatchAny,
  panelId → panelID, tags[] → repeated tag) and AnnotationList → AnnotationEvent[] mapping
- Route K8sAnnotationServer.query through search; forAlert stays on legacy because
  ListOptions has no Type/AlertUID filter on the backend
- Strip the "a-" prefix on the way out so consumers see legacy-shaped ids
- Use loose Record<string, unknown> + typeof narrowing instead of type assertions
- Update setDashboardPanelContext.test to assert the a-{id} prefix the new path produces

AnnoListPanel still uses /api/annotations directly because it depends on
identity fields (login/email/avatarUrl) and a userId filter that the new
spec/endpoint don't expose; migrating it requires backend changes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(annolist): migrate AnnoListPanel to k8s API with IAM identity hydration

When kubernetesAnnotations is on, the Annotations List panel now hits
/apis/annotation.grafana.app/v0alpha1/namespaces/{ns}/search and hydrates
identity fields (userId/login/email/avatarUrl) via the IAM /display endpoint:

- Expose createdBy ("user:<uid>") on AnnotationEventResource by reading
  metadata.annotations["grafana.app/createdBy"] in annotationToEvent
- Branch AnnoListPanel.doSearch on the FF: legacy /api/annotations stays for
  FF-off; FF-on routes through annotationK8sClient.search() then a single
  batch call to /apis/iam.grafana.app/v0alpha1/.../display to resolve
  displayName/avatarURL/internalId for every unique createdBy key
- queryUser carries the uid so subsequent searches filter via createdBy:user:{uid}
- displayName substitutes for both login (gates avatar) and email (tooltip text)
  since /display doesn't return email

No backend changes required.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(annolist): hydrate email via per-user IAM User resource fetch

The IAM /display batch endpoint deliberately omits email, so previously we
substituted displayName for email in the "Created by" tooltip. The User
resource (GET /apis/iam.grafana.app/v0alpha1/namespaces/{ns}/users/{uid})
exposes spec.email, so we now fetch it per unique createdBy uid in parallel
with the /display batch. On per-user fetch failure (e.g. viewer without
iam:users:get) we fall back to displayName so the tooltip still has a label.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* chore(annotations): drop backend FF + installer wiring (moved to separate PR)

All kubernetesAnnotations feature toggle artifacts (Go registry +
generated Go/CSV/JSON + generated TS) and the pkg/registry/apps/apps.go
installer wiring live on branch mdv/annotations-k8s-feature-flag and ship
as a separate PR. Frontend and backend deploy at different cadences, so
they cannot share a PR.

This branch references config.featureToggles.kubernetesAnnotations, so
the backend PR must merge first before this one will typecheck on main.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

and features/annotations/api.ts) to always take the new k8s path so the

ScopedResourceClient construction is just a getAPINamespace() call plus

forced a resetAnnotationK8sClientForTests test-only export. Drop the

toggle. Removes the TEMP force-on hack since the real config can be
flipped via grafana.ini.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor(annotation server): drop test-only reset hatch

Both AnnotationServer implementations are stateless wrappers around
backend calls, so memoizing the chosen instance wasn't earning much,
and the cache forced a resetAnnotationServerForTests test-only export.
Drop the cache and construct on each call; the export and its callers
in api.test.ts and setDashboardPanelContext.test.ts go away. The empty
beforeEach blocks left behind in the dashboard test are removed too.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* cleanup

* feat(annotations): forward selected scopes on the search/query path

Read paths previously omitted scopes, so the backend returned every
annotation regardless of the dashboard's selected scope. Two call sites
now source scopes the same way the create/update path already does:

- GrafanaDatasource.getAnnotations: when options.dashboard is a
  SceneObject, mirror SceneQueryRunner via sceneGraph.getScopes(...).
  Gated on config.annotationAppPlatformEnabled so the legacy
  /api/annotations endpoint never sees the param.
- AnnoListPanel: read this.context?.state.value via ScopesContext (class
  contextType), forward to annotationK8sClient.search. Already only ran
  in the k8s branch, so legacy is unaffected.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(annotations): forward request.scopes to getAnnotations on the panel path

The previous attempt sourced scopes from options.dashboard via
sceneGraph.getScopes, but on a scenes dashboard options.dashboard is the
legacy DashboardModel returned by getDashboardSrv().getCurrent(), so
isSceneObject(...) is false and scopes never get added.

The scenes AnnotationsDataLayer's standardAnnotationQuery already
populates request.scopes via sceneGraph.getScopes(layer) before calling
datasource.query(). Thread that through into getAnnotations so /search
sees the scope filter on the dashboard panel annotation path. The
options.dashboard sceneGraph path stays as a fallback for direct callers
that don't go through query().

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(annolist): re-run search when ScopesContext value changes

ScopesContext exposes a stable Provider value, so static contextType +
React re-render didn't fire on scope changes (panels work via the
scenes-side imperative setContext/observable path). Subscribe to
stateObservable in componentDidMount and re-run doSearch when the joined
scope-name key differs from the last one we queried with. The replay-on-
subscribe initial emission is filtered out via the lastScopeKey written
during the first componentDidMount-driven doSearch.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
Provisioning: Independent fixes for import flow foundations (#125414)

* refactor(provisioning): independent fixes for import flow foundations

- Export DASHBOARD_API_GROUP from DashboardAPIVersionResolver
- Fix useGetResourceRepositoryView skip condition for provisioning view
- Rename repositoryURL → url in PushSuccessMessage + add tests
- Link to configured tree path via getRepoFileUrl in useProvisionedRequestHandler

* fix(provisioning): keep settings-skip guard, gate root instance lookup behind includeInstance

* refactor(provisioning): simplify linkUrl with ensureFolderPathTrailingSlash

* fix(provisioning): handle githubEnterprise in getRepoFileUrl

GHE Server URLs share the github.com path shape (tree/blob), so the
existing switch can fall through to the github arm. Without this,
useProvisionedRequestHandler's linkUrl silently falls back to the repo
root for GHE customers, defeating the PR's 'link to configured tree
path' improvement.

Other helpers in this file (getRepoRawFileUrl, getRepoEditFileUrl,
getRepoNewFileUrl, getRepoHrefForProvider, getRepoCommitUrl,
getHasTokenInstructions) have the same pre-existing GHE gap and are
left as a follow-up.

it to streamed events, but the initial-events backfill path was emitting
every item from the backend without consulting it. Apply the same checker
inside the ListIterator callback so backfill matches the streamed-event loop.

commit.message:
Leader election: add KVLeaseElector and use it for zanzana embedded mode (#124844)

* Unified Storage: extract KV and resource DB construction into Wire providers

Add sql.ProvideKV(cfg, eDB) as the single instantiation point for the
unified-storage kv.KV (Badger for storage_type=file, SQL KV for
storage_type=unified when EnableSQLKVBackend=true, nil otherwise). Add
sql.ProvideResourceDB(cfg, grafanaDB) so the resource-DB wrapper is a
Wire output shared between ProvideKV and NewStorageBackend — keeping
one eDB instance per process.

NewStorageBackend and NewFileBackend now take eDB and kvStore as
parameters instead of constructing them internally. unified.Options
gains KV and EDB fields; populated by Wire. ModuleServer.NewModule
also takes both, stored on the struct and reused in the UnifiedBackend
module callback.

This enables future DI-time consumers (e.g. a KV-lease-based leader
elector) to depend on kv.KV directly without going through the
storage backend's deferred construction.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Leader election: add KVLeaseElector and use it for zanzana embedded mode

Adds a KV-lease-backed Elector (kvlease.Elector) and wires it into the
zanzana embedded server. Standalone mode keeps using KubernetesElector.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* make update-workspace

* regen wire

* Remove KV provider from module server wire

* Unified Storage: skip resource DB init when storage_type doesn't use it

ProvideResourceDB now returns nil for storage_type=file, unified-grpc,
and unified-kv-grpc so Wire DI doesn't open an unused xorm engine /
connection pool at startup. Only storage_type=unified consumes eDB
(legacy SQL backend or SQLKV).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Unified Storage: tighten ProvideResourceDB doc comment

Drop the "single eDB instance per process" wording — the guarantee is
per Wire graph, not per process.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Unified Storage: provide resource DB for legacy and etcd storage types

ProvideResourceDB previously returned nil for every storage_type other
than `unified`, but `legacy`, `etcd`, and unspecified types fall through
to the SQL backend in newClient. That left NewBackend with a nil
DBProvider and broke startup. Skip the resource DB only for the storage
types that genuinely do not consume it (file, unified-grpc,
unified-kv-grpc).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Unified Storage: satisfy exhaustive linter in ProvideResourceDB

Move the dbimpl.ProvideResourceDB call into a default branch so the
switch covers every StorageType variant.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Dashboards: skip flaky tabs scroll Playwright test

Introduced in #123251 (merged the same day this branch was rebased onto
main). The "scroll tabs left" button intermittently stays visible after
the test scrolls all the way to the start, failing the toPass() block
that waits for it to hide.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* wiregen

* Zanzana: hoist embedded reconciler elector out of newServer

ProvideEmbeddedZanzanaElector now builds the leader-election Elector in
the Wire graph; newServer just receives it. The CLI Wire set binds
Elector directly to NewDefaultElector, so grafana-cli no longer pulls in
the unified-storage KV (and therefore no longer opens Badger / SQL
resource DB) when building its dependency graph. Drops the
LeaderElectionMode enum from the zanzana server package.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Zanzana: tighten kvlease elector teardown ordering

- defer close(done) so a panic in the leader fn no longer wedges <-done.
- defer OnStoppedLeading + wait for fn to return before the release, so
  the lease is only handed back after the leader work has actually
  stopped. This matches the release-then-OnStoppedLeading order used by
  the upstream k8s.io/client-go leader-election library while keeping the
  stricter "no work after release" guarantee fn-await provides.
- Launch OnStartedLeading as a goroutine to match upstream's fire-and-
  forget behaviour.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

storage/unified: migrate Masterminds/semver v1 to v3 (#125443)

* storage/unified: migrate Masterminds/semver v1 to v3

Switches the import path from github.com/Masterminds/semver to
github.com/Masterminds/semver/v3 across the bleve search and resource
packages. The v3 API surface we use (NewVersion, MustParse, Version,
Compare, String) is source-compatible, so no call-site changes were

semver.NewVersion accepts for the build-version strings we feed it
from config and from snapshot metadata, since v3 is slightly stricter

The v1 require line stays in go.mod for now because
pkg/services/pluginsintegration/pluginchecker and
pkg/services/rendering/capabilities still use it.

* storage/unified/search: cover real-world build tags in TestBuildVersionParsing

* apps/quotas: drop unused Masterminds/semver v1 indirect

Result of make update-workspace after the search/resource v1 to v3
migration.

commit.message:
search: periodic on-disk cleanup of stale bleve index folders (#125451)

* search: periodic on-disk cleanup of stale bleve index folders

Adds an opt-in background sweep that walks the bleve index root once per
DiskCleanupInterval and removes folders the pod no longer owns or no
longer needs. Disabled by default; enabled via
[unified_storage] disk_index_cleanup_interval = ...

For each candidate timestamp directory under <root>/<ns>/<res>.<group>/:
- in-flight registrations from BuildIndex / newSnapshotStagingDir are
  never touched (re-checked twice, once before and once after the mtime
  gate, to close the narrow window between a candidate being opened and
  registered);
- the currently cached file index for the resource is always kept;
- the newest sibling of an owned resource we haven't opened gets a
  longer 'unopened' grace period (default 24h) so a later BuildIndex can
  reuse it instead of rebuilding from scratch;
- everything else falls through a two-step mtime gate (stat the
  candidate and its store/ subdir, then a short-circuit recursive walk)
  with the normal grace period (default 1h).

Snapshot upload staging dirs under <root>/snapshots/... use the same
sweep with the in-flight + mtime gates only. newSnapshotStagingDir now
registers its upload-* directory so the in-flight check has a real
signal during CopyTo. Empty parent dirs are removed at the end.

All filesystem access is anchored through os.OpenRoot(b.opts.Root), so
the sweep cannot escape the configured root via symlinks or '..'.

Two new metrics:
- index_server_disk_cleanup_runs_total{outcome}
- index_server_disk_cleanup_dirs_deleted_total{kind, outcome}

* search: use os.Root for chtimes walk in disk cleanup tests

gosec G122 forbids race-prone filepath.WalkDir callbacks. The
test helpers used filepath.WalkDir + os.Chtimes to backdate every
entry under a freshly created temp tree; switch to fs.WalkDir over
an os.Root rooted at the target dir and root.Chtimes, matching the
posture of the production sweep. Folds the three call sites into
one chtimesRecursive helper.

commit.message:
CI: Scan all .citools modules with dependabot and patch x/crypto and x/net CVEs (#125481)

Dependabot's gomod entry only listed /.citools/src/govulncheck, so the other
tool modules (air, cog, cue, golangci-lint, jb, lefthook, swagger) were never
scanned. This left known-vulnerable golang.org/x/crypto and golang.org/x/net
versions sitting in their go.mod files.

Adds the missing directories to .github/dependabot.yml and does a one-time
manual refresh of x/crypto and x/net (and their immediate go.* siblings) in
the affected modules so the current advisories clear immediately.
