commit.message:
DataSources: Introduce async APIs and hooks as replacement for datasourceSrv (#123037)

* DataSources: Introduce async APIs and React hooks

Adds module-level async replacements for DatasourceSrv under
packages/grafana-runtime/src/services/dataSource/: getInstanceSettings,
getInstanceSettingsList (with cursor-paginated response), getDataSourcePlugin,
registerRuntimeDataSource, reloadDataSources plus React hooks. The existing
DatasourceSrv is retained but its interface is marked @deprecated so IDEs
surface the migration path. Boot wiring in public/app/app.ts initialises the
new cache alongside the legacy service. Addresses grafana/grafana#121465.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* DataSources: Use useAsync for single-value hooks

Replaces manual useState/useEffect/cancellation-token pattern in
useInstanceSettings and useDataSourcePlugin with useAsync from react-use,
matching the convention already used in services/pluginMeta/hooks.tsx.
useInstanceSettingsList keeps the manual pattern since it needs fetchMore
and accumulating pagination state that useAsync does not model.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* DataSources: Simplify useInstanceSettingsList with useAsyncFn

Replaces the manual cancelRef/token cancellation pattern and separate
isLoading/error useState calls with useAsyncFn from react-use, which
handles stale-call detection via an internal callId counter. Also drops
the useFiltersKey serialisation helper in favour of direct object equality
on the filters dep — callers must pass a stable reference to avoid extra
fetches. Removes ~40 lines and the toError/useFiltersKey helpers entirely.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* DataSources: Drop reset param from useAsyncFn fetch fn

The reset branch in the value effect is unreachable: the filter-change
useEffect already calls setItems([]) synchronously before fetchPage(), so
prev is always [] when a reset fetch resolves. Remove the reset parameter
and the {page, reset} wrapper entirely — the fn now just returns the page.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* DataSources: Use object equality for ref dep in single-value hooks

Removes serializeRef and relies on object equality for the ref dep in
useInstanceSettings and useDataSourcePlugin, consistent with the same
approach used for filters in useInstanceSettingsList. Callers must pass
a stable ref reference to avoid unnecessary refetches.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* DataSources: Rename list API, move plugin loading to core, drop scopedVars from hooks

Three follow-up changes from code review:

1. Rename getInstanceSettingsList → findInstanceSettings (and related
   GetInstanceSettingsListOptions → FindInstanceSettingsOptions,
   useInstanceSettingsList → useFindInstanceSettings,
   UseInstanceSettingsListResult → UseFindInstanceSettingsResult) to
   better reflect its filter/search nature.

2. Move the getDataSourcePlugin implementation into
   public/app/features/plugins/getDataSourcePlugin.ts where it can
   import pluginImporter directly. The runtime package now holds only a
   thin injection stub (setGetDataSourcePlugin / getDataSourcePlugin),
   removing the DataSourcePluginImporter interface from the internal API.
   getRuntimeDataSourcePlugin is exported from @grafana/runtime/internal
   so the core implementation can check for registered runtime data
   sources before doing a full plugin load.

3. Drop the scopedVars parameter from useInstanceSettings and
   useDataSourcePlugin — the plain function APIs retain it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* DataSources: move getDataSourcePlugin back to @grafana/runtime with setDataSourceImporter injection

The full `getDataSourcePlugin` implementation lives in `@grafana/runtime/src/services/dataSource/plugin.ts`.
The only cross-package dependency (`pluginImporter.importDataSource`) is injected via the new
`setDataSourceImporter` setter, exposed through `@grafana/runtime/internal`.
`app.ts` calls `setDataSourceImporter` at boot. The temporary `getDataSourcePlugin.ts` in core is deleted.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* DataSources: rename result fields for clarity in async hooks

Rename `data` → `settings` in `UseInstanceSettingsResult` and
`data` → `dataSource` in `UseDataSourcePluginResult` so the field
names reflect what they hold.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* DataSources: migrate 5 call sites from DataSourceSrv to new async APIs

Demonstrates the migration patterns across different contexts:

- cloudwatch/utils/datalinks.ts: async fn → getDataSourcePlugin()
- cloudwatch/ConfigEditor.tsx: useEffect/useState hook → useDataSourcePlugin()
- datasources/SuggestedDashboardsLoader.tsx: async callback → getInstanceSettings()
- AppChrome/QuickAdd.tsx + browse-dashboards/CreateNewButton.tsx: useMemo sync list → useFindInstanceSettings()
- alerting/useAlertQueriesStatus.ts: useMemo sync loop → useState/useEffect with getInstanceSettings()

Tests updated to mock the new API functions instead of getDataSourceSrv().
New test file added for useAlertQueriesStatus.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* DataSources: rename useFindInstanceSettings → useInstanceSettingsList

The previous name sounded like a function factory; the new name
follows the useInstanceSettings/useInstanceSettingsList (singular/list)
convention and makes clear the hook returns a collection.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* DataSources: improve QuickAdd and useAlertQueriesStatus migrations

QuickAdd: lift useInstanceSettingsList out of QuickAdd into SingleTopBar
so the parent owns loading/error state. QuickAdd now receives a plain
hasTestDataSource boolean prop. Adds SingleTopBar tests covering the
hasTestDataSource derivation logic.

useAlertQueriesStatus: expose isLoading and error alongside
allDataSourcesAvailable. Use a UID key string as the effect dep to
prevent a re-render feedback loop when callers pass an unstable array
reference. Update Query.tsx and PreviewRule.tsx to fold isDsLoading into
their existing loading state and suppress the unavailable warning until
the async check settles.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* DataSources: rename findInstanceSettings → getInstanceSettingsList

Aligns the async function name with its React hook counterpart
(useInstanceSettingsList). Also renames FindInstanceSettingsOptions →
GetInstanceSettingsListOptions for consistency.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* DataSources: restore version guard in CloudWatch ConfigEditor migration

getDataSourcePlugin will eventually fetch from the network on a cache
miss. Calling it for an unsaved datasource (version=0) would then throw.
Restore the original if (props.options.version) guard and use
getDataSourcePlugin directly inside useEffect rather than the hook,
keeping the defensive behaviour intact until a separate PR decides how
to handle that loading state in the UI.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* DataSources: simplify useAlertQueriesStatus with useAsync from react-use

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* DataSources: fix typecheck error in CloudWatch ConfigEditor test

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* DataSources: clarify registerRuntimeDataSource JSDoc re: list exclusion

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* DataSources: extract pluginCache module and clear it on reload

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* DataSources: gate hasTestDataSource on dashboardTemplates feature toggle

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* DataSources: add test asserting getDataSourcePlugin not called when version unset

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Tests: fix failing frontend unit tests caused by missing MSW handler for /api/frontend/settings

The new async instance-settings service fetches /api/frontend/settings on a
cold cache. Tests using setupMockServer() (onUnhandledRequest: 'error') failed
with an unhandled request error. Add a default MSW handler returning empty
datasources to @grafana/test-utils so these tests pass.

For Query.test.tsx, the new cache also needs the test datasource populated so
useAlertQueriesStatus resolves allDataSourcesAvailable: true. Call
initDataSources() in beforeEach/afterEach alongside the existing setupDataSources.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* DataSources: remove migration examples from core async APIs PR

Move all call-site migrations (CloudWatch datalinks, CloudWatch ConfigEditor,
SuggestedDashboardsLoader, QuickAdd/CreateNewButton, useAlertQueriesStatus,
Query.tsx, PreviewRule.tsx) to a separate follow-up PR so this PR stays focused
on introducing the new async API surface.

The migration examples and their descriptions are preserved on the
mckn/async-datasource-migrations branch.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* DataSources: move frontend-settings MSW handler to migrations branch

The /api/frontend/settings handler is only needed by tests for migrated
components (SingleTopBar, Query.tsx etc). Those live on the migrations branch,
so the handler belongs there too.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* DataSources: address review nits on instanceSettings and plugin modules

- Rename init() → initDataSources() so the function name matches its
  exported alias; no more re-export renaming needed in internal/index.ts
- Rename lookup() → lookupFromMaps() to be more explicit
- Add process.env.NODE_ENV guard to _resetForTests() in instanceSettings.ts
  so it throws in non-test environments
- Extract GenericDataSourcePlugin, ImportDataSourceFn (plugin.ts) and
  DataSourceInstanceSettingsPage, GetInstanceSettingsListOptions
  (instanceSettings.ts) into a shared types.ts file

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* DataSources: rename async APIs to better reflect what they return

Rename to align with the four distinct datasource types (PluginMeta,
Plugin, InstanceSettings, DataSourceApi):

  getInstanceSettings        → getDataSourceSettings
  getInstanceSettingsList    → getDataSourceSettingsList
  getDataSourcePlugin        → getDataSource
  useInstanceSettings        → useDataSourceSettings
  useInstanceSettingsList    → useDataSourceSettingsList
  useDataSourcePlugin        → useDataSource
  DataSourceInstanceSettingsPage  → DataSourceSettingsPage
  GetInstanceSettingsListOptions  → GetDataSourceSettingsListOptions
  UseInstanceSettingsResult       → UseDataSourceSettingsResult
  UseInstanceSettingsListResult   → UseDataSourceSettingsListResult
  UseDataSourcePluginResult       → UseDataSourceResult

Also updates all JSDoc, @deprecated comments, tests, and the PR description.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* DataSources: use resolved uid as plugin cache key for template variable refs

When getDataSource receives a template variable ref (e.g. "${datasource}"),
getDataSourceSettings returns settings with uid set to the variable string.
Use settings.rawRef.uid as the cache key so repeated calls don't create
duplicate plugin instances.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* DataSources: handle expression datasource refs in new async APIs

Expression datasources are not included in /api/frontend/settings —
the legacy DatasourceSrv injects them during init. Add an

the routing conditional, delete the entire legacy/ folder (~1.9k LOC),

type that only the legacy slice consumed, and unregister
importDashboardReducers from the root reducer.

commit.message:
Provisioning: Add duplicate-path validation to ResourceEditFormSharedFields (#125415)

* feat(provisioning): add duplicate-path validation to ResourceEditFormSharedFields

- Add async validatePath that checks for existing files at the target path
- Add MSW handler for files/:path returning 404 for test coverage
- Migrate ResourceEditFormSharedFields tests to MSW

* chore(i18n): extract translation strings

* fix(provisioning): always-fresh path check + correct RHF deps direction

Address PR review feedback on ResourceEditFormSharedFields:

- Remove preferCacheValue=true on the pre-save existence check; cached
  404/200 results can be stale by the time the user submits.
- Swap the deps direction. RHF triggers a field's deps when *that field*
  changes, so 'deps: [ref]' on path meant 'when path changes, validate
  ref' (the opposite of intent). Move 'deps: [path]' onto the ref field
  so branch changes correctly re-run validatePath.

* fix(folders): guard against null display/keys in combineFolderResponses

The DisplayList type declares display and keys as required arrays,
but the IAM display mapping API can return null for either field.
Without optional chaining on these properties, indexing into null
throws TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading '0'),
crashing every folder page when foldersAppPlatformAPI is enabled.

commit.message:
Search: split snapshot store interface into file + manifest methods (#125531)

Data-file methods now take *os.File directly instead of io.Reader/io.Writer,
so a chunking backend can call ReadAt/WriteAt for parallel chunk I/O. The
snapshot manifest moves to dedicated WriteSnapshotManifest([]byte) /
ReadSnapshotManifest() ([]byte, error) methods, so backends no longer need
to recognise the manifest by filename.

The size cap on reads moves from the helper into the backend so the
chunking backend can still use WriteAt on a real *os.File. The post-write
Stat size check in DownloadIndexSnapshot stays as a final safety check.

No behaviour change.

commit.message:
Provisioning: Remove GET method from webhook connector (#125539)

* Provisioning: Remove GET method from webhook connector

Removes http.MethodGet from webhookConnector.ConnectMethods so the
webhook subresource only accepts POST. Because the webhook Authorize
returns DecisionAllow unconditionally (GitHub delivers webhooks as
an anonymous caller), allowing GET let unauthenticated callers
distinguish existing/non-existing repositories and webhook
configuration state via response code differences (401 vs 404 vs 400).

Closes https://github.com/grafana/git-ui-sync-project/issues/1157

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Drop webhook GET from OpenAPI spec and generated client

- Fix PostProcessOpenAPI: the existing guard checked sub.Get != nil but
  assigned to sub.Post.Description. After removing GET from
  ConnectMethods, sub.Get is nil and POST loses its description. Switch
  to sub.Post != nil and also clear sub.Get explicitly (defense in depth
  in case anything else registers GET on this path).
- Regenerate the v0alpha1 and v1beta1 OpenAPI snapshots in
  pkg/tests/apis/openapi_snapshots and the published specs under
  packages/grafana-openapi/src/apis to drop the GET operation.
- Remove the now-unused getRepositoryWebhook query, types, and hooks
  from the generated RTK Query client. grep confirms no other code
  imports these symbols.

commit.message:
Provisioning: fix isPublicURL host detection (#125548)

* Provisioning: fix isPublicURL host detection

Replace prefix-matching in isPublicURL with proper URL parsing and CIDR
range checks so webhook registration is gated correctly.

The previous implementation missed several private/reserved ranges
(172.17-172.31, 169.254/16, 100.64/10, IPv6 loopback/link-local/ULA,
and Kubernetes-internal DNS suffixes), and the `strings.Contains(url,
"localhost")` check produced a false negative for legitimate hosts
like `notlocalhost.grafana.com`.

Fixes https://github.com/grafana/git-ui-sync-project/issues/1154

* Provisioning: gofmt isPublicURL test file

Apply gofmt -s to align comment column spacing.

commit.message:
Grafana API clients: Replace plop generator (#125515)

* grafana-api-clients: replace plop with enquirer-based generator

Replace plop.js with a hand-rolled TypeScript generator script using
enquirer for interactive prompts. This drops plop + node-plop +
handlebars + inquirer + liftoff and ~60 transitive packages from the
dependency graph, addressing recurring vulnerability reports from
nested dependencies.

The new generator provides identical functionality:
- 7 interactive prompts (confirm, autocomplete, 5 inputs with
  validators and computed defaults)
- 3 template functions replacing Handlebars templates
- File creation with mkdir-p and overwrite protection
- Marker-based injection into existing files
- ESLint + Prettier post-formatting
- RTK codegen invocation

PLOP_INJECT_* sentinel markers are preserved for enterprise repo
compatibility.

Closes #114570

* grafana-api-clients: deduplicate generator variant config

Extract a declarative Variant record (OSS/Enterprise) into variants.ts,
eliminating duplicated ternaries across 4 files. Collapse the two inject
helpers into one, delete unused injectAfterMarker, and add a runOrWarn
helper for the repeated try/execSync/console.warn pattern.

* grafana-api-clients: rename PLOP_INJECT markers to GENERATED:*

Replace legacy plop-era marker comments with descriptive
GENERATED:API_CLIENT, GENERATED:IMPORT, GENERATED:REDUCER,
and GENERATED:MIDDLEWARE markers.

* grafana-api-clients: add 'do not remove' context to generator markers

* grafana-api-clients: restore generator marker suffixes

* grafana-api-clients: add existing client update flow

* add partial generate

* grafana-api-clients: clarify client update docs

* grafana-api-clients: render confirm answers as yes no

* update lockfile

* grafana-api-clients: address generator review feedback

* Support partial update

* grafana-api-clients: split generator helpers

* Update script

* docs

* Add generator utility tests and fix OSS generateCommand

- Add Jest tests for templates, prompts, files, clientState, and variants
- Fix OSS generateCommand to use root 'yarn generate-apis' instead of
  workspace-scoped command
- 42 tests covering formatEndpoints, renderConfigEntry, renderBaseAPI,
  renderIndexTs, validateGroup, validateVersion, writeNewFileIfMissing,
  repoPathExists, fileContains, injectBeforeMarkerIfMissing,
  getRTKClientEntries, hasAPIConfigEntry, getExistingClientFiles,
  getClientGenerationState, variantFor, MARKERS, PACKAGE_ROOT

* Remove unused MARKERS import from clientState.test.ts

* yarn dedupe

* Add "type": "module" to @grafana/api-clients package.json

Eliminates NODE_MODULE_TYPELESS_PACKAGE_JSON warning when running
generate.ts directly with node.

* Revert "type": "module", suppress MODULE_TYPELESS_PACKAGE_JSON warning

The "type": "module" field breaks attw (FalseESM) because the package
ships dual CJS/ESM with a single .d.ts types entry. Instead, suppress
the Node.js warning in the generate:api-client script via
--disable-warning=MODULE_TYPELESS_PACKAGE_JSON.

* PR feedback

commit.message:
Unified Storage: authz on delegated-only RPCs (#125070)

Five RPCs on the unified-storage resource server (PutBlob, GetBlob,
ListManagedObjects, CountManagedObjects, RebuildIndexes) historically
relied entirely on the calling service to authorize the originating
user request. In deployments where the gRPC surface is reachable
without that calling service in the request path, the contract isn't
enforced. This adds defense in depth.

  * NOTE on each of the five methods: internal RPC, caller owns
    end-user authorization, do not route end-user traffic here directly.
  * PutBlob: validate request, require a user in ctx, load the parent
    resource and authorize "update" against its folder via access.Check.
    The parent must exist (PutBlob is not a staging primitive -- the
    proto comment is updated to match) and backend errors are surfaced
    verbatim rather than collapsed into a misleading 404.
  * GetBlob / ListManagedObjects / CountManagedObjects / RebuildIndexes
    gain a requireUserNamespace gate (claims.NamespaceMatches) -- 401
    when no user, 403 on cross-namespace, allow same-ns or "*". Helper
    lives inline in server.go.

Caller audit: every in-process caller of these RPCs already stamps
identity in ctx with a matching namespace via WithProvisioningIdentity
(jobs/, controller/, persistentstore), WithServiceIdentityFor
SingleNamespaceContext (migration runner), or the k8s apiserver auth
interceptor (REST connectors). The shared blob scenario test is updated
to (a) seed the parent before PutBlob, (b) confirm PutBlob 404s when
the parent doesn't exist, and (c) stamp a namespaced service identity
on the test ctx so it can clear the namespace gate.

Test plan:
  * go test ./pkg/storage/unified/resource/
  * go test ./pkg/storage/unified/sql/test/ -run TestIntegrationSQLStorageBackend
  * go test ./pkg/registry/apis/provisioning/webhooks/pullrequest/

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
Provisioning: Record Grafana user in commit messages (#125571)

* Provisioning: Record Grafana user who saved a resource in commit message

Adds {{userName}}, {{userLogin}}, {{userEmail}} template placeholders to
the per-repo singleResourceMessageTemplate, and appends a git-style
Grafana-saved-by: <name> (<login>) trailer to every single-resource
commit (dashboard save/delete/move, folder create/rename/delete) so the
Grafana user who triggered the write is always recorded in git history,
not just the shared bot account from the access token.

Closes #124191

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Flatten user fields in CommitTemplateVars

Drops the nested CommitUser type in favour of flat userName/userLogin/
userEmail fields on CommitTemplateVars so the regex callback collapses to
a single vars[key] lookup and call sites can spread getCurrentCommitUser()
directly. No behaviour change.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Tag migrate jobs with Grafana-saved-by trailer

Adds a withSavedByTrailer() convenience helper and uses it to tag the
migrate job's commit message with the Grafana-saved-by trailer (the
backend MigrateJobOptions already carries a `message` field).

Leaves TODO markers on bulk delete, bulk move, fix-folder-metadata, and
sync (pull) job sites: their backend job options have no `message` field
yet, so the trailer can't ride through until that's added.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Link Grafana-saved-by TODOs to follow-up issue

Tags the four pending sites (bulk delete, bulk move, fix-folder-metadata,
sync) with the tracking issue number so the cleanup is discoverable.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Drop public issue ref from Grafana-saved-by TODOs

The follow-up backend work is tracked internally; cross-referencing a
private issue number from public code would leak detail and leave a
dangling reference for outside readers. The TODO text alone is enough
to find the relevant sites; the internal tracking issue is linked from
the PR description.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Link Grafana-saved-by TODOs to follow-up issue

Tags the four pending sites with the tracking issue
(grafana/git-ui-sync-project#1162) so the cleanup is discoverable
when the backend adds the missing `message` fields.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Sanitize identity vars to prevent trailer injection

Collapses any CR/LF in the user-controlled userName/userLogin/userEmail
fields to a single space before they reach the commit message — both
when interpolated into a template and when used to build the
Grafana-saved-by trailer. Without this, a profile name containing a
newline could forge additional git trailers in the commit message.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Derive template-var regex and types from a single key array

Replaces the inline regex + parallel TemplateKey union with TEMPLATE_KEYS
and IDENTITY_KEYS arrays that are constrained to keyof CommitTemplateVars
via `as const satisfies`. The regex, the identity-key set, and the
TemplateKey type now all flow from those arrays, so adding or removing a
template variable in one place keeps the others in sync (and the
keyof-constraint surfaces a TypeScript error if an array entry doesn't
exist on the interface).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
Unified storage: add fuzz tests for dashboard parsers and Bleve query builder (#125444)

* Unified storage: add fuzz tests for dashboard parsers and Bleve query builder

Adds three stdlib fuzz targets covering high-value parsers in the
unified storage ingestion and search path:

- FuzzReadDashboard exercises the streaming jsoniter walker used by the
  dashboard indexer.
- FuzzExtractDashboard exercises the independent map[string]any walker
  used for embeddings.
- FuzzBleveRequirementQuery exercises selector-to-Bleve-query
  translation, asserting that every return path produces exactly one of
  (query, error).

The seed corpora reuse existing testdata JSON files. CI runs the seeds
as regular tests; coverage-guided runs are opt-in via `-fuzz=...`.

* Fuzz tests: silence gosec G304 and fail when no seeds loaded

- Add //nolint:gosec on os.ReadFile lines that read from a hard-coded
  seed-directory list joined with names from those directories (not
  user input). This clears the lint-go CI failure.
- Track seedCount and f.Fatalf if zero seeds were loaded, so a moved
  or renamed testdata path fails the test instead of silently passing.
  Addresses review feedback from @RafaelPaulovic.

* Fuzz tests: fail if any seed directory is missing

Previously a missing seed directory was silently skipped, so a renamed
or moved testdata path could go unnoticed while the test kept passing
with seeds from the remaining directories. Now each listed directory
must exist. The overall seedCount == 0 check stays as a backstop for
the case where every directory exists but contains no usable JSON.

Addresses review feedback from @renatolabs.

* Fuzz tests: document byte-level mutator coverage caveat

Acknowledges that Go's stdlib fuzzer mutates inputs at the byte level,
so most random inputs bail out early on structured dashboard JSON and
deep grammar paths are rarely reached in coverage-guided runs. These
targets are most useful for catching panics on shallow inputs and as a
regression harness against the seed corpus. Structure-aware mutation
(e.g. gosentry) is tracked as a follow-up.

The Bleve requirement-query target is unaffected — it fuzzes typed
strings directly, not bytes through a structural parser.

commit.message:
Unified Storage: Pass commit message when routing managed-resource writes (#125556)

* Unified Storage: Pass commit message when routing managed-resource writes

When a non-provisioning client writes a repo-managed resource via the
Dashboard API, the fallback path in handleManagedResourceRouting proxies
the request to the provisioning files endpoint. That endpoint reads the
commit message from the `message` query parameter only — it does not
inspect the body's `grafana.app/message` annotation — so the proxied call
left nanogit StagedWriter.Commit with an empty subject and failed with

commit.message:
Provisioning: replay protection for GitHub webhooks (#125550)

* Provisioning: GitHub webhook replay protection via X-GitHub-Delivery

Track recently-seen delivery IDs in a TTL-bounded in-memory cache and
reject duplicates before they enqueue a sync job. The cache is owned by
the extras builder so it is shared across rebuilt repository instances.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: simplify delivery cache to package-level singleton

NewGithubWebhookRepository no longer takes the cache as a parameter.
Instead, a single sharedDeliveryCache lives in the package — this is
required because extras.Build constructs a fresh repository per webhook
request, so a per-instance cache could never observe a replay across
requests.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: own webhook replay cache on github.Factory

Move the shared delivery-ID cache off the package-level singleton and
onto Factory. ProvideFactory now constructs one cache that the
extras.Build wiring threads into every per-request repository it
produces — the lifetime model the original PR needed but cleaner.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: amortize replay-cache eviction with a FIFO

The earlier implementation scanned every entry on each seenOrAdd to
collect expired ones — O(N) per webhook delivery, held under the cache
mutex. Replace it with a container/list FIFO + lookup map: because
every entry shares the same TTL, insertion order equals expiration
order, so we walk only the actually-expired entries from the front and
stop at the first live one. Work is now O(K) in newly-expired entries,
not O(N) in cache size, addressing https://github.com/grafana/grafana/pull/125550#discussion_r3316887385.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: silently drop replayed webhook deliveries

Returning a 401 with a "duplicate delivery id" message acts as a
side-channel oracle: the response confirmed to a replay attacker that
the captured payload was a real, previously-processed delivery. Switch
to a generic 200 OK + "ok" body — byte-identical to other no-op paths
(e.g., sync disabled, wrong branch) — so an attacker cannot tell from
the response whether the payload was previously seen. Operators still
get visibility via a server-side info log.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: key webhook replay cache on the signed signature

The X-GitHub-Delivery header is not covered by GitHub's HMAC (the
signature is computed over the request body only), so an attacker
replaying a captured (body, signature) could pick a fresh delivery ID
and slip past a delivery-ID-keyed cache. Key the replay cache on the
validated X-Hub-Signature-256 instead: it is bound to both the signed
body and the repository's unique secret, so it can be neither forged
nor collided across repositories. The delivery ID is now logged for
observability only.

Also:
- defensively initialize the cache in NewGithubWebhookRepository so a
  nil argument cannot panic Webhook
- drop the duplicate-replay log from Info to Debug to avoid log flooding
  from repeated replays
- rename deliveryIDCache -> replayCache to reflect the new key

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: back webhook replay cache with golang-lru/v2/expirable

Replace the hand-rolled container/list FIFO with the shared
hashicorp/golang-lru/v2/expirable cache already used elsewhere in the
repo (e.g. pkg/api/avatar). It is thread-safe, TTL-bounded, and — unlike
the previous implementation — size-bounded, so the cache can no longer
grow unbounded within the TTL window under high webhook volume.

seenOrAdd uses Get (which honors per-entry expiry on read) rather than
Contains (which only checks map membership), wrapped in a mutex so the
check-and-set stays atomic across concurrent identical requests. TTL
tests switch from an injected clock to a short TTL plus sleep, since the
library uses real time.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

- Add ProvisionedImportForm and ProvisionedImportOverview components

The old conditional guard hid the import item for provisioned folders.

commit.message:
Alerting: Block Viewers from Alert Group edit route (#125669)

The route `/alerting/:dataSourceUid/namespaces/:namespaceId/groups/:groupName/edit`
required only `AlertingRuleRead`/`AlertingRuleExternalRead`, so Viewers could open
the edit UI by typing the URL directly. The backend correctly rejects saves with
403, but the editable UI should never have been shown.
Aligns the route guard with `/alerting/:id/edit`, which requires
`AlertingRuleUpdate`/`AlertingRuleExternalWrite`.

commit.message:
Search: add KV-backed RemoteIndexStore (no chunking yet) (#125621)

* Search: add KV-backed RemoteIndexStore (no chunking yet)

Adds KVRemoteIndexStore, a RemoteIndexStore implementation backed by
kv.KV with build/cleanup locks via lease.Manager. Unit-tested against
in-memory badgerKV. Not wired into production yet.

Manifests and data live in separate KV sections so listing complete
snapshots scans one key per snapshot. Each data file is stored as a
single KV value; transparent chunking comes in a follow-up.

Folds in a small change to isRetryableSnapshotStoreError to treat
kv.ErrRetryable as retryable, since this is the first file in the
package to import the kv package.

* Address review feedback

- ListIndexKeys: log a warning when skipping a non-ULID manifest key
  instead of silently dropping it
- kvIndexStoreLock.Release: always wrap the underlying error; callers
  can still branch on lease.ErrLeaseLost via errors.Is
- TestKVRemoteIndexStore_ListingSemantics: rename the two namespace/
  resource subtests so the description matches what they assert

commit.message:
Unified storage: add fuzz tests for continue token, key parsers, and snapshot manifest validator (#125713)

Adds six Go stdlib fuzz targets:

- FuzzGetContinueToken — base64+JSON pagination token parser.
- FuzzParseKey, FuzzParseKeyWithGUID, FuzzParseEventKey,
  FuzzParseLastImportKey — storage key parsers.
- FuzzParseLeaseKey — lease keys (internal package, the parser is
  unexported).
- FuzzValidateIndexSnapshotManifest — snapshot manifest path-traversal
  validator.

Seed corpora run as normal `go test` cases; coverage-guided runs are
opt-in via `-fuzz=...`.

Finding: FuzzParseLastImportKey surfaced a real asymmetry — the
formatter writes ts.Unix() with %d (int64) but the parser uses
ParseUint, so timestamps from a uint64 >= 2^63 don't round-trip.
Production never hits this; the fuzz body skips negative Unix() and
the reproducer is committed as a regression marker.

commit.message:
Search: use apimachinery validators and slash-separated KV layout (#125737)

Addresses follow-up review comments on #125621.

- Replace the hand-rolled validateNamespace / validateNsResource with
  the apimachinery validators (IsValidNamespace, IsValidResource,
  IsValidGroup). They cover all the same invariants plus length bounds
  and match what the rest of the codebase uses. The empty-namespace
  case is still rejected explicitly because apimachinery permits it
  for cluster-scoped resources.

- Change the per-resource KV layout from "<namespace>/<resource>.<group>"
  to "<namespace>/<resource>/<group>". '/' is the only character
  always reserved by the apimachinery validators, so it's the natural
  separator and removes the artificial 'no dot in resource' rule.
  ListNamespaceResources now consumes two segments instead of
  dot-splitting one.

commit.message:
Provisioning: reject http:// repository URLs when a token is configured (#125732)

* Provisioning: reject http:// repository URLs when a token is configured

Combining an http:// repository URL with a token caused the token to
travel in cleartext on every git operation, since git.NewRepository adds
basic auth unconditionally regardless of scheme. The validators never
rejected this combination.

Reject http:// + token in the shared ValidateGitConfigFields (covering
git and github, plus future git-based types), with an escape hatch for
local/dev: the combination is still allowed when running in development
mode (app_mode=development) or when the new [provisioning]
allow_insecure_token flag is set. http:// without a token and https://
remain valid everywhere.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs: document [provisioning] allow_insecure_token option

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: rename allow_insecure_token to allow_insecure

Aligns the config key with the internal allowInsecure naming and follows
Grafana's existing convention. The flag still gates only the http:// + token
combination.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: enable allow_insecure in integration test harness

Provisioning integration tests run against a local Gitea container over
http:// with a token, which the new validator rejects by default. Add a
ProvisioningAllowInsecure option to the test GrafanaOpts and enable it in
the default provisioning test config so these tests keep working.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: normalize URL scheme in http+token check

URL schemes are case-insensitive, so a value like HTTP:// could bypass the
case-sensitive prefix check and still send the token in cleartext. Lowercase
the URL before comparing (https:// remains unaffected).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
AccessControl: Resolve built-in grafana datasource type without a store lookup (#125780)

The built-in "-- Grafana --" datasource has no row in the datasource table,
so legacyConnectionClientImpl.GetConnectionByUID could never resolve its plugin
type. For RBAC roles carrying the seeded datasources:uid:grafana grant this was
silently unresolved, and for global roles (orgID 0, multi-org) the store lookup
failed with ErrDataSourceIdentifierNotSet, breaking role provisioning.

Its UID and type are fixed and identical across orgs, so resolve it directly in
the legacy connection client. This fixes datasource-type resolution for every
caller that goes through this client (provisioning save and the k8s migration
type resolvers) without a store row.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
Alerting: Propagate plugin rule origin as X-Rule-Origin header (#125206)

* Alerting: propagate plugin rule origin as X-Rule-Origin header

Rules that originate from a plugin (identified by the __grafana_origin
label) now include that value as an X-Rule-Origin header in datasource
eval requests. GetEvalCondition populates the Origin metadata key;
buildDatasourceHeaders sanitizes all metadata values (strips control
characters, truncates to 128 bytes) before encoding them as headers.
X-Rule-Origin is registered in both the query-API and plugin-middleware
header allowlists so it is forwarded correctly in all eval paths.

* Alerting: add __grafana_origin_uid label to X-Rule-Origin header

Introduce PluginGrafanaOriginUIDLabel (__grafana_origin_uid) as a
standard label plugins can set to identify the specific resource that
owns an alert rule. When present alongside __grafana_origin, the two
values are combined into a single X-Rule-Origin header as
"<origin>|<uid>" (e.g. "plugin/grafana-slo-app|abc-123").

For the SLO plugin, which cannot yet set __grafana_origin_uid, a
fallback reads grafana_slo_uuid when the origin is
"plugin/grafana-slo-app". The generic label takes precedence when both
are present.

Alerting: Support managed Prometheus data sources in rule conversion (#125750)

Allow managed Prometheus rule imports

The converter already receives AWS and Azure Managed Prometheus datasource types from API paths that consider them Prometheus-compatible, so the import path should not reject them before rule conversion. This keeps Loki support unchanged and applies Prometheus-compatible validation to recording-rule targets.

Constraint: Grafana issue #123144 reports AWS and Azure Managed Prometheus rule imports fail because the converter only accepts native Prometheus and Loki datasource types.
Rejected: Special-casing only API handlers | the converter is the shared validation boundary and query model writer.
Confidence: high
Scope-risk: narrow
Directive: Keep future Prometheus-compatible datasource support centralized in converter validation instead of adding route-specific bypasses.
Tested: go test ./pkg/services/ngalert/prom
Tested: go test ./pkg/services/ngalert/api -run "TestRouteConvertPrometheusPostRuleGroup|TestIsPrometheusCompatible|TestIsLotexRulerCompatible"
Not-tested: full Grafana test suite

commit.message:
Zanzana: Translate user- and team-management RBAC actions to tuples (#125850)

* Zanzana: Translate user- and team-management RBAC actions to tuples

The RBAC->Zanzana reconciler (ConvertRolePermissionsToTuples) dropped all
user- and team-management permissions, so roles granting them (Org Admin,
Grafana Admin, Editor, managed team/user admin) produced no tuples; once a
namespace routes iam.grafana.app/{users,teams} to Zanzana, management breaks.

Add dedicated translators, gated alongside the existing role-management bypass:

- Core user actions (users:*, org.users:*) and core team actions (teams:*) map
  to relations on iam.grafana.app/users and iam.grafana.app/teams respectively,
  inverting the iam K8s mapper. On users the global (users:*) and org
  (org.users:*) families converge on the same verbs (union); field-level
  escalation stays enforced by the iam admission validators independently.
- Role assignments: both users.roles:* and teams.roles:* map to
  iam.grafana.app/rolebindings. Team and user role-bindings are the same
  resource (the subject kind is a spec field, not part of the authz tuple), so
  they are not distinguished at the group_resource level.

Wildcard-only scope: specific-instance scopes (users:id:N / teams:id:N) are
dropped (FGA types are uid-based, legacy scopes id-based); users:create and
teams:create are unscoped. No mapper or schema changes: the rolebindings,
users and teams mapper entries and the search access-control checks already
exist on main.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Address feedback

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
Alerting: Reject imported configs with unsupported receiver fields (#125906)

* Alerting: Reject imported configs with unsupported receiver fields

Imported Prometheus/Mimir Alertmanager configs that use receiver fields
Grafana cannot represent (e.g. the *_file / *_ref fields removed in
grafana/alerting#573) were silently dropped during conversion.

Validate now round-trips each receiver through the upstream<->definition
conversion and rejects any field that does not survive, listing the
offending receivers and their YAML field paths in the error's "extra"
payload. Detection is generic, so it stays correct as upstream adds fields.

* Alerting: Add integration test for unsupported receiver fields import

Asserts POST /convert/api/v1/alerts rejects a config whose receiver uses a
field Grafana cannot represent (auth_password_file), returns the YAML field
path, and stores nothing.

* improve test

commit.message:
Alerting: fix MergeTimeIntervals dropping existing mute intervals and wrong collision priority (#125897)

Two bugs in MergeTimeIntervals:
1. existingMuteIntervals were never added to the result — they were passed
   only to build the used-name index, so callers silently lost them.
2. Incoming mute intervals were appended after time intervals in incomingAll,
   giving time intervals the lower index and making them win name collisions.
   Per the alertmanager semantics, mute intervals should win.

Also clear MuteTimeIntervals from the MergeExtraConfig result; they are now
folded into TimeIntervals so keeping them in both fields would create duplicates.

commit.message:
Logs: Fix trace preview for Loki derived fields using TraceQL trace-i… (#125872)

Logs: Fix trace preview for Loki derived fields using TraceQL trace-id lookups

The log line details trace preview sent the derived field's query to Tempo
as-is. For a TraceQL trace-id lookup like `{ trace:id = "<id>" }`, Tempo
returns a search-results table instead of trace spans, so the preview could
not render and the trace section stayed empty. A bare trace ID worked only
because Tempo routes hex-only queries to a trace-by-id lookup.

Extract the trace ID from a `{ trace:id = "<id>" }` query before querying
Tempo so the preview fetches the full trace by ID. Other TraceQL queries are
left unchanged.

commit.message:
Alerting: Include error in Loki state history when exec_err_state is Alerting (#125775)

* Alerting: Include error in Loki state history when exec_err_state is Alerting

The Loki state history backend only wrote the error field when the
alert state was eval.Error. When exec_err_state is configured as
Alerting, the state is eval.Alerting with a non-nil Error, so the
error was silently dropped from history entries.

Remove the state check so the error field is written whenever
state.Error is non-nil, making state history consistent with what
already flows to notifications via annotations.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Alerting: Show error message in state history UI regardless of alert state

The state history UI only rendered the ErrorMessageRow when the base
state was Error. When exec_err_state is Alerting, the state is
Alerting (Error) which maps to Alerting, so the error row was hidden.

Show the error message whenever the error field is present in the

Alerting: Add RuleSequence resource schema, codegen, validation, authorization, and guardrails (#121373)

* Alerting: Add RuleChain resource schema, codegen, validation, authorization, and guardrails

Add the RuleChain API as a new k8s-native resource for the alerting rules
app-platform. RuleChain represents an ordered evaluation chain of
RecordingRules followed by AlertRules within a single folder.

- Define CUE schema (ruleChain.cue, ruleChain_spec.cue) and run codegen
  for Go types, TypeScript types, OpenAPI specs, and CRD manifest
- Add feature flag (alertingRuleChains) with OpenFeature evaluation
- Wire RuleChain into app registration with feature-gated kind registration
- Implement admission validator: interval, folder, provenance, non-empty
  recording rules, duplicate UID detection, cross-chain membership check,
  and rule existence/folder-match validation
- Implement admission mutator: folder label sync, duration clamping
- Implement folder-level RBAC authorizer matching sibling pattern
- Add delete/move guardrails on AlertRule and RecordingRule validators to
  reject operations when a rule belongs to a chain
- Add ResolveRuleRef and ResolveRuleChainMemberships callbacks in register.go
  with bulk resolution and early-exit optimization
- Fix GetLegacyStorage panic for resources without legacy storage
- Fix CUE codegen bug: use [...#RuleRef] to avoid invalid Go/TS defaults
- Add unit tests for validator, mutator, and delete/move guardrails

* Alerting: Add folder support for RuleChain resources

* Alerting: Plumb RuleChain resources into the scheduler

* Regenerate alerting/rules app
* Alerting: Replace ListAll membership resolver with watch-backed index

Admission validators now use an in-memory index kept in sync by the
app-sdk's informer infrastructure instead of doing an O(N) ListAll on
every request. This eliminates the per-admission scan and narrows the
TOCTOU race window to watch propagation delay.

* uid -> name

* Alerting: Handle delete validation before casting req.Object

validateDelete now receives the full AdmissionRequest and casts
req.OldObject itself. This keeps the change minimal while avoiding
the req.Object cast that fails on delete admission requests.

commit.message:
Testinfra: pass live gRPC listener through to avoid port re-bind race (#125749)

When an integration test uses unified-grpc storage, the harness reserved an
ephemeral port by opening a listener, recording its address, then closing it
and re-binding the same address when the gRPC server started. Under parallel
CI load a different process could claim the port in that window, producing an
intermittent "failed to listen" failure.

Keep the reserved listener open and hand it straight to the gRPC server so the
port can never be claimed by anyone else. Add ProvideDSKitServiceWithListener
as an additive constructor so the production ProvideDSKitService signature is
unchanged; gPRCServerService.Run serves the injected listener when set and
otherwise falls back to net.Listen.

commit.message:
Provisioning: Add folderless sync target type (#125809)

* Provisioning: Add folderless sync target type

Add a new `folderless` value to the SyncTargetType enum in the
provisioning v0alpha1 API. Like `folder`, multiple `folderless`
repositories may coexist with each other, with `folder` repositories,
and with unprovisioned resources; unlike `folder`, no repo-named wrapper
folder is created — repo-root files become top-level resources and
subdirectories become top-level folders, with ownership tracked
per-resource via manager annotations.

This commit only introduces the type and regenerates the dependent
artifacts: openapi definitions and snapshots, and the generated
frontend RTK Query client (endpoints.gen.ts). Behavioral wiring
(validation allow-list, sync/migrate handling) and user docs follow
separately.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Reserve folderless target but reject it in validation

The folderless sync target is defined in the API but not supported yet.
Document it as reserved in the type's doc comment and reject repositories
that use it during validation, so the value can ship in the API ahead of
the behavior. Regenerates the openapi definitions/snapshots and the
frontend RTK client with the updated description.

commit.message:
Zanzana: Fix list query-cache corruption from in-place ident stripping (#125936)

The List response helpers (typedObjects/genericObjects/folderObject) stripped
the object-type prefix in place, mutating the *openfgav1.ListObjectsResponse
slice that the query cache owns. With CheckQueryCacheEnabled (the default), a
List call downgraded the cached full object idents to bare ids, so a later
BatchCheck — which reads the same cache entry and matches on the full
FolderIdent/ResourceIdent — failed its membership lookups and hid resources the
user had direct access to (e.g. a root dashboard granted via a role).

Make the strip helpers return a new slice so the cached response is never
mutated. List still returns bare ids (the RBAC-backend ListResponse contract);
BatchCheck keeps seeing the canonical full idents from the cache.

Adds TestStripHelpersDoNotMutateInput (unit) and
TestIntegrationListDoesNotPoisonBatchCheckCache (List-then-BatchCheck with the
query cache enabled).

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
grafana/ui: Sanitize href in LinkButton via textUtil.sanitizeUrl (#125470)

* grafana/ui: sanitize href in LinkButton via textUtil.sanitizeUrl

LinkButton renders an <a> element but did not sanitize its href prop,
unlike Link and TextLink which both apply textUtil.sanitizeUrl. This
means javascript:, data:, and vbscript: URLs could be rendered as-is.

Extract href from the rest-spread, sanitize it when defined, and place
it after {...otherProps} on the <a> so the sanitized value always wins.
Preserve undefined when href is not provided so LinkButton without href
still renders as a non-link anchor (existing behavior).

Add tests for javascript: neutralization, safe URL passthrough, relative
URL passthrough, and missing href. Add a regression lock-in test to
TextLink for its existing sanitization.

* grafana/ui: Fix LinkButton href sanitization for empty strings

sanitizeUrl('') returns 'about:blank', which changes the ARIA role of
the anchor from generic to link — breaking callers that pass href=''
to mean 'no destination'. Use a truthy check instead so empty string
and undefined pass through unchanged while non-empty hrefs are still
sanitized. Add explicit test for the empty string case.

commit.message:
Provisioning: Wire folderless sync target behavior (#125812)

* Provisioning: Wire folderless sync target behavior

Make the folderless target behave like folder for coexistence:

- Repository validation: generalize the instance-exclusivity messages so
  folder and folderless are both blocked when an instance repository
  exists (and instance is blocked when any other repo, including
  folderless, exists).
- Migrate: skip the namespace clean for folderless repositories, since
  like folder they coexist with unmanaged resources and must not delete
  them.

Adds unit tests for folderless coexistence and migrate cleanup skipping,
and updates the quota integration test for the new validation message.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Add folderless integration tests

Enable the folderless target in the provisioning test infra and add
integration tests covering the full feature surface:

- Sync placement: repo-root files land at the top level with no wrapper
  folder; subdirectories become top-level folders.
- Coexistence / deletion safety: two folderless repos and unprovisioned
  content coexist; syncing one never deletes the other's or the
  unprovisioned resources.
- Migrate: unprovisioned dashboards are exported and taken over at the
  top level, no wrapper folder, and the namespace is not cleaned.
- Files endpoint: moving a file between the repo root and a subdirectory
  reparents the resource to and from the top level.

These exercise the existing resources/jobs code paths, which already
handle folderless via resources.RootFolder returning "" (like instance);
no wrapper folder is synthesized in jobs/sync.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Test folderless file creation at root and in subdirectory

Add a files-endpoint integration test asserting that creating a file at
the repository root maps to a top-level resource and creating one in a
subdirectory maps to a resource inside a top-level folder, with no
wrapper folder for the repository.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Wire the folderless backend (not fully implemented yet)

Implements the backend plumbing for the folderless sync target and removes
the temporary hard rejection added with the type. Folderless is not fully
implemented yet: it stays gated behind the provisioning `allowed_targets`
setting (which defaults to `folder`), so it is not available unless an
operator explicitly enables it, and the type's doc comment / openapi
description say so. Regenerates the openapi definitions, snapshots, and
the frontend client.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Test folderless coexistence with folder sync and unmanaged

Add an integration test where a folderless repository coexists with a
folder-sync repository and an unprovisioned dashboard. Each repository
owns only its own resources, the folder repo keeps its wrapper folder
while the folderless repo creates none, and syncing the folderless repo
leaves the folder repo's and the unprovisioned resources untouched.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Fix gosec G104 in folderless file-move test

Explicitly discard the error from resp.Body.Close() instead of relying on
a //nolint:errcheck directive, which gosec G104 does not honor.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
Provisioning: Capability-based config-driven supported resources (#125856)

* Provisioning: Introduce flag-gated seam for supported resources

Add SupportedResources and SupportsFolderAnnotationResources constructors that
accept a featuremgmt.FeatureToggles checker and today return exactly the static
SupportedProvisioningResources / SupportsFolderAnnotation sets. This establishes
a single seam where future flag-gated resources can be appended, without changing
current behaviour and without adding any new resource or feature flag.

Migrate the pipeline consumers (export loop, export quota stats, migrate cleanup,
authorizer, folder-annotation write path) to call the constructors instead of
ranging over the package vars directly. The constructors tolerate a nil checker;
no flag is consulted yet, so the effective set is identical to today.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Make supported-resource set a ResourceClients concern

Move the supported-resource set behind the ResourceClients interface and
register extra types through the client factory instead of a flag-gated
package function.

- SupportedResources() and SupportsFolderAnnotationResources() are now
  methods on ResourceClients, returning the static base set plus any extra
  resources registered with the factory.
- NewClientFactory / NewClientFactoryForMultipleAPIServers accept variadic
  SupportedResource registrations ({GVR, SupportsFolderAnnotation}); the
  factory threads them into the namespaced clients.
- Consumers (authorizer, folder-annotation write path, export loop, quota
  stats, migrate cleanup) resolve the set through the clients they already
  hold; NewAuthorizer now takes a ResourceClients.

No behaviour change today: with no registered extras the effective set
equals the current static set.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Collapse supported-resource accessors into one method

Address review: precompute the supported set and expose it through a single
interface method.

- SupportedResources() now returns []SupportedResource (each carrying its
  folder-annotation flag), replacing the separate SupportsFolderAnnotationResources.
- The merged base + registered set is computed once per factory and reused by
  every ResourceClients it produces, instead of merging on each call.
- Consumers read .GVR / .SupportsFolderAnnotation off the entries; the
  folder-annotation write path uses a supportsFolderAnnotation helper.

Adds a unit test for resources.go covering that the folder annotation is not
written for resources that do not support folders (and the contrasting case
that it is).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Drive the supported-resource set from config

Per the agreed design (git-ui-sync #1167), make the provisionable resource set
config-driven with a sensible default, instead of a package-level var. This
supersedes the per-resource feature-flag approach.

- New [provisioning] keys: resources and folder_resources (both default to
  "dashboards | folders"), parsed into cfg.ProvisioningResources /
  cfg.ProvisioningFolderResources, mirroring allowed_targets / repository_types.
- resources.BuildSupportedResources(resourceNames, folderResourceNames) maps the
  configured short names to the effective []SupportedResource (folder_resources
  is the subset that carries the folder annotation). Unknown names fail fast.
- register.go builds the set from cfg and threads it through NewAPIBuilder into
  NewClientFactory; ResourceClients.SupportedResources() exposes it. With no
  config the factory falls back to the static SupportedProvisioningResources.
- The effective set is surfaced on the settings endpoint (RepositoryViewList
  .availableResources) the way allowed_targets is, so the frontend can read it.

Adding a resource is now a config change (folder-contained kinds go in both
lists; org-scoped kinds only in resources) — no feature flag, no codegen.
Kind/version are still resolved at runtime via discovery; folder-scope is
supplied by folder_resources until it can be declared as kind metadata.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Config carries the group+kind+folder triplet per resource

Address review: drive the supported set entirely from config with no hardcoded
name→GVR map, and identify resources by GroupKind (the API version and plural
resource are resolved at runtime via discovery).

- Each resource is declared in its own [provisioning.resources.<kind>.<group>]
  section (mirroring the per-resource [unified_storage.<resource>.<group>]
  convention), with a folder=<bool> key (extensible for future per-kind settings).
  cfg.ProvisioningResources holds the parsed {Group, Kind, SupportsFolderAnnotation}
  triplets; defaults to folders + dashboards.
- resources.SupportedResource is now {schema.GroupKind, SupportsFolderAnnotation}.
  Consumers that need the plural resource (authorizer bulk checks + resolveFileGVR,
  export loop, migrate cleanup, export quota counter) resolve it via clients.ForKind.
  resolveFileGVR now matches on Group+Kind (a kind that shares a group is no longer
  mis-authorized as the first kind in that group).
- The folder-annotation write path matches on the parsed GVK; no discovery needed.
- The effective set is surfaced on the settings endpoint as "<kind>.<group>"
  identifiers (RepositoryViewList.availableResources), with an integration test.

Folder support is configured per kind because, although unified storage tracks it
(apistore.StorageOptions.EnableFolderSupport), it is server-side and not exposed via
the API/discovery, so a remote provisioning operator cannot read it. Declaring
folder-scope as discoverable kind metadata is a follow-up that would drop the config.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Regenerate frontend API client for availableResources

Run `yarn workspace @grafana/api-clients generate-apis` after adding
RepositoryViewList.availableResources to the OpenAPI: regenerates the processed
specs in @grafana/openapi and the RTK Query types in @grafana/api-clients, so
the frontend client exposes the new field.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Add extra-resources settings integration test + lint fix

- Simplify routes.go to r.String() (staticcheck QF1008: drop redundant embedded
  GroupKind selector).
- Add a ProvisioningResources option to testinfra.GrafanaOpts that writes
  [provisioning.resources.<kind>.<group>] sections.
- Add an integration test asserting a resource added purely through configuration
  is surfaced on the settings endpoint (availableResources).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Surface supported resources as enabled-aware triplets

Address review on the settings endpoint shape:

- availableResources is now a list of structured descriptors (SupportedResource)
  carrying group, kind, supportsFolderAnnotation and enabled — not opaque strings,
  and the folder field is clearly named.
- Each [provisioning.resources.<kind>.<group>] section gains an enabled key
  (default true). Disabled resources are still declared and surfaced, but the
  pipeline (authorizer/export/migrate/quota) acts only on enabled ones —
  ResourceClients.SupportedResources() returns the enabled subset, while the
  settings endpoint surfaces the full declared set.
- defaults.ini declares library panels and playlists as disabled by default
  (folders + dashboards remain enabled).

Regenerated deepcopy, OpenAPI (Go + snapshots + @grafana/openapi specs) and the
@grafana/api-clients RTK Query types. Adds/extends settings + client unit tests
and the settings-endpoint integration tests (default set incl. disabled, and an
extra resource added via config).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Thread supported resources into the operator; rename to EnableFolderSupport

- The operator (multi-API-server path) now builds the supported set from
  cfg.ProvisioningResources and passes it to NewClientFactoryForMultipleAPIServers,
  matching the in-process register.go wiring.
- Rename the folder field/setting/JSON to EnableFolderSupport / enableFolderSupport,
  matching unified storage's apistore.StorageOptions.EnableFolderSupport and its
  camelCase config-key convention. Config key folder -> enableFolderSupport.

Regenerated OpenAPI (Go + snapshots + @grafana/openapi) and the @grafana/api-clients
RTK Query types. Updated unit tests.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Config-driven strict-validation exemption + parser support gate; operator aggregated URL

- Strict-validation exemption is now config-driven (P0.5): per-resource
  skipStrictValidation key (default false), replacing the hardcoded
  `gvr == DashboardResource` check in the parser. Dashboards keep the exemption
  via defaults.ini / the static fallback set.
- The parser now rejects resources that are not enabled/supported with a
  ResourceValidationError, driven by the enabled supported set.
- Operator: add an aggregated_server_url [operator] key; enabled resources whose
  API group has no dedicated server URL are served by the aggregated API server
  (fails loudly if a resource needs it and it is unset). The operator also passes
  SkipStrictValidation through.

Unit tests: parser skip-strict-validation wiring and unsupported-resource
rejection. (folder field/key already renamed to EnableFolderSupport/enableFolderSupport.)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Integration test for rejecting a disabled resource via files API

Writing a playlist (declared but disabled by default) through the files endpoint
is rejected as a client error referencing resource enablement/support.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Operator explicitly skips built-in groups for the aggregated server

Dashboards, folders and provisioning have dedicated server URLs, so skip those
groups explicitly when assigning the aggregated API server URL to extra resources.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Capability-based supported resources (shared grammar + parser)

Reshape the config-driven supported set to a single shared grammar, parser and
type, per the capability-based design:

- One INI key `[provisioning] resources` = comma-separated tokens
  `<group>/<Kind>[:cap...]`. Capabilities (all default off): folder (folder-scoped),
  skipvalidation (skip validation), disabled (declared but inert). No more
  per-resource sections or enabled/folder bools.
- resources.SupportedResource is now {schema.GroupKind; Capabilities sets.Set[string]}
  with IsActive()/IsValidated()/IsFolderScoped(); the shared
  resources.ParseSupportedResources([]string) parses+validates the whole list
  (strict, fails fast at startup) and is the single entry point for both OSS and
  the (future) enterprise MT side.
- pkg/setting holds the raw []string token list (parsed in register.go and the
  operator, avoiding a setting->resources import cycle).
- Settings endpoint surfaces availableResources as {group, kind, capabilities[]}.
- defaults.ini: folders + dashboards (folder), library panels (folder, disabled),
  playlists (disabled).

Regenerated deepcopy, OpenAPI (Go + snapshots + @grafana/openapi) and the
@grafana/api-clients RTK Query types. Updated unit + integration tests.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Revert parser support-gate and strict-validation changes

The parser support-gate and per-resource skip-validation belong to separate
draft PRs. Restore parser.go to its pre-PR state (dashboard exemption hack),
drop the now-unused isSupportedResource/skipsStrictValidation helpers, and
remove the tests that exercised the reverted gate.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Re-attach availableResources $ref in OpenAPI post-processing

The settings connector adds RepositoryViewList to the served spec via an empty
ReferenceCallback, which strips array-item $refs. RepositoryViewList.items is
manually re-attached; do the same for the new availableResources field so its
SupportedResource element type resolves instead of degrading to {default:{}}.
Regenerate the v0alpha1/v1beta1 OpenAPI snapshots to match.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Surface availableResources as enabled/disabled, not capabilities

The settings endpoint only needs to tell the frontend which declared resources
are active and which are disabled, not the full internal capability set. Replace
SupportedResource.capabilities[] with a single disabled bool on the API DTO
(derived from the internal capability model via IsActive). Drop the now-unused
CapabilityList helper, regenerate deepcopy/openapi/snapshots and the frontend
RTK Query client, and update the settings integration test.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Regenerate deepcopy/openapi via codegen

Run hack/update-codegen.sh so the generated deepcopy and openapi for the
SupportedResource disabled-bool change match canonical generator output
(function ordering, shallow-copy for AvailableResources, violation list),
fixing the CODEGEN_VERIFY check.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
Search: chunked snapshot files in KVRemoteIndexStore (#125803)

* Search: chunked snapshot files in KVRemoteIndexStore

Each snapshot file is now split into one or more fixed-size chunks under
key <existing-data-prefix>/<relPath>/<NNNNN>, so files larger than the
KV backend's per-value limit round-trip correctly. Every file (including
small ones) gets at least chunk 000000, keeping the read and write paths
uniform.

KVRemoteIndexStoreConfig gains a ChunkSize field; zero falls back to a
10 MiB default and values are validated to a 1 MiB..1 GiB range.

The reader is self-describing: chunk 0 is read first capped at
expectedSize+1; if it covers the file we're done, otherwise its size is
the writer's chunk size and the rest of the chunks are fetched
accordingly. This means ChunkSize can change between deployments without
breaking previously-written snapshots.

Empty files are not supported because all KV backends reject zero-byte
values, but Bleve snapshot files are always non-empty in practice.

Parallel chunk I/O is left for a follow-up.

* Search: route chunked-snapshot test helpers through os.Root

gosec G304 flagged os.Open(path) where path is a variable derived from
t.TempDir(). Switch newTempFileWithContent to os.OpenRoot + root.Create,
keep a single file handle (write, then seek back to 0). readAllFromFile
also stops handing a variable path to os.ReadFile by reading from the
already-open *os.File via Seek + io.ReadAll.

docs(alerting): detail regex label matchers in rule search (#125913)

Expand the alert rule search syntax section to document how regex
matching actually works. The previous wording said "regex matching is
supported in search values," which is imprecise: regex applies only to
the label filter via Prometheus-style matchers, and the matching is RE2,
fully anchored, and case-sensitive by default.

Add the supported operators (=, !=, =~, !~), quoting rules, anchoring
and case-sensitivity behavior, and note that matchers apply to both rule
and alert-instance labels.

This makes the docs accurate enough for LLMs to answer questions about
the search syntax correctly rather than inferring overly broad regex
support.

commit.message:
Provisioning: Guard SetFolder by folder-scope capability (#125973)

* Provisioning: Guard SetFolder by folder-scope capability

The parser derived a folder ID from the file path and called
parsed.Meta.SetFolder(...) for every parsed resource, unconditionally.
For org-scoped resources (those not contained in folders, e.g.
playlists) this stamps a meaningless, possibly dangling folder
annotation onto the object before it is written to the apiserver.

Guard the SetFolder block so it only runs when the parsed resource is
folder-scoped in the configured supported set, via the existing
supportsFolderAnnotation helper (P0.1 #1167 capability model). Resources
without the folder capability get no folder annotation, making
folder-contained vs org-scoped a pure data decision.

The client/GVR resolution (ForKind) and the nil-clients guard are moved
ahead of the folder block since the guard now consults
r.clients.SupportedResources(); this is a pure reorder of independent
operations. Behaviour is unchanged for existing resources: dashboards
and folders both carry the folder capability and keep their annotation.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Reduce Parse complexity and add config-driven integration test

Extract the folder-ID resolution out of (*parser).Parse into a
resolveFolderID helper. The added folder-scope guard pushed Parse over
the gocyclo threshold (31 > 30); moving the path/metadata branches into
the helper brings Parse back to 20 with no behaviour change.

Add TestIntegrationProvisioning_FolderAnnotationGuardByConfig, which
proves the folder annotation is purely a function of the [provisioning]
resources config: the same dashboard kind synced into a subdirectory
gets a grafana.app/folder annotation when declared with the :folder
capability and none when declared without it. Mirrors the config-driven
custom-resource integration tests added in #125856.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Make folder-annotation guard integration test single-instance

The previous integration test called common.RunGrafana twice in one test
process (one per A/B subtest), which is unreliable: Grafana keeps
process-global state, so the second server's temp dir was rejected as an
unpermitted local-repository path and syncs failed under CI (postgres).

Move the test into its own package with a dedicated shared env (one
Grafana per package, the established pattern) configured to declare
dashboards WITHOUT the folder capability. The test then verifies the new
guard end-to-end: a dashboard synced from a subdirectory gets no
grafana.app/folder annotation when its kind is org-scoped by config. The
positive case (folder-capable kind keeps the annotation) is the default
and stays covered by the foldermetadata suite and the parser unit tests.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

the gocyclo threshold (31 > 30); moving the path/metadata branches into
the helper brings Parse back to 20 with no behaviour change.

Add TestIntegrationProvisioning_FolderAnnotationGuardByConfig, which
proves the folder annotation is purely a function of the [provisioning]
resources config: the same dashboard kind synced into a subdirectory
gets a grafana.app/folder annotation when declared with the :folder
capability and none when declared without it. Mirrors the config-driven
custom-resource integration tests added in #125856.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Make folder-annotation guard integration test single-instance

The previous integration test called common.RunGrafana twice in one test
process (one per A/B subtest), which is unreliable: Grafana keeps
process-global state, so the second server's temp dir was rejected as an
unpermitted local-repository path and syncs failed under CI (postgres).

Move the test into its own package with a dedicated shared env (one
Grafana per package, the established pattern) configured to declare
dashboards WITHOUT the folder capability. The test then verifies the new
guard end-to-end: a dashboard synced from a subdirectory gets no
grafana.app/folder annotation when its kind is org-scoped by config. The
positive case (folder-capable kind keeps the annotation) is the default
and stays covered by the foldermetadata suite and the parser unit tests.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
Provisioning: Generalize the job admission validator (#125978)

* Provisioning: Generalize the job admission validator (P0.9)

validateExportResourceRefs (shared by push and migrate job options)
hard-rejected anything that wasn't a Dashboard, so job-driven flows for
any newly-supported kind failed at admission.

Validate each resource ref's kind/group against the configured
supported-resource set instead of the dashboard constants. The set is
injected into the job AdmissionValidator and threaded through ValidateJob.
When no set is configured it falls back to the dashboard-only default,
preserving legacy behavior. Disabled resources are not accepted.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Integration tests for config-driven job admission validation

Update the existing job-validation integration assertions for the
generalized validator: the default active set is {Folder, Dashboard}, so
Folder is now accepted for export — switch the rejection cases to kinds
that are genuinely outside the active set (declared-but-disabled Playlist
and LibraryPanel, case-mismatched "dashboard") and to the new error
messages.

Add a config-driven integration test that boots Grafana with a custom
[provisioning] resources set and asserts the validator honors it: a kind
added purely through config is accepted for push/migrate, while unknown,
disabled, and wrong-group refs are rejected at admission.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Drop repo dependency from config-driven job validation test

The test created a local repository whose initial sync failed under the
postgres CI runner (the worker's repo status update hit the permitted-path
check), making setup flaky. Job admission only requires a non-empty
repository name and does not check repository existence, so creating Job
objects directly through the resource client exercises the validator in
isolation without a real repository.

commit.message:
unified-storage: fix snowflake RV detection (#126012)

Resources created prior to ~2017-05 have snowflake RVs with 18 digits; in the
previous implementation of the `IsSnowflake` function, these RVs would be
mistakenly classified as old/microsecond RVs, and re-converted to snowflake RVs
when attempting to normalize the RV before processing by the appropriate
storage backend.

In this commit, the boundary is lowered to 1e17, which identifies older
resources snowflake RVs appropriately.
