commit.message:
Fix transformations crashing on panel exit and producing bad group values (#125029)

* Transformations: skip unknown transformer ids instead of throwing

getOperator runs synchronously when stream.pipe() wires up the pipeline, so a throw from standardTransformersRegistry.get() escaped the catchError attached downstream in SceneDataTransformer.transform()
and surfaced as an uncaught error on panel-edit exit. The existing
`if (!info) return source;` guard was unreachable.

Switching to getIfExists makes that guard reachable so dashboards with
broken or unknown transformer ids degrade gracefully instead of
crashing.

* Dashboards: avoid persisting group: "Transformation" for malformed wire input

Some older Go foundation SDK versions (targeting v2beta1) produced
transformations with kind: "Transformation" but without the v2 stable `group` field. normalizeTransformation treated those as v2beta1 and used t.kind as the group, persisting the corrupted shape
{ kind: "Transformation", group: "Transformation", spec: {} } on save.

When kind is the v2 stable literal but `group` is missing, fall back to
spec.id (the real transformer id in v2beta1) so the resulting v2 stable
representation has a valid group. Pure v2beta1 inputs (kind == the
transformer id) are unaffected.
Fixes (in part) #125023

* PanelQueryRunner: clear applyFieldOverridesMock in field-config tests

The two "should not apply field config when applyFieldConfig option is false" tests assert applyFieldOverridesMock was not called, but the module-level mock accumulates calls from earlier tests in the file (e.g. the toBeCalled assertion above), so the assertion failed under test:ci. Clear the mock at the start of each test, mirroring the spy.mockClear()
already used by the sibling transformations tests.

* Transformations: extract matcher registries to break predicates<->matchers cycle

commit.message:
Search: detect incomplete uploads in KVRemoteIndexStore.ListIndexKeys (#125974)

Snapshots whose upload crashed before the manifest was written used to
stay on disk forever because KV's ListIndexKeys scanned only the
manifest section, hiding manifest-less ULIDs from CleanupIncompleteIndexSnapshots.

ListIndexKeys now unions the ULIDs from the manifest section (one key
per complete snapshot) and the data section (which surfaces incomplete
uploads). The cleanup helper's logic is unchanged.

ListNamespaceResources was refactored along the way to share the same
listDistinctValues helper as ListNamespaces and ListIndexKeys.

commit.message:
Storage: add SQL tables and SqlKV sections for snapshot index storage (#125979)

* Storage: add SQL tables and SqlKV sections for snapshot index storage

KVRemoteIndexStore needed two new KV sections (snapshot manifest and
snapshot data) that SqlKV previously rejected, so the store only
worked against the in-memory KV.

Adds two new tables search_snapshot_manifest and search_snapshot_data
(mirroring the kv_leases shape) plus the two new section constants in
SqlKV. The value column is LongBlob rather than MediumText because
snapshot data chunks are arbitrary binary; MediumText on Postgres is
unsafe for non-UTF-8 bytes.

KVRemoteIndexStore keeps IndexSnapshotManifestSection /
IndexSnapshotDataSection as aliases pointing at the new canonical
constants in the kv package, so existing call sites don't change.

* Storage: simplify sqlkv section save condition

commit.message:
Unified Storage: ANALYZE resource_history before backfill on Postgres (#126055)

* Unified Storage: ANALYZE resource_history before backfill on Postgres

The legacy-to-unified migration bulk-loads resource_history and then runs the
resource backfill (a self-join over resource_history) in the same transaction.
On Postgres the planner still sees the table as empty (reltuples=0) and picks an
O(n^2) nested-loop plan, so the backfill can run for hours on large instances.

Run ANALYZE on resource_history before the backfill so the self-join plans
against the real row count. Gated to Postgres (other engines materialize the
subquery once and are unaffected) and to large loads only.

* Unified Storage: Add integration test for resource_history ANALYZE

* Unified Storage: Use dialect Ident for ANALYZE and reuse bulk iterator helper

Provisioning: Make strict-validation exemption opt-in (#125992)

* Provisioning: Make strict-validation exemption opt-in

The parser forced FieldValidation=Ignore only for DashboardResource via a
hardcoded equality check. Drive the exemption from a small opt-in lookup
(strictValidationExemptions) and a skipsStrictValidation predicate instead,
containing only the dashboard GroupResource today. No new resource exempted;
no behaviour change.

commit.message:
Dashboards: Fix variable query editor fields resetting on unrelated re-render (#125985)

QueryVariableEditor: Fix fields resetting when an unrelated re-render occurs

The variable QueryEditor rebuilt `queryWithDefaults` as a fresh object on
every render and passed it as the `query` prop to the datasource variable
editor. Datasource editors (e.g. Prometheus) re-initialize their internal
state from this prop via `useEffect([query])`, so a new reference on every
render caused that effect to re-run constantly. When the parent re-rendered
for an unrelated reason (e.g. typing in the Regex field, which calls
`setState`), the editor re-initialized from the last-persisted query and
wiped any in-flight edits that had not yet been persisted.

Memoize `queryWithDefaults` so the `query` prop keeps a stable reference and
only changes when the query or datasource actually changes.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
Provisioning: Generalize the selective-export job controller (UID→path) (#125993)

ExportSpecificResources resolved every ResourceRef through a single
dashboard client and hard-rejected anything that wasn't a Dashboard, so
job-driven selective export of any newly-supported kind failed even
after admission accepted it (P0.9).

Resolve each reference against its own kind/group via discovery and
export it through the shared write path: the dashboard conversion shim
is applied only to dashboards, folders are skipped (they are exported as
a tree by ExportFolders), and an unresolvable kind is recorded as a
failed item so a misconfigured caller surfaces in the job summary.

The bulk move/delete controllers already resolve generically via
FindResourcePath/ForKind, so no change was needed there.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
Storage: wire KVRemoteIndexStore behind index_snapshot_storage_kv toggle (#126043)

When enable_kv_leases is on and a new index_snapshot_storage_kv toggle
is set, the resource server wires search snapshots through
KVRemoteIndexStore instead of the object-storage bucket. The KV store
and lease manager are shared with the storage backend.

Adds two accessors on KVBackend: KV() and LeaseManager(). The wiring
layer (sql/service.go) builds a KVRemoteIndexStore from those when the
toggle is on, and passes it into NewSearchOptions via a new optional
parameter. buildSnapshotOptions accepts an injected store: when non-nil
it overrides the bucket-derived store; non-Store fields still come
from cfg.

Validation lives in buildKVSnapshotStore and fails loudly at startup:
rejects index_snapshot_bucket_url + index_snapshot_storage_kv set
together, requires enable_kv_leases, requires a KV-backed storage
backend, and requires a non-nil lease manager.

commit.message:
DashboardDS: Fix Mixed panels with a time override stuck in permanent loading (#125954)

DashboardDS: Fix Mixed panels with time override stuck loading

A Mixed datasource panel with multiple `-- Dashboard --` (Other Panels)
subqueries stays in permanent loading when the source panel — or the chain
panel itself — carries a `PanelTimeRange` override (`timeFrom`/`timeShift`),
even though the data arrives.

The Mixed-DS stale-Done filter added in #124665 compared the upstream's
terminal emission range against the chain panel's request range
(`options.range`). With a time override those ranges legitimately differ, so
the fresh `Done` never matched, was dropped, and `emitFirstLoadedDataIfMixedDS`'s
`first(Done || Error)` never completed — the panel spun forever.

Compare against the source panel's own current range
(`sceneGraph.getTimeRange(sourceDataProvider)`) instead. That still discards
the genuinely stale value replayed by the upstream ReplaySubject after a
time-range change (its range differs from the source's current range), while
keeping the fresh terminal emission, which always matches the source's own
range regardless of any override on the chain or source.

Adds a regression test for the Mixed + PanelTimeRange override case and
extends the test helper to model a source range that differs from the chain.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

asynchronously. While the provider was in NotReadyState, flag evaluation
returned the default value (false) instead of the configured in-memory
flag, intermittently failing the "enabled when toggle on" subtest. Use
SetProviderAndWait so the provider is ready before any test runs.

commit.message:
Tempo: prevent case-insensitive header collision when forwarding team headers (#125796)

When streamingForwardTeamHeadersTempo is enabled, gRPC metadata is forwarded
alongside datasource-configured HTTP headers. gRPC lowercases metadata keys,
so an incoming x-scope-orgid would land in the merged map next to the
datasource's canonical X-Scope-Orgid. On the wire both serialize to the same
case-insensitive name and Go's randomised map iteration can deliver the wrong
value, surfacing as Tempo's "no org id" error.

Drop team headers whose key collides case-insensitively with a
datasource-configured header so datasource settings always take precedence.

Fixes #123923

commit.message:
Search: parallel chunk I/O for KV-backed snapshots (#126090)

WriteSnapshotFile and ReadSnapshotFile previously walked chunks serially.
On the write side every chunk is independent, and on the read side chunks
1..N-1 are independent once chunk 0 has been fetched (its size reveals the
writer's chunk size). Both paths now run their chunk loops through an
errgroup with a configurable fan-out.

Concurrency is exposed as index_snapshot_kv_chunk_concurrency in cfg
and plumbed to KVRemoteIndexStoreConfig.ChunkConcurrency. The default
is 1, which is the previous serial behavior. Operators can raise it at
runtime to measure throughput tradeoffs without redeploying.

Parallel reads write to dst via io.NewOffsetWriter, one per chunk, so
no per-chunk buffer is held in memory. *os.File.WriteAt is safe under
concurrent use to non-overlapping regions, which is what our slots are
by construction.

commit.message:
A11y: Announce Card isSelected state with a meaningful name (#126088)

* A11y: Announce Card isSelected state with a meaningful name

The selection radio rendered for a selected Card had a hardcoded generic
'option' accessible name, so assistive tech announced an indistinguishable
'option' for every card in a list of selectable cards. Name the radio after
the card heading via aria-labelledby so each selectable card is
distinguishable.

* Card: Remove explanatory comments

* Card: Only apply selection radio fallback label when heading is empty

aria-labelledby always wins over aria-label in the accessible name
computation, so setting both meant the generic 'option' fallback was
never used for named cards and gave no name at all for cards without
heading text. Apply exactly one labeling mechanism based on whether the
heading has content.

commit.message:
Dashboards: Wire the ResourcePermission API into embedded mode for default permissions (#125931)

* Dashboards: Wire the ResourcePermission API into embedded mode for default permissions

The dashboard API server sets default permissions one of two ways: the
standalone/MT apiserver injects a ResourcePermission dynamic client and uses
the App Platform setter, while embedded mode used the legacy SQL path. Close
that gap so embedded mode uses the same App Platform path when the
kubernetesAuthzResourcePermissionApis flag is enabled.

- register.go: build the ResourcePermission client lazily from the
  restConfigProvider (already a RegisterAPIService param) on first use; select
  setDefaultDashboardPermissions when standalone OR the flag is on. afterDelete
  and setDefaultDashboardPermissions now go through the lazy getter, which uses
  a mutex (no data race, no sticky-error caching).
- dashboard_service.go: set the grafana.app/grant-permissions=default
  annotation on root dashboard creation (flag-gated) so the App Platform setter
  fires, and skip the legacy inline SetDefaultPermissions for dashboards when
  the flag is on. Folders and flag-off behaviour are unchanged.

No wired signatures change, so no wire regeneration is required.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Dashboards: Trim verbose comments

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Dashboards: Address review feedback on embedded default permissions

- Skip the legacy permission deletion in dashboardStorageWrapper.Delete
  when the flag is on, so deletion happens solely via the App Platform
  afterDelete hook and not twice (mirrors standalone, which has no wrapper)
- Guard the grant-permissions annotation with !cmd.IsFolder so a folder
  saved through saveDashboardThroughK8s never gets the dashboard setter
- Add a test for the wrapper delete behaviour under both flag states

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Update comment

Co-authored-by: Gabriel MABILLE <gamab@users.noreply.github.com>

* Dashboards: Fix default permissions for non-admin dashboard creators

The App Platform permission path (active under the
kubernetesAuthzResourcePermissionApis flag) wrote the ResourcePermission
using the requester's identity, which fails for non-admin creators who
don't yet have permission to manage permissions on the brand-new
dashboard. Use a service identity for the write instead, mirroring the
delete hook.

Also grant the creating user or service account admin on their
dashboard, matching the legacy SetDefaultPermissionsAfterCreate
behaviour. The create branch previously only applied the default
basic-role permissions, so creators never received admin.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Fix lint

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Co-authored-by: Gabriel MABILLE <gamab@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
Folders: Wire the ResourcePermission API into embedded mode for default permissions (#125927)

* Folders: Set default permissions via the resource-permission API path

In embedded/monolith mode the folder API was registered with the legacy
folderPermissionsSvc (SQL + GetSignedInUser), whose default-permission step
runs inside the apiserver create hook where there is no web request context.
For root folders this failed with "user not found", so the folder was created
but its default permissions were never written.

When kubernetesAuthzResourcePermissionApis is enabled, register the folder API
with the App Platform path instead: build a loopback ResourcePermission
dynamic client (lazily, from the eventual rest config) and leave
folderPermissionsSvc unwired so the legacy folderStorage wrapper isn't
installed. Default permissions are then written as a ResourcePermission
(Editor/Viewer) which goes to unified storage and syncs to Zanzana — no legacy
SQL and no GetSignedInUser. Creator-admin continues to come from the basic
Admin role.

Also set the grafana.app/grant-permissions=default annotation on root-folder
creation in the unified store, since the legacy /api/folders path (still used
by the frontend) does not set it and the App Platform permission setter is
driven by that annotation. Nested folders are unaffected — they inherit from
the parent via the Zanzana folder hierarchy.

Regenerates the wire graph.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Folders: Fix data race and sticky-error in lazy resource-permission client

Replace sync.Once with a mutex in resourcePermissionsClient:
- The Once approach read resourcePermissionsSvc on the fast path outside
  any synchronization while the Once body wrote it, racing on concurrent
  first-time folder creates (go test -race would flag it).
- sync.Once also cached a transient failure (e.g. a cancelled request
  context in GetRestConfig) permanently, poisoning all later creates.

Branch on restConfigProvider first so the MT path (client injected, field
never mutated) reads without locking, and the monolith path always builds
under the mutex and only caches on success.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Folders: Trim verbose comments

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Add comment for agents

* Folders: Use resourcePermissionsClient in afterDelete hook

In embedded mode the ResourcePermission client is built lazily and the
field is nil until the first create, so afterDelete reading the field
directly would skip permission cleanup. Route through
resourcePermissionsClient so the lazy-build path is used.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Folders: Request default permissions for root folders in resource-permission integration test

The integration tests create root folders directly via /apis, bypassing the
folderimpl layer that requests default permissions on the legacy /api/folders
path. Default permissions are opt-in via the grant-permissions annotation, so
without it no default ResourcePermission was created and
createRootFolderWithoutDefaultPermissions failed when trying to delete one.

Set the grant-permissions=default annotation when the helper creates a root
folder, mirroring the production folder-creation flow.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Folders: Request default permissions for root test folders in dashboard API test

The dashboard integration test created its root test folder without the
grant-permissions annotation, so Editors/Viewers never received default
access via the resource-permission path and dashboard creation in the
folder was denied. Set the annotation for root folders, matching the
resource-permission integration test.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Folders: set default permissions as a service identity with creator admin

When an editor (or any non-admin) created a root folder, setDefaultFolderPermissions
wrote the ResourcePermission through the loopback API server using the requester's
identity. The creator does not yet hold set-permissions on the brand-new folder, so the
ResourcePermission authorizer's parent fetch was denied and folder creation failed with
500 "create root permissions".

Setting the default permissions is a system operation triggered by folder creation, not
an action the requester performs directly. Run it under a service identity (mirroring the
dashboard path and MT, where the injected client uses a service token), and grant the
creator admin on the new folder in addition to the default basic-role permissions.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Folders: add default case to identity type switch for exhaustive lint

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
Dashboards: preserve datasource name through v2 export/import (#125824)

* DashboardExport: include original datasource name in v2 export labels

Adds a new `grafana.app/export-datasource-name` label that captures the
display name of the datasource at export time, alongside the existing
`grafana.app/export-label` grouping key. The new label is written for
panel queries, query variables, ad-hoc/group-by variables, and
annotation queries. Built-in datasources and unresolved UIDs (e.g.
deleted datasources) are skipped, so behaviour is unchanged when no
name is available.

* DashboardImport: surface original datasource name in v2 import picker

Reads the new `grafana.app/export-datasource-name` label produced by
the v2 exporter and uses it as the field label in the import form, so
dashboards exported with multiple datasources of the same type (e.g.
several MySQL instances) can be told apart at import time.

The export label is still the unique input name used for form state;
only the displayed field label and description are enriched. The new
label is stripped alongside the existing export label when the form
is applied, so the saved dashboard does not retain export-only
metadata.

* DashboardImport: tooltip listing panels that reference each datasource

Collects panel titles per export label in extractV2Inputs and surfaces
them through a new `usedByPanels` field on `DataSourceInput`. The v2
import form renders an info icon next to the datasource picker label;
hovering it reveals a tooltip with the list of panels that originally
referenced that datasource, helping users map inputs to dashboard
panels when multiple datasources share the same type.

Panels with no title fall back to their element key. Datasources that
are only referenced from variables or annotations show no tooltip.

* DashboardImport: auto-select matching datasource on v2 import

When an exported v2 dashboard carries the original datasource name and
the importing instance has a datasource of the same plugin type with
an identical name, pre-select it in the import form picker. Saves the
user from manually picking a same-named datasource (a common case when

Alerting: fix missing requester context in alertmanager datasource proxy (#126117)

The alerting proxy (withReq) creates a fresh http.NewRequest with
context.Background(), discarding all context values from the original
request — including the identity set by the auth middleware.
NewDataSourceProxy then fails with "failed to get requester from
context" when it calls identity.GetRequester on that blank context.

Fix by using http.NewRequestWithContext with the original request's
context, so identity, tracing spans, and cancellation are all
propagated correctly into the upstream proxy request.

Regression introduced by #125752.

* Alerting: add test verifying request context is propagated through withReq

commit.message:
IAM: Implement GetByUID in the Kubernetes user service (#125945)

* Add GetByUID implementation, change RBAC user resolution to fix listing team members

* Add tests

* Revert unnecessary changes

* IAM: Propagate request context to k8s GetByUID in resource permission DTO conversion

convertK8sResourcePermissionToDTO resolved User/ServiceAccount subjects via
userService.GetByUID(context.Background(), ...). With the new k8s-backed
GetByUID, the userk8s client needs the *contextmodel.ReqContext from the
request context (getRestConfig -> contexthandler.FromContext); a background
context yields "no request context", silently falling back to the legacy SQL
store. In multi-instance deployments where users live in unified storage but
each instance has its own SQLite, that fallback can't resolve the user, so the
returned permission has empty userId/userLogin and the frontend drops it from
the permissions list.

Thread the request context through convertK8sResourcePermissionToDTO and use it
for the GetByUID call so the k8s user lookup succeeds.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* AccessControl: resolve permission subjects with a service identity

When listing a resource's permissions, resolving each subject UID to its display
name went through the caller's identity. A non-admin authorized to read the
resource's permissions (e.g. an editor viewing a dashboard they created) is not
allowed to read user/team objects, so the lookup 403'd and the subject rendered
without a name. Resolve subjects with a service identity instead, matching the
legacy SQL-join behavior.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
Search: auto-create vector backfill jobs from the reconciler (#126006)

The reconciler provisions a resource's partition leaf and backfill job on
the first write event for it (ensureResourceInitialized), bounded by the
event's RV. It owns the backfiller and runs it on a loop, so jobs created
lazily on the write path get drained within one interval.

Event RVs and the checkpoint are canonicalized to snowflake
(resource.ToSnowflakeRV) at the reconciler/backfiller comparison
boundaries so the cursor stays valid across a SQL<->KV backend swap.

commit.message:
AccessControl: scope Zanzana-merged permissions by resource, not action prefix (#126116)

The Zanzana->legacy RBAC merge derived a permission's scope kind from the
action prefix, so sub-resource actions like folders.permissions:read were
scoped on folders.permissions:uid:<uid> instead of folders:uid:<uid>. Legacy
RBAC (and folder canAdmin) scope these on the base resource, so the grant never
matched and an editor with admin on a folder could not manage its permissions.

Scope objects by the resource type Zanzana listed them under instead. This is
correct for every action uniformly, including permission-management actions.

Add table-driven tests over common.SupportedActions() asserting scope kind
follows the resource for item, folder and All grants.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
Search: Normalize root folder UID to fix root dashboard search during rollout (#126137)

PR #125681 moved the "general" -> "" root-folder normalization out of the
dashboard search API server and into the unified search backend, which expands
a root filter to match both sentinels. The search backend is deployed
separately and can lag this API server. While skewed, the API server sends
"general" but the un-upgraded backend does not expand it and only matches the
"" that root-parented dashboards are still indexed with, so searching the root
("general") folder returns no dashboards.

Re-add foldermodel.ToLegacyFolderUID on the query side so the request always
carries "". An up-to-date backend still expands "" to both sentinels, so this
is correct in both the skewed and fully-upgraded states.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
Frontend Service: Remove compiledBootScript feature flag (#124369)

* Frontend: Fail fast in NewIndexProvider when boot.js is missing

Previously the os.ReadFile error was swallowed and bootScript was set
to empty bytes. With the inline boot script fallback in index.html
about to be removed, a missing boot.js would render an empty <script>
tag and silently break the app at runtime. Surface the error at startup
instead.

* Frontend Platform: Remove compiledBootScript feature flag

The flag is at 100% in prod; the compiled boot.js path is the only path.
Removes the registry entry, regenerates feature-toggle artifacts, drops
the conditional in IndexProvider, and collapses the [[if .BootScript]]
template branch in index.html (~270-line inline duplicate of the TS boot
script).

The test helper now writes a stub boot.js into the temp build dir so
NewIndexProvider's fail-fast read still passes.

commit.message:
Org switching: fix missing dispatch in OrganizationSwitcher (#120967)

* Org switching: fix missing dispatch in OrganizationSwitcher

OrganizationSwitcher called setUserOrganization(orgId) without dispatch,
so the thunk never ran and POST /api/user/using/:orgId was never sent.
The switch only worked incidentally because the OrgRedirect middleware
caught ?orgId in the subsequent page reload.

orgId injection into SPA navigations is handled centrally by
locationService.push/replace via setLocationServiceOrgIdGetter (#120978).

* Org switching: await dispatch before page reload

`setUserOrganization` is an async thunk that POSTs to
/api/user/using/:orgId to persist the user's preferred org server-side.
Without await, window.location.reload() fires before the POST completes,
losing the persistence (the next visit without ?orgId lands in the
default org). Make onSelectChange async and await the dispatch so the
POST is in-flight (or done) before reload.

* Org switching: collapse push+reload into assign, sharpen comment

The previous push + reload sequence did two things when one would do.
locationService.push fires history.pushState (URL changes, React
re-renders with new URL but old Redux/contextSrv state), and the
window.location.reload that follows discards all that SPA state with
a fresh GET on the now-changed URL. That brief intermediate render
is wasted work and a possible source of UI flicker. assign accomplishes
the same end-state in one step and drops the unused locationService
import.

Also reword the comment so it documents the actual bug (the previous
non-dispatched call discarded the action entirely) rather than implying
a race.

* Update public/app/core/components/AppChrome/OrganizationSwitcher/OrganizationSwitcher.tsx

Co-authored-by: Alex Khomenko <Clarity-89@users.noreply.github.com>

* Update public/app/core/components/AppChrome/OrganizationSwitcher/OrganizationSwitcher.tsx

* Apply suggestion from @QuentinBisson

* OrganizationSwitcher: wrap dispatch in try/catch and restore template literal

- catch errors from setUserOrganization so an unhandled rejection can't
  escape; backendSrv already surfaces the toast
- abort navigation on failure to avoid reloading into a half-switched org
- restore backticks on window.location.assign (GitHub stripped them when
  applying the suggestion) and import config from @grafana/runtime

* OrganizationSwitcher: type-only import + cover onSelectChange paths

- Use `import type` for SelectableValue so the lint rule
  `@typescript-eslint/consistent-type-imports` is satisfied
- Add tests that exercise the success and rejected dispatch paths
  through the Select onChange handler so the new try/catch and the
  navigation call are covered

---------

Co-authored-by: Alex Khomenko <Clarity-89@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-authored-by: Clarity-89 <homes89@ukr.net>

commit.message:
Provisioning: Validate branch/commit/pull request options against repository type (#126145)

* Provisioning: Forbid branch and commit options on local repositories

Branch and commit options (spec.branch, spec.commit) are only meaningful
for the branch workflow, which is not supported on local repositories.
Reject them during validation so configuration that can never take effect
is not silently stored.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Also forbid pull request options on local repositories

spec.pullRequest is the third branch-workflow-only sibling alongside
spec.branch and spec.commit; reject it on local repositories for the
same reason.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Forbid pull request options on plain git repositories

Pull requests are a hosting-provider feature. Plain git repositories
support the branch workflow but cannot open pull requests, so reject
spec.pullRequest for the git repository type (branch and commit options
remain valid there).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Extract validateWorkflowOptions to reduce complexity

Move the repository-type vs branch/commit/pull-request option checks out
of RepositoryValidator.Validate into a dedicated helper to bring the
function back under the gocyclo threshold. No behavior change.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Add default case to satisfy exhaustive linter

validateWorkflowOptions switches on RepositoryType; add a default case
(default-signifies-exhaustive is enabled) to cover the hosting-provider
types that support all options.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
Alerting: Return merge stats from convert Alertmanager import API (#126120)

* Alerting: return added and renamed resources from config merge

Receivers and TimeIntervals now also return the incoming resource names
after any rename has been applied. MergeExtraConfig returns the merged
config separately from a MergeResult that embeds RenameResources and
records the resources added during the merge (route, receivers, time
intervals, templates, inhibition rules). LogContext reports all of them.

Callers in MultiOrgAlertmanager and the imported-config legacy storage
adapt to the new signatures; their public return types are unchanged.

* Alerting: include merge stats in convert Alertmanager API response

SaveAndApplyExtraConfiguration now returns merge.MergeResult instead of
merge.RenameResources. The convert Alertmanager endpoint keeps reporting
renamed resources in rename_resources and now also reports what the merge
added (route, receivers, time intervals, templates, inhibition rules) in
a new stats object on ConvertAlertmanagerResponse.

commit.message:
fix(plugins): forward Azure managed identity env vars to plugin processes (#125170)

Azure platforms (Container Apps, App Service, AKS Workload Identity) inject
discovery env vars (IDENTITY_ENDPOINT, IDENTITY_HEADER, AZURE_FEDERATED_TOKEN_FILE,
etc.) that the azidentity SDK reads from the plugin process. PR #113412 stopped
forwarding host env vars by default in 12.4.0, which broke managed identity auth
for Azure plugins (e.g. Azure Data Explorer).

Mirror the AWS fix (#119772): forward these host env vars to plugins on the
existing azure.forward_settings_to_plugins allowlist, gated on
managed_identity_enabled / workload_identity_enabled.

commit.message:
AccessControl: propagate team membership to the Zanzana→RBAC merge (#126126)

* AccessControl: propagate team membership to the Zanzana->RBAC merge

The Zanzana->legacy permission merge built its List request without the user's
teams, so server-side contextual team-membership tuples (team:<name>#member)
were never added and ListObjects didn't traverse team-based grants. Folders and
dashboards a user can only access via a team grant were therefore missing from
the materialized legacy permissions (e.g. the folder list), even though the
forward Check path (which passes teams) allowed access.

Pass the signed-in user's teams into the merge List, mirroring the id token
groups claim (resolveGroupsClaim): proxy/IdP external groups when
id_use_external_groups_for_groups_claim is set, otherwise stored team
memberships. Per-user search paths pass no teams.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Remove comment

commit.message:
i18n: add eslint rules for plural t() and Trans defaults (#125319)

* i18n: add eslint rules for plural t() and Trans defaults

Adds two ESLint rules that enforce the conventions introduced in
the t() and <Trans> plural-defaults migrations:

- t-plural-defaults: when a t() call's options object contains
  "count", the positional defaultValue must be empty and both
  defaultValue_one and defaultValue_other must be declared in
  options.
- trans-plural-defaults: when a <Trans> element passes count
  (directly or via values={{count}}), it must declare a tOptions
  prop containing both defaultValue_one and defaultValue_other.

Both rules are intentionally not auto-fixable; the singular form
cannot be inferred, so violations must be fixed by hand.

Follow-up to the t() and <Trans> migration PRs.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
Dashboards: Refetch folder children after k8s import (#122951)

The k8s-backed import flow (both v1 and v2) calls
getDashboardAPI().saveDashboard() directly against the app-platform
Dashboard client and bypasses the saveDashboard RTK Query mutation.
Because the browse-folder list reads from Redux state that the
saveDashboard mutation normally invalidates via refetchChildren, imports
into an already-visited folder left the cached list stale and required
a hard refresh for the newly-imported dashboard to appear.

Dispatch refetchChildren (and invalidate the quotas cache) from both
ImportOverviewV1 and ImportOverviewV2 after a successful save so the
destination folder picks up the new dashboard immediately. This matches
what the RTK Query saveDashboard mutation does for the editor-save
path.

Covers paste-JSON, file upload, and grafana.com imports - they all flow
through the same form. The legacy non-k8s import path already goes
through the importDashboard RTK mutation and is unaffected.

commit.message:
Provisioning: Degrade gracefully when settings read is forbidden in repository view hook (#126157)

Users with folder permissions but no basic role (org role None) lack
provisioning.settings:read, so the frontend settings query returns 403 and
useGetResourceRepositoryView failed closed, blocking dashboard import into
plain folders. Treat a settings 403 as "not provisioned" when the target
folder's annotations show it is not repo-managed; repo-annotated folders,
name-based lookups, and folder query failures keep failing closed.

commit.message:
Search: Fix Bedrock embedding throttling under token quota (#126249)

* Search: Fix Bedrock embedding throttling under token quota

The Bedrock embedder used the AWS SDK default retryer (3 attempts, no
client-side rate limiting), so transient ThrottlingException (429) on
InvokeModel failed embeds outright. Enable adaptive retry mode and raise
the attempt ceiling via a new bedrock_max_attempts config (default 5).

Also fix a config bug where the Bedrock embedder used VertexBatchSize
instead of BedrockBatchSize, silently ignoring bedrock_batch_size, and
raise the per-batch call timeout to 60s so retries are not cut short.

commit.message:
Search: wire DashboardStats into the standalone server backfiller (#126153)

The registerServer path (storage-server target) built ServerOptions
without DashboardStats, so the vector backfiller's zero-views filter
was silently disabled. The client path already set it.

Provide the stats through a WithDashboardStats ServiceOption. The
InitializeSearchSupport injector (replacing InitializeDocumentBuilders)
builds the document builders and the stats from one graph, so they
share an instance and the sprinkles metrics register once. The
storage-server target without enable_search uses the narrower
InitializeDashboardStats injector instead. Both injectors receive the
module server's already-constructed dependencies as parameters and run
inside the module init, so other dskit targets don't pick up the
dependency chain.

commit.message:
Provisioning: Add Branch settings and Commit options sections (#125928)

* Provisioning: Add Branch settings and Commit options sections

Surface the branch and commit template options from the Commit & PR
Conventions spec scaffolding in both the onboarding wizard and the
repository configuration page. Both sections render only for git-based
repositories.

- Branch settings: branch name template and enforcement (BranchOptions)
- Commit options (advanced): commit message template and enforcement
  (CommitOptions)

The existing PR/merge-request workflow and push-to-branch options are
left unchanged. RepositoryFormData now carries branchOptions (the flat
branch field keeps the branch name); dataToSpec/specToData map the new
options, omitting empty values.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Cover branch/commit option mapping; merge git-only guards

Add data mapping tests for the enforceTemplate paths and the new branch
options (previously only the commit message template path was covered),
restoring branch coverage for the navigation-owned provisioning code.

Also collapse the two adjacent isGitProvider guards in ConfigForm and
FinishStep into a single conditional wrapping both sections.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Gate branch options and commit enforce behind gitConventions

Hide the new git convention controls behind the provisioning.gitConventions
OpenFeature flag (default off):

- BranchOptionsSection renders nothing when the flag is disabled
- CommitOptionsSection hides the enforce-template option when disabled, while
  the commit message template stays available

The flag is read inside each section via useBooleanFlagValue, matching the
existing provisioning pattern (FolderReadmePanel).

commit.message:
Unified Storage: fix flaky TestIntegrationSQLKVConcurrentCreateClientRetry (#126272)

Raise the gRPC retry budget for Create calls inside runConcurrentCreateRetry,
so the test does not run out of retries.

The test starts 10 goroutines that all try to create the same resource. It
expects 1 to succeed and the other 9 to get AlreadyExists.

When the lease backend is used, only one caller at a time can hold the lease.
The other 9 get a conflict and need to retry. The gRPC client is configured
to retry only 3 times, with a 1 second base delay. With 10 concurrent callers,
3 retries is not enough, so some calls give up and return code = Aborted to
the test.

The retry settings can be overridden per call by passing grpc.CallOption's.
The test now passes a larger max retries (concurrency * 2) and a 500 ms linear
backoff, so all 9 losing callers have time to retry until they see
AlreadyExists. Production code is not changed.

expr/sql: enable SQL trace redaction for server-side expressions (#126168)

* expr/sql: enable SQL trace redaction for server-side expressions

Bumps the go-mysql-server fork to a build that includes the merged
upstream opt-in SQL trace redaction (dolthub/go-mysql-server#3537) and
opts the SSE SQL context into it via WithTraceRedaction(true).

GMS trace span attributes (the planbuilder "query" attr and the rowexec
"table"/"left"/"right" attrs) carry the user's SQL verbatim, including
table identifiers and literal filter values. With redaction enabled,
identifiers become stable tokens (n1, n2, ...) and literals become value
tokens ('v1', :v2, ...), deduped per query

commit.message:
Provisioning: Write `_folder.json` when creating dashboards in new folders (#126042)

* Provisioning: Write _folder.json when creating dashboards in new folders

When `provisioningFolderMetadata` is enabled, dashboard creation via
`POST /files/new-folder/dashboard.json` now writes `_folder.json` for
any new folders created along the path. Previously only explicit folder
creation and sync/export wrote folder metadata, causing UID mismatches
when the same folder was later created explicitly.

Adds `WithWriteFolderMetadata()` option to `EnsurePathOption` pattern.
The `createOrUpdate` path in `DualReadWriter` opts in when the metadata
flag is enabled. Only new folders are affected — existing folders without
metadata are not backfilled.

Closes grafana/git-ui-sync-project#1158

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Move _folder.json write into resolveFolderForPath

Move the folder metadata write from the walk callback (after
EnsureFolderExists) into resolveFolderForPath. This ensures _folder.json
is only written for genuinely new folders — those with no existing
_folder.json and not in the in-memory tree.

The previous approach could backfill metadata for folders that exist in
K8s but aren't in the tree, since EnsureFolderExists returns nil for
both new and existing folders.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* correctly generate ID for file

* using different approach, only concerning git files

* push folder metadata in single commits

* addressing comments

* reading folder existence from the repo itself

* using ensureTrailingSlash

commit.message:
search: introduce SearchFieldDefinition and SearchFieldsProvider (#126269)

* search: introduce SearchFieldDefinition and SearchFieldsProvider

Phase 1 of manifest-driven search metadata. Adds the new internal model
behind a translation shim, with no consumer changes.

SearchFieldDefinition replaces *resourcepb.ResourceTableColumnDefinition
as the internal representation for search-mapping decisions. The
protobuf type stays as the wire format for legacy table responses.

SearchFieldsProvider is the read-only interface, keyed by
{group, resource, version}, with PreferredVersion for the
unknown-apiVersion fallback rule. The default mapProvider is an
in-memory implementation populated from Go-level registrations;
later work will swap it for one that reads CUE-generated manifest data.

Capability and type constants match the design: filter, text, partial,
sort, facet, retrieve; string, int32, int64, float, double, boolean,
date. No dateTime, no object, no binary.

The searchFieldsFromTableColumns helper preserves current behavior:
Filterable+STRING translates to [filter, retrieve], everything else to
[retrieve].

* search: address Phase 1 review comments

- Replace local GroupResourceVersion struct with schema.GroupVersionResource;
  we already depend on the k8s schema package for GroupResource.
- Add explicit SearchFieldTypeUnknown constant for protobuf shapes (OBJECT,
  BINARY, UNKNOWN_TYPE) that have no SearchFieldType counterpart, so
  downstream switches can reference it by name instead of comparing to the
  empty string.
- Document that the slice returned by SearchFieldsProvider.Fields is owned
  by the provider and must not be mutated, rather than copying defensively
  on every lookup.

commit.message:
Pyroscope: Fix debug logs bypassing GF_LOG_LEVEL (#126289)

The package-level var logger = backend.NewLoggerWith(...) was evaluated
before coreplugin init() could install the in-process logger override,
so the datasource captured the SDK's default hclog at Debug level and
emitted JSON straight to stderr regardless of configured log level.

Move logger construction into ProvideService and thread it through
NewPyroscopeDatasource and the helpers it calls, matching the pattern
used by Loki, Tempo and the SQL datasources.

commit.message:
SQLStore: exponential backoff with jitter for SQLITE_BUSY transaction retries (#126318)

When a SQLite write hits SQLITE_BUSY, WithTransactionalDbSession retries
the transaction. Today the retry uses a constant 10 ms sleep with 5
retries (worst case 50 ms total), which is too short for the contention
we actually see. The symptom in CI is e.g. plugin signature key writes
failing during server startup, which then cascades into plugin
signature verification errors and flaky e2e tests (e.g. advisor.spec.ts).

Changes:
- Replace the constant 10 ms sleep with exponential backoff capped at
  2 s, with full jitter so concurrent writers don't wake up on the same
  tick and immediately collide again.
- Bump the default transaction_retries from 5 to 10.

commit.message:
unified-storage: fix flaky TestPeriodicBookmarks by ignoring context cancellation in Watch (#126285)

server.Watch has a `case <-ctx.Done(): return nil` branch, but Go's `select`
is nondeterministic: when the context is canceled, the loop sometimes runs a
`srv.Send` instead, which returns context.Canceled. Watch then propagates
that error, even though the cancellation was clean. This is what makes
TestPeriodicBookmarks flaky.

Fix: a deferred check at the top of Watch converts a returned context.Canceled
or context.DeadlineExceeded to nil, but only when our own context is done.
Other errors are still propagated. New TestWatchContextCancellation covers all
three branches.

commit.message:
search: drive bleve field mappings from SearchFieldDefinition capabilities (#126280)

The per-kind "fields.<name>" loop in getBleveDocMappings used to special-case
Filterable STRING columns and rely on Bleve dynamic mapping for everything
else. It now translates the per-kind SearchableDocumentFields into the new
SearchFieldDefinition representation and emits bleve field mappings based
on declared capabilities (filter, text, partial, sort, facet, retrieve).

Behaviour is preserved byte-for-byte for every in-tree builder. Today's
only exercised combination — Filterable+STRING translated to
[filter, retrieve] — still produces a single keyword mapping at
"fields.<name>" with the same Store / DocValues / IncludeTermVectors /
SkipFreqNorm settings as before. Other capability combinations are
reachable through the helper but not exercised by any in-tree builder
yet.

The helper retains the title legacy suffix: a field named "title" gets
its keyword variant under "title_phrase" instead of "title_keyword" for
in-tree gRPC client compatibility.

To lock down the on-disk index mapping shape, a golden JSON snapshot test
covers GetBleveMappings for three representative inputs (no per-kind
fields, a Filterable STRING field, and selectable fields). The snapshots
were generated from origin/main at 518fecc6df7 — the last commit before
this work began — so any future shape change will fail the test until
the operator regenerates with -update-golden.

SearchFieldsFromTableColumns was exported because this is the first
cross-package caller.

Standard hardcoded top-level mappings (title, description, tags, folder,
manager.*, source.*, labels.*, reference.*, etc.) are unchanged. They
will be migrated to capability declarations in a follow-up.

* Provisioning: use SecretTextArea built-in configured/reset for signing key

SecretTextArea already renders a disabled "configured" textarea plus a
Reset button when isConfigured is true. Pass isConfigured and onReset
to it instead of branching on a separate disabled TextArea, and drop the
now-redundant Reset button in the signing-method section (it fired on the
same condition, so it would have rendered a duplicate). Remove the two
orphaned i18n keys.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: deduplicate commit signing fields into one shared object

The five signing fields are identical across github, gitlab, bitbucket
and git providers. Group them into a single signingFields object and
spread it into each provider instead of repeating the assignments.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: scope empty PathValue helper to resetSigning

The empty placeholder is only used inside resetSigning, so declare it
there to keep the scope tight.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: move commit signing validators into utils/validators

Extract the signer, signing-key and S/MIME certificate validators out of
CommitOptionsSection into utils/validators as factory functions that take
the relevant signing state as a parameter. Add unit tests for each.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: place trufflehog:ignore on same line as test URLs

TruffleHog requires the ignore comment on the same line as the detected
secret. The credential URLs in the validateNoUserInfoInUrl tests had the
comment on the following line, so extract each URL to its own line that
carries the trufflehog:ignore.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: derive signing key secret in a shared helper

The set/keep/remove decision for the commit signing key was split between
ConfigForm, useWizardSubmission and useCreateOrUpdateRepository. Extract it
into deriveSigningKeySecret next to dataToSpec, returning the InlineSecureValue
entry directly, and have both submit paths use it. updateOrCreate now takes
the derived entry instead of separate key/remove flags. Add unit tests.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: mock deriveSigningKeySecret in useWizardSubmission test

The test mocks the whole ../../utils/data module. After useWizardSubmission
started calling deriveSigningKeySecret, the unmocked export was undefined and
threw before submitData ran, failing 9 cases. Add it to the module mock.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Reorganize the repository config form so webhook configuration lives in its
own collapsible section and the 'Enable dashboard previews in pull requests'
toggle moves into the pull request options section. Also drop the '(advanced)'
suffix from the branch, commit, and pull request option section labels.

Replace module-level jest.mock of the GettingStarted features helpers with the
MSW-integrated test/test-utils render and real runtime config, matching the
surrounding provisioning test conventions.

dashboard previews toggle itself. ConfigForm just passes isGithub and the field
path; the children prop is gone and DashboardPreviewField is generic over the
form type.

previews/webhook fields and their now-unused i18n keys, and fixes the section
label assertions in FinishStep tests.

commit.message:
Tempo: Unify nested span subframe schema across span sets (#124885)

* Tempo: Unify nested span subframe schema across span sets

When a trace had multiple SpanSets carrying different dynamic
attributes, each nested 'Spans' subframe was built from only that
span set's attributes. Consumers like the Table visualization
require every frame stored under a single nestedFrames cell to
share the same fields in the same order, so the mismatched
subframes were dropped or misaligned.

Compute the union of dynamic-attribute fields (and resolved
types) across every span set on a trace once, then build each
subframe from that unified schema. Span sets that lack an
attribute now emit a nil cell for that column instead of
omitting the column entirely.

Note: hasNameAttribute is now evaluated trace-wide rather than
per-span-set, so every subframe under one trace row shares the
same name-column visibility. This matches the new unified-schema
contract.

The shared schema scan is extracted to collectSpanSetsSchema and
also replaces the equivalent inline loop in
transformSpanSearchResponse.

Fixes #121740

* Tempo: Add test for singular SpanSet in nested subframe schema

Adds end-to-end coverage for the singular trace.SpanSet path through
transformTraceSearchResponse, verifying it produces a single nested
frame whose dynamic-attribute column carries the span's value. The
plural trace.SpanSets path was already covered.

commit.message:
Search: declare standard search fields as SearchFieldDefinitions (#126338)

search: declare standard search fields as SearchFieldDefinitions

Move the top-level standard search fields (name, title, description, tags,
folder, createdBy, ownerReferences, managedBy) from hardcoded bleve
FieldMapping literals to declarative SearchFieldDefinitions. The bleve
mapping builder iterates the new StandardSearchFieldDefinitions() list and
emits the corresponding mappings through the existing capability helper.

Adds SearchCapabilityUnranked: applies to text fields only, drops per-term
frequency stats and field-length norms (an index-size optimization that the
existing description field relied on). The capability helper now sets
IncludeInAll false on every emitted mapping; the composite '_all' field is
disabled at the index level, so this is a no-op semantically and centralizes
the explanation.

bleve_mappings_test goldens lose 'include_in_all: true' entries that the
helper previously emitted and 'name' attributes on FieldMappings (bleve uses
the property path; the redundant attribute is no longer set). Runtime
behaviour is unchanged: TestDocumentMapping still indexes the same 19
fields, TestTermVectorsAndFreqNorm still passes (description retains
SkipFreqNorm via the new unranked capability), TestDocValuesConfiguration
still asserts only folder and title_phrase carry DocValues.

commit.message:
CI: Add unified storage compatibility check and AGENTS.md guidance (#126284)

* ci: add unified storage compatibility PR check and AGENTS.md docs

Unified storage/search can run as separate services deployed
independently from the Grafana API layer at different cadences. A PR
changing both sides may break compatibility between versions during
rollout.

- Fail PRs touching both API-layer and unified storage server code;
  exception via no-check-unified-storage-compatibility label
- Document client/server split and compatibility rules in
  pkg/storage/unified/AGENTS.md, reference it from root AGENTS.md
- Regenerate .policy.yml to register the new required check

* ci: widen api_layer group with remaining unified storage client callers

Repo-wide import sweep found client-side callers outside the original
paths: stats, team search, kv leader election lease, and legacysql
dual-write routing. Migrator paths stay out — migration code ships
together with server changes by convention. pkg/server stays out: it
hosts the standalone server targets and wire glue, which would fire on
server-only PRs.

* ci: document path group rationale and sync requirements

Comment kvlease's non-obvious unified storage dependency, the
intentional pkg/server exclusion, and the two client-side blocks that
must stay in sync. Complete the AGENTS.md client/server/contract split
and note that contract-only PRs don't fire the check.

* docs: condense unified storage AGENTS.md

Fold directory table and deployment modes into the client/server split
and intro; keep rules, CI check, and caveats intact.

commit.message:
Provisioning: take over unmanaged parent folders during selective migrate (#126334)

Selective migrate of a resource living inside a pre-existing unmanaged
folder failed: EnsureFolderExists is the ownership gate for folders, but
unlike CheckResourceOwnership it never consulted the migration takeover
allowlist. The export phase records the folder in the allowlist, yet the
sync phase rejected the unmanaged parent ("cannot take over without an
explicit migration") and the resource was skipped because its parent
folder could not be created.

Honour the takeover allowlist in both EnsureFolderExists branches (the
existing-folder path and the create-then-already-exists race path). When
an unmanaged folder is allowlisted, claim it by stamping repo manager and
source properties and forcing the update, mirroring how other resources
are taken over.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

DataSources: Keep async instance-settings cache in sync on DataSourceSrv.reload() (#126276)

* DataSources: Register built-in datasources within the new async API

Moves client-injected built-in datasource registration (e.g. the expression
pseudo-datasource) out of the callers and into the new async settings API,
so built-ins are applied automatically on every cache populate and survive
cache repopulates without caller-side merging.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* DataSources: Validate uid and guard against collisions in registerBuiltIn

Normalize missing uid to name (matching populateMaps), and throw when the
uid is already registered via init or runtime to prevent silent overwrites.
Re-registering the same built-in uid remains idempotent.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* DataSources: Rename registerBuiltIn to setExpressionDataSourceInstanceSettings

Replace the generic builtInByUid map with a single expressionDsSettings
variable and an explicitly named setter. The function name makes clear this
is a temporary bridge until ExpressionDatasource moves to @grafana/runtime.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* DataSources: Guard setExpressionDataSourceInstanceSettings against multiple calls

Throw if called more than once outside of test runs, matching the pattern
used by other set* functions in @grafana/runtime.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* DataSources: Fix prettier formatting in settings.ts

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* DataSources: Keep async instance-settings cache in sync on DataSourceSrv.reload()

DataSourceSrv.reload() refetched /api/frontend/settings and re-inited only the
legacy cache, so the new async datasource API returned stale data after a
datasource add/update/delete until a full page reload. Conversely, the new
reloadDataSourceInstanceSettings() refreshed only the new cache.

Keep both caches consistent from either reload entry point with a single fetch:
reload() now calls a new synchronous syncDataSourceInstanceSettings() helper, and
reloadDataSourceInstanceSettings() delegates to getDataSourceSrv().reload() when a
srv is registered (falling back to a standalone refetch otherwise). Both
resolved-instance caches are cleared on reload. Transition-only scaffolding that
self-removes when DataSourceSrv is gone.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* DataSources: Remove transition comment from reloadDataSourceInstanceSettings

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* DataSources: Make DataSourceSrv.reload() return Promise<void>

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* DataSources: Guard reloadDataSourceInstanceSettings against concurrent reloads

Coalesce concurrent calls into a single in-flight reload so a burst of mutations
triggers one backend refetch instead of one per caller. The guard clears once the
reload settles, so subsequent calls refetch as before.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* DataSources: Use getCachedPromise for reload coalescing; fix explore mock coverage

Replace the hand-rolled in-flight reload guard with the existing getCachedPromise
utility (purpose-built for coalescing concurrent requests for the same resource),
invalidating after settle so later calls still refetch.

Use jest.fn() for the explore test DataSourceSrv reload mock so the required
Promise<void> return no longer adds an uncovered line (restores team coverage).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* DataSources: Simplify reload coalescing test

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Trigger build

commit.message:
DataFrames: Materialize tabular joins without runtime codegen (unsafe-eval) (#126110)

* DataFrames: Add characterization tests for joinTabular edge cases

Pin the behavior of multi-frame tabular joins (the iterative merge that
re-joins a previously cartesian-expanded left table) and null join-column
values, neither of which was covered. These guard a follow-up refactor of
the materialization step.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* DataFrames: Materialize tabular joins without runtime codegen

joinTabular used new Function() to compile a column-unrolled materialize
step, which requires the 'unsafe-eval' CSP directive. Replace it with a
column-major fill driven by a precomputed per-row source plan: this keeps
the hot path free of an inner per-column loop, is more cache-friendly, and
needs no eval. Behavior is unchanged (guarded by the join test suites).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
Provisioning: Record Grafana user in bulk, move and fix-metadata commits (#126416)

The Grafana-saved-by trailer was only riding through to commits for
single-resource saves and the migrate job. Bulk delete, bulk move, and
fix-folder-metadata jobs left the user unrecorded because their job
options had no message field.

The backend now exposes a top-level JobSpec.Message that applies to every
commit-producing action (delete, move, migrate, push, fixFolderMetadata)
via jobs.CommitMessage(), so wire the frontend to pass
withSavedByTrailer(...) through it:

- Bulk delete / bulk move: use the user's comment when provided, else a
  sensible default, tagged with the trailer.
- Fix folder metadata: tag the default message with the trailer.
- Migrate: move off the deprecated MigrateJobOptions.Message onto the
  top-level JobSpec.Message.

Pull/sync is intentionally left untagged — it replicates the remote branch
locally and produces no commit.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
Navigation: Populate starred nav section client-side (#126148)

* Navigation: Sync starred dashboards into nav tree on the client

Populate the starred nav section from the stars API plus unified search
instead of relying solely on bootData, so the menu stays correct as
stars change and in dual-writer mode 5.

The search index is eventually consistent, so the reducer keeps the
optimistic nav entry for any starred uid missing from the search
response instead of dropping it.

* Navigation: Show skeleton in starred section while items load

Starred items are now synced client-side, so an expanded starred
section flashed the empty message until the stars query and search
round-trip completed. useSyncStarredItemsInNav exposes the full sync
window as isLoading and MegaMenuItem renders skeleton rows instead of
the empty message while it is true.

The loading flag is initialized from the stars query so a remount with
a warm RTK cache does not flash skeletons, and it resolves on the
search error path so a failure falls back to the empty message.

* Navigation: Document starred nav cap parity with backend

* Navigation: Show error state in starred nav section when sync fails

Review feedback: a failed stars query or search round-trip previously
fell back to the misleading empty-state message. The sync hook now
exposes isError and MegaMenuItem renders "Failed to load items" in
the expanded section instead.

Also renames the test file to hooks.test.tsx to match the source file
naming convention, and expands the setStarredItems comment to cover
the deleted-dashboard case.

commit.message:
Fix: Replace email domain with example.com (#126014)

Replace email domain with example.com

Grafana uses the existing domain email.com for documentation, examples
and defaults. This can leak information to email.com which is currently
operated by 1&1 / IONOS Inc.
This changes it to the special domain example.com from RFC-2606 and
RFC-6761. That domain is reserved for testing and documentation.
example.com has no MX record. So no information can leak to an external
domain. This should also avoid harming the SMTP servers IP reputation.

commit.message:
unified-storage/search: keep cached bleve index on disk regardless of ownership (#126525)

After a search-api ring reshuffle, a pod can lose ownership of a resource
while the file-based index for it is still cached and in use. The disk
cleanup sweep gated the "keep the currently-cached active index" branch on
ownership, so in that window it would RemoveAll the directory of a live
bleve index. Subsequent scorch persister writes then failed forever with
"persist err: ... no such file or directory", and the affected pod kept
serving the broken index until restart.

Drop the `owned &&` guard: the cache is the source of truth for "is it
open", and closing unowned cached indexes is runEvictExpiredOrUnownedIndexes's
job, not the disk sweep's.

Home: Add Most Used tab and firing alerts card (#125719)

* feat(home): add Most Used tab, Alerts/Incidents row, and homepage extension points

- Add Most Used dashboards tab (analytics feature gate)
- Add Firing Alerts card and Active Incidents card below dashboard tabs
- Add homepage extension points (HomepagePre, HomepageExtra, HomepageTabs)
- Auto-switch tabs when current tab is empty
- Use Zod for type-guarding HomepageTab from extension points
- Extract SETUPGUIDE_PLUGIN_ID to shared constant

* Remove Active Incidents card from homepage

The IRM/incident data cannot be effectively controlled from the home page.
Remove ActiveIncidentsCard, its tests, the getActiveIncidents API endpoint,
related TypeScript types, i18n keys, and MSW stubs that only the incident
card required. The AlertsIncidentsRow container and FiringAlertsCard are
preserved unchanged.

* Remove redundant return type annotations from branch code

Drop explicit return types where TypeScript can infer them, and remove
the Matcher and DashboardQueryResult type imports that were only needed
for those annotations.

* Remove AlertsIncidentsRow wrapper, render FiringAlertsCard directly

The wrapper existed to hold both FiringAlertsCard and ActiveIncidentsCard.
With incidents removed it adds no value — inline the card in HomePage.

* Home: Reuse canonical severity ranking in FiringAlertsCard

* Home: Use plural defaultValue for FiringAlertsCard count badges

The critical/high count badges passed the plural string as the positional t() defaultValue, which the @grafana/t-plural-defaults lint rule rejects when options include a count key. Move the form into defaultValue_one/defaultValue_other with an empty positional default, matching the catalog's existing _one/_other entries.

* Home: Clarify firing alerts empty-state copy

The generic empty state read 'No firing alerts.', which implied a global zero-alerts claim and contradicted the persistent 'View all firing alerts' footer link. Reword to personal framing 'You have no firing alerts.'. The team-scoped message is unchanged.

* Dashlist: Track item clicks in list layout

* Home: Test Most used tab analytics tracking

* Home: Fix FiringAlertsCard severity counts and team matcher escaping

* Home: Address review cleanups in homepage tabs

* Home: Harden FiringAlertsCard severity handling and links

- Guard canonicalSeverity against alerts with no severity label (was a crash)
- Keep the query string in alert detail links (pathname + search)
- Use the alertmanager query param so "view all" reliably targets Grafana alerts
- Render severity dots by canonical level, matching the count badges

* Home: Stop exporting internal MOST_USED_SORT constant

* Home: Extract HomeSection wrapper and memoize alert severity counts

Single useMemo computes critical/high counts in one pass instead of two
unmemoized filters. HomeSection pins the shared canvas Box props used by
the dashboard tabs, alerts card, and extras wrappers.

* cleanup

* Home: Deduplicate tab error states and reduce per-render work

Extract shared DashboardTabError so all three dashboard tabs render the
same centered error state (MostUsed was missing the centering wrapper).
FiringAlertsCard now derives severity and timestamp once per alert for
sorting, badge counts, and rows, inlines the single-use useUserTeams
hook, and drops memos made redundant by RTK Query arg serialization.

* review feedback

* update tests

* Home: Use alerting SeverityBars for firing alerts severity

Replace the firing alerts card's single severity dot (non-matching palette, notably blue for minor) with alerting's canonical 4-bar SeverityBars, extracted into a shared module so SeverityFilter and the home card render the identical component. Gives exact color+shape parity with alerting and keeps minor/major distinguishable by bar count.

Provisioning: Add Migrate to GitOps overview stat cards (#125811)

* Provisioning: Add Migrate to GitOps overview stat cards

Replace the Migrate tab placeholder with the overview stat cards row:
Dashboards, Managed, Unmanaged, Progress to GitOps, and a Folders-managed
gauge. Driven entirely by useGetResourceStatsQuery; components split into
StatCard, SemicircleGauge, FolderProgressCard, OverviewStatCards and a
stats.ts helpers module.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Add unit tests for Migrate stat-card components

Cover StatCard (label/value/sub-label rendering, optional sub-label,
all tones), SemicircleGauge (decorative aria-hidden svg, fill scales
with percentage, clamps out-of-range values), FolderProgressCard
(fraction + rounded percentage, zero-folder case), and OverviewStatCards
(the five computed cards plus the "start your migration" empty-Git-Sync
prompt).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Align Migrate stat cards with frontend conventions

No behavior change — convention/readability fixes:
- Replace inline prop object types with named Props interfaces
  (OverviewStatCards, FolderProgressCard, SemicircleGauge).
- Add explicit MigrationTotals / FolderCounts domain types in stats.ts
  and use them instead of ReturnType<typeof ...> on the components.
- Extract the shared card surface + hero-value styles into
  statCardStyles.ts so StatCard and FolderProgressCard stop duplicating
  the card chrome.
- Render card labels with <Text> + semantic color roles instead of
  raw <span>s; tokenize the hero number via theme.typography.pxToRem.
- Swap the "primary" tone's purple/color-mix styling for semantic
  theme.colors.primary.* tokens.
- Make the "{{value}} of {{count}} dashboards" string plural-aware.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Extract MigrateToGitopsHeader into its own file

Move the Migrate tab's title/badge/subtitle header out of Migrate.tsx
into MigrateToGitopsHeader.tsx so the page component is just the shell.
Add a small unit test for the header. No behavior change.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Keep the migration guide note on the Migrate cards page

Restore the original "guided migration workflow is on its way" note with
the provisioning docs link, shown below the overview stat cards, and add
a test asserting it renders.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Alerting: Skip retries for deterministic Mimir resource-limit errors (#126473)

Query-limit and write-message-size rejections fail identically on every retry, so retrying them in-cycle wastes query/write cost for no benefit. Classify them as non-retryable so the rule fails fast on the first attempt; recovery is unchanged (still evaluated every cycle). Also fixes a pre-existing miscount of rule_evaluation_failures_total when retries stop early.

Signed-off-by: Tito Lins <tito.linsesilva@grafana.com>

commit.message:
Search: extract declared fields from resources via SearchFieldDefinition Path (#126385)

* search: extract declared fields from resources via SearchFieldDefinition Path

Add a path-based extractor to the standard document builder so that any
kind which declares SearchFieldDefinitions with a Path gets indexed
without a custom builder. The new entry point
StandardDocumentBuilderWithFields wires a SearchFieldsProvider into the
builder; with no provider, behaviour is unchanged.

Path syntax supported:
- Plain dot path ("spec.email").
- Scalar-array passthrough ("spec.tags").
- One [*] array projection per path ("spec.members[*].name"); the
  result is []any with one entry per source element.

Type coercion against the declared SearchFieldType:
- String / Date  -> string.
- Boolean        -> bool.
- Int64          -> int64 directly, or float64 rounded half away from
                    zero (range-checked; NaN, infinities, and out-of-
                    int64-range values rejected).
- Double         -> float64 directly, or int64 promoted.

Number handling is shaped by unstructured.Unstructured.UnmarshalJSON,
which preserves integer JSON values as int64 and fractional values as
float64.

Version lookup is strict: a manifest must declare every served version
of a kind. Cross-version fallback was considered and rejected because
silently extracting an old document with a newer version's path
declarations can produce wrong values when the schema diverges.

Type set tidied: SearchFieldTypeInt32 and SearchFieldTypeFloat have
been removed in favour of SearchFieldTypeInt64 and SearchFieldTypeDouble.
The protobuf translator collapses INT32+INT64 to Int64 and FLOAT+DOUBLE
to Double; bleve indexes all numerics through float64 internally so no
search behaviour is affected. There are no in-tree callers of the
removed types.

* search: lint fix and PreferredVersion fallback for missing apiVersion

- coerceScalar: explicit case for SearchFieldTypeUnknown so the
  exhaustive linter is satisfied.
- gvrForLookup: when the document has no apiVersion at all, fall back
  to the provider's PreferredVersion. apiVersion-present-but-unknown
  still gets the strict behaviour (no extraction); the new fallback
  only covers malformed or partially-constructed documents.
- Two test cases covering the new fallback path (with and without a
  PreferredVersion registered).

* search: skip missing sub-path elements in array projection

When a SearchFieldDefinition declares an array projection path such as
"spec.members[*].name", extractPath preserves the array shape by
contributing a nil entry for any element whose sub-path is absent.
coerceToFieldShape then treated that nil as a coercion failure and
dropped the whole field, so one member without a name silently
removed every member name from the indexed document.

Skip nil elements in the array loop instead. The indexed array now
contains the entries that did resolve, matching the documented
contract of extractPath. An all-nil source array indexes as an empty
slice rather than a dropped field.

* search: document path extractor coercion contract; cover missing sub-path in integration test

Two follow-ups from review of the array-nil-skip fix:

- Clarify extractPath's doc comment. The plain-dot-path case can
  return a map, but coerceToFieldShape only accepts scalars and
  slices of scalars and there is no SearchFieldType for maps;
  spell that out explicitly. The array-projection paragraph also
  notes that nil placeholders are now skipped rather than failing
  the whole field.
- Extend TestStandardDocumentBuilder_DeclaredFields to include a
  members entry without a name sub-field, asserting that the
  member_names array still indexes the resolvable entries. Lower-
  level coverage already exists in path_extract_test.go; this one
  exercises the same behaviour through the full builder.

commit.message:
Provisioning: Run a migration from the Migrate to GitOps tab (#125912)

Builds on the Migrate overview cards: when there are unmanaged dashboards
or folders, the tab offers a "Start migration" action that opens a drawer
(consistent with other provisioning jobs). In the drawer the user selects
the target repository, reviews the Git Sync limitations, and runs the
migrate job — progress and result are shown via the shared JobStatus view.
On success the overview stats refresh.

- Extract the wizard's Git Sync limitations warning into a shared
  GitSyncLimitationsAlert, used by both SynchronizeStep and the drawer.
- Self-fetch repositories in Migrate so HomePage wiring is unchanged.
- Show an "all managed" note when nothing is left to migrate.

commit.message:
Alerting: Replace BuildManagedInhibitionRules with MergeInhibitionRules (#126431)

* Alerting: Replace BuildManagedInhibitionRules with MergeInhibitionRules

Refactors inhibition rule merging to accept existing rules as input, producing stable hash-based UIDs and folding deprecated match/match_re fields alongside modern matchers.

* Alerting: Guarantee stable order in foldMatchers for deprecated match fields

Map iteration is non-deterministic; sorting keys before folding ensures the matcher slice (and the resulting FNV hash UID) is identical across calls with the same inputs.
