commit.message:
Datasources: Simplify expression datasource registration in async APIs (#126390)

* Datasources: store expression DS singleton in runtime plugin cache

Replaces the dedicated `setExpressionDataSourceInstanceSettings` function in
settings.ts with `setExpressionDataSourceInstance` in dataSource.ts, storing
the full DataSourceApi instance in the runtime plugin cache. Settings are read
back via `instance.instanceSettings`, and the existing runtime-cache survival
logic means the singleton automatically survives cache reloads without a
separate re-apply step.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Datasources: extract expression datasource singleton into its own module

Moves expression datasource state into a dedicated expressionDs.ts file with
two argless getters and a setter. The isExpressionReference guard now lives at
call-site in dataSource.ts and settings.ts, and getDataSourceInstance throws
if the singleton has not been registered at boot. setExpressionDataSourceInstance
is exported directly from the new module rather than re-exported via dataSource.ts.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Datasources: fix Prettier formatting in dataSource.ts and dataSource.test.ts

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Datasources: address Copilot review feedback on expressionDs

- Rename getExpressionDatasourceInstance/Settings to getExpressionDataSourceInstance/Settings
  to match the DataSource casing in setExpressionDataSourceInstance
- Make settings._resetForTests() also reset the expression DS singleton so
  tests that only reset settings state don't see stale expression DS entries
- Remove redundant explicit resetExpressionDs() calls from test beforeEach
  blocks now that settings._resetForTests() handles it
- Fix misleading test title: expression DS survives reload because it lives in
  the expressionDs module, not because it is a runtime cache entry

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Datasources: remove unnecessary comment in getDataSourceInstance

commit.message:
Provisioning: Git Sync fixes for bulk actions and sync/migrate jobs (#126568)

* Provisioning: Fix bulk delete ignoring its pre-filled branch

Bulk delete hardcoded a generated bulk-delete/<timestamp> ref regardless of the default workflow, so the form displayed a branch the job never used (write workflows push to the configured branch). Extract a shared getBulkActionInitialValues helper and use it in both bulk delete and move so the displayed branch matches the job's actual target.

* Provisioning: Make finished-job lookup tolerate propagation lag

On completion the worker writes the historic job and deletes the active job non-atomically, so the historic record can lag the active-list watch by more than a second. The drawer polled the historic store with a single 1s retry, surfacing a false "No job found" when propagation was slower. Replace the one-shot retry with a bounded, re-render-safe retry (5 attempts, 1s apart): a pending-timer ref and an in-flight guard ensure each real settle schedules at most one retry, and the timer is cleared only on unmount so spurious re-renders cannot cancel an armed retry. A genuinely absent record after the budget is still reported as an error.

* Provisioning: Show a success alert when bulk delete/move completes

Neither bulk drawer surfaced a success message on completion. Extract a shared BulkActionJobStatus that maps the job's terminal status to a success/warning/error alert with idempotent setters (repeated terminal emissions from the longer retry path don't loop). The success wording is workflow-aware: "Resources deleted/moved successfully" when committed to the configured branch, "Requested changes were pushed to a branch" otherwise (accurate whether the branch is new or pre-existing).

* Provisioning: Extract shared useSyncJob hook for the sync/migrate job runner

SynchronizeStep and MigrateDrawer each held a created Job in local state and
started it via useCreateSyncJob. Move that lifecycle into a shared useSyncJob
hook. Each caller keeps its own retry on purpose: the wizard clears the job to
return to its form, while the migrate drawer keeps it so the drawer doesn't
flash back to the setup form.

* Provisioning: Assert structured job body in useSyncJob test

Parse the posted job request as JSON and assert on structured fields (action
plus the migrate/pull payload) instead of substring-matching the raw text,
matching the FixFolderMetadataDrawer test pattern. Catches malformed payloads
and avoids false positives from the string appearing in an unrelated field.

* Provisioning: Simplify bulk-action job status and sync-job hook

Fold the workflow-aware success title into BulkActionJobStatus: it now takes
committedTitle plus a pushedToBranch flag and owns the shared "pushed to a
branch" wording, removing the duplicated ternary from both bulk forms and
collapsing two identical i18n keys into one. Track a single terminal
StepStatusInfo instead of three separate alert states. Drop the unused Job
return from useSyncJob.startJob.

* tweak

DataSources: Async datasource API parity tests with legacy DatasourceSrv (#126380)

DataSources: Add async datasource API parity tests with legacy DatasourceSrv

Covers the new async datasource API (getDataSourceInstanceSettings,
getDataSourceInstanceSettingsList, getDataSourceInstance) against the behaviour
of the legacy DatasourceSrv ahead of the migration:

- Adds a getList <-> getDataSourceInstanceSettingsList characterization test that
  seeds both implementations with identical data and asserts deep-equal output
  (including ordering) across a labelled filter matrix.
- Expands settings.test.ts: the "default" keyword, DataSourceRef objects,
  expression refs in object form, template variables (interpolating to default,
  multi-value, scopedVars passthrough), pluginId/type aliasIDs matching, and
  datasource-variable injection edge cases.
- Expands dataSource.test.ts: null/type-only ref resolution, settings.meta passed
  to the importer, and legacy non-DataSourceApi instance patching. Adds an it.todo
  marking the expression-singleton divergence (tracked separately).

Tests only; no production code changes.

commit.message:
flamegraph: fix HiDPI font/size changes when switching displays (#123496)

* flamegraph: fix font/size changes when switching between HiDPI and standard displays

DPR-dependent constants were computed once at module load time, so moving
a browser window to a screen with a different devicePixelRatio left them
stale, causing mismatched canvas geometry and font sizes.

- constants.ts: store base values without devicePixelRatio baked in
- rendering.ts: add useDevicePixelRatio() hook (matchMedia-based) so the
  canvas is re-initialized when the display changes; multiply all canvas
  drawing constants by devicePixelRatio at call time
- FlameGraph.tsx: remove now-redundant division by devicePixelRatio in
  CSS margin (base value is already CSS pixels)
- FlameGraphCanvas.tsx: simplify hit-test level index calculation

* fix: Ensure the split between table and flamegraph in both, remains 50% throughout zooming in and out.

commit.message:
fix: normalize undefined and empty array in adHocVariableFiltersEqual (#123976)

adHocVariableFiltersEqual compared filter lists with strict undefined handling, so undefined and an empty array were treated as different. That produced a false unsaved-changes state for dashboards using ad-hoc filters.

Normalize both sides with empty-array fallbacks before length and element comparison.

Fixes #123960

commit.message:
Search: drop IAM custom document builders in favour of declared fields (#126408)

* search: drop IAM custom document builders in favour of declared fields

User, Team, TeamBinding, and ExternalGroupMapping each had a custom
DocumentBuilder that decoded JSON into a typed struct and copied spec
or status values into doc.Fields. The same job can be done by the
standard document builder once the kinds declare paths.

Each kind file now exports an XxxSearchFields slice of
SearchFieldDefinitions (name, path, type, array, capabilities).
GetXxxBuilder wires StandardDocumentBuilderWithFields with a per-kind
MapProvider so the builder reads declarations at extraction time.
The custom builder structs and their BuildDocument methods are gone.

EmitZeroIfAbsent is added to SearchFieldDefinition. When the declared
path resolves to nil, the extractor emits the type's zero value
(false, 0, 0.0, "", or an empty array) instead of leaving the field
absent. Flipped on for USER_DISABLED and USER_LAST_SEEN_AT so every
user document still carries those fields. The user-search API exposes
lastSeenAt sorting, and missing values would otherwise sort last
instead of at epoch 0.

Test input JSONs gain apiVersion and kind because unstructured.
Unstructured.UnmarshalJSON requires them; stored K8s docs always have
both. Output goldens regenerate with title/title_ngram/title_phrase
populated (the standard builder's metadata-accessor title fallback
works through the unstructured path). The team test resource changes
from searchTeams to teams to match what the team-search indexer
actually passes (searchTeams is only an HTTP route / authz subject).

* search: always index teambinding external so false survives a JSON omitempty change

The old custom builder set doc.Fields[external] = tb.Spec.External
unconditionally, so external=false was always present in the index.
The generated TeamBindingSpec uses json:"external" without omitempty,
so the field is still always present in marshalled JSON today and the
phase-4 declaration works in practice. Setting EmitZeroIfAbsent makes
the intent explicit, matches USER_DISABLED, and preserves indexing if
a future schema change adds omitempty.

commit.message:
fix(ci): use published commands action in issue-opened workflow (#126677)

The Install Actions step ran 'npm install' against grafana-github-actions,
which declares engines.npm "please-use-yarn". With engine-strict enforced,
npm 11.x on Node 24 rejects it with EBADENGINE and fails the job.

Drop the manual checkout/setup-node/install and reference the prebuilt
composite action directly, matching commands.yml and pr-commands.yml.

commit.message:
Provisioning: Fix Git Sync save feedback, token permissions, and actions alignment (#126672)

* Provisioning: Show in-progress state on Save while saving a provisioned dashboard

The Save button keyed only on request.isLoading, which flips true after react-hook-form finishes its async validators and dispatches the write. For a new dashboard those validators (name search + git file-exists check) are slow, so the button stayed enabled reading "Save" during the lag. Also gate disabled/label on isSubmitting and isValidating so the button is disabled and shows "Saving..." from click through validation to completion, for both new and existing saves.

* Provisioning: Add Administration read-only to GitHub token permissions

GitHub fine-grained tokens need Administration: Read-only so the configured branch's protection rules can be validated when users may push to it directly. Scoped to the github case only; gitlab/bitbucket are unchanged.

* align items

* Flamegraph: Make useDevicePixelRatio module-local to satisfy knip

The hook is only used within rendering.ts and isn't imported by any test or re-exported, so the export was flagged as unused by knip. Drop the export keyword and the stale 'exported for testing' note.

commit.message:
E2E: add opt-in STRICT_CSP mode to drop unsafe-eval from Playwright CSP (#126104)

* E2E: add opt-in STRICT_CSP mode to drop unsafe-eval from Playwright CSP

Setting STRICT_CSP=1 when starting the e2e server overrides the CSP
template via GF_SECURITY_CONTENT_SECURITY_POLICY_TEMPLATE to remove
'unsafe-eval' from script-src, so a blocked new Function/eval throws and
fails the test. Default behavior is unchanged. Adds an
e2e:playwright:strict-csp convenience script.

commit.message:
Unified: opt-in chunked writes for resource migration (#126565)

* Unified Storage: opt-in chunked writes for the legacy migration

On MySQL/Galera (Percona XtraDB Cluster) the legacy->unified-storage
migration's single transaction exceeds the cluster's wsrep_max_ws_size (2GB)
write-set cap, so the cluster aborts it and the migration can never complete
on large instances.

Add an opt-in chunked-write mode (migration_chunked_writes, default off,
mysql/postgres only) that splits the import into bounded, per-chunk committed
transactions: a byte-bounded wipe (deleteCollectionChunked), per-chunk history
inserts via txChunker, an ANALYZE, and a resource backfill paginated into
byte-bounded name ranges (planNameRanges). Recovery is marker-as-done plus
wipe-and-restart, with best-effort re-wipe of committed chunks on failure.

Background GC start is deferred until the in-process migration completes via an
injected GCGate, so it cannot prune rows a migration is still committing.

Verified on MySQL: a stress reproduction shows the single-tx path aborting at a
scaled max_binlog_cache_size cap while chunked completes with every commit
bounded; integration tests cover correctness vs a non-chunked run, idempotency,
kill-mid-migration recovery, and the sqlite no-op regression.

commit.message:
Modal: don't dismiss when pressing portal-container content (#126261)

* Modal: do not dismiss when pressing inside the portal container

ModalBase already marks the portal container as inside the modal for focus/aria
via getInsideElements, but useDismiss did not honor the same set, so overlays
rendered into the portal container over an open modal (dropdowns, tooltips,
plugin overlays) dismissed it on press. Make outsidePress consistent with
getInsideElements, excluding the backdrop so close-on-backdrop-click still works.

Signed-off-by: Jay Clifford <jay.clifford@grafana.com>

* Portal: document getPortalContainer as public API

Rendering into the portal container is the supported way for overlays to
coexist with an open Modal (inside for focus management, presses do not
dismiss), so drop the internal marker and document the contract.

Replicate the app arrangement (UNSAFE_PortalProvider routing react-aria
overlays into PortalContainer, as in AppWrapper) and cover the press
distinction: portal-container overlays do not dismiss, the backdrop and
page content still do.

commit.message:
Loki: restore /prometheus/* ruler read routes for data-source-managed alerting (#126718)

PR #125752 moved the Loki data source proxy route allowlist into a static
`routes` block in plugin.json, but omitted the Prometheus-compatible ruler
read endpoints that the alerting UI uses to display data-source-managed rule
state and active alerts:

  GET /prometheus/api/v1/rules
  GET /prometheus/api/v1/alerts

These are the paths emitted by lotex_prom.go (lokiEndpoints). With no matching
RBAC-covered route, the data source proxy treats them as uncovered and denies
them, so Loki data-source-managed alert rules and alerts no longer appear in
the Alerting UI. Rule evaluation, notifications, and the ruler config API
(/loki/api/v1/rules, /api/prom/rules) are unaffected, which is why editing
still works while listing/state does not.

Add the two GET routes (alert.rules.external:read, Viewer) to restore
visibility. These are read-only; the /prometheus/* surface has no write
endpoints.

commit.message:
Logging: Preserve original error stack in @grafana/runtime helpers (#126660)

The logging helpers wrapped the original error in `new Error(message,
{ cause })` before handing it to `logError` -> `faro.api.pushError`.
Faro parses stack frames only from the top-level error's `.stack`, and
serializes `.cause` with `cause.toString()` (its message, not its stack).
So the synthetic wrapper's shallow stack (rooted in the catch block) was
reported and the real failure location was dropped from telemetry.

Introduce a `TracedError` class that presents a descriptive `message`
while copying the original error's `.stack` onto itself and keeping the
original on `.cause`. Faro then reports a meaningful title together with
the real failure frames. Applied consistently across all five sites: the
three exported helpers (logDataSourceInstanceError, logPluginMetaError,
logPluginSettingsError) and the two internal getCachedPromise uses.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
Provisioning: carry existing resourceVersion into resource updates (#126383)

* Provisioning: carry existing resourceVersion into resource updates

Reading back or updating an already-provisioned playlist failed with
"metadata.resourceVersion: Invalid value: 0: must be specified for an
update". The parser clears the RV on parse (it is not stored in the repo
file) and then performs a blind client.Update; dashboards/folders tolerate
an RV-less update but the playlist apiserver rejects it.

Carry the existing object's resourceVersion into the update in both DryRun
and Run, re-fetching the existing object when needed (create AlreadyExists
fall-through), and clear the stale RV before the NotFound fallback create.
This makes files GET/PUT, move, move jobs, and re-sync round-trip cleanly
for playlists without regressing dashboards/folders.

Fixes grafana/git-ui-sync-project#1199

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: update playlist round-trip integration tests for the RV fix

With the parser carrying the existing resourceVersion into updates, playlists
now round-trip through the files endpoint and move job. Flip the assertions
that pinned the previous limitation:

- PlaylistFilesEndpoint: files PUT now succeeds and updates the title; files
  move now succeeds (HTTP 200) and refreshes the source-path annotation.
- PlaylistMoveJob: the move job completes without warnings and the post-move
  full sync refreshes each moved playlist's grafana.app/sourcePath.

Both tests verified end-to-end against a local SQLite Grafana.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
Provisioning: Fix TestIntegrationFolderManagerConsistency folder-count flake (#126699)

CreateLocalRepo's post-sync assertion counted every dashboard and folder
in the namespace and required the total to equal ExpectedDashboards/
ExpectedFolders. Because the provisioning integration tests share one
Grafana server and clean up at the start of each test, an orphaned
resource leaked from a prior test inflates that namespace-wide total and
flakes the assertion.

This is exactly what failed TestIntegrationFolderManagerConsistency: an
orphaned "test-repo" folder (left behind when a prior test's repository
was deleted and its finalizer's async orphan-draining raced the folder
cleanup step) pushed the folder count to 2 when the test expected 1.

Count only resources managed by the repo under test via the existing
RequireRepoDashboardCount/RequireRepoFolderCount helpers (matching by the
grafana.app/managerId annotation), mirroring the fix already applied to
the quota sync test in #123872. The assertion still verifies the repo
created exactly its expected resources; it no longer flakes on orphans
leaked by other tests.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

orphaned "test-repo" folder (left behind when a prior test's repository

RequireRepoDashboardCount/RequireRepoFolderCount helpers (matching by the
grafana.app/managerId annotation), mirroring the fix already applied to
the quota sync test in #123872. The assertion still verifies the repo
created exactly its expected resources; it no longer flakes on orphans
leaked by other tests.

commit.message:
Search: rebuild indexes when search field metadata changes (#126576)

* search: rebuild indexes when search field metadata changes

Each kind that uses a SearchFieldsProvider can now declare a stable
hash over the SearchFieldDefinition slices registered for the
(group, resource), across every served version. The hash is
captured in IndexBuildInfo at build time and re-checked on the
periodic rebuild loop so the index is rebuilt automatically when
index-affecting metadata changes (paths, types, capabilities,
EmitZeroIfAbsent, CopyFromStandard). Presentation-only edits such
as Description are intentionally excluded.

Hashing covers every version of the kind because a single bleve
index serves all of them and documents are extracted using the
SearchFieldDefinition slice that matches the document's apiVersion.

The hash flows through DocumentBuilderInfo so each builder owns its
own provider construction. The wiring layer collects the hashes
once and passes the same map to BleveOptions and SearchOptions.
shouldRebuildIndex treats an empty expected hash as no opinion,
which preserves existing behaviour for kinds without a provider.

Existing on-disk indexes have no SearchFieldsHash stored. On the
first periodic check after this change rolls out, each IAM index
rebuilds once. Indexes for kinds without a provider keep stored
and expected hashes both empty and are not rebuilt.

* chore: sync go workspace after rebase onto main

make update-workspace drops an unused arrow-go indirect from
pkg/infra/features after the rebase pulled in the arrow-go bump
on main.

* search: address review feedback on search-fields hash

Expand the comment on the discarded json.Marshal error in
IndexAffectingHash to enumerate the encoder's real failure modes and
spell out why none apply to the current payload. The error branch is
kept defensive: if a future change introduces a type that can fail,
returning "" silently disables the search-field-change rebuild trigger
for that kind, so a logger surfaces the bug for operators.

Document why an empty expected hash means "no opinion" in
shouldRebuildIndex: mirrors SelectableFields semantics, and the stored
hash refreshes naturally on the next rebuild triggered by another
condition.

* search: pin IndexAffectingHash output with a golden test

Go's encoding/json output for plain string, bool, and []string fields
is stable in practice but not explicitly pinned by the language spec.
TestMapProvider_IndexAffectingHash_GoldenHash asserts a fixed hex
digest for a reference SearchFieldDefinition set, so any future Go
release that shifts the canonical form (struct field encoding order,
HTML-escape default, string escape rules) fails CI rather than
silently reindexing every kind that registers a SearchFieldsProvider.

commit.message:
Provisioning: Only export needed folders during selective export (#126566)

* Provisioning: Only export needed folders during selective export

A selective export (Push or Migrate with Resources) previously always
ran the full ExportFolders pass, writing every unmanaged folder in the
instance to the repository even though the caller named only specific
resources.

Now exportAll routes selective exports straight to ExportSpecificResources
without the full-tree pass. Only the folders required to place the
requested resources are written: each resource's parent-folder ancestry
is fetched from the folder API and generated on demand (including
_folder.json metadata), and an explicitly named folder is exported with
its ancestry instead of being skipped. Folders belonging to unrelated,
non-exported resources stay out of the repository.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: address review feedback on selective folder export

- collectFolderAncestry now stops at the first folder owned by a manager,
  mirroring the full ExportFolders filter, so a selected resource's
  ancestry cannot pull a folder owned by another repository/provisioner
  into the target repository. Added a unit test for the skip.
- Selective folder-ref integration test reuses the UID returned by
  CreateUnmanagedFolder instead of a List+title scan.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
Provisioning: Convert useProvisionedRequestHandler to an imperative API (#126358)

* Provisioning: Convert useProvisionedRequestHandler to an imperative API

The hook previously reacted to RTK mutation state in a useEffect guarded
by a hasHandled ref and a 10-item dependency array. Forms now call
handleSuccess/handleError directly after awaiting the mutation, which
removes the effect machinery and fixes three latent issues:

- Move/Delete forms surfaced errors twice (own catch + hook onError)
- SaveProvisionedDashboardForm.handleDismiss read request.data from a
  stale render closure; success handlers now receive the ResourceWrapper
- useImportProvisionedSave needed saveState/saveRef purely to feed
  per-save context into the effect; per-call overrides replace both

Component tests now run the real hook against MSW responses instead of
invoking captured handlers from a jest mock.

* Provisioning: Declare provisioned request handler before submit handlers

* Provisioning: Drive MoveProvisionedDashboardForm test mutations via MSW

* Provisioning: Extract folder handler path constants for MSW tests

* Provisioning: Drop unused handleError from request handler

handleError and the RequestHandlers.onError field it forwarded to were referenced only by tests; every caller handles errors in its own catch. Remove both for a clean surface.

* Fix test

test: fix flaky TestIntegrationProvisioning_MoveResources (#126779)

The "move directory ... MethodNotAllowed" subtest copied timeline-demo.json
and text-options.json into source-dir/, but those dashboard UIDs already
existed in the repo from earlier subtests (deep/nested/timeline.json and
updated/content-updated.json). The full sync writes file creations in
parallel, so two files mapping to the same dashboard UID raced into an
optimistic-lock conflict ("the object has been modified").

Rewrite the source-dir files with unique UIDs so no two files resolve to the
same dashboard during sync, following the existing strings.Replace pattern in
quota/sync_quota_test.go.

commit.message:
search: fix flaky TestIntegrationBleveSnapshotRoundTrip (#126784)

The test compared meta.UploadTimestamp (captured before the upload) to
the timestamp stored in the downloaded manifest. UploadIndexSnapshot
overwrites the persisted UploadTimestamp with one derived from a freshly
generated ULID, so the two values can drift apart by more than the 1s
WithinDuration tolerance on a slow runner.

Capture the ULID returned by UploadIndexSnapshot and compare the tracked
timestamp to ulid.Time(uploadedKey.Time()) instead. The values are now
exact and no longer race with wall-clock drift.

commit.message:
Alerting: Add Config k8s resource for external Alertmanager sync (#125185)

* Alerting: Add AlertingConfig k8s resource

Introduces a new admin app under apps/alerting/admin/ with the
AlertingConfig kind (group admin.alerting.grafana.app/v0alpha1).
Per-org singleton named "default" carrying admin-controllable alerting
configuration. v1 carries external Alertmanager sync settings:

- spec.externalAlertmanagerSync.datasourceUid — admin intent.
- status.externalAlertmanagerSync.{datasourceUid, origin} — observation
  context; origin (api | operator) surfaces which source won when both
  are present.
- status.conditions[type=ExternalAlertmanagerSynced] — sync state via
  the k8s Conditions FSM (transition-only writes).
- status.observedGeneration — forward-compat.

Schema is flat-per-feature so future admin-controllable features land as
sibling sub-objects on spec/status and can be trivially extracted into
their own kinds later if write contention or RBAC isolation needs grow.

The kind ships with a stub admission validator on
spec.externalAlertmanagerSync.datasourceUid; the actual validation
logic (datasource lookup, type/implementation checks, feature flag
gating) is wired from the parent process so the submodule stays free of
grafana-parent imports.

* Alerting: Rename AdminConfig kind to Config and flatten the sync config

The AdminConfig kind becomes Config (resource configs.notifications.alerting.grafana.app)
now that it lives in the notifications app rather than its own admin app. The
external Alertmanager sync config drops the redundant alertmanager section since
the whole kind is alertmanager-specific:

  spec.externalAlertmanagerSync.datasourceUid
  status.externalAlertmanagerSync.{datasourceUid, origin}

RBAC actions move to notifications.alerting.grafana.app/configs:{get,update} and
/configs/status:update.

* fix linter complaints

* Alerting: Stop external Alertmanager sync once the config is merged

Once the imported config has been merged into the org's Grafana Alertmanager
config (a managed route keyed by the datasource UID), the admin owns it in
Grafana — so the syncer stops pulling from upstream rather than overwriting it.

The syncer checks for the managed route before each fetch: if present it records
a terminal ExternalAlertmanagerSynced=True / MergeCommitted condition and skips;
a config-read failure skips the tick (no overwrite of a config we can't read)
and is surfaced via the ConfigReadFailed metric/condition.

* Alerting: Regenerate notifications OpenAPI artifacts after rebase

Picks up upstream #126016 (hides esoteric k8s list options from the list
OpenAPI). Regenerates the notifications v0alpha1 snapshot, published
@grafana/openapi spec, and the RTK-Query client so they match the current
apiserver output.

* Alerting: Clarify external AM sync validator comments and harden nil cfg

Addresses review feedback: correct the validator godoc/comments (flag-first
ordering is intentional; a dormant UID set before the ini override reactivates
when it's cleared; clearing is always allowed), fail closed when cfg is nil
instead of skipping the override check, and reword the merge-committed status
message.

* Alerting: Tighten Config RBAC verbs and rename actions/roles

Addresses PR #125185 review:

- Rename ActionAlertingConfig{Write,StatusWrite} -> {Update,StatusUpdate} to match the :update verb.

- Rename fixed roles alerting.admin-config:{reader,writer} -> alerting.notifications.config:{reader,writer} (leftover from the AdminConfig->Config rename); regenerate RBAC snapshots.

- Authorizer: reject delete/deletecollection on the singleton, gate patch/update behind the update permission, allow create only for the in-process service identity. Humans bootstrap the singleton via create-on-update (PUT/apply, authorized as update).

- Trim the verbose action-constant comment.

* Alerting: Add Config authorizer tests

* Alerting: gofmt service identity permissions

* Alerting: Allow creating the Config singleton

Gate create behind the update permission instead of rejecting it: an upsert (PUT/apply to a missing object) is authorized as create, so blocking create made the singleton uncreatable via the API. Only delete/deletecollection stay rejected; the singleton-name check stays in the validator.

* Alerting: Add Config integration tests

* Alerting: Tidy externalAlertmanagerSync CUE layout

* Alerting: Scope Config RBAC actions

commit.message:
Provisioning: Force-delete folders in cleanup to fix index-lag flake (#126781)

CleanupAllResources deletes dashboards then folders, but the folder-delete
admission check rejects deletion until the eventually-consistent search
index reports the folder empty. Under SQLite write contention that index
lag is effectively unbounded, so the folders step timed out with "folder
is not empty" — flaking TestIntegrationProvisioning_BlockManagerChange on
leftovers from the preceding TestIntegrationFolderManagerConsistency test.
Bumping the timeout (already done in #123902 and #124046, now at 4x) only
masks the race.

Make folder cleanup deterministic by force-deleting folders
(gracePeriodSeconds=0), which bypasses the empty-folder check. Cleanup
issues a delete to every folder anyway, so the check serves no purpose
there. This requires enabling FlagKubernetesFolderCascadeDelete in the
shared test env; the flag only affects force-deletes, so normal
(non-force) deletes still enforce the empty-folder check and test behavior
outside cleanup is unchanged.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
Provisioning: fix folder UID-change full-sync test flake (#126780)

The "UID change replaces folder and re-parents dashboard" subtest only
asserted the folder was present after the first sync, never the
dashboard, before editing _folder.json and triggering the second sync.

The second sync's compare diffs against the eventually-consistent
managed-resources index. When the dashboard from the first sync was not
yet indexed, emitDirectChildrenChanges could not find it in the target
list, so the folder UID change did not emit a re-parent change for it.
The new folder was created, the dashboard was left under the old UID,
and the deferred old-folder cleanup then removed it — surfacing as
"dashboard not found".

Wait for the dashboard to be visible and parented before the second
sync, matching the post-first-sync assertions already used by the
sibling subtests.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
Search: index created and updated as standard search fields (#126800)

Add created and updated to StandardSearchFieldDefinitions so every kind
gets them indexed and retrievable. The proto column list advertised
created as a top-level int64 but the bleve mapping never declared it,
so the value was never stored; updated was missing from both sides.

Both fields ship with [filter, retrieve]. Retrieve is the intent;
filter is a workaround because the bleve mapper emits no mapping for
retrieve-only declarations today, so filter is the only way to get a
stored keyword variant. Exact-ms equality filters are not a useful
query. Sort is omitted because the mapper emits keyword/text regardless
of declared type, so int64 values would sort lexically. Both
compromises go away once the mapper learns to honour
SearchFieldDefinition.Type, tracked as a follow-up.

IndexAffectingHash is extended so the shared standard set contributes
alongside per-kind declarations, otherwise a change to standard fields
would not trigger the automatic rebuild added in #126576. Kinds with a
registered SearchFieldsProvider reindex automatically on rollout;
others inherit the new mapping through the existing build-version
cycle.

A new validator rejects SearchCapabilitySort on non-string-mapped
types at provider construction time (panic — programmer-error
semantics, caught at startup). The allowlist is intentionally minimal:
only SearchFieldTypeString, extended when a concrete consumer needs
sort on a new type.

commit.message:
fix(provisioning): ignore terminating repositories when validating connection delete (#126822)

When `terraform destroy` tears down a connection and its repository together,
the repository is deleted first. The repository DELETE returns 200 but the
object lingers in storage (terminating) until its finalizers complete. The
connection delete validator listed every repository referencing the connection
— including the terminating one — and rejected the connection delete with a
422, breaking the combined destroy.

The validator now ignores repositories that are themselves being deleted
(DeletionTimestamp set). A terminating repository's finalizers rely on its own
stored token, not the live connection, so the connection is safe to delete once
the repository's delete has been issued. Protection against deleting a
connection that still has live repositories is unchanged: a non-terminating
repository still produces the immediate 422.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
Authz: Fix missing service identity permissions for provisioning resources (#124578)

* authz: fix missing service identity permissions

* add tests

* fix provisioning job tests

* fix provisioning subresource authorization

* update workspaces

* chore: use the wildcard

* chore: change to stats

* chore: make it more semantically correct

* Authz: pin refs & admin-view subresource checks to repositories resource

Keep the role tightening from this PR but authorize against semantically-correct
resources/verbs instead of borrowing unrelated resources to match a role tier:

- refs: authorize as repositories:write (admin/repo owner, repo setup) OR
  jobs:create (editor, push/PR flow), each with its own correct resource, instead
  of the jobs resource keyed by the repository name. The repositories resource has
  no Editor tier, hence the OR; viewers still satisfy neither and are denied.
- resources/history/status: gate on repositories:write (admin-only) keeping the
  repositories resource and repository Name, instead of proxying through stats.
  This stays correct if access is later scoped to individual repositories.
- Add tests for the refs OR and the admin-only views.

docs: document Git Sync admin-only jobs and repository subresource access (#126807)

Reflects the fine-grained authorization tightening in #124578:

  jobs:create can push changes / open PRs but can't pull on demand.

commit.message:
Restore dashboards: fetch the dashboard at the RV before delete (#126873)

* Restore dashboards: fetch dashboard at RV before delete

The trash listing returns rows whose metadata.resourceVersion is the
delete event's RV. Reading at that RV returns the tombstone, and on the
unified-storage KV backend it returns 404 because the read path skips
entries whose latest action is delete.

Step back by one when fetching the dashboard for restore, so the read
resolves to the dashboard as it was immediately before the delete on
both SQL and KV backends.

* Replace BigInt literal with BigInt(1) for es2018 target

The 1n literal needs target >= es2020; the repo targets es2018. The
BigInt constructor itself is available because the TS lib includes
es2022, so BigInt(deleteRV) - BigInt(1) keeps the same precision-safe
arithmetic.

commit.message:
Storage: cross-backend test for read at deleteRV-1 (restore-from-trash contract) (#126875)

Storage: cross-backend test for read at deleteRV-1

Add a sub-test to the shared runTestIntegrationBackendHappyPath that
reads a deleted resource at deleteRV-1 and asserts the live pre-delete
state is returned. This is the contract the dashboard restore-from-trash
flow depends on (the trash listing surfaces each item's delete-event
RV, and the frontend reads the dashboard at deleteRV-1 to fetch the
spec to restore). The SQL and KV backends arrive at the same answer by
different code paths, so a shared test guards against future
divergence.

commit.message:
AuthZ: surface external groups as identity groups for the forward Check (#126197)

* AuthZ: surface external groups as identity groups for the forward Check

When id_use_external_groups_for_groups_claim is set, team membership is
delivered via IdP/proxy external groups (external group names match team
UIDs) rather than Grafana-stored team memberships. The ID token already
honours this (idimpl.resolveGroupsClaim) and the Zanzana merge resolver
honours it (ZanzanaPermissionResolver.teamsForCurrentUser), but the forward
authz Check derives its contextual team-membership tuples from
authInfo.GetGroups() (authlib authz client), which returns stored
memberships. With team_sync disabled those are empty, so the forward Check
sends no team contextuals and denies access a user legitimately holds
through a team grant (e.g. creating a dashboard in a folder a team has
edit on).

Add a post-auth hook (priority 115, after FetchSyncedUserHook) that sets the
identity's Groups to its ExternalGroups for user identities under the same
flag, so every GetGroups() consumer - the forward Check, the merge resolver,
and the ID token - is consistent.

commit.message:
Bleve search: prefix-wildcard fallback for short queries (#126863)

Short queries (1-2 chars) against Bleve-backed search behaved inconsistently:
'f' returned all items (match-all fallthrough), 'fi' returned an empty list,
'fir' returned expected matches.

Queries shorter than NGRAM_MIN_TOKEN (3) cannot hit the title_ngram index. We
now rewrite them to a prefix wildcard ('f' -> 'f*') and route them through the
existing wildcard branch, so search-as-you-type returns meaningful prefix
matches. Callers that already include '*' are left untouched.

Tracking issue: grafana/search-and-storage-team#832.

commit.message:
Provisioning: Pre-fill and enforce commit message template in save dialogs (#126687)

* feat(provisioning): drive Save-drawer comment from commit template

Pre-fill the single-resource Save-drawer Comment field from the repository
singleResourceMessageTemplate, re-render as template variables change, lock
it read-only when commit.enforceTemplate is set, and stop overwriting once
the user edits it. Gated behind the provisioning.gitConventions flag via the
new useCommitMessageTemplate hook + a lockComment prop on the shared field.

* feat(provisioning): commit rendered message on write-workflow jobs

The single-resource delete/move/folder-delete drawers submit the write
workflow via createBulkJob, which sent no commit message, so the backend
fell back to its default - diverging from the (locked) Comment field the
drawer shows. Set JobSpec.message from the same getSingleResourceCommitMessage
resolution used on the branch workflow so the committed message matches what
the drawer displays. Backend honours JobSpec.Message via jobs.CommitMessage.

* cleanup

* update description

* Provisioning: Drop redundant useFormState in single-resource drawers

* comments

* Provisioning: Reuse templateVars for branch-workflow commit messages

* Simploify hook

field now contains UIDs rather than names following the ManagedTemplates
storage change.

commit.message:
IAM: Fix user search access control batch checks (#126707)

* IAM: fix user search access control batch checks

Evaluate org.users:add and users.permissions:read at group_resource scope
(empty name) so Zanzana batch checks no longer fail on missing typed user
relations and accessControl metadata is returned.

* IAM: simplify user search access control stamping

Use a groupScope flag on checks instead of separate helpers and slices.

* Remove org.users:create, and user.permissions:read from the stampAccessControl list

commit.message:
Provisioning: Add generateNewFolderIDs option to export/migrate jobs (#126935)

* Provisioning: Add generateNewFolderIDs option to export/migrate jobs

Adds a GenerateNewFolderIDs option to ExportJobOptions and
MigrateJobOptions. When set, each exported folder's metadata
(_folder.json) is written with a freshly generated UID instead of the
original folder identifier.

Without metadata this is a no-op (no UID is materialized). The in-memory
folder tree keeps the original IDs so resources still resolve to their
folder path, and parent nesting is unaffected since it derives from the
directory structure; only the manifest's metadata.name carries the new
UID. This produces a portable export that creates new folders on a
subsequent sync rather than taking over the originals.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Add integration tests for generateNewFolderIDs option

Adds end-to-end integration tests for the export and migrate jobs:
- export with generateNewFolderIDs writes fresh UIDs into _folder.json
  (and the default preserves the original UIDs)
- migrate with generateNewFolderIDs creates a new managed folder under the
  fresh UID and cleans up the original unmanaged folder

Placed in a dedicated local-only package so they run without a git server
(Docker), with provisioningFolderMetadata/provisioningExport on by default.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Move generateNewFolderIDs integration tests to foldermetadata

Relocate the export/migrate integration tests for the generateNewFolderIDs
option into the existing foldermetadata package, alongside the other folder
export tests, instead of a dedicated package. This package enables the
provisioningFolderMetadata flag, which the option requires to have an
observable effect (it only changes the UID written into _folder.json).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Use folder target and nested paths in generateNewFolderIDs tests

Switch the export/migrate generateNewFolderIDs integration tests to a
folder-target repository and exercise a nested parent/child hierarchy:
- export asserts a fresh, distinct UID in each nested _folder.json
- migrate asserts the new UIDs become managed folders with the nested
  parent/child relationship preserved

Folder-target migration skips namespace cleanup, so the test no longer
asserts the original unmanaged folders are removed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Regenerate API client for generateNewFolderIDs option

The Verify API clients CI check regenerates the RTK Query client from the
committed OpenAPI snapshots and fails if the result is not committed. Since
this PR changes the provisioning spec, the generated client and processed
OpenAPI specs must be committed alongside it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
Provisioning: Add the Resources to migrate table with per-resource selection (#125816)

* Provisioning: Migrate selected folders and dashboards from the Migrate tab

Builds on the Migrate to GitOps overview (cards + drawer) by adding the
unmanaged folders/dashboards table and wiring per-resource selection into the
migration flow.

- useFolderMigrationData: pages through every folder and dashboard on the
  instance and rolls them up per folder (recursive counts, direct dashboards,
  managed state). No fixed page cap.
- FoldersToMigrate: foldable, searchable, sortable table of unmanaged folders.
  Folder and dashboard checkboxes; selecting a folder cascades to its subtree.
- selection.ts: resolves the table selection into the dashboard refs the
  migrate job receives (folders cascade to their unmanaged dashboards,
  de-duplicated against individually-picked dashboards).
- MigrateDrawer: gains a selective mode. When given resources it runs a
  `migrate` job scoped to those dashboards; without them it keeps migrating
  everything. useCreateSyncJob now forwards optional resources to the job spec
  (empty = legacy migrate-everything, so the wizard is unaffected).
- Migrate page renders the table under the overview cards. "Start migration"
  still migrates everything; "Migrate selected (N)" opens the drawer scoped to
  the picked resources.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Add select-all + Migrate all, drop the standalone Start migration button

The Resources to migrate table is now the single migration entry point:

- Select-all checkbox in the table (indeterminate when partial). It selects
  every migratable folder, which covers every resource.
- When everything is selected the action button reads "Migrate all (N)" and
  runs the legacy migrate-everything job; a partial selection still reads
  "Migrate selected (N)" and scopes the job to the picked resources.
- Removed the standalone "Start migration" button and the "all managed" note
  from the page — the table (and its empty state) replaces them.

Also renames the panel to "Resources to migrate" and uses resource-generic
wording across these components (table, drawer, page). Resources are dashboards
today; the copy stays generic for future resource types. The component file is
renamed FoldersToMigrate -> ResourcesToMigrate to match.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Fix the Migrate select-all checkbox staying unchecked

Grafana's Checkbox only ever sets the native `indeterminate` property to true
and never clears it, so once the select-all box had been partially selected it
stayed visually indeterminate even after every row was selected — it rendered
unchecked while the action button correctly read "Migrate all". Drive the
`indeterminate` DOM property through a ref so it resets to a plain checked state
when allSelected becomes true.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Remove the Configure button from the Migrate drawer

The migrate drawer's Target repository field showed a Configure dropdown
(ConnectRepositoryButton) next to the repository selector. Migration always
targets an existing repository, so the connect-a-repository affordance was out
of place here — drop it and keep just the repository combobox.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Block migration when the repository can't push to its branch

Migration writes directly to the repository's configured branch (the `write`
workflow). A repository that only opens pull requests (`branch` workflow) can't
run a migration. The drawer now detects this from the selected repository's
workflows: it disables the Migrate button (with an explaining tooltip) and
shows an error alert under the repository selector telling the user to pick a
repository that allows pushing to its branch or update the repository's
workflow.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Make Migrate count strings plural-aware for the updated base

The rebased base enforces @grafana/i18n/t-plural-defaults: a t() call whose
options include `count` must pass an empty positional default plus
`defaultValue_one` / `defaultValue_other`. Update the Migrate table and drawer
count strings (resources-per-folder, the "Showing N of M" footer, the
Migrate selected/all button labels, and the selective drawer description)
accordingly.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Restore Migrate test coverage lost by the table rework

Recover the frontend-navigation coverage the table changes shed:
- Migrate.test stops mocking useRepositoryList and serves repositories via
  MSW, so the real hook (and its transitive utils) are exercised again.
- Add a direct ConnectRepositoryButton test — it used to be covered only via
  the migrate drawer, which no longer renders it after the Configure button
  was removed.
- Cover the new ResourcesToMigrate branches: search by folder/dashboard title,
  the subfolder-only hint, the cascade-locked dashboards, and the sort
  comparator (exported compareFolders + a unit test).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Satisfy knip and the API-migration guard in the Migrate slice

- Drop the `export` on FolderPeekDashboard/FolderPeekSubfolder — they're only
  used within the hook module, so knip flagged them as unused exports.
- Build the dashboard ResourceRef from a literal group/kind in selection.ts
  instead of importing the dashboard k8s API client, which tripped the
  endpoint-migration CI guard (it's a constant, not an endpoint call).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Drive Migrate folder tests via MSW and inline the dashboard ref

- selection.ts builds the dashboard ResourceRef from inline `'dashboard.grafana.app'`
  / `'Dashboard'` literals, matching the rest of provisioning (e.g.
  MoveProvisionedDashboardForm) instead of a local constant or a k8s client import.
- useFolderMigrationData.test and Migrate.test no longer jest-mock the searcher
  or the hook. They drive the real unified searcher through MSW via
  getCustomSearchHandler, consistent with the other provisioning MSW tests, so
  the hook runs for real in both the unit and the page tests.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Split ResourcesToMigrate into focused modules and clarify copy

- Extract the folder-row component into FolderEntry.tsx and the sort helper
  (SortKey + compareFolders) into sorting.ts (+ sorting.test.ts), leaving
  ResourcesToMigrate.tsx as just the panel.
- Reword the subfolder-only hint to be clearer: "No resources directly here —
  they're in subfolders. Selecting this folder migrates everything inside it."

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Address Codex/Copilot review on the Migrate slice

- Keep empty unmanaged folders migratable (Codex P2): isMigratableFolder no
  longer requires a dashboard count, so when the only unmanaged items are empty
  folders the table still lists them and the migrate-all path stays reachable.
  The synthetic General row is now only added when there are real root-level
  dashboards, so it doesn't show up as an empty bogus target.
- Refresh the folder table after a migration (Codex P2): useFolderMigrationData
  exposes a background refetch (no loading flip, so the open drawer isn't
  unmounted) and Migrate calls it from onMigrated alongside the stats refetch.
- Reword repo-no-push-body so it's accurate for read-only repos too, not just
  PR-only ones (Copilot).
- Fix stale comments/JSDoc: the hook returns all folders and the UI decides what
  is migratable; selection.ts refers to the "Resources to migrate" table
  (Copilot).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Fix Resources to migrate footer pluralization

The footer keyed its plural on the number of rows shown, but the noun ("folder")
agrees with the total folder count — so "1 of 1" rendered "folders". Key the
plural on the total and interpolate the shown count separately, giving
"Showing 1 of 1 folder" / "Showing 2 of 5 folders".

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Drop unused subfolders from the folder migration data

`subfolders`/`FolderPeekSubfolder` were built in aggregate() but nothing reads
them — FolderEntry keys off directDashboards/dashboardCount. Remove the field
and the per-render grouping work (leftover from the dropped peek feature).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Parallelize folder/dashboard paging with a safety cap

Paging was sequential and unbounded across every folder and every dashboard,
slowing time-to-interactive. Fetch page 0 to learn totalRows, then fetch the
remaining pages concurrently, bounded by a generous MAX_PAGES guardrail so a
pathological response can't spin off unbounded requests.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Don't block the Migrate overview on the folder enumeration

The header and KPI cards only need the stats query, so gate the page on that
alone instead of also waiting for the full folder+dashboard enumeration. The
Resources to migrate table now carries its own loading state, so the overview
renders immediately on large instances instead of sitting behind "Loading
stats…" until every page is fetched.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Don't surface a bogus General migration target

When the root holds only managed dashboards from mixed tools, the General row
had managedBy undefined and dashboardCount 0 — so it showed up as an unmanaged
migration target with nothing to migrate. Only synthesize the General row when
there are unmanaged root dashboards, or when every root dashboard is managed by
a single agreeing tool (a managed row the table filters out). Skip it for the
mixed-managed-only case.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Gate Migrate on a write-capable repo with a reachable connect action

The table enabled "Migrate selected" whenever any repo existed, but the drawer
then blocked branch-only (non-write) repos — and the disabled-button tooltip
pointed at a connect action that wasn't on the tab. Now the footer gates on a
write-capable repo (matching the drawer's guard); when there isn't one it
renders the shared ConnectRepositoryButton instead of a dead disabled button,
so connecting a repository is reachable from the tab.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Track selective migration explicitly, not via resources.length

A partial selection of only empty folders resolves to no dashboard refs, and
deriving "selective" from resources.length then let it fall through to the
migrate-everything path (the backend treats empty resources as the legacy
all-resource migration). The drawer now takes an explicit `selective` prop, and
the page disables the migrate button when a partial selection has nothing
migratable to send — so an empty selection can never be mistaken for
migrate-everything.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Keep migrate-everything reachable when the resource list fails

When the folder/dashboard enumeration fails, the table and every migrate action
disappeared — but migrate-everything is stats-driven and doesn't need that list.
The folder-error state now offers a "Migrate everything" action (or the connect
action when no write-capable repo) alongside the warning, so migration stays
reachable; the warning copy points at refreshing to pick individual resources.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Harden selective migration and fail loudly on truncation

Address Copilot review:
- The drawer now refuses to run in selective mode with no resources: the
  primary action is disabled (with a tooltip) and startMigration bails, so a
  selective click can never collapse into the migrate-everything job server-side.
- useFolderMigrationData throws when the result set exceeds MAX_PAGES instead of
  returning a silently truncated list — an incomplete enumeration would drop
  rows and corrupt the selective payload. The error surfaces the
  migrate-everything fallback, which doesn't need the full list.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Tailor migrate limitations to the repository sync target

The migrate drawer hardcoded syncTarget="instance", so the instance-only
"existing alerts and library panels will be lost" warning showed even for
folder-target repos. Pass the selected repository's spec.sync.target instead,
so the limitations alert reflects instance vs folder/folderless sync.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

- Extract the folder-row component into FolderEntry.tsx and the sort helper
  (SortKey + compareFolders) into sorting.ts (+ sorting.test.ts), leaving
  ResourcesToMigrate.tsx as just the panel.
- Reword the subfolder-only hint to be clearer: "No resources directly here —
  they're in subfolders. Selecting this folder migrates everything inside it."

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Address Codex/Copilot review on the Migrate slice

- Keep empty unmanaged folders migratable (Codex P2): isMigratableFolder no
  longer requires a dashboard count, so when the only unmanaged items are empty
  folders the table still lists them and the migrate-all path stays reachable.
  The synthetic General row is now only added when there are real root-level
  dashboards, so it doesn't show up as an empty bogus target.
- Refresh the folder table after a migration (Codex P2): useFolderMigrationData
  exposes a background refetch (no loading flip, so the open drawer isn't
  unmounted) and Migrate calls it from onMigrated alongside the stats refetch.
- Reword repo-no-push-body so it's accurate for read-only repos too, not just
  PR-only ones (Copilot).
- Fix stale comments/JSDoc: the hook returns all folders and the UI decides what
  is migratable; selection.ts refers to the "Resources to migrate" table
  (Copilot).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Fix Resources to migrate footer pluralization

The footer keyed its plural on the number of rows shown, but the noun ("folder")
agrees with the total folder count — so "1 of 1" rendered "folders". Key the
plural on the total and interpolate the shown count separately, giving
"Showing 1 of 1 folder" / "Showing 2 of 5 folders".

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Drop unused subfolders from the folder migration data

`subfolders`/`FolderPeekSubfolder` were built in aggregate() but nothing reads
them — FolderEntry keys off directDashboards/dashboardCount. Remove the field
and the per-render grouping work (leftover from the dropped peek feature).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Parallelize folder/dashboard paging with a safety cap

Paging was sequential and unbounded across every folder and every dashboard,
slowing time-to-interactive. Fetch page 0 to learn totalRows, then fetch the
remaining pages concurrently, bounded by a generous MAX_PAGES guardrail so a
pathological response can't spin off unbounded requests.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Don't block the Migrate overview on the folder enumeration

The header and KPI cards only need the stats query, so gate the page on that
alone instead of also waiting for the full folder+dashboard enumeration. The
Resources to migrate table now carries its own loading state, so the overview
renders immediately on large instances instead of sitting behind "Loading
stats…" until every page is fetched.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Don't surface a bogus General migration target

When the root holds only managed dashboards from mixed tools, the General row
had managedBy undefined and dashboardCount 0 — so it showed up as an unmanaged
migration target with nothing to migrate. Only synthesize the General row when
there are unmanaged root dashboards, or when every root dashboard is managed by
a single agreeing tool (a managed row the table filters out). Skip it for the
mixed-managed-only case.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Gate Migrate on a write-capable repo with a reachable connect action

The table enabled "Migrate selected" whenever any repo existed, but the drawer
then blocked branch-only (non-write) repos — and the disabled-button tooltip
pointed at a connect action that wasn't on the tab. Now the footer gates on a
write-capable repo (matching the drawer's guard); when there isn't one it
renders the shared ConnectRepositoryButton instead of a dead disabled button,
so connecting a repository is reachable from the tab.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Track selective migration explicitly, not via resources.length

A partial selection of only empty folders resolves to no dashboard refs, and
deriving "selective" from resources.length then let it fall through to the
migrate-everything path (the backend treats empty resources as the legacy
all-resource migration). The drawer now takes an explicit `selective` prop, and
the page disables the migrate button when a partial selection has nothing
migratable to send — so an empty selection can never be mistaken for
migrate-everything.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Keep migrate-everything reachable when the resource list fails

When the folder/dashboard enumeration fails, the table and every migrate action
disappeared — but migrate-everything is stats-driven and doesn't need that list.
The folder-error state now offers a "Migrate everything" action (or the connect
action when no write-capable repo) alongside the warning, so migration stays
reachable; the warning copy points at refreshing to pick individual resources.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Harden selective migration and fail loudly on truncation

Address Copilot review:
- The drawer now refuses to run in selective mode with no resources: the
  primary action is disabled (with a tooltip) and startMigration bails, so a
  selective click can never collapse into the migrate-everything job server-side.
- useFolderMigrationData throws when the result set exceeds MAX_PAGES instead of
  returning a silently truncated list — an incomplete enumeration would drop
  rows and corrupt the selective payload. The error surfaces the
  migrate-everything fallback, which doesn't need the full list.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Tailor migrate limitations to the repository sync target

The migrate drawer hardcoded syncTarget="instance", so the instance-only
"existing alerts and library panels will be lost" warning showed even for
folder-target repos. Pass the selected repository's spec.sync.target instead,
so the limitations alert reflects instance vs folder/folderless sync.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
Provisioning: Limit selective export to 100 resources (#126949)

* Provisioning: Limit selective export to 100 resources

Selective export (push and migrate jobs with an explicit Resources list)
fetches each requested resource with an individual Get call, so an
unbounded list translates into an unbounded number of per-resource
lookups. Cap the list at 100 resources, validated at admission time so
oversized jobs are rejected before a worker picks them up.

* Add integration test

commit.message:
Provisioning: Mirror branch and pullRequest options on RepositoryView (#126953)

The branch and pull request options were added to RepositorySpec but not to
RepositoryView. The frontend reads per-repository options from the view (as it
already does for the commit template), so spec.branch and spec.pullRequest were
invisible to it.

Expose them on RepositoryView following the same pattern used for commit:
- BranchOptions is surfaced as `branchOptions` because the view already uses the
  flat `branch` field for the git target branch name; PullRequestOptions keeps
  the spec key `pullRequest`. This matches the existing frontend naming in
  RepositoryFormData.
- handleSettings populates both from the repository spec.
- The OpenAPI $refs are re-attached in PostProcessOpenAPI, same as commit.

Regenerated deepcopy/openapi, the OpenAPI snapshots, the grafana-openapi specs,
and the RTK frontend client.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
unified-storage: fix flake in lease expiration handoff test (#126952)

The TTL handoff subtest had holder b acquire the lease with the same
short 50ms TTL used to expire holder a, then release it immediately. On
a loaded CI runner the release path can take longer than 50ms, so b's
own lease expires before it can release it and the test fails with
ErrLeaseLost. Give b a long TTL so its release no longer races its own
expiry; a keeps the short TTL so the handoff is still exercised.

commit.message:
Provisioning: Dashboard-centric, non-recursive migrate flow (#126930)

* Provisioning: Always regenerate folder UIDs on migrate

Set generateNewFolderIDs on every migrate job (selective and migrate-everything,
from both the migrate drawer and the onboarding wizard). Migrated folders are
then created fresh on the subsequent pull instead of taking over the existing
folders — so the originals, and any alerts or library panels still in them, are
left untouched rather than ending up under a now-Git-managed folder.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Provisioning: Make the migrate table dashboard-centric and non-recursive

Selective migration moves only the resources directly inside a picked folder —
the backend doesn't recurse into subfolders — so align the table with that and
drop the machinery that implied otherwise:

- Overview: drop the standalone "Folders" and combined "All resources" cards;
  the objective is zero resources not managed by Git, so only the Dashboards
  card remains.
- Folder list: hide folders with no unmanaged resources directly inside them
  (empty, already-managed, or holding only subfolders). Selecting a folder
  migrates its direct resources; subfolders are migrated through their own row.
- Copy: fix the wording that overclaimed recursive/whole-folder migration, and
  keep it resource-generic (not dashboard-specific) so it still reads correctly
  as more resource types become migratable.
- Drop the dead code this leaves behind: recursive subtree counts, allDashboards,
  folder-level managedBy, and isMigratableFolder.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
TraceView: Detect pruned span summaries in trace model (#126019)

* feat(traceview): detect pruned span summaries in trace model

Span pruning replaces groups of similar spans with summary spans carrying
aggregation.* attributes, and reparents preserved outliers as siblings.
Extend the trace model so downstream TraceView components can identify and
render these without repeating tag lookups.

- Add SpanAggregation type and optional aggregation field on TraceSpan
  (durations kept in raw nanoseconds, source-faithful).
- Detect aggregation.is_summary / is_preserved_outlier in transformTraceData
  and extract span_count, duration min/max/avg/median (ns) and summary_span_id.
  Normal spans are left untouched.
- Add shared pruned-spans.fixture.ts (5 synthetic variants + 1 real-data
  ops baseline) for this and subsequent Tier 1 slices.

Foundation slice for grafana/grafana-adaptivetraces-app#1029 (Tier 1, #1018).

* test(traceview): clone pruned-span fixtures before transform; fix doc

Address Copilot review feedback:
- transformTraceData mutates its input; clone shared fixture singletons via
  structuredClone at each call site so reuse across tests can't share mutated
  state. Document the requirement in the fixture header.
- Correct the SpanAggregation doc comment to state aggregation is set only on
  summary / preserved-outlier spans, not any span with an aggregation.* tag.

* test(traceview): lock shared-fixture clone contract with regression test

Add a regression test asserting repeated transforms of a pruned-span fixture
are stable and the shared module-level singleton is never mutated. Verified it
fails if a structuredClone is dropped at a call site, guarding against future
cross-test contamination from transformTraceData's in-place mutation.

* style(traceview): fix prettier formatting in pruned span test

* test(traceview): lock strict-boolean detection of summary spans

Detection gates the entire pruned-span feature on is_summary === true
(real PutBool boolean). Add a regression test asserting a string "true"
is not detected, making the strict-match contract explicit in CI rather
than relying on point-in-time manual verification.

* fix(traceview): assert tags present in strict-boolean detection test

TraceSpanData.tags is optional; guard the lookup so Typecheck passes.

* docs(traceview): fix SpanAggregation doc, drop speculative TODO

Correct the opening line: aggregation.* tags are written onto summary
spans and preserved-outlier spans, not onto the pruned (removed) spans.
Verified against the spanpruningprocessor source/README.

Remove the speculative Tier 2 TODO block; that work is not planned and
the histogram config-gating rationale already lives in the fixture file.

* test(traceview): cover numeric coercion and NaN guard in detection

extractSpanAggregation coerces span_count / duration_*_ns via Number()
and drops non-numeric values with a Number.isNaN guard. The tag value
type is `any` and the transform is data-source-agnostic, so lock this
defensive behavior: numeric strings coerce, garbage is dropped (not NaN).

* fix(traceview): reject non-numeric aggregation values in detection

Number() coerces null/boolean/[]/'' to a misleading 0 or 1, which the
bare Number.isNaN check let through. Restrict to real numbers and
non-empty numeric strings before coercing. Add cases for null/false/
true/empty-string. (Copilot review feedback)

* chore(traceview): drop unused fixture aggregate export (knip)

summarySpanFixtures was imported nowhere; tests use the individual named
exports. knip flagged it as an unused export, failing Lint Frontend.

* fix(traceview): drop non-string summary_span_id instead of coercing

extractSpanAggregation assigned summarySpanId via String() whenever the
aggregation.summary_span_id tag was not undefined, so a null/false/0/empty
value (the tag type is `any`) was stored as a misleading "null"/"false"/"0".
Accept only a non-empty string. Add a regression test covering each falsey
input.
